title: Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Cobb Angle Beyond 25° in Female Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Patients.
patient_population: 1,119 female adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients treated at a single institution, July 2011-February 2023
clinical_problem: predicting which female adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis will progress to a Cobb angle beyond 25°, using minimal radiographic and questionnaire data collected at the first visit
model_description: Machine learning binary classification models (built with PyCaret) trained on first-visit demographic and whole-spine radiographic data to predict progression to Cobb angle >25° for proximal thoracic, main thoracic, and thoracolumbar/lumbar curves
headline_result: AUC 0.94 (proximal thoracic), 0.89 (main thoracic), 0.84 (thoracolumbar/lumbar); recall 0.90/0.85/0.81 respectively

title: Brain Alteration Patterns in Children with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Machine Learning Approach to Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
model_family: support vector machine on multimodal structural and diffusion measures
patient_population: 18 children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and 18 age- and sex-matched controls with similar cognitive and behavioral profiles
clinical_problem: whether the absent dystrophin in Duchenne muscular dystrophy leaves a detectable mark on the brain, which would explain the cognitive and behavioral features
model_description: Combines cortical thickness, structure volumes and diffusion measures in one multivariate classifier, with controls deliberately matched on cognitive and behavioral profile so that the classification cannot simply be picking up comorbidity. The forward model then localizes the signal to long fiber bundles — cerebellar peduncles, posterior thalamic radiation, fornix, medial lemniscus — and to motor, cingulate, hippocampal and insular cortex. The sample is small and the accuracy correspondingly optimistic.
headline_result: 97.2% classification accuracy between patients and matched controls

title: Diagnostic accuracy of convolutional neural network algorithms to distinguish gastrointestinal obstruction on conventional radiographs in a pediatric population.
patient_population: pediatric patients with abdominal radiographs: 540 normal, 298 surgically-corrected dilatation, 314 inflammatory/infectious dilatation, single center
clinical_problem: differentiating normal pediatric abdominal radiographs from gastrointestinal dilatation/obstruction, and surgical from non-surgical causes
model_description: Five transfer-learning CNN models classify pediatric abdominal radiographs as normal, surgically-corrected dilatation, or inflammatory/infectious dilatation, with and without an automated image-cropping preprocessing step.
headline_result: Best accuracy 96.9% (ConvNeXtXLarge with cropping) for normal vs abnormal; 94.6% (EfficientNetV2L) for surgical vs inflammatory dilatation

title: Predicting Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Ejection Fraction from Echocardiogram Via Deep Learning Approach in Tetralogy of Fallot.
patient_population: children with Tetralogy of Fallot
clinical_problem: Can a deep learning model predict cardiac MRI-derived ejection fraction from echocardiogram videos in children with Tetralogy of Fallot?
model_description: The EchoNet-Dynamic/EchoNet-Peds CNN model, fine-tuned via transfer learning, predicts left ventricular ejection fraction from echocardiogram videos using cardiac MRI-derived ejection fraction as ground truth in Tetralogy of Fallot patients.
study_design: retrospective model fine-tuning and validation study
headline_result: PSAX view: R2 0.79, MAE 4.41; A4C view: R2 0.53, MAE 6.4

title: Perceived Racism, Brain Development, and Internalizing and Externalizing Symptoms: Findings From the ABCD Study.
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
venue_label: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
body_region: brain (subcortical regions: amygdala, hippocampus, nucleus accumbens)
patient_population: 3,321 racial/ethnic minority youth from the ABCD study, split into training (n=2,674) and testing (n=647) sets
clinical_problem: assessing effects of perceived racial discrimination on longitudinal subcortical functional connectivity changes and internalizing/externalizing symptoms in adolescents
model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity of the nucleus accumbens, amygdala, and hippocampus is measured at baseline and two years later in adolescents from the ABCD study. Propensity score-weighted machine learning, trained and cross-validated on 80% of the sample and independently tested on the remaining 20%, assesses the effect of perceived discrimination on 2-year connectivity changes, followed by mediation analyses linking these brain changes to internalizing and externalizing symptoms.
headline_result: Perceived discrimination was significantly associated with 2-year connectivity changes in nucleus accumbens, amygdala, and hippocampus in both cross-validation and independent testing

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Recognition of Fetal Open Neural Tube Defect on Prenatal Ultrasound.
model_family: CNN transfer learning (EfficientNet B0, VGG16, Inception V3)
patient_population: 59 fetuses with open neural tube defect and 116 normal controls, 14-28 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: recognizing open fetal neural tube defect (open spina bifida) via the lemon sign on axial cranial ultrasound using deep learning
model_description: Input: axial trans-thalamic fetal cranial ultrasound images; output: CNN transfer-learning classification of normal vs. open neural tube defect (lemon sign) fetuses.
headline_result: EfficientNet B0 achieved 100%/95.83% training/validation accuracy, sensitivity 100%, specificity 89%

title: Automated Neonatal Hip Ultrasound System for Diagnosing Developmental Dysplasia of Hips Using Assistive AI.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
model_family: convolutional neural network (NASNetMobile, MobileNetV1, DenseNet121, EfficientNetV2B0, ResNet50; segmentation: UnestedUNet, DeepLabV3Plus)
patient_population: newborns undergoing hip ultrasonography
clinical_problem: Can an AI-assisted portable ultrasound system diagnose developmental dysplasia of the hip in newborns?
model_description: An AI diagnostic system, integrated with a smartphone-linked handheld ultrasound device, segments hip anatomy and calculates Graf angles to diagnose DDH; several CNN backbones were compared for classification and segmentation.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study
headline_result: NASNetMobile AUC 0.864 (95% CI 0.850-0.878); average Graf angle error rate 0.21 vs expert

title: A Deep Learning-Based Framework for Automatic Determination of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip from Graf Angles.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
patient_population: newborn hip ultrasound images
clinical_problem: Can a deep learning framework automatically determine Graf angles from newborn hip ultrasound for DDH diagnosis?
model_description: A deep learning framework (DeepLabv3+ with multiple backbone architectures) segments hip anatomy on ultrasound and uses a local maxima method to automatically determine Graf angles for DDH diagnosis.
study_design: retrospective method development and comparison study
headline_result: MobileNetV2 backbone: 94.64% accuracy, 86.99 Cohen's kappa, 94.31 F-score vs expert radiologists

title: Evaluating the reference accuracy of large language models in radiology: a comparative study across subspecialties.
publication_types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Observational Study
clinical_problem: evaluating whether large language models can generate accurate, non-fabricated bibliographic references for radiology literature review/education questions, including in pediatric radiology
model_description: Six general-purpose large language models (ChatGPT o1-preview, ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-4o with canvas, Google Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus) were prompted with 120 open-ended radiology questions (15 per subspecialty, including pediatric radiology) to generate cited references, and each response's reference accuracy and fabrication rate were scored against verified bibliographic sources.
release_evidence: named commercial products: ChatGPT (OpenAI), Google Gemini, Claude (Anthropic)
study_design: cross-sectional observational comparative study of LLM-generated radiology references
dataset_size: 120 questions (15 per subspecialty) across 8 radiology subspecialties
headline_result: Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 80.8% fully accurate references, 3.1% fabrication rate, significantly outperforming other models (P<0.001)

title: Deep Learning Auto-segmentation of Diffuse Midline Glioma on Multimodal Magnetic Resonance Images.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
patient_population: 52 pediatric patients with diffuse midline glioma (H3 K27M-altered), 70 MRI studies
clinical_problem: Automatic segmentation of diffuse midline glioma (DMG) on multimodal brain MRI to support tumor assessment in this rare, poor-prognosis pediatric brainstem cancer.
model_description: A modified 3D U-Net with residual blocks takes T1-weighted and T2-weighted/FLAIR MRI (individually or combined) as input and outputs a segmentation mask of the DMG tumor.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal test-set evaluation
headline_result: Average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 0.883 on the test dataset (best with combined T1W + T2W/FLAIR)

title: Identification of Atypical Scoliosis Patterns Using X-ray Images Based on Fine-Grained Techniques in Deep Learning.
patient_population: 508 pairs of coronal/sagittal spinal radiographs from patients with Chiari-malformation-associated scoliosis, adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, and normal controls
clinical_problem: Screening for scoliosis and, further, for atypical scoliosis patterns associated with Chiari Malformation type I using spinal X-rays.
model_description: Several ResNet-50-based fine-grained classification models (Coronal, Sagittal, Dual, Concat, Bilinear variants) take coronal and/or sagittal spine radiographs as input and output a scoliosis diagnosis and, for scoliotic cases, a classification distinguishing atypical (Chiari-malformation-associated) from typical adolescent idiopathic scoliosis; heatmaps highlight the radiographic features driving classification.
dataset_size: 508 pairs of coronal and sagittal spinal radiographs
headline_result: ResNet-50 Dual model reached the diagnostic level of senior spine surgeons for CMS diagnosis; ResNet-50 Coronal model surpassed senior surgeons in specificity and PPV

title: Automated Sella-Turcica Annotation and Mesh Alignment of 3D Stereophotographs for Craniosynostosis Patients Using a PCA-FFNN Based Approach.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: PCA-FFNN (Principal Component Analysis + Feedforward Neural Network)
patient_population: 153 CT scans, including 68 craniosynostosis subjects (infants)
clinical_problem: Noninvasively predicting the Sella turcica reference point for aligning 3D cranial stereophotographs in infants with craniosynostosis, to avoid the radiation of repeated CT for cranial morphology assessment.
model_description: A PCA-FFNN model takes 3D cranial surface models (derived from CT/stereophotography) as input and predicts the Sella turcica coordinate, used to align 3D stereophotographs within a standardized reference frame as a noninvasive alternative to CT-based cranial assessment.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study
headline_result: PCA-FFNN achieved significantly lower Sella turcica coordinate prediction error than the conventional CCFP method (3.61 vs. 8.38 mm, P < 0.001)

title: Quantifying Sagittal Craniosynostosis Severity: A Machine Learning Approach With CranioRate.
journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
venue_label: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
model_family: machine learning (supervised Sagittal Severity Score + unsupervised Cranial Morphology Deviation)
patient_population: 195 nonsyndromic sagittal craniosynostosis, 221 nonsyndromic metopic craniosynostosis, 178 age-matched controls; 54 surgeons rated 20 patients' CT scans
clinical_problem: objectively quantifying the severity of sagittal craniosynostosis to standardize assessment and surgical planning
model_description: CranioRate uses a supervised machine learning model (Sagittal Severity Score, trained on surgeon Likert ratings) and an unsupervised model (Cranial Morphology Deviation) on CT-derived cranial landmarks to quantify sagittal craniosynostosis severity, compared against the traditional cephalic index.
study_design: cross-sectional model development with expert rating comparison
dataset_size: 195 SCS, 221 metopic CS, 178 controls; 54 surgeons rated 20 CT scans
headline_result: Sagittal Severity Score significantly more accurate than cephalic index in predicting expert ratings (P<.05); Cranial Morphology Deviation correlated with SSS (Pearson 0.92)

title: Characterization of Healthy Pancreas Morphology Throughout Childhood.
patient_population: 140 children under 18 years of age, contrast-enhanced CT
clinical_problem: Characterizing normal pancreas morphology and shape across childhood to establish reference growth patterns using CT-based 3D segmentation
model_description: Manual 3D segmentation of the pancreas on contrast-enhanced CT is used to extract radiomic shape features; elastic net regression models predict pancreas volume and shape metrics from age, weight, height, and body surface area.
headline_result: cross-validated r2 0.71-0.89 for pancreas volume/shape metrics

title: External validation of an artificial intelligence tool for fracture detection in children with osteogenesis imperfecta: a multireader study.
patient_population: 48 patients with osteogenesis imperfecta from a single OI clinic
clinical_problem: fracture detection in children with osteogenesis imperfecta
model_description: A commercially available AI fracture-detection tool analyzes appendicular and pelvic radiographs from children with osteogenesis imperfecta to flag fractures; seven radiologists' accuracy was compared before and after seeing the AI output, against a consensus reference standard.
release_evidence: a commercially available AI tool for fracture detection
dataset_size: 336 images from 48 patients (mean age 12 years), 206 fractures
headline_result: AI per-exam accuracy 74.8%, radiologists alone 83.4%, radiologists with AI 90.7%

title: Super-resolution deep learning in pediatric CTA for congenital heart disease: enhancing intracardiac visualization under free-breathing conditions.
patient_population: 91 pediatric patients aged 1-10 years suspected of congenital heart disease, single center
clinical_problem: improving intracardiac visualization on pediatric cardiac CT angiography for congenital heart disease under free-breathing conditions
model_description: Super-resolution deep learning reconstruction is compared against conventional deep learning reconstruction and hybrid iterative reconstruction for pediatric cardiac CT angiography acquired under free breathing, assessed for image quality and diagnostic accuracy of congenital heart disease.
headline_result: SR-DLR accuracy 99.12%, sensitivity 99.07%, exceeding conventional DLR and hybrid iterative reconstruction

title: Non-invasive meningitis screening in neonates and infants: multicentre international study.
patient_population: 76 patients under 24 months with suspected meningitis, across Spain, Mozambique, and Morocco
clinical_problem: Screening for meningitis in neonates and infants using non-invasive transfontanellar ultrasound instead of lumbar puncture
model_description: A deep learning model classifies high-resolution transfontanellar ultrasound images of cerebrospinal fluid to predict elevated white blood cell counts (>=30 cells/mm3), screening for meningitis without lumbar puncture.
headline_result: sensitivity 94.4%, specificity 94.8%

title: Image quality in ultra-low-dose chest CT versus chest x-rays guiding paediatric cystic fibrosis care.
patient_population: Children with cystic fibrosis; ten paired ULDCT/CXR image sets rated by 75 participants (25 radiologists, 50 radiographers)
clinical_problem: Comparing image quality of ultra-low-dose CT (AI-enhanced reconstruction) versus chest X-ray for monitoring lung disease in children with cystic fibrosis
model_description: Ultra-low-dose CT using AI-enhanced deep-learning iterative reconstruction achieves chest-X-ray-comparable radiation doses; image quality and diagnostic confidence were compared with conventional chest X-ray by radiologists and radiographers in children with cystic fibrosis.
dataset_size: 10 paired ULDCT/CXR image sets; 75 reader participants
headline_result: 88% of readers preferred ULDCT over CXR; VGC AUC 0.63

title: Constructing a Predictive Model for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Whole-Brain MR Radiomics: A Machine Learning Study.
model_family: radiomics + machine learning (decision tree with radiomics signature)
body_region: brain (whole-brain: white matter, gray matter, CSF)
patient_population: 223 subjects from ABIDE database (120 ASD) for training/test; independent external test of 87 participants (38 ASD) from Georgetown/Miami ASD datasets
clinical_problem: Building an objective predictive model to identify children with autism spectrum disorder using whole-brain structural MRI radiomics, to complement subjective behavioral diagnosis
model_description: A radiomics-based machine learning model extracting whole-brain white matter, gray matter and CSF structural MRI features, combined with a clinical predictor (Verbal IQ) via multivariate logistic regression, with a decision-tree joint model classifying children as ASD versus non-ASD and stratifying low-/high-risk subgroups.
study_design: Retrospective multi-cohort model development with independent external validation using public datasets
headline_result: Joint radiomics+VIQ decision-tree model AUC 0.87 (training), 0.84 (test), 0.83 (external test)

title: A Novel Dual-Output Deep Learning Model Based on InceptionV3 for Radiographic Bone Age and Gender Assessment.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
patient_population: 14,048 hand-wrist radiographs from the 2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge open dataset
clinical_problem: Automating bone age and sex assessment from hand-wrist radiographs to support clinical decision-making.
model_description: An InceptionV3-based multi-output model with Squeeze-and-Excitation layers takes a digital hand-wrist radiograph as input and simultaneously outputs a predicted bone age and predicted sex.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal test-set evaluation using a public dataset
dataset_size: 14,048 hand-wrist radiographs (2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge), 7:2:1 train/val/test split
headline_result: Bone age: MSE ~25, MAE 3.1, ICC 0.997; sex classification: accuracy 95%, AUC 97%, Cohen's kappa 0.898

title: Artificial Intelligence for the Detection of Fetal Ultrasound Findings Concerning for Major Congenital Heart Defects.
patient_population: 877 examinations from 11 centers, second-trimester fetal ultrasounds
clinical_problem: identifying second-trimester fetal ultrasound findings suspicious for major congenital heart defects using AI-based software, to improve antenatal CHD detection
model_description: AI-based software analyzes grayscale 2D ultrasound cine clips from second-trimester fetal echocardiographic examinations as input and outputs presence/absence/inconclusive labels for eight morphologic findings associated with severe congenital heart defects.
headline_result: Sensitivity 0.968 for severe CHD; sensitivity 0.987, specificity 0.977 for detecting any suspicious finding vs fetal cardiologists

title: Decoding fetal motion in 4D ultrasound with DeepLabCut.
patient_population: 50 four-dimensional ultrasound recordings of normal singleton fetuses, 12-22 gestational weeks
clinical_problem: Objectively and quantitatively assessing fetal motor behavior and neurodevelopment from 4D ultrasound video.
model_description: A customized DeepLabCut model, trained on manually labeled fetal joint positions, tracks eight fetal joints across 4D ultrasound video frames to quantify joint angular velocity and movement coordination over gestational age.
headline_result: Model achieved a mean likelihood (tracking accuracy) score of 0.960; inter-rater ICC 0.990, intra-rater ICC 0.961 for manual labeling

title: Computer-aided diagnosis of DDH using ultrasound: deep learning for segmentation and accurate angle measurement aligned with radiologist's clinical workflow.
patient_population: 370 newborns (452 raw images)
clinical_problem: Computer-aided diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip via automated ultrasound segmentation and Graf angle (alpha/beta) measurement
model_description: Deep learning segmentation models (U-Net, Mask R-CNN, YOLOv8, YOLOv11) segment hip ultrasound anatomy and calculate Graf alpha and beta angles for developmental dysplasia of the hip assessment, benchmarked against expert measurements.
headline_result: YOLOv11 Dice 0.990, mAP 0.991; ICC alpha/beta 0.929/0.952 (Method-II)

title: Brain Myelin in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Longitudinal T1-Weighted/T2-Weighted Ratio Study.
journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
venue_label: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
patient_population: 400 scans (195 with ADHD), community-based pediatric cohort, ages 9-14
clinical_problem: Characterizing developmental trajectories of white matter myelination in children with ADHD compared to typically developing children
model_description: A deep learning-based automated tractography method defines white matter tracts from diffusion-weighted MRI, from which T1-weighted/T2-weighted ratio myelin estimates are derived longitudinally in children with and without ADHD.

title: Comprehensive analysis of [18F]MFBG biodistribution normal patterns and variability in pediatric patients with neuroblastoma.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
venue_label: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
patient_population: 169 pediatric neuroblastoma patients (20 in confirmed remission)
clinical_problem: Characterizing normal physiological biodistribution of [18F]MFBG PET/CT in pediatric neuroblastoma patients to distinguish normal from pathological uptake
model_description: Deep learning-based automatic segmentation quantifies organ uptake on [18F]MFBG PET/CT scans in pediatric neuroblastoma patients, characterizing normal physiological biodistribution patterns to aid image interpretation.

title: Diagnostic value of artificial intelligence-based software for the detection of pediatric upper extremity fractures.
patient_population: 826 pediatric patients aged 2-18 years
clinical_problem: Detecting upper extremity fractures in children presenting to the emergency department
model_description: The commercial AI software BoneView analyzes radiographs of the pediatric upper extremity to detect fractures, compared against reference readings by two pediatric radiologists.
headline_result: sensitivity 89%, specificity 91% overall; wrist sens 96%/spec 94%, elbow sens 87%/spec 65%

title: Pulmonary T2* quantification of fetuses with congenital diaphragmatic hernia: a retrospective, case-controlled, MRI pilot study.
patient_population: 33 control fetuses and 12 fetuses with congenital diaphragmatic hernia
clinical_problem: Assessing fetal lung volumes and function (via T2* relaxometry) in congenital diaphragmatic hernia to help predict prognosis (survival)
model_description: A pre-trained 3D deep-learning pipeline segments fetal lungs on motion-corrected MRI to quantify lung volume and T2* relaxometry values, assessed as potential prognostic biomarkers for survival in congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
headline_result: CDH lung volumes and T2* significantly lower in non-survivors vs controls (p<0.05 to p<0.001)

title: CINeMA: Conditional Implicit Neural Multi-Modal Atlas for a Spatio-Temporal Representation of the Perinatal Brain.
patient_population: fetal and neonatal brains, including cases with pathologies such as agenesis of the corpus callosum and ventriculomegaly
clinical_problem: Build a spatio-temporal brain atlas to characterize normal and pathological fetal/neonatal brain development for tissue segmentation and age prediction
model_description: Takes multi-modal fetal/neonatal MRI and builds a latent implicit-neural representation conditioned on gestational/birth age and pathology, producing high-resolution spatio-temporal brain atlases that support tissue segmentation, age prediction, and synthetic image generation.
release_evidence: We release the code and atlases at https://github.com/m-dannecker/CINeMA.
study_design: retrospective atlas construction and evaluation with ablation studies

title: FetalMLOps: operationalizing machine learning models for standard fetal ultrasound plane classification.
clinical_problem: Classifying standard fetal ultrasound planes to support prenatal anomaly screening
model_description: FetalMLOps, a ten-step MLOps framework, operationalizes machine learning models for standard fetal ultrasound plane classification, covering data curation, model development, deployment via a RESTful API, explainability, and monitoring for clinical integration.

title: AI-Driven Fetal Liver Echotexture Analysis: A New Frontier in Predicting Neonatal Insulin Imbalance.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
venue_label: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
patient_population: 1,733 fetal liver ultrasound images (after quality exclusion from 2,339), pregnancies 37-42 weeks, with and without gestational diabetes
clinical_problem: Predicting elevated neonatal insulin (C-peptide) levels, a marker of neonatal insulin imbalance related to gestational diabetes, from fetal liver ultrasound echotexture.
model_description: CNN classification models (ResNet-18/34/50, EfficientNet-B0/B7) take fetal liver ultrasound images as input and predict whether the neonate will have elevated umbilical cord C-peptide (>75th percentile) at birth, as a non-invasive marker of neonatal insulin imbalance.
dataset_size: 1,733 fetal liver ultrasound images (606 excluded from 2,339 for quality)
headline_result: EfficientNet-B0 best performer: sensitivity 86.5%, specificity 82.1%, PPV 83.0%, NPV 85.7%, accuracy 84.3%, AUC 0.83

title: What is radiomics?
journal: Archives of disease in childhood. Education and practice edition
venue_label: Archives of disease in childhood. Education and practice edition
clinical_problem: Explaining what radiomics is and its potential clinical applications, for a pediatric clinician audience
model_description: Educational overview of radiomics (quantitative feature extraction from medical images) written for pediatric clinicians; abstract text not available.
study_design: educational review (Archives of Disease in Childhood Education and Practice edition)

title: SurfGNN: A robust surface-based prediction model with interpretability for coactivation maps of spatial and cortical features.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 481 subjects (503 scans) from a harmonized neonatal MRI dataset
clinical_problem: predicting neonatal (postmenstrual) brain age from cortical surface MRI features
model_description: SurfGNN models the cortical surface mesh as a sparse graph, using topology-sampling and region-specific learning modules to handle cortical morphometric features at multiple scales, with a score-weighted fusion of nodal representations to predict neonatal brain age and generate interpretable feature-level activation maps.
release_evidence: The codes will be available at https://github.com/ZhuoshL/SurfGNN
headline_result: MAE 0.827±0.056 postmenstrual weeks, ≥9.0% improvement over prior state-of-the-art

title: The combined use of cervical ultrasound and deep learning improves the detection of patients at risk for spontaneous preterm delivery.
journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
venue_label: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
patient_population: 4,224 pregnancies (7,862 cervical ultrasound images) from women who underwent cervical ultrasound during antenatal care in Denmark, 2008-2018
clinical_problem: predicting spontaneous preterm birth from cervical ultrasound, compared to cervical length measurement
model_description: A deep learning model is trained directly on cervical ultrasound images to predict spontaneous preterm birth, compared against the standard cervical-length measurement; saliency heat maps identify that the model attends to the inner lining of the lower uterine segment.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and validation
dataset_size: 4,224 pregnancies, 7,862 cervical ultrasound images, 19 hospital sites
headline_result: AI AUC 0.75 vs cervical length AUC 0.67 (sensitivity 0.51 vs 0.41 at fixed specificity 0.85)

title: Prediction of CSF Intervention in Fetal Ventriculomegaly via Artificial Intelligence-Powered Normative Modeling.
patient_population: 222 singleton pregnancies with fetal brain MRI; 64 fetuses with ventriculomegaly (14 requiring postnatal intervention)
clinical_problem: differentiating fetal ventriculomegaly from hydrocephalus and predicting need for postnatal CSF intervention
model_description: An nnU-Net segments the fetal ventricles on brain MRI to compute ventricular and subarachnoid volumes, which are compared to a normative reference range to classify ventriculomegaly and predict need for postnatal CSF intervention.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and validation
dataset_size: 222 patients (20 institutional + 80 public segmentations for training; 138 normal + 64 ventriculomegaly for testing)
headline_result: AUC 0.97 for ventriculomegaly and for postnatal intervention prediction; Dice 0.96 for segmentation

title: Early prediction of periventricular leukomalacia from MRI changes: a machine learning approach for risk stratification.
model_family: logistic regression with radiomics / random forest / LASSO feature selection
patient_population: 217 infants (2015-2022) with suspected motor abnormalities
clinical_problem: Early prediction of periventricular leukomalacia (white matter brain injury) in high-risk infants using clinical and MRI data
model_description: Inputs are clinical variables, conventional MRI features, and radiomic features extracted from white matter regions on axial MRI sequences; output is a multivariate logistic regression risk score for periventricular leukomalacia.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: 217 infants (training n=124, internal validation n=31, external validation n=62)
headline_result: AUC 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-1.00) in external validation cohort for combined clinical+MRI+radiomics model

title: Clinical deployment and prospective validation of an AI model for limb-length discrepancy measurements using an open-source platform.
patient_population: Shadow trial: 84 children (168 femoral/tibial lengths); clinical trial: 114 children (228 femoral/tibial lengths)
clinical_problem: Measuring limb-length discrepancy in children from EOS scanogram radiographs, and prospectively validating clinical deployment of the AI measurement tool.
model_description: An AI model, deployed via a Docker container on a clinical computational platform, takes EOS scanogram radiographs as input and outputs automated bilateral femoral and tibial length measurements to assess limb-length discrepancy; results were compared against radiologist-reported measurements in a hidden shadow trial and a visible clinical trial.
release_evidence: deployed using an open-source platform (per title: 'using an open-source platform')
study_design: prospective clinical deployment and validation study (shadow trial then clinical trial)
dataset_size: Shadow trial: 84 children/168 measurements; clinical trial: 114 children/228 measurements
headline_result: Median absolute difference of 0.2-0.3 cm (IQR 0.3-0.4 cm) between AI-measured and radiologist-reported femoral/tibial lengths in both trials

title: Automated detection of neonatal pulmonary hypertension in echocardiograms with a deep learning model.
model_family: spatial and spatio-temporal convolutional neural networks
patient_population: 975 echocardiography videos (training/validation) and 378 videos (held-out set) from infants aged 3-90 days, 2018-2022
clinical_problem: Automating detection of pulmonary hypertension in infants from standard echocardiography videos, which normally requires time- and expertise-intensive manual interpretation.
model_description: Spatial and spatio-temporal CNNs take standard echocardiography videos (five views) from infants as input and classify pulmonary hypertension versus healthy, using labels derived from the systolic eccentricity index, with gradient-weighted class activation mapping for explainability.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
headline_result: Best single-view (parasternal short axis) AUROC 0.91-0.94 (validation), 0.88-0.93 (held-out); combined three-view AUROC up to 0.96

title: Proof-of-concept comparison of an artificial intelligence-based bone age assessment tool with Greulich-Pyle and Tanner-Whitehouse version 2 methods in a pediatric cohort.
patient_population: 203 pediatric patients (mean age 9.0 years, range 2-17) undergoing hand/wrist radiographs for suspected endocrine or growth-related conditions
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for pediatric growth disorders
model_description: BoneView BoneAge, a commercial AI software, estimates skeletal bone age from hand and wrist radiographs; its estimates were compared against radiologist-assessed Greulich-Pyle and pediatric-endocrinologist-assessed Tanner-Whitehouse 2 methods using chronological age as reference.
release_evidence: commercially available artificial intelligence-based software (BoneView BoneAge, Gleamer, Paris, France)
dataset_size: 203 patients, 157 analyzed with AI/GP; 35-patient subset with TW2
headline_result: AI MAE 1.38 years vs GP 1.30 years vs TW2 2.86 years; AI bias -0.05 years, r=0.857

title: End-to-End Spatiotemporal Analysis of Color Doppler Echocardiograms: Application for Rheumatic Heart Disease Detection.
model_name: RADAR (Rapid AI-Assisted Echocardiography Detection and Analysis of RHD)
patient_population: 511 Ugandan children (1,022 echo videos), plus independent test set of 318 cases
clinical_problem: Detect early rheumatic heart disease from color Doppler echocardiograms in resource-limited settings
model_description: Takes color Doppler echocardiogram videos, uses convolutional neural networks to identify key views, analyze cardiac cycle phases, localize anatomy, and assess blood flow patterns, and outputs a classification for early rheumatic heart disease.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation on an independent device
dataset_size: 1,022 echocardiogram videos from 511 Ugandan children (training/validation), plus an independent test set of 318 cases
headline_result: Validation: accuracy 0.92, sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.90; independent test: accuracy 0.79, sensitivity 0.87, specificity 0.70

title: Non-invasive urine flow dynamics characterization of pediatric hydronephrosis based on deep learning and computational fluid dynamics.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
venue_label: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
model_family: deep learning (3D mesh reconstruction) + computational fluid dynamics

patient_population: over 10,000 de-identified pediatric forearm radiographs
clinical_problem: Providing a large annotated dataset and baseline classifier for detecting and classifying pediatric forearm (ulna and radius) fractures on X-ray
model_description: The PediURF dataset provides over 10,000 radiologist-annotated pediatric ulna/radius radiographs labeled by fracture type (proximal, midshaft, distal); URFNet, a dual-view (anteroposterior + lateral) classification model, is proposed and benchmarked on the dataset for automated fracture-type classification.
release_evidence: publicly available collection of >10,000 de-identified images (Scientific Data descriptor)
study_design: dataset descriptor with benchmark model development
headline_result: URFNet achieved the best classification performance compared with other classification models (specific metric not given in abstract)

title: Functional fingerprinting for the developing brain using deep metric learning.
patient_population: longitudinal neuroimaging cohort, childhood through early adolescence
clinical_problem: Characterizing individual functional brain architecture ('fingerprints') during childhood and adolescence using deep learning on longitudinal fMRI
model_description: Metric-BolT, a deep metric learning framework, extracts individual 'brain fingerprints' from longitudinal functional MRI to identify subjects across scan sessions and characterize developmental trajectories.
headline_result: Identification accuracy 97.6% (within-session) and 86.6% (across 4 years)

title: Artificial intelligence-driven 3D surface-topography app for screening and monitoring adolescent scoliosis: early results from a single institution.
patient_population: 125 patients (105 analyzed after exclusions) plus external data (142 controls, 188 scoliosis patients)
clinical_problem: Predicting Cobb angle from smartphone-based 3D surface topography to screen and monitor adolescent idiopathic scoliosis without radiation
model_description: An AI-powered smartphone application analyzes 3D surface-topography scans (standing and forward-bending) to predict radiographic Cobb angle for scoliosis screening and monitoring.
study_design: single-institution observational validation study with external data augmentation
dataset_size: 125 patients (79 training, 26 validation) + 142 external controls, 188 external scoliosis patients
headline_result: Correlation with radiographs r=0.922; MAE 5.9 deg overall, 6.4 deg in AIS 10-50 deg; AUC 0.978 at 10 deg, 0.917 at 25 deg, 1.000 at 40 deg

title: A probabilistic deep learning approach for choroid plexus segmentation in autism spectrum disorder.
patient_population: local ASD/control cohort (adults) and the ABIDE dataset (children and adults)
clinical_problem: segmenting the choroid plexus to study morphological alterations in autism spectrum disorder
model_description: ASCHOPLEX is a finetunable deep learning tool that segments the choroid plexus on brain MRI, with a probabilistic version added to quantify segmentation uncertainty; tested for generalizability to ASD cohorts including children.
study_design: retrospective model finetuning and multi-dataset validation
dataset_size: local dataset plus the ABIDE dataset
headline_result: generalized well in adults; accuracy declined in children (no single number given)

title: Altered white matter integrity in pediatric bipolar disorder and the potential role of psychotic symptoms revealed by free water elimination corrected and superficial white matter DTI analyses.
model_family: support vector machine (SVM) with leave-one-out cross-validation
patient_population: 27 patients with pediatric bipolar disorder and psychotic symptoms, 25 with pediatric bipolar disorder without psychosis, and 19 healthy controls
clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric bipolar disorder (with or without psychotic symptoms) from healthy controls using diffusion tensor imaging white matter metrics
model_description: Input is diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics (fractional, mean, radial and axial diffusivity) from standard, free-water-corrected, and superficial white matter models. A support vector machine with leave-one-out cross-validation uses regional DTI metrics to distinguish children/adolescents with pediatric bipolar disorder (with or without psychotic symptoms) from healthy controls. The abstract states the altered regions could effectively discriminate the groups but gives no numeric accuracy.
dataset_size: 71 participants (27 PBD with psychosis, 25 PBD without psychosis, 19 healthy controls)
headline_result: SVM analyses with leave-one-out cross-validation reportedly discriminated PBD patients from healthy controls using altered DTI metrics; no accuracy percentage given

title: Performance of an adult-trained AI tool for intracranial hemorrhage detection on head CT in children aged 6-17 years.
patient_population: 1,996 non-contrast head CTs, children/adolescents 6-17 years, 21 sites
clinical_problem: Evaluating whether an adult-trained, FDA-cleared AI tool for intracranial hemorrhage detection performs adequately on non-contrast head CT in children aged 6-17
model_description: An FDA-cleared, adult-trained AI tool analyzes DICOM head CT images to flag intracranial hemorrhage; performance is compared against radiologist-adjudicated ground truth derived with an NLP tool applied to reports.
release_evidence: FDA-cleared, adult-trained AI tool for ICH detection
headline_result: Sensitivity 94.2%, specificity 94.7%, accuracy 94.6%, PPV 62.5%, NPV 99.4%

title: Radiation-free Cobb angle estimation in adolescent scoliosis using surface topography and a linear regression model.
clinical_problem: Predicting Cobb angle without radiation using 3D surface topography for adolescent scoliosis monitoring
model_description: Principal component analysis reduces dimensionality of 3D surface-topography data; several machine-learning models (linear regression, neural networks, XGBoost, stacking) were compared, with a linear regression model (LRM) selected as best for predicting Cobb angle.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation study
headline_result: MAE 3.97 deg, RMSE 4.70 deg, correlation r=0.91 (linear regression model)

title: Infants have rich visual categories in ventrotemporal cortex at 2 months of age.
patient_population: more than 100 2-month-old infants (awake fMRI), with follow-up at 9 months
clinical_problem: characterizing the development of visual category representations in the infant brain using functional MRI, compared against a deep neural network model of vision
model_description: Input: awake fMRI responses to visual categories in infants; output: comparison of infants' neural representational geometry to that of a deep neural network model of vision, to characterize the developmental origin of visual category representations.
study_design: prospective developmental neuroimaging cohort study with computational model comparison

title: Performance Evaluation of a Commercial Deep Learning Software for Detecting Intracranial Hemorrhage in a Pediatric Population.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
patient_population: 2,502 pediatric patients aged 6-17 undergoing head CT, single center
clinical_problem: detecting intracranial hemorrhage on pediatric head CT
model_description: Aidoc, a commercial AI tool originally trained on adult data, analyzes head CT images to flag suspected intracranial hemorrhage; evaluated here in a pediatric population against a radiologist-adjudicated reference standard.
headline_result: sensitivity 96.0%, specificity 93.7%, accuracy 93.8%

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines.
patient_population: 30 structured clinical scenarios (hip ultrasound Graf classification and radiographic acetabular index findings)
clinical_problem: guideline-concordant management decisions for developmental dysplasia of the hip
model_description: ChatGPT-5.0 is given text descriptions of clinical and imaging (Graf ultrasound, acetabular index radiograph) findings for DDH scenarios and produces a management recommendation, scored for concordance with AAOS/AAP guidelines.
headline_result: 100% guideline-concordant accuracy in concordant scenarios with guided prompting; 95% for non-logged-in ChatGPT

title: 3D-QALAS synthetic MRI with Zero-DeepSub in children: initial experience including post-contrast imaging feasibility.
patient_population: 26 pediatric patients (mean age 8.4 years) undergoing clinically indicated brain MRI
clinical_problem: Generate multiple synthetic MRI contrasts (T1, T2, FLAIR) from a single accelerated acquisition to reduce pediatric brain MRI scan time while preserving diagnostic image quality
model_description: Takes an accelerated single 3D-QALAS MRI acquisition and applies scan-specific deep-learning-based subspace reconstruction (Zero-DeepSub) to synthesize T1-weighted, T2-weighted and FLAIR contrast images, including post-contrast sequences.
headline_result: High sensitivity/specificity for mass/lesion, encephalomalacia, collections (perfect agreement); abnormal enhancement sensitivity 0.40; kappa 0.55-1.00

title: Contribution of artificial intelligence to the imaging diagnosis of pediatric pulmonary tuberculosis.
journal: Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de Sao Paulo
venue_label: Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de Sao Paulo
patient_population: 179 patients aged 0-14 years with pulmonary TB or other diseases, Brazil
clinical_problem: diagnosing pediatric pulmonary tuberculosis from chest radiographs
model_description: CAD4TBv7.1, a WHO-approved adult CAD tool, analyzes pediatric chest radiographs to generate an abnormality score, compared against a clinical scoring system and microbiological confirmation of TB.
headline_result: AUROC 0.71 vs microbiological diagnosis; sensitivity 52%, specificity 86.3%

title: Image quality comparison between low-dose thin-slice deep-learning reconstruction and standard-dose thick-slice hybrid iterative reconstruction in pediatric abdominal CT.
patient_population: 82 children (<=6 years)
clinical_problem: Comparing image quality between low-dose deep-learning-reconstructed and standard-dose iteratively-reconstructed pediatric abdominal CT
model_description: Deep-learning reconstruction (DLR) applied to thin-slice (0.5mm) low-dose pediatric abdominal CT images is compared against standard-dose thick-slice (3.0mm) hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR), evaluating noise, contrast-to-noise ratio, edge sharpness, and diagnostic confidence.
headline_result: 59.5% lower radiation dose with DLR; equivalent contrast-to-noise ratio and higher diagnostic-confidence score (4.5 vs 3.4, p<0.001)

title: ESM-AnatTractNet: Advanced deep learning model of true positive eloquent white matter tractography to improve preoperative evaluation of pediatric epilepsy surgery.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
patient_population: 85 drug-resistant pediatric epilepsy patients, age 10.70+/-4.41 years
clinical_problem: preoperative identification of eloquent white matter pathways to reduce functional deficits in pediatric epilepsy surgery
model_description: ESM-AnatTractNet classifies true-positive eloquent white matter pathways from preoperative diffusion MRI tractography, combining electrical-stimulation-mapping coordinates with atlas-based anatomical labels, and predicts postoperative language outcomes.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and validation
headline_result: 97% accuracy classifying eloquent areas; 94% accuracy predicting no postoperative deficit; R=0.73 for language outcome

title: Pediatric coronary MR angiography with a two-minute scan using de-aliasing regularization based compressed sensing.
model_family: de-aliasing regularization-based compressed sensing deep learning reconstruction
patient_population: 123 pediatric patients (96 retrospective, 27 prospective)
clinical_problem: accelerating pediatric coronary MR angiography while preserving detection of coronary artery aneurysms
model_description: DARCS is a deep-learning reconstruction method that accelerates coronary MR angiography acquisition (to a two-minute scan) while preserving image quality and diagnostic detection of coronary artery aneurysms, compared with SENSE, PROST and hybrid DL-IR.
study_design: retrospective technique development with prospective clinical validation
headline_result: 100% sensitivity/specificity for CAA detection at 8x acceleration; scan time 92.4s vs 208.8s

title: Validation of an AI model for pediatric myelin maturation age assessment and benefits for junior radiologists.
patient_population: 817 brain MRI scans (0-12 months), 768 normal, 49 with documented delay
clinical_problem: estimating myelin maturation age from pediatric brain MRI, including in infants with delayed myelination
model_description: A pretrained CNN predicts myelin maturation age from pediatric brain MRI; the study validates its accuracy and tests whether providing AI predictions improves junior radiologists' myelin-age assessment accuracy and speed.
study_design: retrospective single-center validation with reader study
headline_result: AI MAE 1.3 months; AI assistance reduced junior radiologist MAE from 0.5-0.8 to 0.2 months

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based deep-learning radiomics score for survival prediction and risk stratification in pediatric hepatoblastoma receiving surgical resection.
patient_population: 106 patients (74 training, 32 external testing), two hospitals
clinical_problem: Predicting event-free survival and stratifying risk in children with hepatoblastoma before surgery, to guide neoadjuvant chemotherapy decisions
model_description: Deep-learning-based radiomics features automatically extracted from segmented pre-treatment MRI (T1 and T2) are combined into a deep-learning-based radiomics (DLBR) score, integrated with clinical variables into a nomogram to predict event-free survival in pediatric hepatoblastoma.
study_design: retrospective two-center study with external validation
headline_result: Integrated clinical-DL nomogram outperformed clinicopathologic predictors and the DLBR score alone for survival prediction (specific AUC not given)

title: Automated Echocardiographic Detection of Congenital Heart Disease Using Artificial Intelligence.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
model_family: multi-task, view-agnostic transformer-based deep learning model (built on PanEcho)
patient_population: 54,727 echos (median age 7.1 years) internal; 3,356 echos (median age 2.5 years) external, Boston Children's Hospital and referred patients
clinical_problem: automated detection of critical and non-critical congenital heart disease on echocardiography
model_description: EchoFocus-CHD is a transformer-based, view-agnostic model that analyzes echocardiogram videos to detect 12 critical and 8 non-critical congenital heart disease lesions.
dataset_size: 3.4 million videos, 54,727 echos internal; 167,484 videos, 3,356 echos external
headline_result: internal AUROC 0.94 (composite critical CHD); external AUROC 0.77, improving to 0.87 after retraining

title: Normative volumetric growth modeling of the whole fetal body, placenta and amniotic fluid for 3-dimensional T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
body_region: whole fetal body, placenta, amniotic fluid
patient_population: 357 healthy control pregnancies (16-41 weeks GA) plus 95 longitudinal scans (42 fetuses) and 86 preterm pregnancies
clinical_problem: Automating volumetric measurement of the fetus, placenta and amniotic fluid on 3D reconstructed T2-weighted MRI to enable normative growth curves for clinical use
model_description: A 3D U-Net, applied after deformable slice-to-volume 3D reconstruction of motion-corrupted T2-weighted MRI stacks, automatically segments the fetus, placenta and amniotic fluid; a reporting tool then generates centiles and z-scores for normative volumetric growth.
study_design: retrospective methodology-development study with normative modeling (medRxiv preprint)
dataset_size: 357 healthy controls; 95 longitudinal scans (42 fetuses); 86 preterm pregnancies
headline_result: Automated 3D segmentation required only minor corrections (<1% volume difference) in <25% of control datasets; preterm pregnancies had significantly lower fetal, placental and amniotic-fluid volumes/centiles than term controls

title: Machine learning to infer neurocognitive testing scores among adolescents and young adults with congenital heart disease.
patient_population: 89 adolescents and young adults with CHD (mean age 16 years)
clinical_problem: Inferring neurocognitive test scores in adolescents/young adults with congenital heart disease from brain imaging combined with genetic, clinical and socioeconomic factors
model_description: A multivariate model combining structural and diffusion brain MRI features with biological, socioeconomic, clinical and genetic data, built via forward-inclusion/backward-elimination with cross-validation, infers scores across 15 neurocognitive tests in seven domains.
study_design: retrospective cohort study with cross-validated multivariate modeling
headline_result: Correlation r=0.245-0.648 across domains; mean MAE 6.3 points; best for Digit Span (r=0.65)

title: The diagnostic value of enhanced CT radiomics and deep learning in differentiating pediatric peripheral neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma.
model_family: 3D-UNet segmentation with radiomics and LDA/LR classifiers
patient_population: 225 pediatric patients (161 neuroblastoma, 64 ganglioneuroblastoma)
clinical_problem: differentiating pediatric neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma
model_description: A 3D-UNet segments tumors on enhanced CT to automatically extract radiomic features, which are combined with clinical data (age, NSE) in LDA/LR classifiers to differentiate neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma.
headline_result: best model AUC 0.922 training, 0.913 validation; segmentation Dice 0.818

title: Radiography-based AI decision support for further post-traumatic knee MRI referral in children.
patient_population: 873 pediatric and adolescent patients up to age 19 with acute knee trauma, two sites
clinical_problem: deciding whether pediatric knee trauma radiographs warrant further MRI referral for internal injury
model_description: EfficientNet models analyze initial pediatric knee radiographs to predict clinically relevant internal knee injuries (confirmed on same-day MRI), aiming to guide further MRI referral.
study_design: retrospective two-site model development and evaluation
headline_result: best model (EfficientNet-B5) precision 0.7445, recall 0.7890, accuracy 0.7450

title: Deep learning model for identification of metabolic bone disease of prematurity using wrist radiographs.
patient_population: preterm infants under 1500g birth weight; internal 814 subjects, external 261 subjects
clinical_problem: identifying metabolic bone disease of prematurity
model_description: A DenseNet-based deep learning model analyzes wrist radiographs (postnatal age 4-8 weeks) of preterm infants to identify radiographic features of metabolic bone disease, tested as decision support especially for non-radiologists.
study_design: retrospective two-site model development with external validation and reader study
headline_result: internal AUROC 0.961 (sensitivity 94.4%, specificity 91.2%); external AUROC 0.927; non-radiologist reader accuracy improved 65.4% to 78.7%

title: Application of 3T contrast-enhanced Dixon water-fat separation coronary magnetic resonance angiography with artificial intelligence-assisted compressed sensing on coronary artery aneurysm in children with Kawasaki disease.
patient_population: 60 children with Kawasaki disease and suspected coronary artery disease, mean age 7+/-3 years
clinical_problem: detecting coronary artery aneurysms in children with Kawasaki disease
model_description: An AI-assisted compressed sensing reconstruction technique accelerates 3T contrast-enhanced coronary MR angiography, compared with a conventional compressed sensing technique for detecting coronary artery aneurysms in Kawasaki disease.
headline_result: sensitivity 96%, specificity 80%, accuracy 95% for CAA detection; scan time 230.6s vs 335.3s

title: Feasibility of single-phase DECT as an alternative to triple-phase CT for imaging-defined risk factors assessment in neuroblastoma for dose reduction.
patient_population: 94 pediatric neuroblastoma patients, ages 0-17 years
clinical_problem: reducing radiation dose in imaging-defined risk factor assessment for pediatric neuroblastoma
model_description: Deep learning image reconstruction is applied to single venous-phase dual-energy CT images (40 keV) to evaluate imaging-defined risk factors in neuroblastoma, compared with conventional triple-phase CT reconstructed with iterative reconstruction, for radiation dose reduction.
headline_result: over 60% radiation dose reduction; no difference in IDRF assessment between protocols

title: Parameter-efficient convolutional neural network for drug treatment outcome studies of pediatric epilepsy.
patient_population: 95 pediatric TSC patients
clinical_problem: predicting antiseizure medication treatment outcome in pediatric epilepsy due to tuberous sclerosis complex
model_description: eTSC-Net, a 3D CNN trained on T2-weighted and FLAIR brain MRI, predicts whether a child with tuberous sclerosis complex will achieve seizure control one year after starting anti-seizure medication.
headline_result: AUC 0.833 in test cohort (vs baseline ResNet3D 0.652)

title: A Multi-parametric MRI and Machine Learning Study of Cerebellar Structure in Youth with Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
patient_population: youth 5-16 years: 30 with NF1, 40 unaffected controls
clinical_problem: characterizing cerebellar structural differences in neurofibromatosis type 1 and their relation to cognitive/motor difficulties
model_description: Multi-parametric structural and diffusion MRI metrics of the cerebellum (volume, MD, FA, NDI, ODI) are combined with neuropsychological measures in a support vector model to classify NF1 versus unaffected youth.
headline_result: support vector modeling correctly classified 90.20% of participants

title: Prognostic role of delta radiomics in pediatric pontine diffuse midline gliomas.
model_family: texture/radiomics analysis with ROC and Cox regression (MaZda software)
patient_population: 35 pediatric patients with pontine diffuse midline glioma, 2012-2020
clinical_problem: prognostic stratification of pediatric pontine diffuse midline glioma
model_description: Delta-radiomics texture features (changes between pre- and post-treatment T1/T2 MRI) are used to predict overall survival in pediatric pontine diffuse midline glioma.
headline_result: median OS 13 months; delta radiomics (sum entropy) outperformed static features for predicting survival

title: [Deep Learning-Based Automated Segmentation Algorithms of Brain and Vertebral Substructures for Radiotherapy in Pediatric Medulloblastoma].
journal: Zhongguo yi liao qi xie za zhi = Chinese journal of medical instrumentation
venue_label: Zhongguo yi liao qi xie za zhi = Chinese journal of medical instrumentation
patient_population: 60 pediatric medulloblastoma radiotherapy patients, grouped by age (<=5 and >5 years)
clinical_problem: automated segmentation of organs at risk for radiotherapy planning in pediatric medulloblastoma
model_description: U-Net, nnU-Net and FuseNet are compared for automatic segmentation of brain substructures on CT-MRI fusion images and vertebral substructures on CT, to support radiotherapy planning in pediatric medulloblastoma.
study_design: retrospective model development and external validation
dataset_size: 60 patients (24 train/6 test per group, 20 external)
headline_result: FuseNet DSC >0.8 for most substructures, outperforming Atlas-based methods and U-Net

title: Modification of Objective Dejour Criteria Yields Excellent Diagnostic Accuracy for Pediatric Patellofemoral Instability.
journal: The American journal of sports medicine
venue_label: The American journal of sports medicine
patient_population: 144 knees (127 patients) with objective patellofemoral instability, age- and sex-matched to 144 controls; children and adolescents
clinical_problem: Diagnose pediatric patellofemoral instability from MRI-based trochlear dysplasia measurements using pediatric-specific thresholds
model_description: Takes seven MRI-based morphological measurements of the patellofemoral joint (e.g., sulcus angle, lateral patellofemoral angle) and uses regression-tree-derived pediatric-specific cutoffs, benchmarked against a random forest model, to classify patients as having patellofemoral instability.
study_design: retrospective case-control study with regression tree analysis
headline_result: Best cutoff combination (sulcus angle + LPFA): sensitivity 98%, specificity 85%, AUC 0.97

title: Demographic-aware deep learning for multi-organ segmentation: Mitigating gender and age biases in CT images.
patient_population: 489 adult (AMOS2022) and 370 pediatric (Pediatric CT-SEG) CT scans, 355 female scans
clinical_problem: mitigating age and gender bias in multi-organ segmentation for radiotherapy planning
model_description: DA-Net incorporates demographic prompts (age, gender) into hyper-convolution and attention modules to segment 30 organs on CT, explicitly aiming to reduce accuracy disparities between pediatric and adult patients and between genders.
study_design: retrospective multi-dataset model development with external validation
dataset_size: 489 adult + 370 pediatric CT scans; external validation on 150 WORD scans
headline_result: Dice 88.6% (adults), 75.3% (pediatric); 11-30% Dice improvement for gender-specific organs

title: Machine Learning-Based Identification of Functional Dysregulation Characteristics in Core Brain Networks of Adolescents with Bipolar Disorder Using Task-fMRI.
model_family: conventional machine learning classifiers (e.g., random forest)
body_region: brain (limbic system, prefrontal cortex, default mode network)
patient_population: 43 adolescents with bipolar disorder (15 remission, 11 depression, 17 mania) and 43 matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: identifying neuroimaging markers distinguishing adolescent bipolar disorder from healthy controls
model_description: Machine learning classifiers are applied to activation features from an emotional Go/NoGo task-based fMRI to distinguish adolescents with bipolar disorder from healthy controls and identify discriminative neuroimaging predictors.
headline_result: random forest accuracy 94.29%, AUC 98.57% (remission state)

title: Atlas-Assisted Bone Age Estimation from Hand-Wrist Radiographs Using Multimodal Large Language Models: A Comparative Study.
model_name: ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-3, Claude 4 Sonnet (comparative)
patient_population: 245 pediatric patients (109 male, 136 female) under age 18 undergoing left wrist radiography
clinical_problem: Estimate skeletal (bone) age from hand-wrist radiographs using the Gilsanz-Ratib atlas
model_description: Takes a hand-wrist radiograph plus the Gilsanz-Ratib bone age atlas as prompt input to four multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-3, Claude 4 Sonnet) and outputs an estimated bone age, compared with radiologist assessment.
release_evidence: four multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-3, and Claude 4 Sonnet)
headline_result: ChatGPT-5 best: MAE 1.46 years, ICC 0.849; Gemini 2.5 Pro MAE 2.24; Grok-3 MAE 3.14; Claude 4 Sonnet MAE 4.29

title: Assessing the Diagnostic Accuracy of BiomedCLIP for Detecting Contrast Use and Esophageal Strictures in Pediatric Radiography.
patient_population: 143 pediatric esophageal X-rays (2021-2025)
clinical_problem: Evaluating whether a vision-language foundation model can detect contrast-agent presence and esophageal strictures on pediatric esophageal radiographs
model_description: BiomedCLIP, a vision-language foundation model, is applied zero-shot (no fine-tuning) to classify pediatric esophageal radiographs for contrast-agent presence, esophageal visibility, and stricture presence.
headline_result: Contrast detection: precision 88.7%, AUC 85.4%; stricture detection: accuracy 24%, sensitivity 44%, AUC 0.26 (poor)

title: A Comprehensive Review of Artificial Intelligence Methods in Bone Age Assessment.
clinical_problem: Reviewing AI-based methods for pediatric bone-age assessment from hand/wrist radiographs and the challenges limiting generalizability
model_description: Educational review of AI approaches (including an RCNN-based model evaluated by mean absolute error) for automated bone-age assessment from hand and wrist radiographs, discussing dataset diversity and validation limitations.

title: Deep learning-based cerebellar segmentation on T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery magnetic resonance imaging for detecting cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy in infants.
patient_population: 558 neonatal MRI scans for training; 492 normal and 40 abnormal (cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy) scans for validation
clinical_problem: detecting cerebellar hypoplasia/atrophy in infants via cerebellar volume measurement
model_description: A deep learning model segments the cerebellum on T2-weighted FLAIR infant brain MRI to quantify cerebellar volume; a brain-age-gap-like metric (predicted vs actual age from cerebellar volume) is used to detect cerebellar hypoplasia or atrophy.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation using public and independent datasets
dataset_size: 558 training scans; 492 normal + 40 abnormal validation scans
headline_result: Dice 0.962 (normal), 0.882 (abnormal); AUC 0.851 for detecting hypoplasia/atrophy

title: A Novel Method for Predicting and Diagnosing Fetal Growth Restriction: Texture Analysis Based on Ultrasound Images of Placenta During the Second Trimester (20-24 weeks).
model_family: artificial neural network classifier on texture features
patient_population: 200 placental ultrasound images (100 FGR, 100 normal) at 20-24 weeks
clinical_problem: predicting and diagnosing fetal growth restriction before clinical diagnosis
model_description: Texture features (grayscale histogram, co-occurrence and run-length matrices, wavelet transform) extracted from second-trimester placental ultrasound images are fed into an artificial neural network to predict fetal growth restriction.
study_design: retrospective case-control study with train/test split
headline_result: classification accuracy 86.50%, AUC 0.89

title: Neuroprognostication via Radiomics and Machine Learning Following Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Insult.
model_family: elastic-net penalized linear regression on radiomic features
patient_population: 167 neonates (gestational age >=35 weeks) with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia
clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcomes after neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
model_description: MRI-based radiomic measures from post-rewarming brain MRI in neonates with HIE are entered into an elastic-net regression model to predict 18-month Bayley cognitive, language, and motor developmental outcomes.
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort study with 10-fold cross-validation
headline_result: mean correlation 0.94, predictive R2 0.87 between predicted and observed outcomes

title: Application of AI to Ultrasonographic Images to Aid the Clinical Care of Pregnant Women With Pre-eclampsia in Uganda: A Protocol for a Pilot Study.
model_family: convolutional neural networks, ensemble learning, transfer learning (planned)
patient_population: 150 pregnant women seeking obstetric ultrasound in Mbarara, Uganda, about half with pre-eclampsia
clinical_problem: predicting pre-eclampsia complications from obstetric Doppler ultrasound
model_description: Study protocol to build an annotated Doppler obstetric ultrasound image dataset and train machine learning models (CNNs, ensemble and transfer learning) to predict maternal and fetal complications of pre-eclampsia.

title: Machine Learning Methods to Identify Pediatric Shunt Malfunction in the Acute Care Setting and the Development of ShuntGPT.
model_family: large language model + traditional ML (SVM, KNN, random forest, ANN)
patient_population: 1,167 pediatric ED neurosurgical consults for suspected shunt malfunction (2017-2022)
clinical_problem: Predicting need for shunt-revision surgery in pediatric ED patients with suspected shunt malfunction, using clinical, historical and radiographic (shunt series) variables
model_description: Multiple machine-learning models (SVM, K-nearest neighbors, random forest, artificial neural network) and a proprietary large language model (ShuntGPT) take 24 historical, clinical and radiographic variables (including shunt series findings) as input to classify whether a child needs shunt-revision surgery.
headline_result: Best models: ANN accuracy 84%/AUC 0.88; ShuntGPT accuracy 87%/AUC 0.927; without imaging, ShuntGPT AUC dropped to 0.84

title: Impact of Test Set Composition on AI Performance for Pediatric Radiograph Appendicular Skeleton Fracture Detection.
patient_population: 39,703 pediatric patients, appendicular trauma radiographs
clinical_problem: Evaluating how test-set composition (difficulty) affects measured performance of AI fracture-detection models for pediatric appendicular radiographs
model_description: EfficientNet (classification) and YOLOv8 (object detection) models trained to detect pediatric appendicular fractures on radiographs are evaluated on a 'difficult' test set (discordant initial/final reads) versus a 'matched' test set to quantify the effect of test-set composition on measured AI performance.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing test-set compositions
dataset_size: 39,703 patients; difficult set 392 patients/786 radiographs, matched set 526 patients/786 radiographs
headline_result: Difficult test set: 40% lower odds of correct classification for EfficientNet (OR 0.60) and 80% lower odds of detection for YOLOv8 (OR 0.20) vs matched set

title: Quality-label-free fetal brain MRI quality control based on image orientation recognition uncertainty.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: fetal brain MRI atlases and clinical datasets (normal and abnormal fetuses)
clinical_problem: automated quality control of fetal brain MRI stacks without quality labels
model_description: OR-KAN predicts fetal MRI stack orientation (axial/sagittal/coronal) and uses the prediction uncertainty as a label-free image-quality score, used to select the highest-quality stacks for brain volume reconstruction.
study_design: methods development and validation across two MRI sequence datasets
dataset_size: seven fetal brain atlases plus TSE and BTFE clinical datasets
headline_result: AUROC 0.840 (TSE); improved brain reconstruction success rate from 64.4% to 83.2% (normal) and 60.0% to 85.5% (abnormal)

title: Dual-Modal Deep Learning with In-Domain Training and Attention for Infant Brain Myelination Prediction.
patient_population: 833 samples from a publicly available infant brain MRI dataset
clinical_problem: assessing myelin maturation in infants from MRI
model_description: A dual-input deep learning model fuses T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI features via cross-attention to predict myelin maturation age, with Grad-CAM interpretability.
study_design: retrospective model development using a public dataset
headline_result: MAE 1.18 months, PCC 0.98, R2 0.96

title: Cognitive Process Models Reveal Meaningful Brain-Behavior Associations in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study Stop-signal Task.

title: Automated bone age assessment in rare pediatric growth disorders: a comparative study using Deeplasia.

title: Three-Dimensional Postmortem Ultrasound of the Fetal Corneal Volume to Estimate Postmortem Interval.

release_evidence: A Shiny web application was developed to facilitate clinical implementation (no URL or open-source statement given)
study_design: single-center model development with prospective validation cohort
headline_result: training R2 0.91 (RMSE 11.49h, MAE 8.45h); validation R2 0.75 (RMSE 18.32h, MAE 14.49h)

title: Insights into Accelerated MRI Protocols for Pediatric Brain Assessment in Emergency Cases.

clinical_problem: shortening emergency pediatric brain MRI while preserving diagnostic image quality
model_description: Two vendor deep-learning-accelerated MRI protocols, GOBrain (3D volumetric encoding, compressed sensing, DL reconstruction) and Deep Resolve Swift Brain (multi-shot EPI with DL reconstruction), are demonstrated on a series of pediatric emergency brain cases to produce a multi-contrast diagnostic brain MRI in minutes.
release_evidence: GOBrain and Deep Resolve Swift Brain, developed by Siemens Healthineers

title: Analysis of fetal MRI data reveals no effect on liver maturation following prenatal alcohol exposure.
model_family: random forest (ensemble) and L2-penalized logistic regression radiomics
patient_population: 21 fetal MRIs with prenatal alcohol exposure and 45 without, gestational age matched

title: AI-powered ultrasound radiofrequency analysis for non-invasive pediatric liver fat quantification.
patient_population: 40 pediatric patients (age 12.16+/-2.56 years) referred for suspected MASLD
clinical_problem: noninvasive quantification of liver fat (MASLD) in obese children

title: Nomogram combining ultrasound radiomics and clinical factors for predicting placenta accreta spectrum in patients with placenta previa: a two-center study.
