headline_result: clinical-radiomics nomogram AUC 0.859 (training), 0.822 (external validation)

title: Development and validation of a prognostic model of postnatal circulation in fetuses with pulmonary atresia or critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum: protocol for an observational cohort study with prospective validation.
model_family: multivariable logistic regression (planned); machine learning as secondary analysis
patient_population: non-intervened fetuses diagnosed with PA/CS-IVS between 16+0 and 28+6 weeks' gestation, international cohort, retrospective (from 2013) plus prospective validation
clinical_problem: predicting postnatal circulation outcome in fetuses with pulmonary atresia/critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum, for counseling and intervention selection
model_description: Study protocol for an international cohort that will use standardized prenatal and postnatal fetal echocardiographic data to build a multivariable logistic-regression prognostic model (with a planned machine-learning secondary analysis) predicting postnatal circulation outcome in fetuses with pulmonary atresia/critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum.
study_design: protocol for an international observational cohort study with prospective external validation

title: Limbic structural markers of language delay in late-preterm children by NeuroQuant and machine learning.
model_family: automated brain volumetry + machine-learning-style feature selection with logistic regression
body_region: brain (limbic structures: amygdala, hippocampus, nucleus accumbens)
patient_population: 151 late-preterm children (31 with language delay, 120 without), T1-weighted MRI at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: identifying structural brain correlates of language delay in late-preterm children
model_description: NeuroQuant, an automated volumetry tool, measures limbic and striatal brain structure volumes from term-equivalent-age T1 MRI in late-preterm infants; exploratory feature selection and logistic regression relate these volumes to later receptive and expressive language delay.
headline_result: language delay associated with increased left amygdalar volume and decreased hippocampal volume

title: TLEUDS: a cascade Dual-Transfer learning system with quality- and knowledge-enhanced for precise fetal CHD screening.
model_family: cascaded dual-transfer learning (TEN-S: transfer EfficientNetV2; TY-PS: transfer YOLOv11)
patient_population: 9,142 fetal aortic arch echocardiographic long-axis view images and 58 ultrasound clips from three medical institutions
clinical_problem: screening for ductal-dependent congenital heart disease and differentiating critical subtypes (coarctation of aorta, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of great arteries) on fetal echocardiography
model_description: TLEUDS is a cascaded dual-transfer-learning system for fetal echocardiography: a first module (TEN-S, based on EfficientNetV2) screens for ductal-dependent congenital heart disease, and a second module (TY-PS, based on YOLOv11) further classifies critical subtypes (coarctation of the aorta, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of the great arteries), designed to handle variable image quality across sites.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and validation
dataset_size: 9,142 fetal aortic arch images and 58 ultrasound clips from three institutions
headline_result: sensitivity 0.988 (D-CHD overall), 0.941 (CoA), 0.966 (IAA), 0.900 (TGA); specificity 0.988, 0.987, 1.000, 0.956 respectively

title: Improved BG-PVS Quantification in Infant Brain MRI Using Anatomy-Informed Pseudo-Labels for Joint BG and PVS Segmentation.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
venue_label: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 150 neonates (dHCP), 133 infants (BCP), 70 infants (in-house) = 353 total
clinical_problem: Reliably quantifying perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia on infant brain MRI to study the glymphatic system, which is challenging in infants
model_description: A deep-learning method using anatomy-informed pseudo-labels jointly segments the basal ganglia (BG) and BG perivascular spaces (PVS) on infant brain MRI across three cohorts with different acquisition protocols.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort technical development and validation study
headline_result: BG Dice 0.91 (dHCP), 0.86-0.89 (external with fine-tuning); PVS quantification agreement r=0.90-0.99, ICC>=0.96

title: FDA-Regulated AI-Enabled Medical Devices With Pediatric Indications.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: pediatric patients (ages 0-17) captured in FDA device labeling; analysis of 952 FDA AI device submissions (Nov 1995-June 2024)
clinical_problem: Characterize the landscape of FDA-regulated AI-enabled medical devices with pediatric indications, including radiology devices
model_description: A cross-sectional analysis of the FDA AI-Enabled Medical Device List characterizing which of 952 marketed AI devices (most in radiology) carry pediatric age-range indications, review times, and clinical trial registration.
release_evidence: FDA's AI-Enabled Medical Device List... Marketing submissions reviewed by the FDA
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional study of FDA regulatory submissions
dataset_size: 952 FDA AI device submissions; 42 (4.4%) with pediatric age ranges
headline_result: 42/952 (4.4%) devices had pediatric indications; radiology = 75.9% of all devices but only 42.9% of pediatric-labeled devices; pediatric device review time longer (162 vs 134 days, P=.049)

title: Scalable and Robust Artificial Intelligence for Spine Alignment Assessment: Multicenter Study Enabled by Real-Time Data Transformation.
model_family: deep learning (HRNet-based) with pixel intensity data transformation
patient_population: 3,899 full-spine radiographs from 7 hospitals (2 in Hong Kong, 5 in Mainland China), January 2012-August 2024
clinical_problem: automating Cobb angle measurement and severity classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis across multiple hospitals
model_description: SpineHRNet+ is a deep learning model that predicts Cobb angle and scoliosis severity from full-spine radiographs; this study adds a real-time pixel-intensity data transformation step to standardize contrast/brightness across scanners and hospitals, improving robustness when applied to radiographs from centers outside the training sites.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation
dataset_size: 3,899 radiographs from 7 hospitals (3,034 training/internal validation, 865 external validation)
headline_result: mean Cobb angle prediction error within 4 degrees (SD 3.12 degrees), R2 >0.90 across all centers; sensitivity 90.18%, negative predictive value 93.16% for severity grading

title: DeepSeek-R1 performance in fusion planning of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A preliminary study.
patient_population: 203 consecutive AIS surgical patients
clinical_problem: Using a large language model to recommend surgical fusion levels (upper/lower instrumented vertebrae) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis surgery, based on structured clinical and radiological (Lenke classification) data
model_description: DeepSeek-R1, a large language model, receives structured clinical and radiological data (including Lenke classification derived from spinal imaging) as text prompts and outputs recommended upper and lower instrumented vertebrae levels for scoliosis fusion surgery.
release_evidence: DeepSeek Reasoning Model R1 (DeepSeek-R1) is a publicly available large language model
headline_result: Surgically reasonable fusion levels (Likert >=3) in 70.9% of cases (144/203); ICC 0.840 inter-rater agreement

title: Beyond benchmarks of IUGC: Rethinking requirements of deep learning method for intrapartum ultrasound biometry from fetal ultrasound videos.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 774 videos (68,106 images), 3 hospitals (IUGC Grand Challenge dataset)
clinical_problem: Improving deep-learning-based automatic biometry from intrapartum ultrasound video to monitor labor progress where trained sonographers are scarce
model_description: The Intrapartum Ultrasound Grand Challenge (IUGC, with MICCAI 2024) framework integrates standard-plane classification, fetal head-pubic-symphysis segmentation, and biometry measurement; this paper reviews eight teams' submitted deep-learning methods and analyzes their preprocessing, augmentation, architecture and post-processing choices.
release_evidence: "The solutions and the complete dataset are publicly accessible"

title: CNN-based detection of pediatric lymphoma on whole body [18F]FDG-PET/MRI.
journal: American journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
venue_label: American journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
patient_population: 53 pediatric lymphoma patients for training, 30 additional scans for testing
clinical_problem: detecting pediatric lymphoma lesions on whole-body PET/MRI
model_description: A convolutional neural network is trained on annotated whole-body [18F]FDG-PET/MRI scans from pediatric lymphoma patients to detect lesions across five anatomical regions, and its sensitivity, specificity, and reading time are compared with a pediatric radiologist and a radiology resident.
headline_result: CNN sensitivity 84.6%, specificity 93.7% (vs resident 69.2%/81.5%, vs pediatric radiologist 98.7%/99.5%); median read time 4 min (CNN) vs 8 min (radiologist) vs 15 min (resident)

title: Deep learning model for automated identification of ventrally positioned right hepatic artery in contrast-enhanced computed tomography of pediatric congenital biliary dilatation: development and clinical application.
patient_population: 232 patients with congenital biliary dilatation (116 with ventrally positioned right hepatic artery, 116 controls), single center
clinical_problem: preoperative identification of a ventrally positioned right hepatic artery in children with congenital biliary dilatation, to reduce surgical risk
model_description: A YOLOv12-based model trained on radiologist-selected key arterial-phase CT slices detects a ventrally positioned right hepatic artery, a surgically important anatomic variant, in children with congenital biliary dilatation, and is compared against two radiologists.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and reader comparison
headline_result: best sub-model (YOLOv12n) recall 0.842, F1 0.914, mAP50 0.989, AUC 0.977; outperformed junior radiologist (AUC 0.737, P<0.001), comparable to senior radiologist (AUC 0.947, P=0.515)

title: A 23-µJ-per-Frame All-on-Chip TinyML U-Net Processor for Real-Time Autonomous Image Segmentation in Miniaturized Ultrasound Devices.
journal: IEEE transactions on biomedical circuits and systems
venue_label: IEEE transactions on biomedical circuits and systems
patient_population: bladder and fetal head ultrasound segmentation datasets (not further specified)
clinical_problem: enabling real-time autonomous ultrasound image segmentation (e.g. prenatal fetal biometry, bladder/urinary retention monitoring) on wearable, battery-powered devices
model_description: A custom 28nm chip implements a binarized U-Net with 4-bit skip connections for on-device, real-time medical image segmentation in wearable ultrasound patches, validated on bladder and fetal head segmentation datasets, aiming to preserve accuracy while eliminating external memory and cutting energy use for battery-powered, privacy-preserving deployment.
headline_result: 13.4 frames per second, 23 microJ per frame on bladder and fetal head segmentation datasets

title: Towards Objective Obstetric Ultrasound Assessment: Contrastive Representation Learning for Fetal Movement Detection.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
model_family: self-supervised contrastive learning (dual spatial/temporal contrastive loss)
patient_population: 92 subjects, each with 30-minute extended fetal ultrasound video recordings
clinical_problem: objectively detecting fetal movement from ultrasound video to assess prenatal health
model_description: CURL is a self-supervised contrastive learning framework that learns motion representations from extended obstetric ultrasound video recordings, using a dual spatial-temporal contrastive loss and a task-specific sampling strategy, to detect fetal movement without relying on maternal perception or cardiotocography.
release_evidence: Our code is available at: https://github.com/Mr-TalhaIlyas/CURL/
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
headline_result: sensitivity 78.01%, AUROC 81.60%

title: Neuroanatomy reflects individual variability in impulsivity in youth.
model_family: multivariate brain-based predictive machine learning models
body_region: brain (cortical thickness, surface area, gray matter volume)
patient_population: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study participants at baseline (n=8630), 2-year (n=5998), 4-year (n=4844), and 6-year (n=3100) follow-up
clinical_problem: identifying neuroanatomical correlates of impulsivity in youth
model_description: Multivariate brain-based predictive models use regional cortical thickness, surface area, and gray matter volume from structural MRI to predict self-reported impulsivity measures in a large, longitudinal youth cohort, examining consistency across sexes and developmental timepoints.

title: U-Net-based transfer learning for automated tumour segmentation enabling fully automated [18F]F-DOPA PET analysis in paediatric gliomas.
patient_population: 103 pediatric patients (median age 11 years), 2011-2024
clinical_problem: Automating tumor segmentation and PET parameter extraction for pediatric glioma [18F]F-DOPA PET scans, replacing time-consuming manual delineation
model_description: A U-Net deep-learning model, fine-tuned via transfer learning from adult glioma datasets, automatically segments pediatric brain tumors on [18F]F-DOPA PET scans and extracts static and dynamic PET parameters (e.g., tumor-to-striatum ratio).
dataset_size: 103 pediatric patients (90 for statistical/survival analysis, 32 for dynamic analysis)
headline_result: Dice score 0.82 +/- 0.11; automated indices correlated significantly with tumor grade and survival (p<0.05)

title: Optimizing pediatric chest CT: superior image quality and lower radiation dose with deep learning reconstruction.
patient_population: 142 pediatric patients (<16 years), 2021-2024
clinical_problem: Comparing image quality and radiation dose between deep-learning and hybrid iterative reconstruction in unenhanced pediatric chest CT
model_description: Deep-learning image reconstruction (DLIR) is compared against hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) for unenhanced pediatric chest CT, assessing subjective and objective (noise, attenuation) image quality and radiation dose across age groups.
headline_result: Lower image noise with DLIR (e.g., lung 63 vs 81 HU, p=0.017); radiation dose reduced (CTDIvol 1.6 vs 4.3 mGy; effective dose 0.70 vs 2.51 mSv, p<0.001)

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted triage of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures in emergency departments: A single-centre validation study.
patient_population: 1,811 annotated AP/lateral radiographs from a single tertiary pediatric orthopedic center, 2010-2017; tested on 215 independent radiograph pairs
clinical_problem: classifying and triaging pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures (Gartland system) into operative versus non-operative management in the emergency department
model_description: A convolutional neural network trained with transfer learning classifies pediatric elbow radiographs into operative (Gartland IIB, III, flexion type) versus non-operative supracondylar humerus fracture categories, to support emergency-department triage where specialist orthopedic input may not be immediately available.
headline_result: accuracy 77% (95% CI 71-82%), AUROC 0.84 (95% CI 0.78-0.89); kappa vs surgeon consensus 0.51

title: Altered brain network topology in adolescents with major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder: A resting-state fMRI graph-theoretical and machine learning study.
patient_population: 125 adolescents aged 12-19 years (48 with major depressive disorder, 36 with bipolar disorder, 41 healthy controls)
clinical_problem: distinguishing adolescent major depressive disorder from bipolar disorder using resting-state fMRI network features
model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI functional network features, including nodal centrality and clustering coefficient from graph-theoretical analysis. A support vector machine trained on these network features distinguishes adolescent major depressive disorder from bipolar disorder, driven mainly by insula and cingulate gyrus features. It is presented as a research classifier, not a validated diagnostic test.
dataset_size: 125 adolescents (48 MDD, 36 bipolar disorder, 41 healthy controls)
headline_result: SVM classifier distinguished adolescent MDD from bipolar disorder with 88.24% accuracy (p < 0.001)

title: Spinal morphology-based multimodal AI for predicting pulmonary dysfunction in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
venue_label: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

study_design: retrospective model development study, five-fold cross-validation
headline_result: macro-AUC 0.827 (FVC AUC 0.814, FEV1 AUC 0.841), outperforming logistic regression on tabular features (macro AUC ~0.71)

title: digiBONE: an automated tool for segmental Greulich-Pyle bone age assessment of Indian children and adolescents.

title: Enhancing efficiency in pediatric brain tumor segmentation using a pathologically diverse single-center clinical dataset.

clinical_problem: segmenting pediatric brain tumor subregions across heterogeneous tumor types
model_description: A 3D nnU-Net is trained on multi-sequence MRI (T1, T1 post-contrast, T2, FLAIR) to segment four pediatric brain tumor subregions (whole tumor, T2-hyperintensity, enhancing tumor, cystic component), compared against inter-rater variability.
headline_result: Mean Dice 0.85 whole tumor / T2-hyperintensity, 0.75 enhancing tumor, 0.26 cystic component

title: Determination of Modified Waldenström Staging in Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease Using Deep Learning.
journal: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
venue_label: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
model_family: deep learning automated segmentation + classification pipeline
patient_population: 2,164 images from institution 1 for training/hold-out testing; external validation at institution 2 (533 radiograph pairs); patients with confirmed LCPD at two tertiary children's hospitals

model_description: A deep-learning pipeline automatically segments the femoral epiphysis on paired AP and frog-lateral hip radiographs, extracts quantifiable epiphyseal parameters (e.g., sclerosis, epiphyseal area), and classifies modified Waldenstrom stage of Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, evaluated for both early-vs-late staging and full staging.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation
headline_result: hold-out AUROC 0.82 (early vs late); external validation AUROC 0.75; segmentation Dice 0.93

title: Evidence-Guided Diagnostic Reasoning for Pediatric Chest Radiology Based on Multimodal Large Language Models.

patient_population: VinDr-PCXR public pediatric chest radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: generating interpretable, evidence-based diagnoses from pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: A two-stage system: a vision-language model fine-tuned on pediatric data first extracts structured radiological findings from a chest radiograph, then a multimodal large language model combines the image, extracted findings, patient demographics, and retrieved external medical knowledge to generate a final diagnosis, aiming to mirror radiologists' evidence-based reasoning rather than a black-box classification.
study_design: retrospective technical development on a public benchmark dataset
headline_result: 90.1% diagnostic accuracy, 70.9% F1-score, 82.5% AUC; up to 13.1% accuracy improvement over baselines

title: Quantification of Craniofacial Growth Pattern Based on Deep Learning.

study_design: retrospective large-scale deep learning development study

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Assessment of the Four-Chamber View in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Videos.
patient_population: 301 patients, second-trimester fetal cardiac ultrasound
clinical_problem: Automating extraction of the four-chamber view and cardiac biometric parameters from fetal cardiac ultrasound to screen for congenital heart disease
model_description: YOLOv7 detects the four-chamber view (4CV) in fetal cardiac ultrasound videos; UNet 3+ and SegFormer segment cardiac structures to automatically compute cardiothoracic area ratio, cardiac axis, and cardiac position for congenital heart disease screening.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study with clinical comparison
headline_result: AI models achieved screening performance comparable to expert obstetricians (22 obstetricians in comparison study)

title: Automated Echocardiographic Detection of Congenital Heart Disease Using Artificial Intelligence.
model_family: multitask, view-agnostic transformer-based architecture (expands on PanEcho)
patient_population: internal cohort: 54,727 echocardiograms (3.4 million videos) from Boston Children's Hospital, median age 7.1 years; referral cohort: 3,356 echocardiograms (167,484 videos) from external US and international centers, median age 2.5 years
clinical_problem: automated detection of critical and non-critical congenital heart disease on echocardiography, to extend expert-level interpretation to under-resourced settings
model_description: EchoFocus-CHD is a multitask, view-agnostic deep learning model (built on the PanEcho architecture with an added transformer encoder) that detects 12 critical and 8 noncritical congenital heart lesions, individually and as composites, from full pediatric echocardiogram studies, trained and tested internally then evaluated on an independent US/international referral cohort.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external referral-cohort validation
dataset_size: 54,727 echocardiograms internal (3.4M videos); 3,356 echocardiograms referral cohort (167,484 videos)
headline_result: internal AUROC 0.94 (critical CHD composite), 0.90 (noncritical composite); referral cohort AUROC 0.77 for critical CHD, improving to 0.87 after retraining on all US data

title: Placenta-pulmonary coupling-guided multimodal AI for fetal lung maturity staging and individualized glucocorticoid therapy.

clinical_problem: staging fetal lung maturity and individualizing antenatal glucocorticoid dosing
model_description: A physiology-informed multimodal AI framework combines 2D/3D ultrasound, shear-wave elastography, Doppler, and maternal metabolomics, constrained by a placenta-pulmonary coupling model, to unsupervised-stage fetal lung maturity and predict an individualized antenatal glucocorticoid dose and administration window, using a cross-modal attention transformer and a convolution-LSTM dosing branch.
study_design: prospective cohort study with multimodal AI framework development
headline_result: downstream classifier 92.3% accuracy distinguishing early vs late maturity; dosing predicted within +/-0.5 mg of clinical dose, 27% reduction in projected RDS risk vs standard dosing

title: Attention-Driven Deep Learning for Hydrocephalus: Preliminary Benchmarking of Multiscale 3D Attention Against Conventional 3D CNN Models Using Ventricular Enlargement on CT.

clinical_problem: Automated 3D classification of pediatric hydrocephalus from ventricular enlargement on head CT, improving on conventional 2D CT indices

title: Artificial Intelligence as an Add-On Instrument in Fetal Ultrasound; Sonographers' and Obstetricians' Expectations.

clinical_problem: clinician attitudes toward AI as a diagnostic aid during fetal anomaly ultrasound
model_description: A survey of Dutch obstetric sonographers and gynecologists on their attitudes, expectations, and concerns about AI applications (already used by 62% of respondents, mainly for automated biometry) as a diagnostic aid during fetal anomaly ultrasound scans.

title: Decoding adolescent TMJ osteoarthritis with multimodal machine learning.

venue_label: Journal of oral & facial pain and headache
patient_population: 79 adolescents (10-18 years) with TMJ pain undergoing panoramic radiography and MRI
clinical_problem: diagnosing adolescent temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis using clinical and imaging predictors

title: KidMesh: Computational Mesh Reconstruction for Pediatric Congenital Hydronephrosis Using Deep Neural Networks.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

title: Magnetic resonance imaging diagnosis of knee injuries after skiing in adolescents under deep learning.

headline_result: Segmentation Dice 0.89, IoU 0.82; classification accuracy 0.90, F1 0.91, AUC 0.95

title: Deep learning improves image quality in motion-robust and sedation-free pediatric brain MRI.
patient_population: 62 pediatric patients (mean age 7.4 +/- 4.9 years), sedated and awake
clinical_problem: Improving diagnostic image quality of motion-robust, sedation-free single-shot T2-weighted pediatric brain MRI
model_description: A deep learning framework combining compressed sensing and CNNs to reconstruct and enhance single-shot T2-weighted brain MRI, taking undersampled single-shot data as input and producing higher-quality T2-weighted images.

title: Artificial intelligence support for diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders during childhood: an umbrella review.
model_family: machine learning / deep learning (SVM, ANN, CNN) [review]
patient_population: children with suspected/diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorders (64 studies from an umbrella review, Jan 2015-Aug 2025)
clinical_problem: Synthesize evidence on AI-assisted diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders (ASD, ADHD, intellectual disability, communication and learning disorders) in children, largely from neuroimaging data
model_description: An umbrella review of 64 systematic reviews/meta-analyses on machine learning and deep learning models (SVMs, neural networks, CNNs) that take neuroimaging and other data (electrophysiological, clinical, motion/sensor) as input and output a diagnostic classification for autism, ADHD, and related neurodevelopmental disorders.
study_design: umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
dataset_size: 64 included studies (148 records screened); neuroimaging modality used in 59 studies
headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy ranged 66% (facial/eye movement-based) to 99% (neuroimaging/voice/motion-based); 80% of studies rated critically low methodological quality (AMSTAR-2)

title: Automatic lateral ventricle and choroid plexus segmentation method in infant brain MR images.
patient_population: Infants (Baby Connectome Project dataset n=154; in-house retrospective dataset n=52)
clinical_problem: Segmenting the lateral ventricles and choroid plexus on infant brain MRI to study cerebrospinal fluid dynamics and neurodevelopment
model_description: A fully automated deep learning segmentation method for joint lateral ventricle and choroid plexus segmentation on T1-weighted infant brain MRI, using an anatomy-aware loss enforcing that the choroid plexus is contained within the ventricles.
study_design: retrospective method development and validation on two independent datasets
headline_result: Dice 0.818+/-0.075 (LV) and 0.827+/-0.084 (CP) in BCP dataset; Dice 0.964+/-0.060 (LV) and 0.932+/-0.059 (CP) in in-house dataset

title: Quantitative radiomics and morphometry analysis of brain sub-regions reveals neurodevelopmental alterations in children with Tetralogy of Fallot.
patient_population: 60 children with Tetralogy of Fallot and 61 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Identifying brain structural alterations associated with neurodevelopmental risk in children with Tetralogy of Fallot
model_description: A radiomics-morphometry fusion model combining Pyradiomics and FreeSurfer-derived features from 68 brain regions on 3D T1-weighted MRI, using LASSO feature selection and SVM classification to distinguish children with Tetralogy of Fallot from healthy controls.
headline_result: AUC 0.99 (training), 0.77 (testing)

title: Developing an artificial intelligence tool for detecting fractures of child abuse: preliminary findings.
patient_population: 1740 children under 5 years old undergoing skeletal survey for suspected physical abuse
clinical_problem: Detecting inflicted (non-accidental) fractures on skeletal survey radiographs in suspected physical abuse
model_description: A deep learning-based AI tool (BoneView) retrained to detect inflicted fractures on pediatric skeletal survey radiographs.
headline_result: Baseline AUC 0.46; after preliminary retraining AUC 0.55, sensitivity 52%, specificity 67%

title: Real-time deep learning interpretation of echocardiographic video for automated detection of anatomical features associated with tetralogy of fallot in pediatric patients : a feasibility study.
patient_population: 174 pediatric patients at Seoul Asan Medical Center (2018-2023)
clinical_problem: Automating detection of anatomical features of Tetralogy of Fallot from echocardiograms for screening
model_description: A Detectron2/Mask R-CNN-based deep learning model trained to detect four characteristic anatomical defects of Tetralogy of Fallot in echocardiographic images and videos, for screening in regions lacking pediatric cardiology specialists.
headline_result: AUC ~1.00, F1 score 96.8%, >97% accuracy

title: A machine learning approach to using ultrasound for body composition and nutritional status assessment in newborns: a pilot study protocol.
patient_population: 50 infants (20 preterm, 30 full-term) at two sites (Boston, USA and Jimma, Ethiopia)
clinical_problem: Assessing infant body composition (fat and fat-free mass) and nutritional status using ultrasound
model_description: Planned CNN-based machine learning models to predict whole-body composition (fat/fat-free mass) from ultrasound images, as part of a feasibility pilot study establishing the scanning protocol and image database.
study_design: pilot study protocol (feasibility); ML models not yet trained/validated on full data

title: Early identification of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children using CT-based radiomics: a multicenter study.
patient_population: 419 children (248 training, 62 testing, 109 external validation)
clinical_problem: Early prediction of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children using clinical, imaging and radiomics features from chest CT
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from chest CT (via PyRadiomics) are combined with clinical and imaging variables in random-forest models to predict which children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia will develop a refractory (treatment-resistant) course.
study_design: retrospective multicenter study with external validation
headline_result: Integrated model AUC 0.811 (95% CI 0.704-0.917) in external validation, vs radiomics-only 0.784 and clinical-imaging-only 0.675

title: Deep Learning-based Bone Mineral Density Prediction Using Pediatric Chest Radiographs: A Multicenter Feasibility Study.
patient_population: Patients <18 years undergoing DXA and chest radiography at two tertiary hospitals
clinical_problem: Predicting bone mineral density (lumbar spine areal BMD) and detecting low BMD in children from chest radiographs
model_description: An AI model combining chest radiograph images with clinical variables (age, sex, height, weight) to predict lumbar spine areal BMD Z scores and detect low BMD, using DXA as the reference standard.
dataset_size: 1464 radiograph-DXA pairs (774 development, 376 internal test, 314 external test)
headline_result: Internal test: r=0.85, AUC 0.92 for low BMD; External test: r=0.76, AUC 0.90

title: Automated Detection of Pediatric Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis: A Deep Learning Approach Using Anatomically Informed Attention Guidance.
patient_population: 174 pelvic radiographs (139 training, 35 testing)
clinical_problem: Detecting slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) on pediatric pelvic radiographs
model_description: A two-stage deep learning model: U-Net++ segments the femoral head to define a region of focus, then an attention-guided EfficientNet B1 classifies the radiograph as SCFE or no SCFE, with Grad-CAM for interpretability.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development and testing
headline_result: AUC 0.893, accuracy 91.4%, sensitivity 93.3%, specificity 90.0%

title: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven ensemble model for comprehensive chest X-ray abnormality detection and deployment.
journal: The Indian journal of medical research
venue_label: The Indian journal of medical research
model_family: ensemble deep learning (multi-model CNN ensemble with lung segmentation)
patient_population: children and adults; 54,000 CXR images (36,500 abnormal, 17,500 normal) from 18 centers across 11 Indian states; prospective validation on 13,927 CXR images from outpatient clinics
clinical_problem: Detect abnormalities including tuberculosis on chest radiographs for large-scale screening in resource-limited settings
model_description: Takes chest radiographs (no metadata/clinical input required) and, via a multi-model ensemble including lung segmentation and lesion-specific models, classifies the image as normal or abnormal for large-scale TB/thoracic screening.
study_design: multicentric retrospective development with prospective independent validation
dataset_size: 54,000 CXR images (282,000 annotated data points) for training; 13,927 CXR images for prospective validation
headline_result: Sensitivity 92.2% (95% CI 91.6-92.7), specificity 77.4% (95% CI 76.1-78.6) in blind prospective validation

title: Preoperative MRI-Derived Navigation Reduces Radiation Exposure in Pediatric Spinal Fusion.
patient_population: 94 pediatric patients undergoing posterior spinal fusion for AIS (fluoro-only n=39, CT-only n=28, MRI-to-CT n=27)
clinical_problem: Eliminating preoperative CT and reducing radiation exposure during pediatric spinal fusion for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis by converting MRI to synthetic CT for surgical navigation
model_description: A machine learning model that translates MRI signal intensities into CT-equivalent Hounsfield units to generate synthetic CT for intraoperative navigation, eliminating the need for a preoperative CT scan.
study_design: retrospective cohort study, single tertiary center
headline_result: MRI-to-CT group: intraoperative dose 0.55+/-0.49 mSv vs 0.91+/-0.57 mSv fluoro-only (P=0.008); zero preoperative radiation vs 19.6 mSv for CT-only (P<0.05)

title: Automated quantification of coronal balance in spinal deformity: a safety-aware clinical workflow.
patient_population: 847 full-spine radiographs
clinical_problem: Automated quantification of coronal balance parameters (shoulder height difference, pelvic obliquity, C7 plumb line offset) in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: An HRNet-based deep learning system with a Clinical Safety Gating Mechanism that automatically measures shoulder height difference, pelvic obliquity, and C7 plumb line offset from full-spine radiographs, suppressing unreliable outputs in anatomically ambiguous cases.
headline_result: Mean absolute error 0.86-2.45mm; Pearson r>0.95 agreement with manual measurements

title: CT-based radiomics models for predicting the prognosis of children with mycoplasma pneumonia.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
venue_label: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
patient_population: 356 children with mycoplasma pneumonia from two hospitals
clinical_problem: Predicting prognosis of mycoplasma pneumonia in children using clinical and CT radiomics features
model_description: A radiomics model extracting features from chest CT lesion regions using LASSO feature selection, combined with clinical variables, to predict prognosis of mycoplasma pneumonia in children.
headline_result: Combined clinical+radiomics model AUC 0.842 (training), 0.825 (validation), 0.748 (test)

title: Quality evaluation of ultrasound images for fetal crown-rump length measurement at 11 to 14 weeks' gestation: A fusion model can be interpreted using SHAP method.
model_family: DeepLabV3 ResNet101 (segmentation) + radiomics/deep transfer learning fusion model
patient_population: 1149 midsagittal plane images from two hospitals, early pregnancy
clinical_problem: Automated quality evaluation of ultrasound images used for fetal crown-rump length measurement in early pregnancy
model_description: A fusion model combining radiomics and deep transfer learning features (using a DeepLabV3-ResNet101 segmentation model for ROI extraction) to classify fetal CRL ultrasound images as standard or non-standard planes, interpreted using SHAP.
headline_result: Fusion model AUC 0.947, accuracy 88.4%, sensitivity 83.0%, specificity 92.7%; performance comparable to senior radiologists

title: Automatic detection of the fetal brain midsagittal plane on MRI using a deep learning pipeline.
journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
venue_label: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
patient_population: 432 fetal brain MRI stacks from 225 fetuses (normal anatomy, 18-36 weeks)
clinical_problem: Automated localization of the fetal brain midsagittal plane on MRI for quality control and standardized assessment of midline brain structures
model_description: A multitask 2D U-Net detects four midline brain structures (corpus callosum genu/splenium, cerebellar vermis, pons) to generate slice-level midsagittal-plane probability scores, aggregated by a LightGBM classifier into a case-level decision.
headline_result: Slice-level AUC 0.95, accuracy 0.87; case-level AUC 0.81, accuracy 0.74

title: EVALUATION OF NEUROCOMBAT AND DEEP LEARNING HARMONIZATION FOR MULTI-SITE MAGNETIC RESONANCE NEUROIMAGING IN YOUTH WITH PRENATAL ALCOHOL EXPOSURE.
patient_population: Pediatric cohort (age 7 to 21) with controls and cases of prenatal alcohol exposure, three scanners
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Harmonizing multi-site MRI signal differences prior to volumetric analysis in a pediatric cohort with prenatal alcohol exposure
model_description: HACA3, a deep learning image harmonization method, processes MRI signals across scanners/sites prior to downstream volumetric quantification (MaCRUISE), aiming to remove site-related variance while preserving biological signal; compared against the statistical method neuroCombat.
headline_result: HACA3 qualitatively improved inter-site contrast variation but statistical methods (neuroCombat) reduced more site-related variance in MaCRUISE volume metrics (ANCOVA)

title: The Use of Machine Learning to Enable Objective Assessment of Surgical Outcomes in Sagittal Craniosynostosis.
journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
venue_label: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
patient_population: 108 healthy children and 239 preoperative sagittal craniosynostosis patients; 21 CVR and 37 SAC pre/postoperative pairs
clinical_problem: Objective assessment of head shape and quantification of surgical outcomes after correction of sagittal craniosynostosis
model_description: A Swap Disentangled Variational Autoencoder (SD-VAE) trained on CT, MRI, and 3D photographs to objectively quantify global and regional head shape relative to healthy norms, used to assess surgical outcomes after spring-assisted cranioplasty and calvarial vault remodeling.
dataset_size: 108 healthy children, 239 preoperative SC patients, 58 pre/postoperative pairs
headline_result: SD-VAE accurately distinguished SC patients from healthy controls based on global/regional morphology; both SAC and CVR resulted in head shape normalization

title: Composition, Pediatric Representation, and Transparency Disclosure Among FDA-Cleared Radiology Artificial Intelligence Products.
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
venue_label: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
clinical_problem: Assessing the composition, pediatric representation, and transparency of disclosures among FDA-cleared radiology AI products
model_description: Analysis of the composition, pediatric patient representation, and transparency of disclosures among FDA-cleared radiology AI products (abstract text not available; based on title only).
study_design: cross-sectional analysis of FDA-cleared radiology AI products (inferred from title; abstract unavailable)

title: Developing new methods for the accurate evaluation of children's bone age based on X-ray images: a study on the accuracy and consistency of artificial intelligence and manual bone age evaluation.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
venue_label: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
model_family: AI bone age assessment system (not otherwise specified)
patient_population: 1083 images from children
clinical_problem: Accurate evaluation of children's bone age from hand/wrist radiographs and comparison with pediatric radiologists' manual assessment
model_description: An AI bone age assessment system evaluated against three pediatric radiologists using Greulich-Pyle, RUS-CHN, and TW3-Carpal methods, compared with chronological age as reference.
headline_result: AI-manual agreement ICC 0.962-0.982, MAE 0.38-0.45 years; AI vs chronological age MAE 0.75-1.45 years

title: A multicentre benchmark dataset for comprehensive landmark-based fetal ultrasound biometry.
patient_population: 1904 subjects, 4513 images from four clinical sites, seven ultrasound devices
clinical_problem: Providing an open, multi-site annotated benchmark dataset and baseline AI model for automated fetal biometric landmark detection (head/abdominal diameters, femoral length)
model_description: An open-access multicentre benchmark dataset of fetal ultrasound images with expert landmark annotations for biometric measurements (head, abdomen, femur), with an automated landmark-based baseline model to quantify domain shift across centers/devices.
release_evidence: All data and annotations are available on the UCL Research Data Repository. Training code and evaluation pipelines are available at https://github.com/surgical-vision/Multicentre-Fetal-Biometry.git
study_design: multicentre benchmark dataset with baseline model evaluation
headline_result: Single-center training/evaluation overestimates performance relative to multicentre testing (domain shift demonstrated)

title: Image Quality Advancements in Low-Dose Pediatric CT Using Super-Resolution Deep-Learning Reconstruction.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
patient_population: 38 children (<10 years, median age 2.0 years) with low-radiation abdominal CT
clinical_problem: Improving image quality of low-dose thin-slice pediatric abdominal CT
model_description: Super-resolution deep-learning reconstruction (SR-DLR) applied to raw low-dose pediatric abdominal CT data to reduce noise and improve edge sharpness, compared with hybrid-iterative and conventional deep-learning reconstructions.
study_design: retrospective quantitative and qualitative image quality comparison
headline_result: SR-DLR showed greatest noise reduction, highest CNR and ERS, outperforming hybrid-IR and C-DLR (p<0.001)

title: Predicting adult functional outcomes in childhood-onset attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder using multimodal MRI and machine learning: A prospective follow-up study.
patient_population: 104 children with ADHD followed into adulthood (mean follow-up 8.2 years)
clinical_problem: Predicting adult functional outcomes in children with ADHD using baseline clinical and multimodal MRI features
model_description: Random forest models combining baseline clinical characteristics, structural MRI, and resting-state functional MRI features from children with ADHD to predict adult functional outcome (Global Assessment of Functioning), interpreted with SHAP.
headline_result: Multimodal model AUC 0.816 vs clinical-only AUC 0.589

title: Deep learning for pediatric synovial recess distension detection in hemophilia: synthetic image augmentation with styleGAN2-ADA.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
venue_label: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
patient_population: 2,499 real pediatric and adult knee ultrasound images; independent pediatric test set of 278 images, ages 0-18
clinical_problem: Classifying pediatric synovial recess distension (joint bleeding) on musculoskeletal ultrasound in children with hemophilia
model_description: A conditional StyleGAN2-ADA generates age- and diagnosis-specific synthetic pediatric musculoskeletal ultrasound images to augment scarce real data, used to fine-tune an EfficientNet-B4 classifier for synovial recess distension (SRD) classification.
dataset_size: 2,499 real + 21,550 synthetic images; independent pediatric test set of 278 images
headline_result: Accuracy improved +17.3pp for ages 0-8 (85.3% vs 68.0%, p<0.001) and +6.1pp for ages 14-18 (89.9% vs 83.8%, p=0.033) vs adult-trained baseline

title: Development and validation of a combined model based on MRI radiomics for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and adverse pregnancy outcomes: a multicenter retrospective study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Validation Study
patient_population: 610 singleton pregnancies (292 PAS, 318 controls)
clinical_problem: Prenatal prediction of placenta accreta spectrum and adverse pregnancy outcomes from MRI
model_description: A combined radiomics-clinical model using T2-weighted MRI radiomics features and prenatal clinical features to predict placenta accreta spectrum and associated adverse pregnancy outcomes.
headline_result: Combined model AUC for PAS: 0.767/0.795/0.792 (training/validation/external test); for pregnancy outcomes: 0.852/0.879/0.907

title: Independent bone-level diagnostic accuracy study of an AI tool for detecting appendicular skeletal fractures on radiographs.
patient_population: consecutive trauma radiograph patients at seven Danish hospitals, median age 38 (IQR 21-64), including children
clinical_problem: Can a commercially available AI tool reliably detect fractures on radiographs across anatomical regions and confounding factors, including in children?
model_description: Commercially available AI software analyzes trauma radiographs and flags fractures; performance was benchmarked against the clinical radiologic report and stratified by patient and bone subgroups including children.
study_design: retrospective multi-hospital diagnostic accuracy study with subgroup stratification (including children)
headline_result: Overall sensitivity 89% (95% CI 87-91%), specificity 88% (95% CI 86-89%); specificity dropped to 57% with old fractures

title: Evaluation of functional spiral artery count and jet dispersion index using power Doppler ultrasound: in vivo insights into the vascular pathology of placental dysfunction.
patient_population: 6246 pregnancies from two prospective cohorts (FirstPLUS, OxPLUS), first-trimester (11+2 to 14+1 weeks)
clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of placental and vascular structures on 3D power Doppler ultrasound to derive novel vascular markers associated with pre-eclampsia and fetal growth restriction
model_description: The OxNNet convolutional neural network automatically segments placental and vascular structures on 3D power Doppler ultrasound images, from which functional spiral artery count and jet dispersion index are derived and tested for association with pre-eclampsia and fetal growth restriction.
study_design: prospective cohort study (combined dataset of two cohorts)
dataset_size: 6246 pregnancies; 5555 evaluable FSA counts, 2991 DI results
headline_result: Lower FSA z-score associated with FGR (p<0.001); lower DI associated with PE (p=0.005) and FGR (p<0.001)

title: Ultrafast Infant Brain Quantitative MRI Using Overlapping-Echo Acquisition with Volumetric Physical Simulation of Slice-level Non-Idealities.
model_family: deep learning quantitative reconstruction (synthetic data-driven, MOLED)
patient_population: 30 infants (0-1 year)
clinical_problem: Ultrafast quantitative MRI (T2, T2*, T2') mapping of the infant brain to characterize early brain development, overcoming motion and scan-time limitations
model_description: A deep learning quantitative reconstruction framework trained on physics-informed synthetic data (VoluSimu) applied to multiple overlapping-echo detachment (MOLED) MRI acquisitions to rapidly generate T2, T2*, and T2' maps of the infant brain without prolonged scan times.
study_design: prospective method development and in vivo validation study
headline_result: Network trained on synthetic data provided accurate quantitative T2/T2*/T2' maps despite imperfect RF pulses and B0 inhomogeneity; motion-artifact-free maps obtained

title: Performance of Open-Source LLMs in Identifying Pediatric Pneumonia From Free-Text Chest Radiograph Reports.
patient_population: 1000 pediatric emergency department encounters with CXR (2016-2022), median age 4.2 years
clinical_problem: Classifying free-text pediatric chest radiograph reports for community-acquired pneumonia
model_description: Five open-source large language models (Gemma2 9B, Gemma2 27B, Falcon3 7B, DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama 8B, Llama3.1 8B) were evaluated to classify free-text chest radiograph reports as positive, negative, or indeterminate for pneumonia.
release_evidence: evaluated five open-source LLMs (Gemma2 9B, Gemma2 27B, Falcon3 7B, DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama 8B, and Llama3.1 8B)
dataset_size: 1000 pediatric ED encounters with CXR reports
headline_result: Gemma2 9B: pneumonia F1 0.82 (three-class), F1 0.97 (binary); outperformed traditional NLP classifiers

title: Automated Deep Learning-Based Demyelination Load Segmentation in Metachromatic Leukodystrophy.
patient_population: 35 MLD patients for training (189 scans); independent testing on 130 scans from 49 patients
clinical_problem: Automated segmentation and quantification of demyelinated white matter (demyelination load) in metachromatic leukodystrophy as an imaging biomarker of disease burden
model_description: A self-configuring nnU-Net convolutional neural network trained on 3D T1- and axial T2-weighted MRI to automatically segment demyelinated white matter in metachromatic leukodystrophy, compared with a conventional semi-automated method.
study_design: retrospective method development and independent testing
dataset_size: 189 scans from 35 patients (training); 130 scans from 49 patients (independent test)
headline_result: Median Dice 0.82 (3D T1) and 0.75 (2D); CNN-derived demyelination load correlated with motor impairment (rS=0.38-0.56, p<0.001)

title: BIBSNet: A deep learning baby image brain segmentation network for MRI scans.
model_name: BIBSNet (Baby and Infant Brain Segmentation Neural Network)
patient_population: 90 participants, age range 0-8 months (median 4.6 months)
clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting infant brain tissue on MRI to support studies of typical and atypical early brain development
model_description: BIBSNet, an open-source deep neural network trained using manually annotated real images plus synthetic segmentations (SynthSeg) with a 10-fold procedure, performs infant brain tissue segmentation that outperforms joint label fusion and is faster at inference, producing FreeSurfer-compatible labels.
release_evidence: an open-source model for robust and generalizable brain tissue segmentation
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation against joint label fusion and iBEAT segmentation
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient: gray matter 0.849 (BIBSNet) vs 0.713 (joint label fusion); white matter 0.862 vs 0.791; BIBSNet is about 600x faster than joint label fusion at inference

title: Brain entropy as a biomarker of major depression in adolescents and young adults: insights from multimodal resting-state functional magentic resonance imaging.
patient_population: 204 individuals aged 12-24 years (119 with MDD, 85 healthy controls)
clinical_problem: Can resting-state fMRI markers of brain entropy help diagnose major depressive disorder in adolescents and young adults?
model_description: SVM-RFE classifier uses brain entropy plus standard resting-state fMRI features (ALFF, ReHo, FCD) from brain regions to classify patients as having major depressive disorder or not.
study_design: cross-sectional case-control machine learning classification study
headline_result: AUC 0.877 (combined BEN+ALFF+FCD model)

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted quality assessment of mid-trimester ultrasound examinations using large vision-language models.
patient_population: 22,544 ultrasound planes from 273 internal and 29 external examinations plus public data
clinical_problem: Automated quality assessment of mid-trimester fetal ultrasound examinations (standard plane identification and examination completeness)
model_description: A SonoNet-based CNN identifies standard fetal ultrasound planes and key anatomical structures; a fine-tuned vision-language model synthesizes the CNN-derived descriptions to assess overall exam completeness and quality, providing interpretable feedback on missing/low-quality planes.
study_design: multicenter retrospective study with reader study
dataset_size: 22,544 ultrasound planes (273 internal + 29 external examinations, plus public data)
headline_result: Best VLM F1 0.944 (internal), 0.922 (external) for exam-level assessment; AI assistance improved reader diagnostic consistency and recall

title: Graph theory reveals functional connectome disruptions in adolescent major depressive disorder with childhood trauma.
patient_population: 343 adolescents with MDD aged 10-18 years (211 with childhood trauma, 106 without) and 149 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Can baseline brain connectivity predict which adolescents with depression and childhood trauma will respond to antidepressant treatment?
model_description: Machine learning models use baseline resting-state functional connectome (graph theory network metrics) to predict whether an adolescent with depression will respond to antidepressant treatment.
study_design: longitudinal case-control study with machine learning outcome prediction
headline_result: 82% accuracy predicting antidepressant response from baseline connectome

title: Optimized fetal head circumference estimation in 2D ultrasound using EfficientNet-B7 and Adam optimizer.
patient_population: HC-18 public dataset; test set of 335 images
clinical_problem: Automated estimation of fetal head circumference on 2D ultrasound for monitoring fetal growth and diagnosing microcephaly/macrocephaly
model_description: A regression-based deep learning model using EfficientNet-B7 with the Adam optimizer to directly estimate fetal head circumference from 2D ultrasound images, trained/evaluated on the public HC-18 dataset.
study_design: retrospective model development on public benchmark dataset
dataset_size: HC-18 dataset, test set of 335 images
headline_result: Normalized MAE 0.028, HC-specific MAE 1.978mm, inference time ~0.03s

title: Raphe subregion seeds reveal whole-brain functional connectivity differences underlying adolescent depression.
patient_population: 102 adolescents with depression and 54 matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: Identifying adolescents with depression from raphe nucleus functional connectivity patterns on MRI
model_description: A support vector machine classifier using dorsal and medial raphe nucleus functional connectivity features derived from resting-state MRI to discriminate adolescents with depression from healthy controls.
headline_result: SVM using FC features from left precentral gyrus and right gyrus rectus effectively discriminated depressed adolescents (accuracy not numerically stated)

title: AI-Based Denoising for Simulated Dose Reduction in Pediatric Chest Radiography: A Prospective Multicenter Evaluation of Image Quality and Diagnostic Performance.
patient_population: 420 pediatric patients across four tertiary hospitals
clinical_problem: Improving image quality and preserving diagnostic performance in simulated low-dose pediatric chest radiography
model_description: A vendor-neutral deep residual convolutional neural network denoising system applied to simulated low-dose (~50% dose reduction) pediatric chest radiographs, evaluated for image quality and diagnostic performance (pneumonia, atelectasis, cardiomegaly) by blinded radiologists.
headline_result: Image quality improved (4.4+/-0.5 vs 4.5+/-0.4 full-dose); delta-AUC=-0.03 for diagnostic performance, non-inferiority not formally established

title: Evaluating the usability and practicality of AI-enabled smartphone-based obstetric ultrasound in Sierra Leone: a mixed-methods study.
patient_population: 2,315 obstetric sweep protocols conducted by 81 healthcare providers across seven facilities in Sierra Leone
clinical_problem: Evaluating usability and practicality of AI-enabled smartphone-based obstetric ultrasound for antenatal care in a low-resource setting
model_description: An AI-enabled smartphone-based obstetric ultrasound device used by frontline providers to perform obstetric sweeps, with scans reviewed via remote expert interpretation and (later) AI-supported analysis; study assessed scan quality and usability.
headline_result: 83.8% of sweeps were of sufficient quality for remote/AI analysis; 59.3% of providers achieved 80% quality threshold

title: Silent Verb Generation during fMRI Reveals Post-Radiotherapy Alterations in Cerebellar-Cerebral Language Regions in Patients Treated for Medulloblastoma.
patient_population: 31 children and adolescents with medulloblastoma (mean age 14.1+/-4.7 years) on SJMB12 protocol
clinical_problem: Detecting radiotherapy-related functional reorganization in language-related brain networks in children treated for medulloblastoma
model_description: A two-stage nested feature-selection framework with a linear support vector machine classifies pre- versus post-irradiation task-fMRI (silent verb generation) scans in pediatric medulloblastoma patients, using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
headline_result: Classifier distinguished pre- vs post-irradiation scans with 80.7% leave-one-subject-out accuracy (p=0.0149)

title: Automated Detection of Pediatric Pneumonia via Clinically Driven AI Analysis of Lung Ultrasound.
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing lung ultrasound
clinical_problem: Can an AI tool help trainees reliably identify lung ultrasound findings of pneumonia in children?
model_description: Semi-automated AI system analyzes lung ultrasound images to identify pleural line thickening, consolidation morphology, and B-line patterns associated with pneumonia, with real-time visual annotations to assist trainees.

title: Explainable 3D VGG-style convolutional neural network for pediatric hydrocephalus detection on computed tomography: A segmentation-free and fully volumetric deep learning framework.
patient_population: 98 pediatric CT scans (48 hydrocephalus, 50 normal) across 4 age groups (<1, 1-5, 5-10, 10-15 years); external validation on 118 scans
clinical_problem: Automated detection of hydrocephalus on pediatric CT scans across age groups
model_description: A segmentation-free, explainable 3D VGG-style CNN trained from scratch to detect hydrocephalus directly from volumetric pediatric CT, with 3D Grad-CAM for anatomically interpretable explanations.
study_design: retrospective model development with 5-fold cross-validation and external validation
headline_result: Internal: AUC-ROC 0.95+/-0.06, accuracy 0.94+/-0.06; External validation: AUC-ROC 0.88, AUC-PR 0.85

title: VerteRo: A Fully Automated Deep Neural Network Tool for Estimating Axial Vertebral Body Rotation in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
model_family: convolutional neural network (Faster R-CNN/YOLO object detection pipeline)
patient_population: 97 AIS radiographs (training)
clinical_problem: Automated estimation of axial vertebral body rotation from standard scoliosis radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: VerteRo, a multi-stage CNN pipeline (automated ROI extraction, vertebral segmentation, pedicle localization via Faster R-CNN/YOLOv11/YOLOv12, and geometric rotation estimation) that automatically estimates axial vertebral body rotation from posteroanterior scoliosis radiographs.
headline_result: Mean absolute error 8.239 degrees vs Stokes-derived reference; 71.34% exact agreement with Nash-Moe grading

title: A Preliminary Study on the Auto-Segmentation of Targets and Organs at Risk in Pediatric Total Marrow and Lymphoid Irradiation.
body_region: whole body (bone marrow, lymphatic regions, organs at risk)
patient_population: 36 pediatric patients treated with TMLI (2018-2024)
clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk for total marrow and lymphoid irradiation in pediatric leukemia patients undergoing bone marrow transplant conditioning
model_description: 2D U-Net and 3D V-Net deep learning models trained to auto-segment target volumes (bone marrow, lymphatic drainage regions) and organs at risk on CT for pediatric total marrow and lymphoid irradiation radiotherapy planning.
