patient_population: 360 subjects with imaging data, 493 with molecular subtype data, Children's Brain Tumor Network
clinical_problem: Risk stratification (survival prediction) in pediatric low-grade glioma integrating deep learning imaging features, molecular subtype, and clinical data, with uncertainty quantification
model_description: A pretrained deep learning model fine-tuned for pediatric brain tumor segmentation extracts imaging features from T2-weighted MRI, which are combined in a regularized survival model (clinico-ResNet) with clinical data, and further fused with a clinical-molecular survival model; bootstrap resampling quantifies per-patient prediction uncertainty for risk stratification in pediatric low-grade glioma.
study_design: retrospective multicenter cohort study with deep learning survival modeling and independent replication
dataset_size: 360 subjects with imaging (752 for segmentation fine-tuning), 493 with molecular data, 294 with both
headline_result: DL-M1 C-index 0.73 discovery, 0.70 replication; multimodal fusion reduced uncertainty interval width by approximately 75%

title: Artificial intelligence for pediatric fracture detection: impact on diagnostic revisions and patient recall rates in a tertiary emergency setting.
patient_population: Children and adolescents (2-18 years) undergoing appendicular skeletal radiography in a tertiary emergency department
clinical_problem: Whether AI-assisted fracture detection reduces diagnostic revisions and patient recalls after pediatric emergency skeletal radiographs interpreted out-of-hours.
model_description: A commercial AI system (TechCare Kids, Milvue) analyzes appendicular skeletal radiographs of children to flag fractures, with output used to support treating physicians' interpretation.
release_evidence: commercial AI system (TechCare Kids, Milvue, Paris, France)
study_design: prospective single-center study of AI-assisted fracture detection in pediatric emergency radiography
dataset_size: 667 patients enrolled (296 with fractures) of 1515 screened
headline_result: AI accuracy 95.1%; diagnostic revisions 8.6% without AI vs 5.7% with AI (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.37-1.19)

title: Automated readings of imaging reports by natural language processing (NLP) supplemented by clinical data predict disease course in children and adults with Crohn's disease: report from the epi-IIRN.
patient_population: Children and adults with newly diagnosed Crohn's disease from a nationwide cohort (epi-IIRN)
clinical_problem: Whether automated extraction of imaging findings from MR/CT enterography reports, combined with clinical data, can predict difficult-to-treat disease course in Crohn's disease
model_description: An NLP model (HSMP-BERT) extracts imaging-based variables (stricturing/penetrating disease, MaRIAs score) from free-text MR/CT enterography reports; these features feed Cox and gradient boosting survival models to predict difficult-to-treat disease course.
study_design: retrospective cohort study using NLP-extracted imaging features and machine learning survival models
headline_result: Imaging-based predictors AUC 0.59 (95% CI 0.53-0.65); combined imaging+clinical AUC 0.69 (0.64-0.74)

title: Artificial intelligence-based ultrasound screening for antenatal detection of placenta accreta spectrum.
journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
venue_label: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
model_family: CNN (EfficientNetB0) + ensemble (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting)
patient_population: Pregnant patients at risk for placenta accreta spectrum, imaged 2018-2025
clinical_problem: Whether an AI model can predict placenta accreta spectrum from prenatal placental ultrasound images to improve antenatal detection
model_description: An EfficientNetB0 convolutional neural network classifies frames from 2D placental ultrasound DICOM images for placenta accreta spectrum; frame-level probabilities are averaged and combined with clinical risk factors (prior cesareans, previa) in an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest, and gradient boosting to output a per-patient prediction.
study_design: single-center retrospective diagnostic model development study
dataset_size: 756 ultrasound DICOM files, 38,907 frames from 113 patients (79 train/17 val/17 test)
headline_result: Accuracy 88% (95% CI 63.6-98.5%), sensitivity 100%, specificity 75%, AUC 0.972 (0.875-1.000)

title: Radiomics of the Airway (RadAr): Multi-Scale Airway Phenotyping for Disease Characterization on Routine CT Imaging.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: N=1331 patients across four cohorts: fibrotic interstitial lung disease, COVID-19, progressive pulmonary fibrosis (adults), and pediatric cystic fibrosis
clinical_problem: Whether quantitative multi-scale airway radiomic measurements from routine chest CT can characterize airway disease and correlate with outcomes across several respiratory diseases, including pediatric cystic fibrosis
model_description: RadAr extracts over 400 interpretable multi-scale airway measurements (tapering, luminal dimensions, architectural distortion) from chest CT airway segmentations; in pediatric cystic fibrosis, these measurements were correlated with prior exacerbations and airway inflammation markers.
study_design: retrospective radiomics feature-development and correlation study across four disease cohorts including pediatric cystic fibrosis
dataset_size: N=1331 patients total across four cohorts (pediatric CF subset size not stated)
headline_result: In pediatric CF, reduced tapering and increased cylindricity associated with prior exacerbations and BAL neutrophilia (rho -0.64 to -0.78)

title: AI segmentation requires accounting for brain size to maintain performance on developmental MRI cohorts.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
venue_label: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
patient_population: 26,000 MRI scans spanning infant to adult development
age_groups: neonate; infant; child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Whether an adult-trained deep learning brain segmentation tool (SynthSeg) can be adapted to reliably segment brain MRI in infants and children despite differences in brain size and morphology
model_description: SynthSeg, a deep learning brain segmentation tool, is applied to T1 MRI after rescaling infant scans to adult brain size and cropping to adult field-of-view; output is automated brain segmentation with quality-control pass/fail assessed against expert segmentations.
study_design: retrospective methodological evaluation and adaptation of a deep learning segmentation tool across a developmental MRI cohort
headline_result: Automated QC pass rate in infants improved from 36% (1094/3069) to 91% (2803/3069) after rescale+crop pipeline

title: Ultrasound-based machine learning models for assisting the prediction of neonatal size and mode of delivery.
model_family: random forest / K-nearest neighbors / stochastic gradient descent / stacking ensemble
patient_population: 5375 pregnant women with routine prenatal ultrasound within 2 weeks of delivery (3447 in final model dataset)
clinical_problem: Whether machine learning models using prenatal ultrasound biometric measurements can predict neonatal birth weight, head circumference and mode of delivery
model_description: Four ML algorithms (SGD, random forest, KNN, stacking ensemble) take the last prenatal ultrasound measurements (biparietal diameter, abdominal circumference, head circumference) as input and predict newborn head circumference, birth weight, and likely mode of delivery.
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort study developing ML models from prenatal ultrasound
headline_result: Predicted newborn weight comparable accuracy to Hadlock IV formula; predicted head circumference superior accuracy to last ultrasound measurement (no single summary AUC given)

title: Global and Voxel-Wise Brain Age Prediction Analyses Following Perinatal Stroke.
patient_population: 105 children with perinatal stroke (arterial ischemic stroke or periventricular venous infarction) and 105 age/sex-matched typically developing controls; training set of 5969 scans of typically developing children
clinical_problem: Whether machine learning-based brain age prediction from MRI can serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopment and correlate with motor outcomes after perinatal stroke
model_description: Machine learning models trained on 5969 T1-weighted MRI scans of typically developing children predict global and voxel-wise 'brain age'; the gap between predicted and chronological age (brain age gap) is computed for children with perinatal stroke and correlated with motor scores.
study_design: retrospective case-control study applying a machine learning brain age model to children with perinatal stroke
dataset_size: 5969 training scans; 105 stroke cases and 105 matched controls for application
headline_result: Children with perinatal stroke had more positive brain age gaps (predicted older than actual); motor scores negatively correlated with brain age gap

title: Deep learning-based estimation of sagittal spinal alignment from coronal radiographs.
patient_population: 449 adult subjects (train/val/test) and an external cohort of 69 adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
clinical_problem: Whether sagittal spinal alignment parameters can be predicted from coronal radiographs alone (reducing need for biplanar imaging), evaluated in adults and externally in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: A CNN-based multiple-output regression (MOR) model takes a coronal spine radiograph and directly predicts six sagittal alignment parameters (thoracic kyphosis, lumbar lordosis, sacral slope, pelvic incidence, pelvic tilt, sagittal vertical axis), compared against GAN-based image-synthesis approaches.
study_design: retrospective model development in adults with external validation in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
dataset_size: 449 adults (313 train/68 val/68 test); external validation 69 adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
headline_result: Adult test set median absolute errors 4-8 degrees for angular parameters, 1.6 cm for SVA; CCC 0.20-0.69; adolescent cohort errors ~7 degrees

title: Image quality evaluation of neonatal brain magnetic resonance imaging using a deep learning reconstruction algorithm: A quantitative and multireader study using variable denoising levels at 3 tesla.
patient_population: 15 neonates undergoing 3D T1-weighted brain MRI at 3T
clinical_problem: Whether a deep learning reconstruction algorithm improves image quality of neonatal brain MRI, particularly conspicuity of early myelinating structures
model_description: A deep learning reconstruction algorithm is applied at variable denoising levels to 3D T1-weighted neonatal brain MRI; three radiologists rate qualitative image quality and myelinating-structure conspicuity, and objective SNR/CNR are measured.
study_design: pilot prospective single-center multireader image-quality evaluation study
headline_result: Increased denoising level associated with increased SNR/CNR and radiologist-rated image quality (no single summary statistic given); diagnostic accuracy not evaluated

title: Comparative Analysis of Bone Age Estimation Using the Manual Greulich and Pyle Method Versus Artificial Intelligence Algorithms in an Indian Pediatric Population Aged 1-18 Years.
patient_population: Children aged 1-18 years, Indian population, 74 hand radiographs
clinical_problem: How accurately do AI-based bone age assessment software platforms agree with manual Greulich-Pyle atlas assessment in an Indian pediatric population
model_description: Three commercial AI software platforms (Xrayhead, 16-Bit Physis, FreeBoneAge) each take a hand radiograph and output an estimated bone age, compared against manual Greulich-Pyle atlas reading.
release_evidence: three automated AI software platforms: Xrayhead (AI1), 16-Bit Physis (AI2), and FreeBoneAge (AI3)
headline_result: 16-Bit Physis: ICC 0.983 (0.973-0.989), MAE 1.24 years vs GP; Xrayhead moderate agreement ICC 0.729, unreliable under age 6

title: Deep learning reveals a neurocomputational mechanism predicting depression risk in adolescents.
patient_population: Population-based adolescent cohort IMAGEN (N=1332), with follow-up N=725; validated in STRATIFY patient cohort N=411
clinical_problem: Whether a computational biomarker derived from functional MRI and deep learning can predict future depression risk in adolescents before symptom onset
model_description: A brain-aligned deep learning model of emotion perception is fit to functional MRI signals; perturbation experiments identify an overregularized emotion-perception signature, used as a computational biomarker to predict later depression symptom onset.
study_design: prospective cohort study with computational modeling and external cohort validation
headline_result: Neurocomputational signature predicted depression symptom onset up to 4 years later and improved depression classification in the STRATIFY cohort

title: Multi-modal ensemble learning prediction of anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric patients with Crohn's disease using clinical, radiomic, and deep learning MR enterography features.
patient_population: 92 pediatric Crohn's disease patients (median age 14.6 years) who underwent MRE before starting anti-TNF therapy, 2009-2021
clinical_problem: Whether combining radiologist assessment, radiomic features, and deep learning features from pre-treatment MR enterography with clinical data can predict which pediatric Crohn's disease patients will respond to anti-TNF therapy
model_description: A two-stage stacking ensemble model combines radiologist MRE assessment, radiomic features from bowel regions, deep learning features from bowel images, and non-imaging clinical data to output a predicted probability of anti-TNF treatment response (mucosal healing).
headline_result: Combined MRE+clinical ensemble AUROC 0.817 (95% CI 0.793-0.842) vs individual feature types 0.706-0.724

title: Human-AI Interaction With AI-Assisted Tumor Overlays in Pediatric Whole-Body Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Exploratory Reader Study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: Children with Li-Fraumeni syndrome undergoing surveillance whole-body MRI
clinical_problem: Whether an AI-assisted tumor-highlighting overlay changes radiologist workflow, lesion marking, follow-up recommendations and workload during surveillance whole-body MRI in children with a cancer predisposition syndrome
model_description: A patch-based deep learning segmentation model trained on augmented 2D slices from 675 surveillance whole-body MRI volumes highlights regions with high tumor probability as an overlay for radiologists during interpretation.
study_design: exploratory reader study evaluating human-AI interaction with an AI-assisted overlay
dataset_size: 675 surveillance whole-body MRI volumes (training); reader study with 2 radiologists
headline_result: AI assistance increased case evaluation time; mixed effect on number of candidate lesions marked between the two radiologists

title: Bone age estimation from chest radiographs using deep neural networks: a proof-of-concept study.
body_region: chest (opportunistic bone age from chest radiograph)
patient_population: Children aged 3-15 years who underwent both chest and hand radiography at a tertiary center over 20 years
clinical_problem: Whether bone age can be opportunistically estimated from chest radiographs using deep learning when dedicated hand radiographs are unavailable
model_description: Three pretrained deep neural networks are fine-tuned (with and without sex as an input) to estimate bone age directly from chest radiographs, using hand-radiograph-derived TW2-RUS bone age as the reference standard.
headline_result: Sex-considering model ICC up to 0.87 (95% CI 0.63-0.99), RMSE 1.30 years

title: Latent Koopman Dynamics of Brain Structure-Function Coupling for Identifying Adolescent Prenatal Drug Exposure.
model_family: graph neural network (GNN) with Koopman operator
patient_population: 10,199 adolescents from the ABCD (Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development) cohort
clinical_problem: Whether joint structural and functional brain connectivity modeling can identify adolescents with a history of prenatal drug exposure
model_description: NeuroKoop++ uses graph neural network encoders to extract structural and functional connectivity from brain MRI, fuses them via cross-attention, and models their coupling with a Koopman operator conditioned on cognitive scores to classify prenatal drug exposure history.
study_design: retrospective cohort study developing a graph neural network model on a large adolescent neuroimaging cohort
headline_result: Outperformed leading multimodal approaches with statistically significant improvements for PDE classification (no single summary statistic given)

title: Integrated quantitative biomarkers of placental texture and hemodynamics improve assessment of pregnancies at risk for adverse fetal outcomes.
patient_population: 129 pregnant patients imaged at 28-32 and 34-38 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: Whether quantitative texture analysis of B-mode placental ultrasound, combined with Doppler and clinical variables, improves identification of pregnancies at risk for adverse fetal outcomes (e.g., preeclampsia, severe fetal growth restriction, perinatal hypoxia)
model_description: Texture features are extracted from B-mode placental ultrasound pixel data and combined with Doppler measurements and clinical variables in logistic regression and random forest models to predict high-risk pregnancy status.
study_design: prospective cohort study developing predictive models from ultrasound texture and Doppler biomarkers
headline_result: Quantitative placental texture features had predictive performance comparable to Doppler; combined clinical+Doppler+texture model improved performance over clinical alone (no single AUC reported)

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics for noninvasive risk stratification of pediatric neuroblastoma: a pilot study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: XGBoost (and five other ML classifiers), radiomics
patient_population: 30 children with histologically confirmed neuroblastoma (mean age 38±40 months)
clinical_problem: Whether multiparametric MRI radiomics can noninvasively stratify pediatric neuroblastoma into low/intermediate vs. high risk without relying solely on tissue and molecular characterization
model_description: 208 radiomic features are extracted from T1, T2, and diffusion-weighted whole-tumor MRI volumes, reduced by feature-selection methods, and used to train machine learning classifiers (best: XGBoost) that output a binary risk classification (low/intermediate vs. high-risk neuroblastoma).
headline_result: Best discrimination AUC 0.88 ± 0.06-0.07 (T2-weighted and combined T1w+T2w+ADC features with XGBoost)

title: Placental Blood-Flow Velocity Quantification From Diffusion MRI.
patient_population: In vivo placental diffusion MRI plus simulated data (patient number not stated)
clinical_problem: Whether machine learning applied to diffusion MRI can quantify placental capillary blood velocity to help identify placental blood-flow pathology (e.g., preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction)
model_description: Monte Carlo simulations of placental perfusion/diffusion generate training data for supervised regressors (random forest, multilayer perceptron) that estimate capillary blood velocity, perfusion fraction, and diffusivity directly from diffusion MRI signal, applied to simulated and in vivo placental scans.
study_design: methodological development study combining Monte Carlo simulation and machine learning regression, with in vivo validation
headline_result: MC-based MLP produced physiologically reasonable in vivo velocity estimates with greater sensitivity than IVIM methods (no single quantitative error metric stated)

title: Pretreatment Coronary Ultrasound Radiomics Combined With the Prognostic Nutritional Index for Predicting IVIG Resistance in Children With Kawasaki Disease.
patient_population: 352 children diagnosed with Kawasaki disease, 2020-2026
clinical_problem: Whether radiomic features from pretreatment coronary artery ultrasound, combined with a nutritional index and clinical data, can predict IVIG resistance in children with Kawasaki disease
model_description: Radiomic features are extracted from segmented 2D coronary artery ultrasound images (LCA, LAD, RCA) via LASSO selection and combined with the Prognostic Nutritional Index and clinical variables in a logistic regression model to predict IVIG treatment resistance.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and validation study
headline_result: Combined Clinic+PNI+Radiomics model AUC 0.880 (95% CI 0.817-0.944) in validation cohort

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Multimodal Ultrasound Model for Prediction of Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Development and Validation.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
venue_label: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
patient_population: 721 pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound screening at 20-24 weeks gestation (44 with spontaneous preterm birth)
clinical_problem: Whether a multimodal AI model combining cervical ultrasound images, elastography, and ultrasound parameters can predict spontaneous preterm birth in the second trimester
model_description: A DenseNet121 deep learning model scores cervical 2D ultrasound and elastography images; these deep-learning scores plus ultrasound parameters (elasticity contrast index, hardness ratio, etc.) feed five machine learning classifiers, the best being a neural network, to predict spontaneous preterm birth.
study_design: prospective cohort study developing and validating a multimodal AI model
headline_result: Best multimodal neural network AUC 0.85 (95% CI 0.73-0.96) in validation set; DenseNet121 image-only AUC 0.92-0.93

title: Text-prompted foundation-model segmentation of intrapartum fetal ultrasound: a controlled methodological study with F-TPA-SAM2.
patient_population: Intrapartum fetal ultrasound images (PSFHS training/test dataset); zero-shot transfer evaluated on 779 HC18 images
clinical_problem: Whether text-conditioned prompting can direct a frozen segmentation foundation model (SAM 2) to segment fetal anatomical structures on intrapartum ultrasound for labor-progress monitoring, without manual geometric prompts
model_description: F-TPA-SAM2 is a small trainable adapter (0.871M parameters) that maps frozen FetalCLIP text embeddings into a prompt for a frozen SAM 2 mask decoder, enabling text-selected segmentation of fetal anatomical structures on intrapartum B-mode ultrasound.
study_design: controlled methodological development study with ablation controls
dataset_size: PSFHS dataset with label budgets N=20/100/400; zero-shot test on 779 HC18 images

title: MDIFN: a deep learning-based multi-dimensional interaction fusion network for placental MRI segmentation.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
venue_label: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
patient_population: 267 placental MRI cases
clinical_problem: Whether a deep learning model combining 2D and 3D feature fusion can automatically and accurately segment the placenta on MRI
model_description: MDIFN combines a 2D-UNet and 3D-UNet branch via a bidirectional gated cross-dimension fusion module, plus global context recalibration and residual refinement, to output an automatic placental segmentation mask from MRI.
study_design: retrospective model development study with 10-fold cross-validation and ablation
headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.8749±0.0132, an improvement of 16.2% over pure 2D-UNet and 8.4% over pure 3D-UNet

title: Artificial intelligence model based on the detection of key anatomical structures for identifying standard planes on ultrasound of the first-trimester fetal central nervous system: a multicenter study.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
venue_label: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
patient_population: 2,901 first-trimester fetal CNS ultrasound standard-plane images from three hospitals, plus external validation of 300 images from a fourth hospital
clinical_problem: Whether an AI model can identify standard first-trimester fetal CNS ultrasound planes by detecting key anatomical structures, to assist sonographers of varying experience
model_description: FCNS-Model detects key anatomical structures on first-trimester fetal ultrasound images to classify/identify standard CNS planes (midsagittal, transthalamic, coronal frontal, transventricular), compared against physicians of varying seniority against an expert-team reference standard.
study_design: prospective multicenter model development and validation study
dataset_size: 2,901 images (train 2,124/test 264/internal val 254/clinical val 259) plus external validation 300 images
headline_result: Test set precision/recall/F1 >92%; clinical validation AUC up to 0.984 vs senior physician 0.906 (P<0.001) for midsagittal plane

title: Echo-Mamba: A Lightweight Mamba-Based Framework for Generalizable Left Ventricular Segmentation Across Multiple Echocardiographic Views.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
patient_population: public echocardiography datasets including EchoNet-Dynamic, EchoNet-Pediatric, CAMUS, HMC-QU
clinical_problem: Can a lightweight AI model accurately segment the left ventricle on echocardiograms across different views and age groups, including children?
model_description: Echo-Mamba is a lightweight state-space-model architecture with an Adaptive Feature Enhancement module that segments the left ventricle across multiple echocardiographic views, tested on adult and pediatric public datasets.
release_evidence: The implementation of our approach is publicly available at https://github.com/Beliefs666/EchoMamba
study_design: retrospective method development and benchmark comparison
dataset_size: four public datasets (EchoNet-Dynamic, EchoNet-Pediatric, CAMUS, HMC-QU)
headline_result: 0.323M parameters; generalizable segmentation across anatomical targets, age groups, and views (specific Dice not given)

title: Pediatric vs. Adult Pneumonia Detection: Quantifying Age-related Generalization Gaps in Zero-shot Multimodal Large Language Models.
model_name: GPT-5.2; Claude Opus 4.5; Gemini 2.5 Pro; InceptionV3 (CNN baseline)
patient_population: Balanced pediatric and adult chest radiograph test sets (n=1000 each, 500 pneumonia/500 normal); pediatric development pool n=4715, adult n=13,863
clinical_problem: How well do zero-shot multimodal large language models detect pneumonia on pediatric versus adult chest radiographs compared with a domain-trained CNN, and how large is the pediatric-adult generalization gap
model_description: Three general-purpose multimodal LLMs (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) are evaluated zero-shot for pneumonia detection on frontal chest radiographs, compared to cohort-specific InceptionV3 CNNs trained separately on pediatric and adult images; performance and age-related generalization gap (Matthews correlation coefficient) are measured for each.
study_design: retrospective comparative diagnostic accuracy study, zero-shot LLMs vs domain-trained CNN
dataset_size: Pediatric: 4715 development + 1000 test; Adult: 13,863 development + 1000 test
headline_result: Pediatric: CNN MCC 0.799 vs GPT-5.2 0.484, Claude Opus 4.5 0.470, Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.272; LLMs showed a larger adult-pediatric generalization gap than the CNN

title: AI-driven Assessment of Vertebral Rotation in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Using Weight-bearing Cone-beam CT.
patient_population: 72 adolescents with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
clinical_problem: Whether an AI algorithm can automatically and accurately quantify 3D vertebral rotation on weight-bearing cone-beam CT in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, and how well the standard 2D Nash & Moe grading system represents true 3D rotation
model_description: A U-Net-based algorithm processes weight-bearing cone-beam CT images of the spine to automatically compute vertebral rotation angles for each vertebra, compared against manual measurements by two radiologists and against the 2D Nash & Moe grading system from standing radiographs.
headline_result: ICC 0.881 (95% CI 0.852-0.905) between automated and manual vertebral rotation measurements

title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics: Current Trends and Future Directions.
patient_population: Pregnant patients / fetuses, literature 2016-2026
clinical_problem: State of evidence for AI applications across obstetric care, including fetal ultrasound biometry and anomaly detection, fetal monitoring, and maternal risk stratification
model_description: Narrative review of AI (machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, NLP) across obstetric care, with a focus on image-based tasks (ultrasound fetal biometry and structural anomaly detection) alongside non-imaging applications (cardiotocography, genomic screening, telehealth); reports that image-based tasks often exceed AUC 0.85 while most evidence is retrospective and internally validated.
headline_result: Image-based tasks often AUC/accuracy >0.85; intrapartum CTG analysis AUROC ~0.60-0.70

title: Quantitative assessment of fetal lung development using MRI-based radiomics: a comparative analysis of 3D and 2D approaches with external validation.
model_family: support vector regression / partial least squares regression
patient_population: 292 fetal MRI scans (28-38+6 weeks gestation), original dataset n=252 and independent test set n=40, from two institutions
clinical_problem: Whether 2D or 3D MRI radiomics better quantifies fetal lung development, using gestational age estimation as a surrogate marker
model_description: 102 radiomics features are extracted from manually segmented 2D (single-plane) and 3D (whole-lung) regions of interest on T2-weighted fetal MRI; support vector regression and partial least squares regression models estimate gestational age from these features as a surrogate for lung maturity, with external validation.
study_design: retrospective model development study with external validation of 2D vs 3D radiomics
dataset_size: 292 fetal MRI scans (252 development, 40 independent external test)
headline_result: 3D radiomics r=0.904 (SVR)/0.902 (PLSR) in original dataset, 0.846/0.861 in independent test set; 2D-3D correspondence ICC median 0.379 (original)/0.247 (test)

title: Prospective Comparison of Ultra-Low-Dose Versus Standard-Dose Computed Tomography for Esophageal Foreign Body Detection.
publication_types: Journal Article; Video-Audio Media; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study
patient_population: 180 patients with suspected esophageal foreign body ingestion (120 adults, 60 children)
clinical_problem: Whether ultra-low-dose CT (incorporating deep learning image reconstruction) is non-inferior to standard-dose CT for detecting esophageal foreign bodies while reducing radiation dose, in a mixed adult and pediatric population
model_description: An ultra-low-dose CT protocol combines reduced kV/mA acquisition with deep learning image reconstruction (plus iterative reconstruction) to maintain diagnostic image quality for esophageal foreign body detection, compared against standard-dose CT with conventional reconstruction.
headline_result: AUC 0.985 (ULD-CT) vs 0.991 (SD-CT), non-inferior; effective dose reduced 63% (P<0.001)

title: Evaluating the impact of segmentation strategies on radiomic feature stability for paediatric brain tumour diagnosis using diffusion weighted imaging.
patient_population: 106 pediatric brain tumor patients
clinical_problem: How much do different tumor segmentation (ROI drawing) strategies affect the stability of radiomic features and downstream diagnostic classification accuracy for pediatric brain tumors on diffusion-weighted MRI
model_description: Ground-truth tumor ROIs on ADC maps are systematically eroded or dilated to simulate conservative versus extensive segmentation, and radiomic feature stability and machine learning diagnostic classification accuracy are compared across these segmentation strategies.
headline_result: Classification accuracy reduced by 3.8±0.8% (erosion) and 5.6±0.9% (dilation) vs ground-truth ROI features; stable-feature selection reduced the drop to 1.4±0.7%/2.9±0.3%

title: Automated segmentation of postsurgical resection cavities on magnetic resonance imaging in focal epilepsy: A Multicentre Epilepsy Lesion Detection study.
patient_population: 969 subjects across 27 centers (MELD project) plus 133 from the EPISURG dataset; children and adults
clinical_problem: Whether a deep learning tool can automatically and accurately segment postsurgical resection cavities on MRI after epilepsy surgery in a heterogeneous multicenter cohort of children and adults
model_description: MELD-PostOp is an nnU-Net-based deep learning model trained on postoperative T1-weighted MRI to automatically segment resection cavities after epilepsy surgery, compared against existing automated tools (Epic-CHOP, ResectVol, RESSEG) and evaluated on stratified and independent test cohorts.
release_evidence: MELD-PostOp is an open-source research tool
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and validation study
dataset_size: 969 subjects (27 centers) + 133 (EPISURG); final model trained on 965 masks; Stratified Test Cohort n=50, Independent Test Cohort n=87
headline_result: Median DSC 0.85, HD95 3.61 on combined test cohort, outperforming existing tools (DSC 0.43-0.69)

title: Radiomics of planar Tc-99m methylene diphosphonate bone scintigraphy for pediatric osteomyelitis: a paired infected-contralateral analysis.
patient_population: 28 pediatric patients with suspected osteomyelitis
clinical_problem: Whether radiomics analysis of planar Tc-99m MDP bone scintigraphy can quantitatively distinguish infected from normal bone in children with suspected osteomyelitis
model_description: 62 quantitative radiomic features (shape, intensity, texture) are extracted from paired infected and contralateral normal bone ROIs on planar Tc-99m MDP bone scintigraphy; a compact radiomics score from top features is derived via LOOCV logistic regression to discriminate infected from normal bone.
headline_result: Single-feature LOOCV AUC 0.60-0.63; texture features showed large effect sizes (Cohen's d ~0.80-0.85, P<0.001) distinguishing infected vs normal bone

title: Benchmarking Generalizability in Deep Learning-Based White Matter Tract Segmentation.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
venue_label: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
patient_population: Independent diffusion MRI datasets with varying acquisition protocols and populations, including pediatric data
clinical_problem: How well do deep learning white matter tract segmentation models generalize across datasets, particularly when adult-trained models are applied to pediatric diffusion MRI data
model_description: Four state-of-the-art deep learning architectures (including CNN-based TractSeg) for white matter tract segmentation on diffusion MRI/tractography are benchmarked across datasets; an ensemble model (EWMTS) combining complementary models is introduced to partially recover accuracy lost under domain shift, notably when adult-trained models are applied to pediatric data.
release_evidence: openly releasing this benchmark and a reproducible processing pipeline
headline_result: Performance dropped sharply under domain shift, most severely when applying adult-trained models to pediatric data; EWMTS partially recovered accuracy

title: A Non-enhanced CT Dataset for Differential Diagnosis of Pediatric Extracranial Germ Cell Tumors.
patient_population: Children with extracranial germ cell tumors
clinical_problem: Providing a public imaging dataset and preliminary radiomics models to aid differential diagnosis of pediatric extracranial germ cell tumor histological subtypes on non-enhanced CT
model_description: The CT-PEGCT-Diag dataset provides 642 non-enhanced CT scans across six histological subtypes of pediatric extracranial germ cell tumors with expert-annotated tumor masks; preliminary radiomics-based machine learning models are used to demonstrate the dataset's utility for subtype classification.
release_evidence: publicly available imaging dataset... designed to facilitate the validation of AI models
study_design: dataset paper with preliminary radiomics classification experiments
dataset_size: 642 non-enhanced CT scans, six histological subtypes

title: Radiological assessment of pulmonary vascularity in congenital heart disease: standardized clinician assessment versus deep learning-based prediction.
patient_population: 400 CXRs from CHD patients evaluated by pediatric cardiology/radiology experts and trainees; DLM trained on a separate 1,088 CXRs
clinical_problem: Whether a deep learning model can more accurately and reproducibly assess pulmonary vascularity on chest radiographs in congenital heart disease than standardized clinician assessment, using Fick-derived Qp:Qs as reference
model_description: A deep learning model is trained on 1,088 chest radiographs to predict the pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp:Qs) and classify pulmonary vascularity as increased or decreased, compared against Fick-catheterization-derived values and against structured clinician assessment by experts and trainees.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing DLM to structured clinician assessment
headline_result: ICC between Fick- and DLM-derived Qp:Qs 0.782 (P<0.001); AUROC 98% for Qp:Qs>1.5 and <0.9 thresholds; DLM concordance 88%/98% vs clinician 75%/66% (P=0.03)

title: Association of sleep symptom burden with default mode network homogeneity in first-episode drug-naïve adolescents with major depressive disorder.
patient_population: First-episode, drug-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder (162, split into higher and lower sleep-symptom-burden groups) plus 53 healthy adolescent controls
clinical_problem: classification of adolescent major depressive disorder subgroups by sleep symptom burden using resting-state fMRI connectivity
model_description: Exploratory SVM models were trained on voxel-wise default mode network (DMN) homogeneity values derived from resting-state fMRI to distinguish adolescents with major depressive disorder (higher vs. lower sleep symptom burden) from healthy controls. The abstract reports only modest discriminative performance, indicating limited individual-level classification utility.
study_design: cross-sectional case-control resting-state fMRI study with exploratory SVM classification
dataset_size: 162 adolescents with MDD (86 higher sleep-symptom-burden, 76 lower) and 53 healthy controls
headline_result: Exploratory SVM analyses showed modest discriminative performance, indicating limited utility of network homogeneity alterations alone for individual-level classification.

title: Multimodal Transformer Fusion of Clinical Information, Medical Text, and Pituitary MRI 2.5D Deep Learning Features for Differentiating Growth Hormone Deficiency and Idiopathic Short Stature.
patient_population: 618 children (internal training cohort, two centers) and 164 children (independent external test cohort)
clinical_problem: Whether combining pituitary MRI deep learning features with clinical information and medical text can non-invasively differentiate pediatric growth hormone deficiency from idiopathic short stature
model_description: A 2.5D deep learning model extracts features from pituitary MRI; these are fused via a multimodal Transformer with clinical data and medical text features to output a probability distinguishing growth hormone deficiency from idiopathic short stature.
study_design: retrospective two-center model development study with an external test cohort
headline_result: MM_Fusion AUC 0.942 (training), 0.896 (external test)

title: Structure-Aware Deep Learning for Pediatric Echocardiographic Standard-View Classification in Ultrasonic Imaging.
patient_population: Private pediatric ventricular septal defect echocardiography dataset (4 standard views)
clinical_problem: Whether a structure-aware deep learning framework can accurately classify standard views in pediatric echocardiography (specifically ventricular septal defect imaging) to support downstream automated interpretation
model_description: PVTv2-ASEF adds an Adaptive Structural Enhancement Module and a Dual Auxiliary Fusion Head to a PVTv2 transformer backbone to classify pediatric echocardiographic images into one of four standard views, evaluated on a private ventricular septal defect dataset and cross-task on the public FETAL_PLANES_DB.
study_design: retrospective model development study with cross-task external evaluation
headline_result: Improved macro-F1 by 0.093 over PVTv2-B2 baseline on the private dataset; 0.023 improvement on cross-task FETAL_PLANES_DB evaluation

title: Deep learning-based detection of pediatric brain tumor presence on MRI.
patient_population: 285 pediatric patients (140 with confirmed brain tumors, 145 controls)
clinical_problem: Whether a CNN can accurately detect the presence of a brain tumor on pediatric T1-weighted MRI (tumor vs. no tumor)
model_description: A CNN with convolutional, max-pooling, and dropout layers classifies T1-weighted pediatric brain MRI images as tumor-present or tumor-absent.
study_design: retrospective model development study with cross-validation
headline_result: Precision 99%, recall 100%, F1-score 99% at 40 training epochs

title: Edge-centric brain connectomes reveal two molecularly distinct neurobiological subtypes of adolescent major depressive disorder.
model_family: data-driven clustering with machine learning classification
patient_population: Adolescents with major depressive disorder
clinical_problem: identifying molecular subtypes of adolescent major depressive disorder from brain connectome to improve case-control discrimination
model_description: Individualized edge-centric functional brain connectomes were derived from MRI and used to compute nodal entropy per region; a data-driven clustering algorithm identified two adolescent MDD subtypes, and machine learning models were then built to test whether subtype division improved case-control discrimination. Subtype-specific entropy patterns were further linked to transcriptomic and neurotransmitter profiles.
study_design: cross-sectional case-control connectomics study with unsupervised subtyping and machine learning classification
headline_result: Subtype-based models significantly improved case-control discriminability, with the two subtypes characterized by distinct core predictive factors.

title: Deep learning segmentation of paediatric brain tumours using diffusion-weighted MRI: towards an early, in vivo classification pipeline.
patient_population: 107 pediatric brain tumor patients (Imaging of Tumors study)
clinical_problem: Whether an automated deep learning segmentation approach using only diffusion-weighted MRI can delineate pediatric brain tumor margins to support extraction of quantitative biomarkers, avoiding time-consuming manual delineation
model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network (DeepMedic), using transfer learning and multi-modal ensembling, automatically segments pediatric brain tumors from diffusion-weighted MRI alone, compared against manual expert annotations.
headline_result: Median Dice score of 0.63 for the best-performing model

title: Machine-learning classification of children and adolescents with ASD using resting-state frequency-specific intrinsic activity.
patient_population: 251 participants with ASD (146 children, 105 adolescents) from ten ABIDE sites
clinical_problem: Whether frequency-specific resting-state fMRI features can distinguish children from adolescents within autism spectrum disorder, informing understanding of ASD developmental stages
model_description: ALFF and ReHo features computed from resting-state fMRI across three frequency bands and 246 brain regions are used to train logistic regression, SVM, and random forest classifiers (with SHAP interpretation) to distinguish children from adolescents with ASD.
study_design: retrospective multi-site cohort study with a held-out test set
headline_result: Best model slow-4 ReHo Logistic Regression AUC 0.811, accuracy 0.745; combined slow-4 ALFF+ReHo AUC 0.819

title: Improved Deep Learning Segmentation of Pediatric Diffuse Midline Gliomas After Treatment.
patient_population: Patients aged 1-30 years with diffuse midline glioma from an institutional pediatric cancer center, BraTS-PEDs 2024, and the PNOC007 trial
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Whether an auto-segmentation tool optimized with post-treatment data can accurately track pediatric diffuse midline glioma volume over the course of treatment for longitudinal response assessment
model_description: DMGtracker, an nnU-Net-based model trained on four-sequence multiparametric MRI (T1, T1 post-contrast, T2, FLAIR) including both pre- and post-treatment scans, automatically segments whole-tumor and contrast-enhancing pediatric diffuse midline glioma, benchmarked against the BraTS-PEDs 2024 winning model.
study_design: multi-institutional retrospective model development and external validation study
dataset_size: 153 scans/74 patients (training/internal test); 88 external PNOC007 studies (49 patients); 261 BraTS-PEDs 2024 pre-treatment studies
headline_result: External validation whole-tumor DSC 0.90 [0.72-0.95] vs BraTS-PEDs winner 0.81 [0.66-0.90]; clinically acceptable segmentation (DSC>0.80) in 64.0% vs 52.0% of post-treatment cases

title: Large Language Model Decision Support for Cranial CT in Pediatric Head Trauma.
patient_population: 819 pediatric patients (<18 years) with blunt head trauma who underwent cranial CT
clinical_problem: Whether AI-based (LLM) cranial CT recommendations in pediatric blunt head trauma are associated with clinically important adverse outcomes, assessing diagnostic performance and clinical utility for CT decision support
model_description: A general-purpose large language model generates a binary cranial CT recommendation ('CT recommended' or 'CT not recommended') from structured clinical information available at ED presentation in pediatric head trauma, evaluated against a composite adverse outcome (surgery, ICU admission, intubation, neurological sequelae, or death).
headline_result: Sensitivity 90.9%, specificity 40.8%, PPV 24.5%, NPV 95.5% for predicting adverse outcome via AI CT recommendation

title: External Validation of Deeplasia for Automated Bone Age Assessment Compared with Four Commercial AI Systems.
model_name: Deeplasia; four CE-certified commercial AI systems
patient_population: 306 children and adolescents aged 1-18 years (bone age cohort); 1653 children and adolescents undergoing hand radiography after trauma (chronological age cohort)
clinical_problem: How well does Deeplasia, a deep-learning bone age tool, perform for Greulich-Pyle bone age and chronological age estimation compared with four commercial CE-certified AI systems
model_description: Deeplasia and four commercial AI systems each take a hand radiograph and output an automated Greulich-Pyle-based bone age estimate; performance for bone age and, separately, chronological age estimation is compared against expert reader consensus.
study_design: retrospective single-center external validation and comparison study
dataset_size: 306 children/adolescents (bone age cohort); 1653 children/adolescents (chronological age cohort)
headline_result: Deeplasia RMSE 0.59y (boys)/0.55y (girls), MAE 0.45y (boys)/0.43y (girls) for bone age; chronological age estimation substantially less accurate for all systems, with systematic overestimation especially in adolescent girls

title: State-Specific Segmental Abnormalities of White Matter Structure and Function in Pediatric Bipolar Disorders.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 19 manic-phase and 20 euthymic-phase pediatric bipolar disorder patients and 17 matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: distinguishing manic-phase and euthymic-phase pediatric bipolar disorder from healthy controls using multimodal white-matter structure/function features
model_description: Input: DTI tensor metrics and functional ALFF values from 100 segments of 8 white-matter tracts plus clinical information; output: random forest classification of manic-phase pediatric bipolar disorder vs. healthy controls.
headline_result: random forest classifier achieved 84% accuracy distinguishing manic-phase PBD from healthy controls

title: Completely free-breathing cardiac MRI using deep learning reconstruction reduces sedation and scan time in children.
patient_population: 150 pediatric patients imaged with free-breathing DL cardiac MRI compared to 150 sequential patients with conventional breath-hold imaging
clinical_problem: reducing scan time and need for anesthesia/intubation in pediatric cardiac MRI while preserving diagnostic quality
model_description: Input: highly accelerated single-cardiac-cycle free-breathing cine MRI k-space data; output: deep-learning-reconstructed cine images used for volumetric/functional cardiac assessment.
headline_result: CMR duration 29.2±9.8 min vs 43.0±13.2 min; intubation with muscle relaxation 14% vs 90% (both P<0.01)

title: Deep Learning-Based Classification for Grading of Respiratory Distress Syndrome on Neonatal Chest Radiographs.
patient_population: neonates with normal and RDS chest radiographs from training, validation and external test sets
clinical_problem: automated grading of respiratory distress syndrome severity on neonatal chest radiographs
model_description: Input: neonatal chest radiographs, lungs segmented with UNet++; output: five ordered RDS severity grades from a ResNet-50-based classifier.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: quadratic weighted kappa 0.696; AUROC 0.966 for detecting RDS, 0.866 for clinically significant RDS (Grade >=3)

title: Machine learning for prediction of large-for-gestational-age neonate with adverse outcome at routine ultrasound examination at 35-37 weeks.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
venue_label: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
model_family: random forest, XGBoost, elastic net, support vector machine (compared to logistic regression)
patient_population: 21,743 singleton pregnancies undergoing routine ultrasound at 35+0 to 37+6 weeks' gestation
clinical_problem: predicting a large-for-gestational-age neonate and associated adverse perinatal outcome from routine late third-trimester ultrasound
model_description: Input: third-trimester fetal biometry and Doppler ultrasound parameters plus maternal demographic characteristics; output: predicted probability of a large-for-gestational-age neonate and of associated adverse perinatal outcome.
headline_result: AUC 0.888 for LGA neonate and 0.859 for LGA with adverse outcome; ML did not outperform logistic regression

title: Non-invasive differentiation of diffuse midline glioma and midline glioblastoma using DCE-MRI perfusion parameters and machine learning classification in pediatric and young adult patients.
model_family: random forest and other classifiers on DCE-MRI perfusion features
patient_population: 62 pediatric and young adult patients with histologically confirmed midline gliomas (30 mGBM, 32 DMG)
clinical_problem: non-invasively differentiating diffuse midline glioma from midline glioblastoma to guide treatment when tissue diagnosis is difficult to obtain
model_description: Input: quantitative DCE-MRI perfusion parameters (rCBV, rCBF, Slope-2, Ktrans, Vp, Ve); output: machine-learning classification distinguishing diffuse midline glioma from midline glioblastoma.
headline_result: random forest combination (rCBV+rCBF+Ve) achieved 76.67±7.16% cross-validation accuracy; individual parameter AUCs 70.6-75.3%

title: Distributed gray-white matter structural covariance alterations and interindividual heterogeneity in adolescents with functional/dissociative seizures.
model_family: Elastic Net and Random Forest on structural MRI covariance features
patient_population: 70 adolescents with functional/dissociative seizures and 70 healthy controls
clinical_problem: characterizing distributed brain structural differences in adolescents with functional/dissociative seizures and testing whether structural features predict symptom severity
model_description: Input: gray- and white-matter structural covariance features from structural MRI; output: cross-validated Elastic Net/Random Forest prediction of dissociative symptom severity (did not significantly predict severity).
headline_result: structural features differentiated FDS from controls but did not significantly predict dissociative symptom severity (all p>0.05)

title: Accelerated Cardiac MRI Using Deep Learning Cine Imaging: Validation in Pediatric Patients both with and without Congenital Heart Disease.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
venue_label: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
patient_population: 50 pediatric patients (median age 16.1 years, 56% with congenital heart disease) with two-ventricle physiology
clinical_problem: accelerating cardiac MRI cine imaging while preserving diagnostic accuracy in children with and without congenital heart disease
model_description: Input: undersampled breath-held and free-breathing cine bSSFP acquisitions at three acceleration levels; output: deep-learning-reconstructed cine images for biventricular volumetric and functional quantification.
headline_result: acquisition time reduced 66-89%; radial strain ICC 0.92 vs conventional cine; LV/RV volumes differed <5-10 mL/m2

title: Clinical Implementation and Validation of Automated Slice-to-Volume Reconstruction for Fetal MRI Using a Vendor-Neutral MONAI-Based Imaging Informatics Pipeline.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
model_family: automated slice-to-volume reconstruction (MONAI Deploy Express pipeline)
patient_population: 65 consecutive singleton fetal MRI examinations (mean gestational age 28.9 weeks, range 19-36 weeks), most with structural abnormalities
clinical_problem: implementing and validating a fully automated clinical pipeline for fetal MRI slice-to-volume reconstruction
model_description: Input: routine single-shot fast spin-echo fetal MRI series triggered by DICOM routing; output: motion-corrected slice-to-volume reconstructed brain and body volumes returned to PACS for radiologist review.
release_evidence: open-source Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI) Deploy Express, DICOM routing, and PACS return
headline_result: brain SVR rated pass-or-higher in 90.8% and body SVR in 87.7% of examinations; inter-reader ICC 0.93 (brain), 0.92 (body)

title: Quantifying human variability in pediatric bone age assessment: a multi-institutional multi-reader study and benchmark for AI evaluation.
model_family: atlas-based automated system (BoneXpert) and a deep-learning algorithm, compared against human readers
patient_population: 1,285 left-hand and wrist radiographs from five US academic centers, interpreted by 22 radiologists across nine institutions
clinical_problem: benchmarking automated bone age assessment against human reader variability using the Greulich and Pyle method
model_description: Input: left-hand and wrist radiographs; output: bone age estimate compared between multiple human readers, BoneXpert, and a deep-learning algorithm against a three-rater consensus reference.
release_evidence: BoneXpert (named commercial automated bone age system)
headline_result: BoneXpert MAE 4.8 months vs 6.5 months for individual human readers; deep-learning algorithm MAE 6.3 months; substantial deviations in 0.7% (BoneXpert) vs 3.4% (single human reader)

title: Improving pediatric hip fracture detection using deep learning: multicenter validation and clinical reader study.
patient_population: 640 pediatric patients (median age 4.1 years) with 794 hip radiographs from four tertiary hospitals
clinical_problem: detecting femoral neck fractures on hip radiographs in young children
model_description: Input: pediatric hip radiographs; output: automated real-time localization and diagnosis of femoral neck fractures, also used to assist reader interpretation.
study_design: retrospective multicenter validation with clinical reader study
headline_result: AUROC 0.911 internal, 0.873 external; AI assistance improved junior-reader accuracy (delta AUROC +0.083) and agreement (kappa 0.49 to 0.61)

title: Diagnostic classification of children and adolescents with high-functioning autism spectrum disorder based on brain functional network characteristics of the dense individualized and common connectivity-based cortical landmark model.
model_family: linear support vector machine on DICCCOL-based functional connectivity
patient_population: 37 children/adolescents with high-functioning autism spectrum disorder and 33 typically developing controls
clinical_problem: distinguishing high-functioning autism spectrum disorder from typically developing children and adolescents using brain connectivity MRI
model_description: Input: DTI-derived structural connectivity and resting-state fMRI functional connectivity among individualized DICCCOL cortical landmarks; output: SVM classification of HF-ASD vs. typically developing controls.
headline_result: classification accuracy 84.29%, sensitivity 83.78%, specificity 84.85%, AUC 0.832

title: Two-Plane AI-Assisted Renal Ultrasound for Grading Unilateral Hydronephrosis in Infants: A Single-Center Proof-of-Concept Internal Validation Study.
patient_population: 186 infants younger than 12 months with unilateral hydronephrosis
clinical_problem: grading severity of unilateral hydronephrosis on renal ultrasound in infants
model_description: Input: one transverse and one sagittal renal ultrasound still image; output: mild/moderate/severe hydronephrosis grade from a two-branch CNN.
study_design: retrospective single-center proof-of-concept internal validation study
headline_result: exact agreement with expert consensus 85.5% (weighted kappa 0.83); sensitivity 92.5%, specificity 86.1% for clinically significant hydronephrosis

title: Identifying optimal dose head CT acquisition techniques through cluster analysis from 904,209 scans.
patient_population: 904,209 head CT scans, including 40,027 in children, from an international CT dose registry
clinical_problem: identifying low-dose head CT acquisition protocols, including in children, using cluster analysis of a large international dose registry
model_description: Input: CT acquisition parameters (tube current, voltage, collimation, scan length, pitch) from head CT scans; output: k-means clusters of acquisition technique compared by radiation dose (DLP, CTDIvol).
headline_result: size-adjusted dose-length product varied more than two-fold, up to 3.4-fold, across clusters within each stratum

title: Automated segmentation and length measurement of metacarpal and phalangeal bones for hand radiograph evaluation.

patient_population: pediatric hand radiographs (normal and dysmorphic cases) from public datasets, including patients with Turner syndrome, achondroplasia, and pseudohypoparathyroidism
clinical_problem: measuring metacarpal and phalangeal bone lengths on pediatric hand radiographs to screen for skeletal dysplasias and genetic conditions
model_description: Input: pediatric hand radiographs; output: automated segmentation of 19 metacarpal and phalangeal bones and their lengths, used to derive relative metacarpophalangeal pattern profiles for genetic conditions.
study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation study
headline_result: segmentation Dice 98.7% (normal bones), 95.0% (dysmorphic bones); length estimation relative error 2.2% (normal), 4.5% (dysmorphic)

title: Orientation-robust latent motion trajectory learning for annotation-free cardiac phase detection in fetal echocardiography.

clinical_problem: automated, annotation-free detection of cardiac end-diastolic and end-systolic phases in fetal echocardiography to support congenital heart disease assessment
model_description: Input: fetal four-chamber-view echocardiography video frames; output: self-supervised latent motion trajectory whose turning points localize end-diastolic and end-systolic cardiac phases without manual annotation.
headline_result: mean absolute error 1.9 frames (ED) and 1.6 frames (ES) on normal cases; 2.4 and 2.1 frames on CHD cases

title: Early risk stratification of adverse progression in pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia using a multicenter CT radiomics model.
model_family: random forest (clinical-imaging, radiomics, and integrated models)
patient_population: 419 children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia from three hospitals
clinical_problem: early prediction of adverse progression (refractory pneumonia or plastic bronchitis) in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia using CT
model_description: Input: CT radiomics features from pulmonary lesions plus clinical/inflammatory indices; output: random forest prediction of adverse disease progression, externally validated.
study_design: multicenter retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: integrated model AUC 0.828, accuracy 0.906 in external validation cohort, outperforming clinical-imaging (AUC 0.736) and radiomics-only (AUC 0.813) models

title: Agreement Between WebCeph and Manual Cephalometric Analysis: Cleft and Non-Cleft Patients Comparison: A Retrospective Method-Comparison Study.

clinical_problem: evaluating agreement of AI-based cephalometric landmark analysis (WebCeph) with manual tracing in children with cleft lip and palate
model_description: Input: lateral cephalograms; output: automated angular cephalometric measurements (WebCeph) compared against manual tracing in cleft and non-cleft children.

title: Comparative evaluation of large language models for text-based diagnostic reasoning in fetal central nervous system MRI: A retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study.

model_description: Input: standardized text summaries of fetal CNS MRI findings and clinical information (no images); output: ranked differential diagnoses, reasoning, management and counseling text generated by ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek.

headline_result: DeepSeek highest principal diagnosis match 77.6% (66/85), Gemini 69.4%, ChatGPT 61.2% (Cochran's Q P=0.044)

title: Automated fetal magnetic resonance imaging lung segmentation for rapid lung volume estimation across diverse pulmonary hypoplasia phenotypes.

clinical_problem: automating fetal MRI lung volume measurement for prenatal risk stratification of pulmonary hypoplasia
model_description: Input: fetal MRI; output: automated lung segmentation used to estimate total lung volume and percent predicted lung volume, compared with expert-adjudicated manual segmentation.
study_design: retrospective model development and testing study
headline_result: ICC 0.955 for total lung volume (mean Dice 0.81); ICC 0.727 for percent predicted lung volume; median inference time 4 s per exam

title: Automated reconstruction of dynamic 2D fetal cardiac MRI using deep learning in late third-trimester fetuses.
patient_population: 23 late third-trimester pregnancies (34-36 weeks gestational age), 21 healthy fetuses and 2 with congenital heart disease
clinical_problem: automating region-of-interest selection for fetal cardiac MRI motion-corrected cine reconstruction
model_description: Input: real-time multi-slice fetal cardiac MRI images; output: nnU-Net-selected regions of interest feeding a motion-corrected cine reconstruction pipeline with metric-optimized gating.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study
headline_result: nnU-Net mean Dice score 0.83±0.23 (81% of scores exceeding 0.8); comparable image quality between automatic and manual cine reconstruction

title: Dual-Approach AI for Pediatric Supracondylar Fractures: Multiclass Radiograph Classification with Explainable AI and Diagnostic Meta-analysis of AI-Based Computational Approaches.
model_family: YOLOv11 Nano deep learning and radiomics-based machine learning (meta-analysis)
patient_population: 1,082 pediatric elbow radiographs (2004-2018); meta-analysis pooling 4 studies covering 2,232 images
clinical_problem: detecting and classifying (Gartland type) pediatric supracondylar fractures on elbow radiographs
model_description: Input: pediatric elbow radiographs; output: multiclass YOLOv11 Nano classification of no fracture vs. Gartland Type I-III supracondylar fractures, with explainable-AI attention maps, synthesized with a diagnostic meta-analysis of prior AI approaches.
study_design: retrospective model development with diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis
dataset_size: 1,082 pediatric elbow radiographs; meta-analysis of 2,232 images across 4 studies
headline_result: multiclass accuracy 90.98-93.12% across validation strategies; meta-analysis pooled sensitivity 92.0%, specificity 85.0%

title: Deep Learning Pipeline for Automatic Segmentation, Classification, and Molecular Subtyping of Three Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumors Using T2-Weighted MRI.

venue_label: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
patient_population: 1,305 patients (490 medulloblastoma, 327 ependymoma, 488 pilocytic astrocytoma) from three centers

model_description: Input: T2-weighted MRI; output: automatic tumor segmentation, classification among medulloblastoma/ependymoma/pilocytic astrocytoma, and molecular subtyping of medulloblastoma and ependymoma.

headline_result: PF-nnU-Net Dice 0.94-0.96, classification accuracy 0.824-0.918; MB-nnU-Net accuracy 0.794; EP-nnU-Net accuracy 0.789

title: A pretreatment multiphasic CT-based decision-support model for differentiating pediatric hepatoblastoma from focal nodular hyperplasia.
model_family: 2.5D ResNet-18 deep learning combined with a quantitative enhancement feature (logistic regression) model
patient_population: 612 children (523 hepatoblastoma, 89 focal nodular hyperplasia) undergoing pretreatment multiphasic CT
clinical_problem: differentiating pediatric hepatoblastoma from focal nodular hyperplasia using pretreatment multiphasic CT

title: Automated Diagnosis of Infantile Skull Fractures From X-Ray Images Using an Ensemble Deep Learning Model.
model_family: ensemble convolutional neural network (ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B5)
patient_population: 1,184 patients with head trauma (2010-2021) undergoing skull X-rays
clinical_problem: detecting skull fractures in neonates and infants on plain radiographs to reduce radiation exposure from CT
model_description: Input: anterior-posterior and lateral skull radiographs with CLAHE-enhanced preprocessing; output: ensemble CNN classification distinguishing skull fractures from normal cranial anatomy (e.g., sutures).
study_design: retrospective model development with internal and external validation
dataset_size: 1,184 patients; internal test 4,298 images, external test 460 images
headline_result: ensemble model AUC 0.938, accuracy 91.6% on external validation dataset

title: Gut microbiota correlating with glycerophospholipid metabolism dysregulation is associated with brain functional alterations in adolescent depression.

clinical_problem: identifying multi-omics biomarkers, including brain functional MRI features, linking gut microbiota dysbiosis to brain dysfunction in adolescent depression
model_description: Input: fecal metagenomics, serum metabolomics, resting-state fMRI functional connectivity/structure-function coupling, and spatial brain transcriptomics; output: cross-validated multi-omics machine-learning biomarker panel distinguishing adolescents with depression from controls, with imaging changes (precuneus/precentral gyrus) linked via mediation analysis.
headline_result: cross-validated multi-omics biomarker panel showed strong predictive performance for depression status; no single quantitative metric stated in the abstract

title: AI-based mid-term effectiveness prediction of bracing treatments for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
patient_population: 294 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis treated with bracing at two tertiary referral centers
clinical_problem: predicting mid-term Cobb angle response to brace treatment in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: A deep learning regression model takes baseline (pre-brace) and early post-brace standing full-spine radiographs, together with age, sex, and Risser stage, and predicts the mid-term Cobb angle for the thoracic and thoracolumbar/lumbar curves in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis treated with bracing. It was developed and cross-validated on a two-center retrospective cohort of 294 patients and externally validated, aiming to support individualized risk stratification and shared decision-making about brace management.
study_design: retrospective multicenter cohort study with external validation
dataset_size: 294 patients from two tertiary referral centers
headline_result: Cross-validation MAE 4.06° (T curve, R2=0.811) and 3.75° (TL/L curve, R2=0.746); external validation MAE 5.13° (R2=0.678) and 3.89° (R2=0.723)

title: Resolution-dependent self-supervised transfer in chest radiograph classification.
model_family: Self-supervised vision transformer pretraining (DINOv3 vs DINOv2) and supervised ImageNet initialization, with ViT-B/16 and ConvNeXt-B backbones
patient_population: pediatric and adult patients across seven chest radiograph datasets (816,183 radiographs total)
clinical_problem: chest radiograph abnormality classification
model_description: Benchmarks self-supervised vision transformer pretraining (DINOv3 versus DINOv2) against supervised ImageNet initialization for classifying findings on chest radiographs, using ViT-B/16 and ConvNeXt-B backbones fully fine-tuned at multiple resolutions across seven chest radiograph datasets spanning pediatric and adult cohorts. In adults, DINOv3 became the strongest initialization at 512x512 pixels (especially with ConvNeXt-B), with the largest gains for small, boundary-dependent findings; the pediatric cohort showed no significant benefit from DINOv3, higher resolution, or backbone choice.
study_design: retrospective multicenter benchmark study of self-supervised pretraining for chest radiograph classification
dataset_size: 816,183 radiographs from seven chest radiograph datasets (pediatric and adult cohorts)
headline_result: DINOv3 with ConvNeXt-B at 512x512 pixels was the strongest adult initialization, with the external-validation advantage preserved; the pediatric cohort showed no significant benefit from DINOv3, higher resolution, or backbone choice

title: Abdominal landmark detection and classification of fetal growth conditions on obstetric ultrasound: a gestational age-conditioned multi-task network.
model_family: Swin Transformer backbone with FiLM-based gestational-age conditioning, multi-task deep learning network
patient_population: 2,712 pregnant women (18-34 weeks gestation) across three institutions
clinical_problem: fetal growth condition classification (IUGR, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, amniotic fluid abnormalities) and abdominal landmark detection on obstetric ultrasound
model_description: GA-MTNet is a deep learning model with a Swin Transformer backbone and a gestational-age conditioning module that takes an obstetric B-mode ultrasound image plus gestational age as input, and simultaneously detects four fetal abdominal landmarks, classifies five patterns of fetal growth condition (IUGR, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, normal growth, amniotic fluid abnormalities), and performs biometric regression. It was developed on images from two centers and externally tested at a third center, with an uncertainty-guided continual-learning mechanism for post-deployment adaptation.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external validation
dataset_size: 9,046 B-mode ultrasound images from 2,712 pregnant women; 6,750 images/2,278 patients for development, 1,296 images/434 patients for external test
headline_result: Internal macro-AUC 0.863, accuracy 84.7%, landmark detection mAP@0.5 0.791; external test set AUC 0.841, accuracy 82.3% (2.2-point AUC drop)

title: Deep Learning with Attention Mechanism for Pediatric Appendicitis Detection on Plain Abdominal Radiographs.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
model_family: EfficientNet-B0 with Squeeze-and-Excitation attention (compared against ResNet50, DenseNet121, Swin-Tiny, ConvNeXt-Tiny and CBAM/Coordinate/Parallel Coordinate-Channel attention modules)
patient_population: 162 pediatric patients who underwent surgery for appendicitis and 206 control subjects
clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicitis on plain abdominal radiographs in children
model_description: A deep learning image classifier (EfficientNet-B0 with an added Squeeze-and-Excitation attention module) takes a plain abdominal radiograph, after manual cropping and unsharp-masking preprocessing, and outputs whether the image shows appendicitis. It was trained and evaluated with five-fold stratified cross-validation on radiographs from 162 children with surgically confirmed appendicitis and 206 controls, and Grad-CAM visualizations showed the model attending to the right lower quadrant and pelvic region, the anatomic site of disease.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with cross-validation
dataset_size: 162 appendicitis cases and 206 controls (plain abdominal radiographs)
headline_result: Best model (EfficientNet-B0 + SE attention) aggregated AUC 0.824 (95% CI 0.781-0.863); baseline EfficientNet-B0 AUC 0.804

title: FetalMLOps: operationalizing machine learning models for standard fetal ultrasound plane classification
journal: Medical and Biological Engineering and Computing
venue_label: Medical and Biological Engineering and Computing
model_family: MLOps framework encompassing the model development/deployment pipeline for fetal ultrasound plane classification
patient_population: fetal ultrasound imaging for prenatal care
clinical_problem: operationalizing machine learning models for fetal ultrasound standard-plane detection to support prenatal screening workflow
model_description: FetalMLOps is a ten-step MLOps framework adapting the full machine-learning lifecycle, from defining the clinical objective through data curation/annotation, ETL standardization and anonymization, model development, and deployment via a RESTful API with continuous performance monitoring, specifically for fetal ultrasound standard-plane detection. It aims to operationalize ML models for prenatal screening workflows while embedding explainability and environmental-sustainability principles.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence-Derived Pulmonary Signatures and Uterine Hemodynamics: A Novel Dual-Pathway Framework for Predicting Neonatal Respiratory Distress in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
journal: Clinical and Experimental Obstetrics and Gynecology
venue_label: Clinical and Experimental Obstetrics and Gynecology
model_family: TensorFlow-based GLCM texture feature extraction with a support vector machine (SVM) classifier
patient_population: 50 pregnant patients with gestational diabetes mellitus; standardized four-chamber-view fetal ultrasound images
clinical_problem: prediction of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) risk in gestational diabetes mellitus pregnancies from fetal lung texture
model_description: A TensorFlow-based framework extracted 342 gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features from fetal lung regions on standardized four-chamber-view ultrasound images in 50 pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes. A support vector machine classifier used these texture features, combined with uterine artery Doppler pulsatility index, to stratify risk of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
dataset_size: 50 patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (22 with NRDS, 28 controls)
headline_result: standalone AI pulmonary texture analysis: 86.4% sensitivity, 78.6% specificity for NRDS prediction (kappa=0.67); combined AI plus uterine artery PI model: 92.0% overall accuracy (46/50)

title: Performance of a Deep Learning-Based Fetal Magnetic Resonance Imaging System in the Assessment of Fetal Growth Restriction and Placental Insufficiency
journal: Clinical and Experimental Obstetrics and Gynecology
venue_label: Clinical and Experimental Obstetrics and Gynecology
model_family: deep learning MRI reconstruction algorithm (AIR Recon DL) combined with U-Net segmentation
patient_population: 120 pregnant women, gestational age 24-36 weeks, divided into FGR (n=60) and non-FGR (n=60) groups undergoing fetal MRI
clinical_problem: screening for fetal growth restriction (FGR) and placental insufficiency
model_description: Fetal MRI images were reconstructed using the commercial AIR Recon deep-learning algorithm to improve image quality. A U-Net segmentation model delineated the fetal abdomen on the reconstructed MRI to calculate estimated fetal weight (combined with ultrasound-measured femur length via the Hadlock formula), which was used to diagnose fetal growth restriction and placental insufficiency against birth weight as reference.
release_evidence: images reconstructed using the 'AIR Recon Deep Learning (DL) algorithm', a named GE scanner reconstruction product; femur length measured on a GE Voluson E10 system
dataset_size: 120 pregnant women (60 FGR, 60 non-FGR), gestational age 24-36 weeks
headline_result: Dice coefficient for segmentation 0.892 +/- 0.021, EFW mean absolute error 148.2 g, FGR diagnostic accuracy 91.7% (AUROC 0.938) vs manual assessment 84.5% (AUROC 0.864, p=0.032)

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Improving the Accuracy of Fetal Ultrasound
journal: Iranian Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Infertility
venue_label: Iranian Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology and Infertility
patient_population: second-trimester pregnancies; dataset of 1,200 labeled fetal ultrasound images
clinical_problem: detection of fetal structural and functional anomalies (cardiac and cerebral) on second-trimester ultrasound
model_description: A convolutional-neural-network-based deep learning model was developed to automatically analyze second-trimester fetal ultrasound images (1,200 labeled images) for detection of structural and functional anomalies. Its performance was compared against traditional manual interpretation and clinical expert assessment for detecting fetal cardiac and cerebral anomalies.
dataset_size: 1,200 labeled fetal ultrasound images, second trimester
