headline_result: improved diagnostic accuracy by up to 25% compared to conventional methods; over 93% accuracy detecting fetal cardiac and cerebral anomalies

title: LU-NET: A REPRODUCIBLE LAPLACIAN-UNCERTAINTY FRAMEWORK FOR FETAL HEAD ULTRASOUND SEGMENTATION
model_family: compact U-Net with dual uncertainty heads (Laplacian-uncertainty framework)
patient_population: fetal ultrasound images from the HC18 public benchmark dataset
clinical_problem: fetal head biometry / segmentation for obstetric assessment
model_description: A compact U-Net with two uncertainty-estimation heads segments the fetal head from 2D ultrasound images (HC18 benchmark), producing both an anatomical mask and pixel-wise confidence maps that flag anatomically ambiguous or out-of-distribution frames. The framework standardizes dataset preparation and evaluation for reproducible fetal head segmentation.
headline_result: Mean Dice 0.9716, mean IoU 0.9454 on test set

title: Multimodal AI for Automated Staging of Neuroblastoma and Paediatric Sarcomas Using MRI, CT, and Reports
model_family: multimodal pipeline: U-Net (MRI segmentation), YOLOv8 (CT lesion detection), RuBERT NLP module (report text extraction)
body_region: abdomen/pelvis and whole body (tumor sites for neuroblastoma and sarcomas, including lung metastases)
patient_population: 84 pediatric patients aged 6 months to 17 years with neuroblastoma (n=50) or sarcomas (n=34), single-center retrospective cohort
clinical_problem: automated staging of neuroblastoma and pediatric sarcomas by integrating tumor segmentation, metastasis detection, and radiology report information
task: segmentation; detection / diagnosis; report generation / LLM
model_description: A multimodal AI system for automated cancer staging combines three deep learning modules: a U-Net for tumor segmentation on MRI, a YOLOv8-based detector for metastatic lung lesions on CT, and a RuBERT natural-language-processing module that extracts staging information from Russian-language radiology reports. The combined outputs feed a classifier that assigns overall tumor stage, benchmarked against multidisciplinary tumor board decisions in 84 children (6 months to 17 years) with neuroblastoma or sarcoma.
dataset_size: 84 patients (50 neuroblastoma, 34 sarcomas), aged 6 months to 17 years
headline_result: segmentation Dice 0.79 (neuroblastoma), 0.81 (sarcomas); metastasis detector sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.85 for lung nodules; overall staging accuracy 92.8% (78/84); pipeline took 8 minutes/patient vs ~45 minutes manual; surgeons agreed with AI-generated 3D tumor models in 92% of cases

title: Machine Learning Models Based on Clinical–Radiological and Radiomics Features for Preoperative Prediction of Locoregional Staging in Pediatric Wilms Tumor
model_family: logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine on radiomics and clinical features
patient_population: 95 children with pathology-confirmed Wilms tumor (training cohort n=66, test cohort n=29)
clinical_problem: preoperative locoregional staging of Wilms tumor
model_description: Preoperative portal-venous-phase abdominal CT images from children with Wilms tumor are used to extract radiomics features, combined with clinical/radiological predictors (tumor morphology). Logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine models are trained to preoperatively classify tumors as stage I versus stage II-III to help guide surgical and treatment planning.
headline_result: Random forest best model: test-cohort AUC 0.737, F1 score 0.615, accuracy 65.5%

title: Machine Learning-Based Early Prediction of Selective Fetal Growth Restriction in Monochorionic Diamniotic Twins Using Crown–Rump Length Discordance and Abnormal Placental Cord Insertion
journal: Clinical and Experimental Obstetrics and Gynecology
venue_label: Clinical and Experimental Obstetrics and Gynecology
patient_population: 144 monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twin pregnancies (January 2015-December 2024), 44 (30.56%) developed selective fetal growth restriction
clinical_problem: early prediction of selective fetal growth restriction in monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies
model_description: First-trimester ultrasound measurements of crown-rump length discordance between twins and placental abnormal cord insertion were used as predictors in 8 supervised machine learning models, trained on 70% and validated on an independent 30% of MCDA twin pregnancies, to predict which pregnancies will develop selective fetal growth restriction.
headline_result: In the validation set, crown-rump length discordance AUC 0.687 (95% CI 0.4849-0.8881); placental abnormal cord insertion showed limited discrimination; overall discrimination was moderate

title: Self-Supervised Multi-Organ Segmentation in Pediatric Abdominal CT Based on Vision Foundation Models
journal: Medical Journal of Peking Union Medical College Hospital
venue_label: Medical Journal of Peking Union Medical College Hospital
model_family: Self-supervised vision foundation model (DINOv3-based) with Gram-anchoring domain adaptation, multi-scale feature aggregation and a lightweight Primus decoder
patient_population: pediatric abdominal CT (867 cases used for pretraining; evaluated on the public Pediatric-CT-SEG dataset, 359 cases)
clinical_problem: multi-organ segmentation on pediatric abdominal CT, addressing scarce pediatric annotation and poor generalization of adult-trained models
model_description: A general radiological visual representation was pretrained on a large adult CT dataset, then adapted to unlabeled pediatric CT using a frozen adult model as a structural teacher (Gram-anchoring) to align local anatomical topology. A multi-scale feature aggregation strategy and lightweight decoder were added for downstream multi-organ segmentation, evaluated on a public pediatric abdominal CT dataset and compared against nnU-Net.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 867 abdominal CT cases (367,588 slices) for pretraining; 359 cases (Pediatric-CT-SEG) for evaluation
headline_result: Mean Dice similarity coefficient 71.38±1.08% and mean IoU 63.73±1.01% on Pediatric-CT-SEG, improvements of 3.22% and 3.59% over baseline nnU-Net (P<0.05), with larger gains for small organs (duodenum +5.78%, pancreas +4.69%)

title: Predictive performance of supervised machine learning models for temporomandibular joint disc displacement in adolescents diagnosed by magnetic resonance imaging
model_family: Supervised machine learning classifiers (MLPClassifier, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, CatBoost, and other models; 15 total)
patient_population: 260 TMJs from 130 adolescent patients aged 12-18 years undergoing MRI for suspected TMJ disc displacement
clinical_problem: temporomandibular joint disc displacement diagnosis
model_description: Morphological measurements (condylar shape, anteroposterior and mediolateral diameters, condylar ratio) and signal-intensity ratios of the lateral pterygoid muscle were extracted from MRI of the temporomandibular joint. Fifteen supervised machine learning models were trained on these features, with patient-level data splitting to avoid leakage, to classify disc status as normal or displaced. The best model (MLPClassifier) is intended as a decision-support tool for diagnosing TMJ disc displacement in adolescents.
headline_result: MLPClassifier achieved the highest ROC-AUC (0.797), followed by Random Forest (0.777) and HistGradientBoosting (0.773); CatBoost had the highest recall (0.839)

title: SSL-OHE: A self-supervised ensemble approach for early diagnosis of biliary atresia from sonographic images
model_family: self-supervised representation learning combined with an optimized heterogeneous ensemble of lightweight base learners
patient_population: infants/children evaluated for biliary atresia by sonographic gallbladder imaging
clinical_problem: early diagnosis of biliary atresia from sonographic gallbladder images
model_description: SSL-OHE combines self-supervised representation learning (online clustering-based pretraining initialized from a large general vision dataset) with a heterogeneous ensemble of lightweight base learners, fine-tuned to classify biliary atresia from sonographic gallbladder images. A numerical optimization step determines ensemble weights across base learners to improve diagnostic performance despite the rarity and imbalance of biliary atresia data.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

title: AC_Branch_MobileNet: An effective hybrid branch network for plane classification in fetus brain ultrasound image
model_family: hybrid-branch convolutional neural network (MobileNetV2 backbone with an attention module)
patient_population: public fetal ultrasound dataset used for prenatal screening
clinical_problem: classification of standard fetal brain ultrasound planes for prenatal screening
model_description: AC_Branch_MobileNet is a lightweight convolutional neural network that automatically classifies fetal ultrasound images into three standard fetal brain planes (trans-ventricular, trans-cerebellar, trans-thalamic) to support prenatal screening. It uses a MobileNetV2 backbone with an added attention-based branch structure, preceded by an unsharp-masking preprocessing step to reduce speckle noise, and was evaluated on a public fetal ultrasound dataset.
study_design: retrospective technical development / classification benchmark study
dataset_size: public fetal ultrasound dataset (exact count not stated)
headline_result: accuracy 95.11%, precision 94.62%, recall 94.39%, F1-score 94.50%, outperforming the best baseline by up to 7.43% in accuracy

title: PedVision: A manual-annotation-free and age scalable segmentation pipeline for bone analysis in hand X-ray images
model_family: segmentation pipeline combining an ROI detection network, a foundation model for instance generation, and an instance classifier network, trained with semi-automated annotation and curriculum learning
patient_population: 552 hand X-ray images of children from the public RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas (DHA) datasets, diverse ages and racial backgrounds
clinical_problem: bone segmentation on pediatric hand radiographs to support bone analysis across a wide age range
model_description: PedVision is a segmentation pipeline for pediatric hand X-rays designed to scale across ages without manual annotation. It uses a region-of-interest network to localize relevant areas, a foundation model to generate instance-level predictions, and an instance classifier network to map instances to 19 hand bones grouped into 5 classes, trained via a semi-automated annotation framework and curriculum learning across rounds of increasing model complexity. It was evaluated on 552 hand X-rays from the public RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas datasets against U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer baselines.
release_evidence: "The project is open source at github.com/mohofar/PedVision"
study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study
dataset_size: 552 hand X-ray images of children (RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas datasets)
headline_result: for pediatric cases (0-7 years): 11.08% Dice improvement over U-Net on RSNA and 7.68% on DHA; 14.43%/14.78% improvement over DeepLabV3+; 8.16%/1.91% improvement over the best SegFormer variant

title: A convolutional neural networks with spatial configuration and attention mechanism for Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age assessment
model_family: convolutional neural network with heat-map regression key-point detection and spatial/channel attention
body_region: hand and wrist (radius, ulna, carpal bones)
patient_population: children and infants undergoing hand radiography for skeletal maturity assessment
clinical_problem: Tanner-Whitehouse 3 (TW3) bone age assessment including carpal-bone scoring, for diagnosis of skeletal growth abnormalities
model_description: A two-stage deep learning pipeline first uses a heat-map regression key-point detection network with spatial configuration to locate and segment all 20 TW3 regions of interest on a hand radiograph, then a skeletal-maturity classification network with spatial and channel attention predicts maturity scores and bone age for both the radius-ulna-short-bone (TW3-RUS) and carpal bone (TW3-C) series, extending prior automated methods that could only assess TW3-RUS.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 5,235 left hand radiographs of children of different ages
headline_result: mean absolute error of bone age 0.42 years (TW3-RUS) and 0.44 years (TW3-C)

title: A dual encoder–decoder multi-task 3D deep learning framework for the segmentation of focal cortical dysplasia lesions
model_family: 3D multi-view dual encoder-decoder CNN with attention mechanism
patient_population: patients with intractable epilepsy due to focal cortical dysplasia, adults and children
clinical_problem: segmentation of focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) lesions for pre-surgical epilepsy evaluation
model_description: A 3D deep learning model with a multi-view dual encoder-decoder architecture and residual connections segments focal cortical dysplasia lesions on brain MRI. It processes FLAIR MRI volumes together with corresponding cortical thickness maps through two encoders linked by a 3D attention mechanism, and two decoders for dual-task learning using ground-truth-derived distance maps, intended to assist neuroradiologists in presurgical evaluation of epilepsy patients including both children and adults.
study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 4.8% and 2.3% higher than state-of-the-art 2D and 3D FCD segmentation methods, respectively

title: Enhanced pediatric age estimation from head MRI via self-distillation hybrid-attention network
model_family: self-distillation hybrid-attention network (ResNet50 backbone with Squeeze-and-Excitation and Spatial Transformer attention modules)
patient_population: children undergoing 3-Tesla head MRI
clinical_problem: automatic age estimation from head MRI in children, as a radiation-free alternative to radiographic age estimation
model_description: SDHA is a self-distillation network with Squeeze-and-Excitation and Spatial Transformer attention modules built on a ResNet50 backbone (teacher) with early-exit student branches, trained on 3T head MRI to estimate a child's age without ionizing radiation. Grad-CAM visualization showed the model attends to age-relevant dental, facial, and brain structures. It was compared against manual assessment and conventional CNN methods.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: SDHA mean absolute error 0.34 years vs manual method 0.44 years; 63.4% MAE reduction vs a non-distilled SENet (MAE 0.93 years); prediction time reduced from 120 s (manual) to 0.11 s per subject

title: SCANet: automated Cobb angle measurement using deep learning model in X-ray images for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
model_family: deep learning pipeline: GAN-based data augmentation, hybrid U-Net segmentation (UDANet) with dilated convolution and decoder attention, IpLU activation
patient_population: adolescents/children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing spine X-ray, including presurgical severe cases
clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) severity grading
model_description: SCANet is an end-to-end pipeline for Cobb angle measurement from spine X-rays in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. It augments training images with geometric transformations and a generative adversarial network, segments the vertebral region with a hybrid U-Net (UDANet) that incorporates dilated convolutions and a decoder attention module, derives a vertebral compression ratio from the segmentation, and computes the Cobb angle from these segmentation coordinates.
study_design: retrospective technical development / measurement accuracy study
headline_result: 98.65% accuracy in Cobb angle measurement, 2.06% and 4.16% higher than DNN and CNN comparators respectively

title: Lightweight G-YOLOv11: Advancing efficient fracture detection in pediatric wrist X-rays
model_family: ghost convolution-based YOLOv11 lightweight object detector
patient_population: children undergoing wrist radiography (GRAZPEDWRI-DX public dataset)
clinical_problem: fracture detection on pediatric wrist radiographs
model_description: G-YOLOv11 is a lightweight computer-aided detection system for fractures on pediatric wrist X-rays, built on the YOLOv11 object detector with ghost convolution layers that generate the same feature maps as standard convolution with fewer computations. It was evaluated on the public GRAZPEDWRI-DX pediatric wrist radiograph dataset against the standard YOLOv11l model.
release_evidence: Code and models are available at https://github.com/AbdesselamFerdi/G-YOLOv11
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: GRAZPEDWRI-DX public pediatric wrist radiograph dataset
headline_result: mAP@0.5 of 0.535, inference time 2.4 ms; 13.6% lower mAP@0.5 than standard YOLOv11l with a 68.7% reduction in model size

title: FHSS-Net: A novel instance segmentation network for multi-class fetal heart structures via global context and multi-scale learning
model_family: instance segmentation network with a lightweight Vision Transformer (EfficientViT), dilated convolutions, and E-Focal Loss
patient_population: fetuses undergoing standard fetal heart ultrasound views (newly constructed FH-3K dataset)
clinical_problem: segmentation of fetal heart anatomical structures for congenital heart disease (CHD) screening and prenatal diagnosis
model_description: FHSS-Net is a deep learning instance segmentation model for fetal heart ultrasound images. It combines a lightweight Vision Transformer module (EfficientViT) for long-range feature modeling, dilated convolutions for a wider receptive field, and an E-Focal Loss to address class imbalance, segmenting ten key anatomical structures across five standard fetal heart views. It was developed and benchmarked on the newly constructed FH-3K fetal heart ultrasound dataset.
study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study
dataset_size: FH-3K dataset: five standard fetal heart views, ten annotated anatomical structures
headline_result: 93.7% localization accuracy and 92% segmentation accuracy across ten anatomical structures under five-fold cross-validation, outperforming mainstream models

title: FCNSU-NET: Comprehensive recognition of the first trimester fetal CNS ultrasound standard planes and anatomical structures with linear transformer attention
model_family: YOLO-based detection with linear transformer attention (Agent Attention, SEn-CBAM, CGRFPN) and Swin Transformer classification with GRU
patient_population: 3425 expert-annotated first-trimester fetal CNS ultrasound images (2440 training, 612 test, 373 independent clinical validation)
clinical_problem: first-trimester fetal CNS standard plane and anatomical structure recognition for prenatal screening
model_description: A deep-learning framework (FCNSU-NET) combines a YOLO-based object detector with attention modules to localize fetal CNS anatomical structures on first-trimester ultrasound images, then encodes detected structures and fuses them with a Swin Transformer image classifier to recognize standard imaging planes. It is intended to support earlier, more consistent detection of fetal brain abnormalities on first-trimester ultrasound.
study_design: retrospective technical development with clinical validation
headline_result: mAP@0.5 95.3%, standard-plane classification accuracy 98.53%; on clinical validation set outperformed junior/intermediate physicians and matched senior experts (Kappa 0.90)

title: Fetal brain anomaly identification from ultrasound images using multiclass classifiers
model_family: GLCM texture features with LDA, SVM, and shallow neural network classifiers
patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound images from an open-access dataset covering four anomaly types plus normal
clinical_problem: fetal brain anomaly classification (arachnoid cyst, Arnold-Chiari malformation, cerebellar hypoplasia, colpocephaly)
model_description: Gray-level co-occurrence matrix texture features are extracted from fetal brain ultrasound images and used to train multiclass classifiers (linear discriminant analysis, support vector machines, and shallow neural networks) to distinguish normal fetal brain from four specific anomalies: arachnoid cyst, Arnold-Chiari malformation, cerebellar hypoplasia, and colpocephaly.
headline_result: LDA best classifier: 100% accuracy for normal, arachnoid cyst, and cerebellar hypoplasia; 89% for Arnold-Chiari malformation; 93% for colpocephaly

title: Automatic Detection of Pediatric Craniofacial Fractures in Computed Tomography Using a 2.5D Deep Learning Model and Grad-CAM
model_family: 2.5D deep learning model (ResNet-18 with transfer learning on multiplanar CT reconstructions)
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing CT for craniofacial trauma
clinical_problem: detection of craniofacial fractures
model_description: Axial, coronal and sagittal CT reconstructions are stacked as a three-channel input to a ResNet-18 convolutional network with transfer learning to flag pediatric craniofacial fractures. The pipeline includes isotropic resampling, bone-window normalization and 384x384 image generation; Grad-CAM highlights the regions driving each prediction, which an independent clinical review confirmed corresponded to fracture-related structures.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: AUC 0.822, AUPRC 0.855; at optimal threshold (t=0.54): sensitivity 0.556, specificity 1.000, F1-score 0.714

title: Automated right ventricular assessment in pediatric echocardiography via deep learning improves measurement reliability and reduces variability
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing echocardiography (664 pediatric echocardiograms)
clinical_problem: right ventricular functional assessment (fractional area change) in pediatric echocardiography
model_description: Multiple deep learning segmentation models were trained on 664 pediatric echocardiograms to automatically delineate the right ventricle and calculate right ventricular fractional area change (RVFAC), a measure of RV function. The best-performing model (FCBFormer architecture) was compared against ground-truth and four expert readers in a blinded evaluation to assess whether it reduces inter-observer variability in RV assessment.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.926, mean absolute error 5.913% for RVFAC prediction; model-generated segmentation favored over human segmentation in 57.3% of evaluated cases

title: AXNet: Attention-enhanced X-ray network for pneumonia detection
model_family: Lightweight attention-augmented CNN (ResNet-18 backbone with CBAM and Efficient Channel Attention modules)
patient_population: 5,863 pediatric chest X-ray images from the public Kaggle pneumonia dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection on pediatric chest X-ray, for use in low-resource settings with limited radiologist access
model_description: AXNet+ECA embeds Convolutional Block Attention Module blocks within each stage of a ResNet-18 backbone and appends an Efficient Channel Attention head for fine-grained calibration, to classify pediatric chest X-rays for pneumonia while remaining lightweight and interpretable. Grad-CAM was used to check whether the model attended to radiologist-annotated abnormal regions.
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: Test accuracy 93.6%, F1-score 93.1%, AUC 0.964, using only 13.1M parameters and 4.7ms/image inference time; Grad-CAM showed 86.7% alignment with radiologist-annotated abnormalities

title: Expertise-Dependent Verification Behaviors in Response to AI Reliability in Neonatal Pneumoperitoneum: A Multi-Reader Multi-Center Study
model_family: AI decision-support model (architecture not specified) for pneumoperitoneum detection
patient_population: 14 readers (pediatric radiologists, neonatologists, radiology residents) interpreting 125 neonatal radiographs
clinical_problem: detection of pneumoperitoneum (free air) on neonatal radiographs, a time-critical surgical emergency
model_description: This multi-reader multi-center study evaluated how AI assistance for detecting pneumoperitoneum on neonatal radiographs affects clinician verification behavior. Fourteen readers of varying specialty and seniority (pediatric radiologists, neonatologists, radiology residents) interpreted 125 neonatal radiographs across two sessions, under three conditions: unaided, aided by a reliable AI, and aided by an error-injected (unreliable) AI, with outcomes including diagnostic accuracy, deliberation time, and automation bias.
headline_result: neonatologists overrode 91.6% of AI errors under error-injected AI (OR 4.16 vs unaided baseline, p=0.020); radiology residents accepted incorrect advice from reliable AI in 52.0% of discordant cases vs 20.0% for pediatric radiologists (p=0.016)

title: External validation of self-supervised transfer learning for noninvasive molecular subtyping of pediatric low-grade glioma using T2-weighted MRI
model_family: self-supervised transfer learning binary classification models
patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade glioma (pLGG); external validation cohorts from the Hospital for Sick Children (n=336, 2000-2018; and n=87, 2019-2023)
clinical_problem: noninvasive molecular subtyping of pediatric low-grade glioma (BRAF Fusion vs BRAF Mutation vs Wild Type) from MRI
model_description: Three binary self-supervised transfer-learning classification models, pretrained on data from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute/Boston Children's Hospital, were externally evaluated on T2-weighted MRI from two independent cohorts at the Hospital for Sick Children to classify the molecular subtype of pediatric low-grade glioma (BRAF Fusion, BRAF Mutation, or Wild Type). Manually annotated tumor segmentations were used as input, and per-class probabilities from the three models were combined via a softmax function to compute a multi-class AUC.
study_design: retrospective external validation diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: macro-average AUC 0.7671 on the newer dataset, 0.6463 on the older dataset

title: Deep learning-based multimodal fusion of imaging, pathology, and CTCs for early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma
model_family: Multimodal deep learning fusion (VGG16/ResNet50 transfer learning for imaging and pathology, SVM/Hough transform for circulating tumor cell classification)
patient_population: pediatric patients with distal femur osteosarcoma, using public imaging and genomic datasets (TCIA, TCGA, GEO)
clinical_problem: early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma
model_description: MRI, CT, histopathology slides and circulating tumor cell (CTC) data are each processed by modality-specific pipelines (CNN transfer learning for imaging and pathology, flow cytometry and machine learning for CTCs) and fused into a single multimodal deep learning model for early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma, particularly to aid metastasis assessment when imaging alone is inconclusive.
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: Accuracy 92.5%, sensitivity 88.7%, specificity 94.3%, AUC 0.96 on an independent test set; adding CTC data notably improved performance for metastasis assessment when imaging was inconclusive

title: Multi-parametric MRI-based radiomics to differentiate medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children
model_family: Radiomics with LASSO feature selection, combined with MRI findings (Rad-score based classification model)
patient_population: children with posterior fossa brain tumors: 113 medulloblastoma and 31 ependymoma patients
clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children
model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from ADC, T2-weighted and DCE-T1-weighted MRI sequences of children with posterior fossa tumors. LASSO regression selected features to build a radiomics score, which was combined with radiologist MRI findings into a nomogram to distinguish medulloblastoma from ependymoma. Diagnostic performance was compared against radiologists using the DeLong test.
headline_result: Combined sequence radiomics model AUC 0.981 (primary cohort) and 0.939 (validation cohort), outperforming radiologists and single-sequence models

title: A transfer learning − based DeepLabV3–UNet3+ hybrid model for automated fetal head circumference measurement
model_family: Hybrid deep learning model combining a ResNet-50-based DeepLabV3 network with a UNet3+ architecture (transfer learning)
patient_population: fetal head ultrasound images (public HC18 dataset)
clinical_problem: automated fetal head circumference measurement for monitoring fetal development
model_description: A hybrid DeepLabV3-UNet3+ deep learning model, assisted by transfer learning, segments the fetal head from an ultrasound image; an ellipse is then fitted to the segmentation to compute head circumference automatically, aiming to replace expert-dependent, inconsistent manual measurement.
headline_result: 97.83% Dice similarity coefficient, 0.67±2.62mm difference, 1.96±1.86mm absolute difference, 1.30±0.79mm Hausdorff distance on the HC18 dataset, achieved without data augmentation and with ~20 minutes training time

title: Artificial Intelligence methods for ultra-low- field MRI enhancement comparing brain volumes and neurodevelopment scores for small vs appropriate for gestational age children
model_family: pre-trained deep learning super-resolution model (GAMBAS) for ultra-low-field MRI
patient_population: 64 children aged 3-5 years (from a birth cohort of 180 children: 90 small-for-gestational-age, 90 appropriate-for-gestational-age), scanned with a portable 64mT ultra-low-field MRI system
clinical_problem: brain volume assessment and neurodevelopmental correlation using portable ultra-low-field MRI in small-for-gestational-age vs appropriate-for-gestational-age children
model_description: The pre-trained GAMBAS deep learning model generated super-resolved images from ultra-low-field (64mT, Hyperfine Swoop) brain MRI scans of children. Brain volumes derived from the super-resolved images were compared against high-field MRI in a subset for validation, and correlated with neurodevelopmental scores (Malawi Developmental Assessment Tool) to compare small-for-gestational-age and appropriate-for-gestational-age children.
dataset_size: 64 children aged 3-5 years from a cohort of 180 (90 SGA, 90 AGA); ground-truth comparison subset n=10
headline_result: strong correlation and high concordance between super-resolved and high-field brain volumes for total intracranial volume, white matter, cerebral cortex, basal ganglia and thalamus; correlation between super-resolved volumes and neurodevelopmental (MDAT) z-scores was not statistically significant

title: A self-supervised representation-transfer multimodal learning for automated diagnosis of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip
model_family: Self-supervised representation-transfer framework (BYOL pretraining) with a multi-scale attention module and a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network classifier
patient_population: pediatric pelvic X-ray dataset spanning patients aged 6 months to 16 years
clinical_problem: automated diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip
model_description: A large set of unlabeled pelvic X-rays is used to pretrain global feature representations with self-supervised (BYOL) learning; these are transferred into a detector and fine-tuned on a small labeled subset, reducing the need for large-scale annotation. An attention module highlights key anatomical structures, patient age and gender are embedded into the image features, and extracted anatomical indices are fed into a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network to classify developmental dysplasia of the hip severity.

title: Intersecting effects of social circumstances and transcendent thinking on mid-adolescents’ longitudinal functional connectome development
model_family: graph theory network analysis combined with machine learning on functional brain network features
patient_population: mid-adolescents from low-socioeconomic-status contexts, longitudinal 2-year fMRI cohort (n=65)
clinical_problem: identifying social and psychological predictors of longitudinal functional brain network development in mid-adolescence
model_description: Graph theory measures were computed from a 2-year longitudinal resting-state fMRI dataset of 65 mid-adolescents. Machine learning analysis was used to identify which factors, among parental education, community violence exposure, IQ, and a measured psychological disposition ('transcendent thinking'), best predicted changes in functional brain network organization (segregation, integration, entropy, energy) over the study period.
headline_result: machine learning identified transcendent thinking and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as the principal predictors of functional brain network change across groups

title: Distal Radial Epiphyseal Fusion Timing in Northwest Europeans and Middle Eastern Asylum Seekers: An Automated Ultrasound and Machine Learning Approach
patient_population: Northwest European and Middle Eastern individuals aged 13-25 years, including asylum seekers, assessed at German clinical sites and reception facilities
clinical_problem: forensic age assessment via distal radial epiphyseal fusion timing (medico-legal age-of-majority determination)
model_description: A fully automated ultrasound device assesses distal radial epiphyseal fusion status. Gradient-boosting machine learning models (LightGBM) were trained on 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets to classify fusion status against reference ages (documented birthdate or Greulich-Pyle bone age), evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation across sex- and population-specific age thresholds, for forensic determination of whether an individual has reached a legally relevant age threshold.
dataset_size: 1,061 recordings; 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets analyzed, ages 13-25 years
headline_result: AUC approximately 0.81-1.00 near optimal thresholds; optimal discrimination thresholds ranged 17.0-18.5 years across sex/population groups

title: Structure-aware fine-grained instance segmentation for fetal brain ultrasound images
model_family: instance segmentation framework with structure-aware overlap metric, Laplacian regularization, and Stable Diffusion/LoRA augmentation
patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound images across five standard planes
clinical_problem: fetal brain anatomical structure segmentation
model_description: A structure-aware instance segmentation framework detects and segments 25 anatomical structures across five standard fetal brain ultrasound planes. It uses a structure-aware overlap metric and improved non-maximum suppression to better detect small structures, a fine-grained segmentation head, Laplacian-based spatial regularization for boundary consistency, and a diffusion-model-based data augmentation strategy to synthesize additional training images.

title: Image Quality Evaluation of Neonatal Brain MRI Using a Deep Learning Reconstruction Algorithm: A Quantitative and Multireader Study Using Variable Denoising Levels at 3 Tesla
patient_population: 15 neonates undergoing 3D T1-weighted brain MRI at 3 Tesla
clinical_problem: image quality improvement for neonatal brain MRI to support assessment of early myelinating structures
model_description: A deep learning image reconstruction algorithm was applied at low, medium and high denoising levels to 3D T1-weighted brain MRI scans of 15 neonates. Three radiologists rated image quality (signal-to-noise, artifacts, clarity) of eight early myelinating brain structures on a 4-point scale, and objective signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratios were measured across denoising levels.
study_design: prospective single-center image quality evaluation, multireader study
headline_result: overall increase in all image-quality categories and conspicuity of early myelinating structures with increasing denoising; significant increases in apparent SNR and CNR for nearly all pairwise comparisons

title: High-Sensitivity Radiation-Free Triage for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis via 3D Point Cloud Geometry
model_family: 3D point cloud geometric processing pipeline (segmentation plus classification)
patient_population: adolescents screened for scoliosis, multi-center validation cohort
clinical_problem: radiation-free triage screening for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)
model_description: PointScol is a radiation-free triage system that processes 3D point clouds of the back surface, obtained by optical/depth scanning rather than X-ray, to screen for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. It first segments the dorsal region of interest, then classifies spinal deformity, acting as a binary screening gate at a 10-degree Cobb angle threshold and as a 5-class severity grading tool to guide referral urgency. It was validated on a multi-center dataset.
study_design: technical development / multi-center diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: 100.00% sensitivity in the external cohort for the primary screening task (10-degree Cobb angle threshold)

title: Protocol for a prospective accuracy study on an artificial intelligence-based ultrasound system for gestational age estimation among pregnant women in Ghana, Kenya and South Africa
model_family: AI algorithm for gestational age estimation from handheld blind-sweep ultrasound (commercial product)
patient_population: 969 pregnant women at 13 health facilities across Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, presenting 11+0 to 13+6 weeks' gestation with follow-up to 27+6 weeks
clinical_problem: gestational age estimation for antenatal care and pre-eclampsia risk screening in low-resource settings
model_description: This study protocol describes a prospective multi-country accuracy study of the commercial Intelligent Ultrasound ScanNav FetalCheck AI system, which estimates gestational age from handheld blind-sweep ultrasound scans performed by a trained midwife using a GE VScan Air device. Its accuracy will be compared against conventional fetal biometry (crown-rump length) performed by a trained sonographer as the reference standard, in 969 women across 13 facilities in Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa.
release_evidence: "the AI-based Intelligent Ultrasound ScanNav FetalCheck system (experimental)"
dataset_size: 969 pregnant women, 13 health facilities in 3 countries

title: Automated Segmentation of Post-Surgical Resection Cavities on MRI in Focal Epilepsy: a MELD Study
patient_population: children and adults who underwent epilepsy surgery, from the multicentre MELD project (27 centres) and the EPISURG dataset, with a range of resection locations and pathologies
clinical_problem: automated segmentation of the postoperative resection cavity after epilepsy surgery to quantify extent of tissue resection
model_description: MELD-PostOp is a deep learning tool built on nnU-Net that automatically segments the surgical resection cavity on postoperative 3D T1-weighted brain MRI following epilepsy surgery. It was trained on 965 manually and semi-automatically segmented cases from 27 centres (children and adults, temporal and extra-temporal resections) and evaluated on stratified and independent held-out test cohorts against existing tools (Epic-CHOP, ResectVol).
release_evidence: "This open-source tool facilitates large-scale quantitative analysis"
study_design: retrospective multi-center technical development / segmentation validation study
dataset_size: 965 subjects for training across 27 centres; stratified test cohort n=50; independent test cohort n=87
headline_result: median Dice similarity coefficient 0.85 and HD95 3.61 on the combined test cohort, outperforming Epic-CHOP (DSC 0.68) and ResectVol (DSC 0.66); detected 99% (135/137) of resection cavities

title: Parameter-Efficient Heterogeneous Ensemble with Analytic Geometry for Automated Fetal Head Descent Assessment
model_family: heterogeneous ensemble of a MedSAM-based vision transformer with low-rank adaptation and a self-configuring nnU-Net v2, fused via probability averaging
patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing transperineal ultrasound during labor for fetal head descent assessment
clinical_problem: automated angle of progression (AOP) measurement for intrapartum fetal head descent assessment
model_description: A dual-model ensemble combines a MedSAM-based vision transformer with low-rank adaptation and a self-configuring nnU-Net v2 to segment relevant structures on transperineal ultrasound images. The segmentation is used to compute the angle of progression (AOP), a measure of fetal head descent during labor, via closed-form tangent-line geometry on fitted ellipses. The model was trained on 4,000 images and evaluated on an independent set of 1,101 images.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 4,000 training images; independent validation set of 1,101 images (858 limited descent, 243 advanced descent)
headline_result: F1 0.865 (95% CI 0.831-0.896), AUC 0.960 (0.947-0.971), sensitivity 86.8%, specificity 96.0%; mean absolute AOP error 5.93 degrees (median 4.10)

title: Early Neurosurgical Intervention In Congenital Hydrocephalus: Predictive Biomarkers, Imaging Trends, And The Transformative Role Of Artificial Intelligence
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
venue_label: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
model_family: 3D U-Net and attention-based CNNs for ventricular segmentation; SVM, random forest, XGBoost and RNN/LSTM for prediction
patient_population: children with congenital hydrocephalus, with MRI, CT and CSF biomarker data
clinical_problem: predicting timing of neurosurgery and prognosis in congenital hydrocephalus
model_description: MRI and CT images from children with congenital hydrocephalus were segmented with 3D U-Net and attention-based CNN architectures to automate ventricular measurement. Clinical and CSF biomarker features (after KNN imputation and PCA) were combined with the imaging findings and fed into machine learning (SVM, random forest, XGBoost) and deep learning (RNN, LSTM) models to stratify risk, predict disease progression and evaluate surgical outcomes; explainable AI identified ventricular enlargement, CSF dynamics and periventricular changes as the top predictive features.
headline_result: test accuracy exceeding 95% with high precision, recall and F1-scores; XGBoost outperformed traditional classifiers, LSTM best predicted longitudinal progression

title: A Temporal Pole-Centered Neural Circuit Predicts Social Cognition in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
patient_population: 69 children (34 with autism spectrum disorder, 35 typically developing)
clinical_problem: classification of autism spectrum disorder and prediction of social cognitive ability from brain functional connectivity
model_description: The NBS-Predict machine-learning framework was applied to resting-state fMRI functional connectivity data from 69 children to build a classifier distinguishing autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from typically developing children, and a regression model predicting each child's Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2) social cognition score from the same connectivity patterns.
headline_result: FC-based classifier distinguished ASD from typically developing children with 62.8% accuracy; regression model predicted individual SRS-2 scores (r = 0.252, p < 0.001)

title: Artificial Intelligence for Facial Analysis: Exploring Fetal Neuromuscular Development by Correlating Facial Muscle Activity and Emotion Variability with Kurjak Antenatal Neurodevelopmental Test Scores from 28 to 36 Weeks of Pregnancy
journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
venue_label: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
patient_population: 30 normal singleton pregnancies, 28-36 weeks of gestation
clinical_problem: fetal neuromuscular / neurodevelopmental assessment via facial movement analysis
model_description: 4D ultrasound recordings of fetal facial movement (blinking, mouth movements, grimace duration) are planned to be analyzed with the VISAGE|SDK AI tool, which estimates emotional states and their variability, and correlated with Kurjak Antenatal Neurodevelopmental Test (KANET) scores to assess whether facial movement patterns reflect fetal neuromuscular development. This is a prospective study protocol; the abstract reports anticipated, not actual, results.
study_design: prospective observational study protocol (results not yet reported)
dataset_size: 30 pregnancies, two 4D ultrasound sessions each between 28 and 36 weeks gestation

title: FCUFormer: A multi-view informed vision-language foundation model for interpreting fetal cardiac ultrasound abnormalities
model_family: Vision-language foundation model (Multi-view informed Multiple Instance Learning module and Multi-Level Vision-Language Alignment module), with an LLM-driven report standardization pipeline
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal cardiac ultrasound screening (5,495 real-world fetal cardiac ultrasound records)
clinical_problem: interpretation of fetal cardiac ultrasound for prenatal screening of congenital heart defects
model_description: An LLM-driven pipeline standardizes free-text fetal cardiac ultrasound reports and multi-view images into structured training data without large-scale manual annotation. A cross-modal foundation model (FCUFormer) is then pretrained on this data, learning cross-view anatomical dependencies and fine-grained alignment between image regions and clinical text, to interpret fetal cardiac ultrasound and flag abnormalities.
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: Average accuracy of 87.37% in diagnosis of various fetal ultrasound abnormalities on standardized downstream benchmarks

title: Developmental Trajectories of White Matter Geometry and Relationships With Cognitive Maturation
model_family: machine learning combined with canonical correlation analysis
body_region: white matter tracts (48 tracts, whole brain)
patient_population: 598 participants, ages 67-263 months (about 5.6-22 years), from the Human Connectome Project
clinical_problem: relating white matter geometric development to executive function and crystallised intelligence
model_description: Diffusion MRI from 598 participants aged 5.6-22 years was analyzed with director field analysis to quantify tract-level splay, bend, twist, and distortion across 48 white matter tracts. Canonical correlation analysis and machine learning related these geometric features to cognition, finding that patterns in the cingulum and internal capsule predicted individual differences in executive function and crystallised intelligence.
study_design: cross-sectional diffusion MRI study with machine learning and canonical correlation analysis
headline_result: Canonical correlation analysis (r = 0.60-0.64) and machine learning showed geometric patterns, particularly in the cingulum and internal capsule, predicted individual differences in executive function and crystallised intelligence.

title: A New communication efficient federated online distillation for Non-IID Data: Application to fetal brain ultrasound plane classification
model_family: Communication-efficient federated learning framework with online ensemble knowledge distillation (dual-branch student network with an attention-convolution module)
body_region: fetal brain (primary); also tested on brain tumor MRI and chest X-ray
patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound datasets across multiple simulated institutions with non-independent and non-identically distributed (non-IID) data
clinical_problem: fetal brain ultrasound standard-plane classification under multi-institutional, privacy-preserving conditions
model_description: FedFB is a federated learning framework in which multiple institutions each train a local teacher model on private fetal brain ultrasound data, then collectively distill their knowledge (via a small shared public dataset of soft labels) into a lightweight shared student classifier, without exchanging raw data or full model parameters. It was designed to remain accurate under heterogeneous (non-IID) data across sites while sharply reducing communication overhead, and was also tested for generalization on brain tumor MRI and chest X-ray datasets.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: 91.07% accuracy, 91.28% precision, 91.03% recall, 91.15% F1-score under non-IID conditions on fetal brain ultrasound plane classification, while reducing communication overhead by more than 85% compared with traditional federated learning methods

title: A twin-aware multimodal deep learning framework with optimized late fusion for early prediction of adolescent anxiety disorder
model_family: twin-aware multimodal deep learning framework: 3D CNN for neuroimaging with prototype-based residual encoders for behavioral/phenotypic data, combined by optimized weighted late fusion
patient_population: adolescents from the QTAB (Queensland Twin Adolescent Brain) dataset, a twin cohort
clinical_problem: early prediction of adolescent anxiety disorder
model_description: A multimodal deep learning framework applies a 3D convolutional neural network to adolescent brain MRI and prototype-based residual encoders to behavioral and phenotypic questionnaire data, then combines the modality-specific outputs through optimized weighted late fusion (23% MRI, 63% questionnaire, 14% phenotypic) to predict risk of adolescent anxiety disorder in a twin cohort.
study_design: retrospective technical development / predictive modeling study
headline_result: AUC 0.8935 (95% CI 0.792-0.969), an 11-percentage-point gain over the best unimodal (questionnaire-only) baseline (AUC 0.7766), with 85.7% sensitivity and 87.3% specificity

title: Bone2Gene: Next-generation Phenotyping of Rare Bone Diseases
model_family: deep learning image classifiers (binary and multi-class CNNs) with occlusion sensitivity mapping
patient_population: children undergoing hand radiographs for bone age assessment, with 45 different rare bone diseases (RBDs) compared to unaffected controls
clinical_problem: differential diagnosis of rare bone diseases from hand radiographs
model_description: Bone2Gene takes a hand radiograph as input and first classifies whether it shows a rare bone disease (RBD) versus not, then, for RBD-positive cases, a second multi-class model predicts which of ten RBD groups is most likely. It was trained and evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation on 5,623 multi-institutional hand radiographs from 2,471 patients with 45 RBDs and 1,382 controls, using occlusion sensitivity mapping and embedding analysis to visualize the features driving each prediction.
dataset_size: 5,623 multi-institutional hand radiographs from 2,471 patients with 45 different RBDs and 1,382 unaffected controls
headline_result: affected vs unaffected classifier: balanced accuracy 85.5%; ten-class classifier: balanced top-1 accuracy 76.6%, top-3 accuracy exceeding 90%

title: Study on clinical-MRI radiomic models for graded diagnosis of neonatal acute bilirubin encephalopathy based on machine learning
model_family: light gradient boosting machine radiomics model combined with a logistic-regression clinical model
patient_population: 233 neonates with hyperbilirubinemia from two centers (training/internal validation n=187; external validation n=46)
clinical_problem: grading of neonatal acute bilirubin encephalopathy
model_description: T1-weighted MRI hyperintense globus pallidus regions in neonates with hyperbilirubinemia are manually delineated for radiomics feature extraction; after feature selection, a light gradient boosting machine model is combined with a clinical logistic-regression model (birth weight, feeding method, bilirubin levels) to grade acute bilirubin encephalopathy as none, mild, or moderate-to-severe, with internal and external validation across two hospitals.
headline_result: Combined model AUC 0.930/0.775/0.959 (internal validation) and 0.835/0.713/0.924 (external validation) for the three severity grades

title: Artificial intelligence-based automated measurement of fetal lateral ventricles on MRI
model_family: nnU-Net segmentation with NiftyMIC reconstruction and a dedicated measurement algorithm
patient_population: 300 fetal brain MRI cases, 209 normal and 91 with isolated lateral ventricular dilation
clinical_problem: fetal ventriculomegaly assessment (lateral ventricular width and volume)
model_description: Fetal brain MRI slice stacks are reconstructed into high-resolution 3D images (NiftyMIC), then an nnU-Net deep-learning model automatically segments the lateral ventricles; a dedicated algorithm computes ventricular width and volume. Results were compared against manual radiologist measurements for agreement in diagnosing ventricular dilation.
headline_result: Strong correlation with manual measurement (r=0.921 left, r=0.898 right); diagnostic accuracy 97.7% (left) and 98.7% (right) for ventricular dilation, Kappa 0.942/0.953

title: Multimodal explainable AI approach to pediatric appendicitis detection: integrating clinical data and ultrasound images
model_family: multimodal attention fusion framework (CNN image features fused with structured clinical/laboratory data via cross-attention)
patient_population: children in the Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset
clinical_problem: diagnosing acute appendicitis in children using ultrasound plus clinical and laboratory data
model_description: A multimodal attention-fusion model combines patient symptoms, laboratory indicators, and ultrasound images to detect pediatric appendicitis. A convolutional neural network extracts image features, clinical variables are encoded as structured inputs, and a cross-attention mechanism fuses the two modalities for final classification. It was trained and evaluated on the public Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development on a public dataset
dataset_size: Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset (size not given numerically in the abstract)
headline_result: 97.3% accuracy, 96.5% precision, 97.8% sensitivity, 96.2% specificity, 97.1% F1-score, 96.8% AUROC

title: Deep neural mapping reveals shared functional connectivity signatures of disorders of neurodevelopment
patient_population: Children with ADHD, ASD, and typically developing controls (fMRI n=549, MEG n=215)
clinical_problem: differentiating ADHD, ASD, and typically developing children using brain connectivity signatures
model_description: A deep neural mapping model was applied to resting-state fMRI and MEG functional connectivity matrices from children with ADHD, ASD, and typically developing controls. The model extracted low-dimensional latent embeddings of connectivity patterns and aligned them with clinical symptom scores to reveal shared and disorder-specific network signatures distinguishing the groups.
study_design: cross-sectional multimodal (fMRI/MEG) connectivity study using deep learning representation learning
headline_result: Typically developing children clustered more closely with the ADHD group than the ASD group; MEG-derived embeddings showed stronger associations with symptom dimensions than fMRI.

title: Multimodal MRI-based neuromarkers trace longitudinal changes in cognitive functioning in ADHD
model_family: multimodal machine-learning markers derived from resting-state functional and structural MRI
patient_population: children with and without ADHD from the longitudinal Oregon ADHD-1000 study
clinical_problem: prediction of cognitive functioning and its longitudinal trajectory in children with ADHD
model_description: Multimodal markers were developed from resting-state functional and structural brain MRI to predict cognitive functioning in a longitudinal, ADHD-enriched cohort of children (Oregon ADHD-1000, n=594, 1,053 annual timepoints). The markers predict both between-child differences in cognitive functioning and within-child changes over time, and performed comparably in children with and without ADHD.
study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort, predictive modeling study
headline_result: out-of-sample prediction accuracy r=0.459; explained 29.09% of interindividual variance, 33.48% of intraindividual cognitive trajectories, and 60.87% of intraindividual age-related cognitive development

title: Towards Reliable and Reproducible Fetal Brain Biometry: A Deep Learning Approach Using MRI
model_family: 3D convolutional neural network landmark regression pipeline
patient_population: 150 3D super-resolution reconstructed fetal brain MRI volumes, gestational age 20-37 weeks, from two publicly available datasets
clinical_problem: fetal brain biometry (developmental monitoring)
model_description: A four-step deep learning pipeline takes 3D super-resolution reconstructed fetal brain MRI, uses a 3D convolutional neural network to regress anatomical landmark coordinates from brain segmentation label maps, then applies geometric optimization to refine landmarks and compute five key fetal brain biometric measurements automatically, aiming for reproducible measurement without manual tracing.
dataset_size: 150 fetal MRI volumes from two public datasets
headline_result: Mean absolute error below 2 mm for most measurements; mean landmark localization error below 4 mm

title: Automated fetal head circumference measurement using a novel Graph-Mamba network
model_family: Graph neural network combined with Mamba state-space model (Mixing MLP Mamba encoder, Pixel-level Structure Prediction GNN, Maximal Perceptual Feature Fusion Mamba decoder)
patient_population: fetal head measured on prenatal ultrasound (public HC18 and FH-PS-AOP datasets)
clinical_problem: automated fetal head circumference measurement for growth monitoring and anomaly screening
model_description: An ultrasound image of the fetal head is processed by a Mamba-based encoder and a graph neural network module to predict a contour of the head, which is used to compute head circumference. The model is designed to be more robust than prior automated methods to blurred boundaries and acoustic shadow artifacts common in low-quality ultrasound images.
headline_result: On the HC18 dataset: Dice similarity coefficient 98.91±0.76%, difference 0.06±1.18mm, absolute difference 1.05±1.21mm, Hausdorff distance 1.16±0.69mm, exceeding prior state-of-the-art methods; generalization confirmed on the separate FH-PS-AOP dataset

title: Exploration of Volumetric Patterns of Brain Structures Associated with Criminal Behavior in Youth
model_family: machine learning classifier (unspecified) on structural MRI volumetric features
patient_population: Male adolescents 14-18 years old in conflict with the law: 19 offenders and 21 non-offenders
clinical_problem: classification of adolescent offender status from structural brain volumetry
model_description: Structural MRI-derived regional brain volumes (including globus pallidus and cerebellar lobules) were used as input to a machine learning classifier to distinguish adolescent offenders from non-offenders. The volumetric features showed only modest discriminative ability (balanced accuracy approximately 0.78), and the authors caution against causal interpretation.
study_design: cross-sectional case-control structural MRI study with machine learning classification
headline_result: Machine learning analyses indicated volumetric features contain modest discriminative information between groups (balanced accuracy approximately 0.78).

title: Automated Pediatric Bone Age Prediction Using Multitask Deep Learning Techniques
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
venue_label: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
model_family: multitask deep learning (EfficientNetB4-based classification and regression)
patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment (RSNA pediatric bone age dataset)
clinical_problem: skeletal (bone) age assessment for growth and developmental disorders
model_description: Hand radiographs are fed into an EfficientNetB4-based multitask model that jointly performs classification of developmental stage and regression to estimate bone age, with a gender-based input representation, a six-layer validation framework, a three-layer safety mechanism, and a confidence estimation module for clinical decision support. The model was trained on the public RSNA pediatric bone age dataset.

title: Distal radial epiphyseal fusion timing in Northwest Europeans and Middle Eastern asylum seekers: An automated ultrasound and machine learning approach
patient_population: Northwest European and Middle Eastern individuals aged 13-25 undergoing forensic age assessment via automated distal forearm ultrasound
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity / age assessment (epiphyseal fusion)
model_description: An automated ultrasound device scans the distal radius; gradient-boosting (LightGBM) models classify epiphyseal fusion stage against sex- and population-specific age thresholds, trained using reference ages from documented birthdates or Greulich-Pyle bone age. The output is a probabilistic estimate of whether an individual is below or above defined legal age thresholds, intended for radiation-free skeletal age assessment.
headline_result: AUC approximately 0.81-1.00 near optimal age thresholds across sex-population clusters

title: Pneumonia Detection in Paediatric Chest X-Rays using Ensembled Large Language Models
model_family: multimodal large language model ensemble (MedGemma agents with soft/majority voting, GPT-OSS-20B aggregation)
patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs from balanced (n=900) and real-world (n=1300) datasets at a children's hospital
clinical_problem: pediatric pneumonia detection and severity classification
model_description: Fifteen instances of a multimodal large language model (MedGemma-4B-it) each independently classify a pediatric chest X-ray into one of five pneumonia-likelihood categories, mapped to three severity classes agreed on by two radiologists. Ensemble strategies (majority voting, soft voting, and an additional LLM aggregator) combine the fifteen outputs into a single prediction, aiming for explainable, near-real-time triage support.
release_evidence: described as a research system with potential for future integration into emergency departments; no code or product release stated
headline_result: Soft voting OvR-AUROC 0.829 (balanced dataset) and 0.728 (real-world dataset) vs baseline 0.764 and 0.655

title: Developmental brain age gap in prematurity and postnatally emerging delay in congenital heart disease
model_family: deep learning brain-age regression models (structural MRI and segmentation-derived cortical morphology models)
patient_population: 1056 fetal and neonatal MRI scans (21-44 weeks) from six datasets at three centers, including preterm neonates (n=90 term-equivalent) and fetuses/neonates with congenital heart disease (n=50 fetal, n=110 postnatal)
clinical_problem: neurodevelopmental delay assessment in prematurity and congenital heart disease via a brain-age biomarker
model_description: Structural MRI and segmentation-derived cortical-morphology deep learning models are trained on normative fetal and neonatal brain MRI (21-44 weeks) from three centers to predict a continuous 'brain age.' The difference between predicted and chronological/postmenstrual age (brain age gap) is used as a marker of neurodevelopmental delay, applied to preterm neonates and neonates with congenital heart disease before and after cardiac surgery, with saliency maps highlighting associated brain regions.
dataset_size: 1056 scans from six datasets across three centers
headline_result: Preterm neonates born <28 weeks: brain age gap -0.7 to -0.8 weeks at term; CHD neonates: brain age gap -1.3 to -1.8 weeks presurgery, up to -3 weeks postsurgery (p<0.05)

title: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Focal Cortical Dysplasia in Children: External Validation of the MELD Graph and 3D-nnUNet pipelines
model_family: graph-based deep learning (MELD Graph) and 3D nnU-Net segmentation
patient_population: 71 children evaluated for epilepsy (35 MRI-positive suspected FCD, 36 MRI-negative), single-center retrospective cohort
clinical_problem: focal cortical dysplasia detection in pediatric epilepsy
model_description: 3D T1-weighted and FLAIR brain MRI from children being evaluated for epilepsy are processed by two previously developed deep-learning lesion-detection pipelines, MELD Graph and 3D-nnUNet, to flag candidate focal cortical dysplasia lesions. Detected lesions were reviewed by a pediatric neuroradiologist and scored as true or false positive/negative, externally validating both models in an independent pediatric cohort.
headline_result: Lesion-level: MELD Graph precision 0.85/recall 0.52; 3D-nnUNet precision 0.91/recall 0.48; patient-level sensitivity 0.63 vs 0.54

title: Multi-BOUNTI: Multi-lobe Brain vOlUmetry and segmeNtation for feTal and neonatal MRI
patient_population: 267 fetal and 593 neonatal MRI scans (21-44 weeks gestational/postmenstrual age), developing Human Connectome Project cohort without reported clinically significant brain anomalies
clinical_problem: fetal and neonatal brain lobar segmentation and volumetric growth assessment
model_description: A 3D Attention U-Net trained on a 43-label parcellation protocol automatically segments fetal and neonatal T2-weighted brain MRI into multiple lobar regions. The pipeline computes regional volumes, builds normative growth curves across 21-44 weeks gestational/postmenstrual age, and generates an automated report giving subject-specific centiles and z-scores for perinatal brain development.
release_evidence: The full pipeline is publicly available at https://github.com/SVRTK/perinatal-brain-mri-analysis
headline_result: Fast (<10 min/case) segmentation with high agreement to manually refined labels

title: Geometric Radiomic Analysis of Hip Joint Space for Automatic Detection of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip in Infants
model_family: geometric/radiomic feature extraction with supervised machine learning classifiers
patient_population: infants (mean age 4.5 +/- 0.83 months) undergoing pelvic radiography
clinical_problem: developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) detection
model_description: Pelvic radiographs of infants are segmented to isolate the hip joint articulation space, from which 99 geometric and radiomic features are extracted. Supervised machine learning classifiers use these features to distinguish normal from dysplastic hips, intended as a supplementary, more objective tool alongside traditional angular measurements for DDH screening.
dataset_size: not stated (infant cohort, mean age 4.5 months)
headline_result: F1-score ~80% on full dataset; 94% accuracy and 93% recall on age-matched subset

title: The relationship between childhood obesity and bone age advancement based on artificial intelligence digital radiography image analysis algorithm
journal: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
venue_label: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
model_name: United Imaging Intelligence Greulich-Pyle AI software
model_family: deep learning bone age atlas software
patient_population: 442 children and adolescents 6-18 years, categorized by BMI (normal weight, overweight, obese), enrolled December 2023-February 2025
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in relation to childhood obesity
model_description: Left-hand wrist digital radiographs are input to a commercial AI system (United Imaging Intelligence Greulich-Pyle atlas software) that automatically outputs bone age; results were manually verified by two physicians. Bone age advancement (bone age minus chronological age) was then analyzed against BMI category, waist circumference, and hormonal/metabolic markers.
release_evidence: United Imaging Intelligence Greulich-Pyle (G-P) atlas AI software
headline_result: AI vs manual ICC = 0.992; advanced bone age (>=1 year) in 67.8% of obese vs 9.8% of normal-weight participants; obesity OR 12.63 for accelerated bone age

title: Cluster-guided machine learning framework for accurate estimated fetal weight: A case study on sudanese antenatal ultrasound data
journal: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
venue_label: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
model_family: cluster analysis with PCA and random forest
patient_population: Sudanese pregnant women undergoing antenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: estimated fetal weight prediction
model_description: Ultrasound-derived maternal and fetal measurements (maternal age, height, weight, gravity, parity, and ultrasound readings) are first grouped by cluster analysis, then reduced with PCA and fed into a random forest model to predict estimated fetal weight. The approach targets improved fetal weight prediction for a Sudanese population using routine antenatal ultrasound data.

title: Network-Level Associations in Nonlinear Brain Dynamics Predict Transcendent Thinking in a Diverse Adolescent Sample
model_family: machine learning on multiscale-entropy functional brain network features
patient_population: Diverse sample of adolescents with resting-state fMRI
clinical_problem: predicting adolescents' disposition to transcendent thinking from nonlinear resting-state fMRI brain dynamics
model_description: Resting-state fMRI was used to build nonlinear functional brain networks based on multiscale entropy (MSE) similarity between regions; graph-theoretical, spectral, and information-theoretic features were computed and fed into machine learning models to predict adolescents' disposition toward transcendent thinking, compared against conventional linear connectivity-based networks.
study_design: cross-sectional resting-state fMRI study with machine learning prediction of a psychological trait
headline_result: MSE-based network features (particularly spectral energy and Shannon entropy) reliably predicted transcendent thinking, while conventional time-series-based network measures did not; no features predicted IQ.

title: Latent neural network representations of the brain reflect broad-scale adolescent phenotypic variation
patient_population: Adolescents with longitudinal structural MRI data
clinical_problem: deriving brain-based markers of adolescent phenotypic (personal, social, neighborhood) variation from structural MRI
model_description: A convolutional neural network was trained on longitudinal structural MRI data to derive latent, low-dimensional brain representations capturing structural variability during adolescence. These learned representations were used to map associations between brain structure and personal, social, and neighborhood conditions.
study_design: longitudinal structural MRI study using a convolutional neural network for representation learning

title: Predicting children's literacy from task-based fMRI: Neural heterogeneity and task-dependent performance
model_family: machine learning model with PCA-derived whole-brain predictors
patient_population: School-aged children, 6.7-10.3 years, in subgroups of 73-97 completing different fMRI tasks
clinical_problem: prediction of children's literacy (reading, verbal, naming) skills from task-based fMRI activation
model_description: Whole-brain activation contrast maps from four task-based fMRI paradigms (a phonological-lexical decision task, audiovisual character learning, and two passive viewing tasks) were reduced with principal component analysis and used in a machine learning model to predict continuous reading, verbal, and naming scores in school-aged children. Active tasks (phonological-lexical decision, character learning) outperformed passive viewing tasks for prediction.
study_design: cross-sectional task-based fMRI study with machine learning prediction of behavioral scores
dataset_size: Subgroups of 73-97 children per fMRI task
headline_result: Highest predictive performance for Reading and Naming scores was with the phonological-lexical decision task, outperforming character-learning and passive viewing tasks.

title: Diagnostic value of a fetal echocardiography-based multimodal feature fusion model for fetal coarctation of the aorta
model_family: multimodal fusion of radiomics and deep learning (Vision Transformer, ResNet, Vision Mamba, Masked Autoencoder, Fixmatch)
patient_population: 81 fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta undergoing fetal echocardiography
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of coarctation of the aorta
model_description: Fetal echocardiography images from fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta are analyzed with several deep learning architectures (Vision Transformer, ResNet, Vision Mamba, Masked Autoencoder, Fixmatch) and radiomics features, then combined in a multimodal fusion model to output a diagnostic prediction for coarctation of the aorta, compared against a baseline model using standard echocardiographic features alone.
headline_result: Multimodal fusion model AUC 0.906 vs baseline model AUC 0.707 on test set

title: DSP: Dynamic Token Selection and Semantic Injection for Pediatric Pneumonia Detection
model_family: vision-language framework (Semantic Injection Module, Dynamic Token Selection, Collaborative Mixture of Experts)
patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs (population not further specified)
clinical_problem: pediatric pneumonia detection
model_description: A vision-language deep learning framework (DSP) takes pediatric chest radiographs and generated radiology-style text captions as input. Three modules fuse image and text semantics, adaptively select informative image tokens, and route fused features through multiple experts to output a pneumonia detection prediction with interpretable, radiology-aligned reasoning.

title: Prenatal ultrasound radiomics features combined with clinical indicators for predicting outcomes of fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
model_family: radiomics (LASSO feature selection) combined with logistic regression
patient_population: 100 fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation detected on prenatal ultrasound and confirmed after birth
clinical_problem: predicting postnatal outcome of congenital pulmonary malformation detected prenatally
model_description: Radiomics features were extracted from targeted prenatal grayscale ultrasound images of fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation and reduced with LASSO regression to a radiomics score. This score was combined with an independent clinical predictor (congenital pulmonary airway malformation volume ratio) in a logistic regression model to predict postnatal outcome.
headline_result: AUC 0.809 (combined model) vs 0.728 (clinical model) and 0.770 (radiomics model) in the test set

title: Application value of 60 kVp ultra-low-dose chest CT with deep learning reconstruction in children
patient_population: 70 children under 4 years old undergoing non-contrast chest CT for suspected pulmonary disease (plus a phantom study)
clinical_problem: radiation dose reduction in pediatric chest CT
model_description: A deep learning image reconstruction algorithm (ClearInfinity) is applied to ultra-low-dose 60 kVp chest CT scans in young children, tested at multiple reconstruction weights (40/50/60%) against a conventional 80 kVp adaptive-iterative-reconstruction protocol. Objective noise/signal-to-noise ratio and subjective image quality were compared across dose levels and reconstruction settings in both a phantom and a prospective pediatric cohort.
release_evidence: ClearInfinity (CI), a named deep learning reconstruction product
dataset_size: 70 children (35 conventional-dose, 35 low-dose) plus phantom study
headline_result: Low-dose group reduced SSDE/CTDIvol/DLP by ~79-80% versus conventional dose, with comparable or better image quality at 50% CI reconstruction weight

title: Thyroid ultrasound diagnostic report generation method based on large language model
model_family: multimodal large language model (dual-stream encoding with weighted attention, fine-tuned MiniCPM-V 2.6)
patient_population: cross-sectional study across seven Chinese provinces; thyroid ultrasound performed in adults, pregnant women, and children
clinical_problem: thyroid ultrasound diagnostic report generation and TI-RADS classification
model_description: A large-language-model-based framework (fine-tuned MiniCPM-V 2.6 with a dual-stream, cross-modally aligned encoder) takes thyroid ultrasound images and generates structured diagnostic reports, including standardized terminology and TI-RADS classification. Performance was measured with text-generation metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU-4, CIDEr) and expert blind comparison against manually written reports.
study_design: cross-sectional model development and reader evaluation
dataset_size: not stated (multi-province dataset spanning adults, pregnant women, and children)
headline_result: TI-RADS classification accuracy 82.3%; blind-evaluation scores higher than manually written reports (9.55/9.85 vs 9.41/9.52)

title: Optimizing Screening for Intrauterine Fetal Growth Restriction in Low-Resource Settings Using 2D Ultrasound: A Deep Learning Approach
patient_population: 1588 annotated fetal abdominal ultrasound images from 169 term pregnancies in a low-resource setting (Uganda)
clinical_problem: screening for severe fetal growth restriction
model_description: A DenseNet-121-based deep learning model classifies 2D fetal abdominal ultrasound images by growth-restriction severity, using abdominal circumference mapped to INTERGROWTH-21st percentiles as a gestational-age-independent proxy label. It is designed as a first-line triage tool for severe fetal growth restriction in low-resource settings lacking reliable dating or Doppler access.
release_evidence: presented as a research framework requiring prospective multi-site validation; no repository or commercial product named
dataset_size: 1588 fetal abdominal images from 169 term pregnancies
headline_result: 93.7% accuracy, weighted F1-score 0.76, ROC AUC >=0.98 per class on held-out data (3-fold patient-wise cross-validation)

title: Automated Brain and CSF Volume Assessment in Infant Hydrocephalus Using Deep Learning
model_family: DenseNet/U-Net hybrid with feature smoothness regularization
patient_population: 167 T2-weighted MRI scans from infants with hydrocephalus
clinical_problem: hydrocephalus brain and CSF volume assessment
model_description: T2-weighted MRI scans from infants with hydrocephalus are automatically segmented into CSF, brain parenchyma, and background by a DenseNet/U-Net hybrid deep learning model with feature-smoothness regularization. The model outputs volumetric measurements of brain and CSF volume for clinical monitoring of hydrocephalus, trained and evaluated on a retrospective single-center cohort split into training/validation/hold-out sets.
