headline_result: Dice 95.7% (CSF) and 96.4% (brain parenchyma) on hold-out test set, outperforming FSL FAST (85.0%, 77.9%); processing time 0.8 s/scan

title: Validation of a Paediatric-Optimized Computer-Aided Detection System for Tuberculosis Using Bayesian Latent Class Analysis
patient_population: 932 Gambian children under 15 years undergoing chest radiography for suspected pulmonary tuberculosis
clinical_problem: pulmonary tuberculosis detection
model_description: Digital chest radiographs from children with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis are analyzed by qXR (version 4.2.1, Qure.ai), a paediatric-optimized computer-aided detection algorithm that outputs a probability of TB-consistent abnormality. Performance was assessed against microbiological and clinical reference standards, with Bayesian latent class analysis used to account for imperfect reference standards in children.
release_evidence: qXR-version 4.2.1 (Qure.ai), a paediatric-optimized computer-aided detection (CAD) algorithm
headline_result: Against microbiological reference standard: AUROC 0.68, sensitivity 54%, specificity 82%; Bayesian LCA sensitivity 79-89%, specificity 82%

title: Brain Age Gap as a Neuroimaging Biomarker for Neurodevelopmental Alterations and Cognitive Impairment in Beta-Thalassaemia Major: A Deep Learning-Based Multicentre Study
model_family: 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning framework for brain age prediction
patient_population: 275 participants from two centers (139 children/adolescents with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls), enrolled May 2020-October 2023
clinical_problem: neurodevelopmental alteration and cognitive impairment assessment via brain age gap in beta-thalassaemia major
model_description: A 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning model was applied to 3D T1-weighted brain MRI to predict brain age and derive a harmonized, corrected brain age gap (BAG) and voxel-level local BAG maps across two centers. Mediation analyses linked haematological indices and regional brain features to cognitive test scores, to evaluate BAG as an imaging biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk in beta-thalassaemia major.
dataset_size: 275 participants (139 with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls)
headline_result: Model achieved brain age prediction MAE 0.74 years (r=0.93) in healthy controls; patients with beta-thalassaemia major had lower corrected brain age gap than controls (-0.645±1.461 vs 0.000±0.954 years; p<0.001), consistent after age-stratification and propensity matching

title: EF-ConsNET: Physiologically Anchored Multimodal Deep Learning for Diagnosis and Severity Grading of Pediatric Myocarditis
model_family: Multimodal deep learning framework integrating chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured clinical/lab features, with echocardiographic ejection fraction as a physiological supervision anchor
patient_population: two-center inpatient cohort: 5,147 cases (700 myocarditis, 4,447 non-myocarditis) for internal training/validation, plus 529 cases (197 myocarditis, 332 non-myocarditis) from a separate hospital for external validation
clinical_problem: diagnosis and severity grading of pediatric myocarditis
model_description: EF-ConsNET fuses chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured laboratory/demographic data to detect pediatric myocarditis and grade its severity (mild vs severe), using echocardiographic ejection fraction during training as a physiological anchor to keep the multimodal representation clinically consistent and to make the model's image attention focus on cardiopulmonary regions. It was designed to remain robust when some input modalities are missing.
study_design: retrospective two-center diagnostic study with external validation
dataset_size: 5,147 cases internal (700 myocarditis); 529 cases external (197 myocarditis)
headline_result: Internal AUROC 0.926 (myocarditis detection) and 0.911 (severity grading); external validation AUROC 0.812 (detection) and 0.765 (severity grading); performance remained above 0.899 AUROC with up to 20% simulated single-modality missingness

title: AI-Augmented Multimodal Model for Predicting Macrolide Resistance in Pediatric Mycoplasma Pneumonia: An External Validation Study
model_family: Multivariable logistic regression combining an automated AI-derived chest radiograph consolidation score with clinical and laboratory markers
patient_population: hospitalized children with PCR-confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: 503 in the development cohort, 138 in an independent external validation cohort
clinical_problem: predicting macrolide resistance in pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia at hospital admission
model_description: An AI algorithm automatically quantifies a consolidation score from admission chest radiographs in children with confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. This score is combined with routine clinical markers, laboratory findings and PCR cycle threshold values in a logistic regression nomogram to predict macrolide-resistant disease at admission, to guide earlier escalation to second-line therapy.
study_design: multi-institutional retrospective diagnostic study with external validation
headline_result: Adding the AI consolidation score to the clinical model improved internal AUC from 0.819 (95% CI 0.762-0.876) to 0.860 (95% CI 0.812-0.909; P=0.004); external validation AUC 0.726 (95% CI 0.588-0.863)

title: FSU-YOLOv12 for vertebral abnormalities detection in fetal spinal ultrasound
model_family: YOLOv12-based real-time object detection network, adapted for fetal spinal ultrasound
patient_population: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development) and 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test) at two hospitals
clinical_problem: detecting vertebral abnormalities (hemivertebrae, butterfly vertebrae, block vertebrae) on prenatal spinal ultrasound
model_description: FSU-YOLOv12 is a deep learning object detector adapted from YOLOv12 to detect vertebral abnormalities on fetal spinal ultrasound images, with targeted optimizations to handle small vertebrae, acoustic shadowing, artifacts, and low tissue contrast. It was trained and validated on images from one hospital and independently tested on an external hospital's data, running in real time (149 frames per second) with a lightweight architecture (2.6M parameters).
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external test set
dataset_size: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development); 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test)
headline_result: mAP(50) 91.9%, mAP(75) 55.9%, mAP 52.3%, precision 94.2%, recall 86.3%, F1 90.1%, 149 fps inference with 2.6M parameters

title: Deep learning model integrated with data augmentation strategy based on CT for detecting and classifying pediatric pancreatic tumors
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
model_family: YOLOv8 object detector with CMUNeXt encoder module, plus fusion data augmentation
patient_population: 21 children with pancreatoblastoma and 70 children with solid pseudopapillary neoplasm
clinical_problem: detection and classification of pediatric pancreatic tumors (pancreatoblastoma vs solid pseudopapillary neoplasm)
model_description: Abdominal CT images from children with pancreatoblastoma or solid pseudopapillary neoplasm are manually annotated for tumor regions, then an 8-fold data-augmented training set is used to train a modified YOLOv8 object detector (with a CMUNeXt encoder module) to detect tumors and classify them into the two tumor types.
headline_result: Best model (post-augmentation YOLOv8-CMUNeXt): precision 92.53%, recall 78.64%, mAP@0.5 86.29%, mAP0.5:0.95 68.45%, accuracy 85.71%/72.86% for the two tumor types

title: Assessment of the accuracy of lung lesions diagnosis in adolescents with osteosarcoma using artificial intelligence
model_family: AI lung-nodule detection algorithm, previously trained on an adult dataset
patient_population: adolescents with osteosarcoma undergoing chest CT (248 CT scans evaluated)
clinical_problem: detecting pulmonary metastases (lung nodules) in adolescents with osteosarcoma
model_description: An existing AI algorithm for lung nodule detection, originally trained on an adult dataset, was applied retrospectively to chest CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma to detect pulmonary nodules ≥4 mm (a target finding for metastasis staging), and its accuracy was compared against the reference diagnosis, quantifying false positives and false negatives.
dataset_size: 248 CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma
headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy 0.843 (95% CI 0.794-0.887); false positive rate 2%, false negative rate 13.7%; using the AI algorithm would increase sensitivity from 0.805 to 0.891, an absolute false-negative reduction of 8.6% (relative 44%)

title: Automated assessment of neonatal internal capsule maturation on T2-weighted MRI across 7T and 3T
model_family: Fully automated 3D deep learning segmentation framework
patient_population: neonates (term and preterm) imaged with structural T2-weighted MRI at 7T and 3T
clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of neonatal brain white-matter (internal capsule) maturation
model_description: A fully automated 3D deep learning model segments internal capsule subregions and myelin-related signal on structural T2-weighted neonatal MRI, trained on both high-resolution 7T and conventional 3T datasets. Derived volumetric and intensity metrics were modeled against postmenstrual and postnatal age, with normative modeling used to flag individual deviations, particularly in preterm infants.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
headline_result: Segmentation accuracy Dice > 0.95 and relative volume difference < 5% across both field strengths; significant postmenstrual-age-related volumetric and intensity changes; normative modeling revealed significant deviations in preterm infants, especially for myelin-related intensity measures

title: Conus Medullaris Position in 9,808 Pediatric Lumbosacral MRI Examinations: A Large-Cohort Reference Distribution and the Normally Positioned Conus in Surgically Treated Tethered Cord
model_family: nnU-Net deep learning segmentation with IBSI-compliant radiomics and L1-penalized logistic regression
patient_population: 9,808 pediatric lumbosacral MRI examinations at a single center; 475 preoperative children surgically treated for tethered cord
clinical_problem: reference distribution of conus medullaris position and radiomic diagnosis of tethered cord syndrome
model_description: Conus medullaris termination levels were extracted from a large archive of pediatric lumbosacral MRI reports to build a normative reference distribution. An nnU-Net deep learning model was separately trained to automatically segment the conus medullaris on axial T2-weighted images, from which IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted and tested (with cross-validated logistic regression) for their ability to distinguish children surgically treated for tethered cord from controls.
study_design: retrospective single-center large-cohort reference-distribution and nested case-control study
headline_result: Conus terminated at L1 in 85.7% and L2 in 14.3% of the reference cohort (n=9,655); low-lying conus (≥L3) in only 0.05%; among 475 children surgically treated for tethered cord, 99.6% had a normally positioned conus; automated segmentation achieved held-out Dice of 0.85; neither conus position nor radiomics distinguished tethered cord from controls

title: Three-phase learning framework for first-trimester fetal echocardiography plan classification via knowledge distillation and CBAM-enhanced DenseNet
model_family: DenseNet-201 backbone with convolutional block attention module (CBAM) and knowledge distillation, staged/progressive training
patient_population: first-trimester fetuses (12-14 weeks gestation) undergoing fetal echocardiography
clinical_problem: classifying first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes to support early detection of congenital heart defects
model_description: A three-phase progressive learning framework built on a DenseNet-201 backbone enhanced with a convolutional block attention module and knowledge distillation classifies first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes, addressing the challenge of underdeveloped cardiac structures and probe-movement variability at this gestational stage. Training proceeds in stages, from clear to deformed to the full image set, to progressively improve generalization on a minority, harder-to-classify view class, with the aim of supporting earlier detection of fetal heart defects.
study_design: retrospective technical development and benchmark evaluation
headline_result: 3% and 1% overall accuracy/metric improvement over state-of-the-art baselines; approximately 5% recall and 3% F1 improvement for the minority X-sign view class

title: AI-based Psychiatric Prediction in Youth: Neuroimaging Provides Minimal Gains Beyond Confounds
model_family: deep neural networks vs. simple demographic models (comparative benchmarking)
patient_population: Youth from a large developmental clinical cohort, evaluated for diverse psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes using EEG and fMRI
clinical_problem: benchmarking AI prediction of psychiatric phenotypes from neuroimaging versus demographic confounds in youth
model_description: Machine learning models, including deep neural networks, were trained on EEG and fMRI data from a large youth developmental cohort to predict psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes. Their performance was compared against simple models using only demographics and recording site; imaging-based models did not outperform the demographic-only models for clinical phenotypes.
study_design: retrospective benchmarking study of machine learning models on a developmental neuroimaging cohort
headline_result: Simple models using only demographics and recording site matched deep neural network performance using EEG/fMRI data for clinical phenotype prediction.

title: Accurate Recognition of Pneumonia and COVID-19 by Geometric Shape Normalization of Lung Region Using Automatic Landmark Detection and Piecewise Affine Warping
model_family: ResNet-18 CNN with geometric shape normalization (landmark detection, Procrustes analysis, piecewise affine warping) and Grad-CAM interpretability
patient_population: COVID-19 Radiography Database and a balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset including pediatric cases from the Kermany dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia and COVID-19 classification on chest X-ray
model_description: A ResNet-18 landmark detector locates 15 points defining the lung contour on a chest X-ray, which are used to geometrically normalize (warp) the lung region to a standard shape and remove positioning/scale variation. A second ResNet-18 classifier then labels the normalized image as COVID-19, viral pneumonia, or normal. Grad-CAM and a cropping experiment were used to check whether classification relied on true lung pathology versus acquisition artifacts.
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: 98.60±0.26% accuracy and 98.00% F1-Macro on the COVID-19 Radiography Database (5-fold cross-validation); geometrically normalized images outperformed non-aligned artifact-masked images, 94.67% vs 94.17%, on the balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset

title: Variation in infant subcortical brain development from 6 to 12 months in Down syndrome
model_family: Deep-learning repeated-measures segmentation approach for harmonized multisite MRI
body_region: brain (subcortical structures: amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus)
patient_population: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants without Down syndrome, imaged at 6 and 12 months in a multisite cohort
clinical_problem: characterizing subcortical brain development in infants with Down syndrome
model_description: High-resolution T1- and T2-weighted MRI acquired during natural sleep in infants was harmonized across sites and passed through a deep-learning, repeated-measures segmentation approach to derive total intracranial volume and bilateral subcortical structure volumes. Hierarchical linear modeling was then used to compare longitudinal brain growth between infants with and without Down syndrome.
dataset_size: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants
headline_result: Intracranial volume in infants with Down syndrome was 12.6% lower at 6 months and 16.3% lower at 12 months than controls (p<.001); subcortical structure volumes were 6.9-13.1% lower (p≤.003), with slower growth from 6 to 12 months except in the amygdala and putamen

title: Bidirectional Domain Shift Failure in Radiograph Fracture Classification Across Out-of-Distribution Pediatric and Mixed-Age Multi-Region Data
model_family: Two separately trained ResNet-50 CNN classifiers
patient_population: pediatric wrist radiographs (GRAZPEDWRI-DX, n=20,327) and a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset (FracAtlas, n=4,083)
clinical_problem: fracture detection generalizability between pediatric and adult radiographs
model_description: Two ResNet-50 fracture classifiers were trained separately, one on a pediatric wrist radiograph dataset and one on a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset, then each was tested on the other (opposing) population's data. Grad-CAM was used to visualize what each model relied on.
study_design: retrospective cross-dataset diagnostic accuracy and generalizability study
headline_result: Both models achieved acceptable internal test accuracy (82.2% and 83.7%), but cross-testing on the opposing population caused specificity to collapse to 0% in both directions while sensitivity was artificially inflated to 100%; the FracAtlas-trained model misread normal pediatric growth plates as fractures

title: A machine-learning model for quantitative assessment of maxillary sinus volume and involvement in children based on computed tomography
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing CT for chronic rhinosinusitis
clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of chronic rhinosinusitis severity (sinus volume and inflammatory involvement)
model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network was trained to automatically segment the maxillary sinuses on pediatric CT scans, using manually annotated expert segmentations as ground truth, then compute sinus volume and the percentage of the sinus affected by inflammatory changes, giving a quantitative alternative to descriptive CT scoring of chronic rhinosinusitis in children.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 92 CT scans of the paranasal sinuses in pediatric patients
headline_result: mean sensitivity, precision and Dice coefficient near 90%; root-mean-square error 0.4 cm3 for sinus volume and 1.3 percentage points for inflammatory involvement

title: Accurate Gestational Age Estimation with a Deep Learning Model Using Ultrasound Images to Enhance Detection of Fetal Growth Restriction and Small-For-Gestational-Age Fetuses in Late Pregnancy: A Prospective Cohort Study​
model_name: GAUGE (GARBH-Ini Ultrasound image-based Gestational age Estimator)
model_family: Multi-task deep learning model with an image-based conformal prediction framework for out-of-distribution rejection
patient_population: 6,579 participants from the GARBH-Ini and WINGS prospective cohorts in North India (development); 1,577 internal test participants; 311 external test participants from a separate ultrasound lab
clinical_problem: gestational age estimation and detection of fetal growth restriction / small-for-gestational-age fetuses in late pregnancy
model_description: A multi-task deep learning model segments the fetal head in an ultrasound image and estimates gestational age directly from image features, rather than relying on standard fetal-size biometry formulas. A conformal-prediction step rejects out-of-distribution images before inference. It was trained on two prospective Indian cohorts and tested on an internal held-out set and an independent external site using a different ultrasound machine.
study_design: prospective multi-cohort development and external validation study
dataset_size: 46,926 head ultrasound images from 6,579 participants (development); 1,577 participants internal test set; 311 participants external test set
headline_result: Mean absolute error 3.5 days on internal test set (37.2% lower than Hadlock, 25.4% lower than INTERGROWTH-21st formulas); external test MAE 5.89 days; detected 77.6%, 88.7% and 89.7% of fetal growth restriction cases at 26-28, 30-32 and ≥35 weeks respectively, versus 48.6% (Hadlock) and 64.1% (INTERGROWTH-21st) at ≥35 weeks

title: Bone age assessment via joint feature learning, epiphyseal evaluation, and hybrid vision-language modeling
model_family: hybrid deep-learning framework: multi-scale joint detection, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining for pseudo-labeling, and LDA/normalization-based global attention
patient_population: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 additional clinical radiographs
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for diagnosing pediatric growth disorders
model_description: A deep-learning bone age assessment pipeline combines a multi-scale joint-detection module for the hand and wrist, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining used to generate pseudo-labels for epiphyseal maturity, and an attention-enhanced classification network, producing a continuous bone age estimate from a hand radiograph. It was validated on the public RSNA bone age dataset plus additional clinical radiographs, improving joint-detection rate over a YOLO baseline.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 clinical radiographs
headline_result: 99.98% joint-detection rate (4.12% improvement over YOLOv10), 81.8% average classification accuracy, mean absolute error 0.25 years, RMSE 0.29 years

title: Diverse Concept Modeling (DiCoMX): Domain-specific self-supervised pre-training strategy for chest X-ray foundation models
model_family: self-supervised learning Vision Transformer with knowledge-distillation pseudo-labeling (domain-specific chest X-ray foundation model)
patient_population: adult and pediatric patients across multiple downstream chest radiograph datasets
clinical_problem: chest X-ray foundation model for pneumonia and COVID-19 detection, multi-label disease classification, and lung segmentation
model_description: DiCoMX is a self-supervised learning framework that pretrains a Vision Transformer on 600,638 unlabeled chest radiographs using pseudo-labels distilled from a teacher model at both the local (token) and global (whole-image) level. The pretrained backbone is then applied to independent downstream tasks including pneumonia and COVID-19 detection in adult and pediatric populations, multi-label disease classification, and lung segmentation, and the pre-training code is publicly released.
release_evidence: The code for pre-training foundation models using DiCoMX is publicly available at: https://github.com/Pediatric-Accelerated-Intelligence-Lab/DiCoMX
study_design: retrospective technical development and benchmark evaluation
dataset_size: 600,638 chest radiographs for pretraining; multiple independent downstream datasets including adult and pediatric cohorts
headline_result: DiCoMX outperforms existing self-supervised learning methods on downstream pneumonia/COVID-19 detection, multi-label classification, and lung segmentation tasks (specific metric values not given in the abstract)

title: Learning to read a second language establishes a parallel L2 representation alongside the native one in the VWFA
patient_population: Native Mandarin-speaking children at three stages of second-language (English) literacy acquisition: pre-readers, beginning readers, and advanced readers
clinical_problem: classification of second-language literacy acquisition stage from fMRI activation patterns
model_description: fMRI was collected while native Mandarin-speaking children at different stages of learning to read English (L2) passively viewed L1 and L2 words. A supervised machine learning classifier used visual word form area activation patterns to discriminate the three L2 literacy-acquisition groups; L2-based activation, but not L1-based activation, reliably separated the groups.

patient_population: 75 children with cystic fibrosis imaged at 1.5 T
clinical_problem: measuring regional ventilation and perfusion in children with cystic fibrosis without contrast, breath-holds or ionizing radiation
model_description: An end-to-end pipeline that turns free-breathing, contrast-free lung MRI into ventilation and perfusion maps and quantified defect percentages, delivered as a short clinical report. It was feasible in every child attempted, with a six-minute scan and twenty-minute processing. The authors also report how often a human had to correct the segmentation and what difference that made to the numbers, which is the honest way to describe an automated pipeline in clinical use.
headline_result: feasible in all children, 6 min 20 s mean scan time; automatic whole-lung quantification satisfactory in 88% of patients and lobar quantification in 73%; manual refinement changed relative ventilation and perfusion by 0.7% and 2.0%

title: An Explainable Unified Framework of Spatio-Temporal Coupling Learning With Application to Dynamic Brain Functional Connectivity Analysis.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: explainable deep learning framework for spatio-temporal coupling (dynamic functional connectivity)
patient_population: children and young adults undergoing resting-state functional imaging
model_description: A deep learning framework jointly models the time-varying coupling between brain regions and their connectivity (dynamic functional connectivity) while providing step-by-step explainability of the results. Applied to resting-state imaging spanning brain development, it captured two distinct patterns of change with age: decreasing connectivity in emotion-regulation regions and increasing connectivity in cognitive regions, with children and young adults showing cyclic fluctuations.
headline_result: Identified two distinct developmental functional-connectivity patterns (decreasing emotion-regulation connectivity, increasing cognitive-network connectivity) with age

headline_result: Top-8 challenge algorithms elevated the state-of-the-art in automatic PSFHS segmentation (no single leaderboard metric quoted in abstract)

title: A critical comparative study of the performance of three AI-assisted programs for bone age determination.
model_family: three commercial bone age programs compared head to head
patient_population: 306 children aged 1-18, stratified by sex and age, at a Central European centre
clinical_problem: which of the bone age products approved for the European market a department should buy
model_description: The comparison the vendors do not run: three commercially available bone age programs on one cohort, against a three-expert Greulich-Pyle ground truth, reporting dropout rates alongside accuracy. All three were reliable across the main age range and differed mainly at the edges of childhood, and the spread between the programs was smaller than the spread between the human readers. Dropout rate varied enormously, from 0% to 20%, which is a practical difference a purchaser would not otherwise see.
release_evidence: three AI-supported programs approved for medical use in Europe: BoneXpert, PANDA and BoneView
headline_result: root mean squared error 0.62 years (BoneXpert), 0.65 (BoneView) and 0.75 (PANDA), with dropout rates of 2.3%, 20.3% and 0%; variation between AI readers was lower than between human readers (0.54 vs 0.62 years, p < 0.01)

title: Efficient labeling for fine-tuning chest X-ray bone-suppression networks for pediatric patients.

dataset_size: 240 adult CXR (pretraining); 40 labeled + 220 unlabeled pediatric CXR (P260 dataset)

title: Clinical validation of explainable AI for fetal growth scans through multi-level, cross-institutional prospective end-user evaluation.

title: Adjacent point aided vertebral landmark detection and Cobb angle measurement for automated AIS diagnosis.

venue_label: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (dataset size not stated)

model_description: A deep learning framework (LAD-Net) predicts spine centre and corner landmark points and their offset vectors on spinal X-rays, refined by correction modules, from which Cobb angles and Lenke classification are computed for AIS diagnosis.

title: Automatic Identification of Fetal Abdominal Planes from Ultrasound Images Based on Deep Learning.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

study_design: prospective cohort study with retrospective deep learning model development (ten-fold cross-validation)
headline_result: Best models MobileNetV3Large 79.89% and EfficientV2S 79.19% accuracy

title: Rib suppression-based radiomics for diagnosis of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome in chest X-rays.

study_design: retrospective single-cohort radiomics model development study
headline_result: GBM AUC 0.781 post-rib-suppression vs 0.556 pre-suppression; combined-feature LDA AUC 0.762, LR AUC 0.756

title: Deep learning radiomics nomogram for preoperatively identifying moderate-to-severe chronic cholangitis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction: a multicenter study.

study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation study
dataset_size: 323 patients across training, internal validation, and two external test cohorts
headline_result: AUC 0.895-0.916 across internal and external test cohorts

title: Artificial Intelligence and Teleradiology in Pediatric Radiology: A Survey by the Society for German-speaking Pediatric Radiologists (GPR) and the Swiss Society for Pediatric Radiology (SGPR).

patient_population: not applicable (survey of pediatric radiologists, not patients)

headline_result: Second review with AI video clips improved CHD detection sensitivity from 0.792 to 0.975 (vs 0.892 with still images)

title: Harmonizing flows: Leveraging normalizing flows for unsupervised and source-free MRI harmonization.

clinical_problem: Harmonizing brain MRI acquired across different sites/scanners without needing paired data or source-site access, evaluated including neonatal brain segmentation and neonatal brain age estimation

study_design: retrospective algorithm development and cross-domain validation study
headline_result: Superior performance compared with existing harmonization methods (exact metric not given in abstract)

title: Ultrasonic-Based Radiomics Signature With Machine Learning for Differentiating Prognostic Subsets of Pediatric Peripheral Neuroblastic Tumors: A Retrospective Study.

patient_population: 73 children with neuroblastic tumors

model_description: Ultrasound radiomics features are combined with clinical characteristics in machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting selected as best) to differentiate prognostic subsets of pediatric neuroblastic tumors.
headline_result: Validation AUC 0.941 (combined model), 0.918 (radiomics-only model)

title: BO-CLAHE enhancing neonatal chest X-ray image quality for improved lesion classification.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

patient_population: preterm and high-risk neonates undergoing portable chest X-ray
clinical_problem: improving image quality of low-quality portable neonatal chest X-rays to aid lesion classification without increasing radiation dose

headline_result: Improved classification performance for diagnosing transient tachypnea of the newborn

title: AXpert: human expert facilitated privacy-preserving large language models for abdominal X-ray report labeling.

headline_result: Gemma-7B F1 score 0.9 ± 0.015 for detecting NEC-positive samples, a 132% improvement over the BlueBERT baseline

title: Disorganization of Small-World Functional Brain Networks in First-Episode, Treatment-Naïve Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder.

clinical_problem: differentiating adolescents with first-episode major depressive disorder from healthy controls
model_description: A machine-learning multivariate diagnostic model uses resting-state fMRI graph-theory network topology metrics to classify adolescents with major depressive disorder versus healthy controls.

title: Active search for tuberculosis in three youth detention centers in Peru.

clinical_problem: Automatically measure the frontomaxillary facial angle on prenatal ultrasound for trisomy 21 screening
model_description: Trains a deep learning network to segment critical facial regions on 2D fetal ultrasound images, then uses a keypoint detection network to locate landmark points and compute the frontomaxillary facial angle automatically.
headline_result: Mean absolute error 2.354 degrees, outperforming typical junior-expert accuracy standards

title: The value of CT-based radiomics for differentiation of pleural effusions in bacterial pneumonia and Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children.

clinical_problem: Distinguishing bacterial pneumonia from Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia as the cause of pleural effusion in children using chest CT
model_description: Radiomics features are manually extracted from non-contrast chest CT regions of pleural effusion, reduced by feature-selection methods (Select K Best, mRMR, LASSO), and input to a logistic regression model that classifies the effusion as bacterial or Mycoplasma pneumoniae-related
headline_result: AUC 0.942 (training set), 0.917 (test set)

title: An artificial intelligence model for Lhermitte's sign in patients with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis: A follow-up study.
journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
venue_label: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
patient_population: 92 patients with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (from 1,298 records screened)
clinical_problem: Investigate correlation between Lhermitte's sign and AI-based radiological characteristics (upper cervical spinal cord lesions) in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis
model_description: Uses AI-based radiological analysis of spinal cord MRI to characterize cervical lesions (C1-4) and correlate them with the clinical sign Lhermitte's sign in pediatric-onset MS patients.
headline_result: Upper cervical lesion (C1-4) frequency higher in groups with current/past Lhermitte's sign vs never (p=0.017)

title: Association between deep learning radiomics based on placental MRI and preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction: A multicenter study.
model_family: deep learning radiomics on semi-supervised placental segmentation
patient_population: 420 pregnant women across centres: 140 with preeclampsia (65 with fetal growth restriction) and 280 normotensive
clinical_problem: identifying preeclampsia and, within it, the pregnancies where the fetus is growth restricted
model_description: Segments the placenta automatically on T2-weighted MRI and derives a combined radiomic and deep-learning signature that separates preeclamptic from normotensive pregnancies, and then separates those where the fetus is growth restricted. The discrimination is markedly better for the growth-restricted subgroup than for preeclampsia without restriction, which is the clinically consequential half.
headline_result: AUC 0.84-0.89 across training, test, internal and external validation for preeclampsia; 0.918 for preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction versus normotensive, and 0.742 without restriction; placental segmentation Dice 0.917

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging traits associated with adverse right ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot: A Single Center Outcomes Using cardiovascular magnetic resonance in Tetralogy of Fallot study.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
venue_label: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
patient_population: 758 patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia; 152 with 2 analyzable CMR scans
clinical_problem: Automate segmentation of cardiac MRI to study right ventricular remodeling and identify imaging traits associated with adverse RV remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
model_description: Uses the nnU-Net deep learning method to automatically segment left and right ventricular blood pool and myocardium from 2D short-axis cardiac MRI, then computes volumetric remodeling rates to study risk factors for right ventricular deterioration after tetralogy of Fallot repair.
headline_result: Pulmonic valve replacement patients had significantly lower RV remodeling rates than natural-history patients; baseline LV measures associated with RV remodeling rates

title: A fully automated U-net based ROIs localization and bone age assessment method.
patient_population: adolescents undergoing hand-wrist radiography for bone age assessment (public RSNA dataset and an in-house dataset)
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity / bone age assessment
model_description: Given a hand-wrist radiograph, a U-Net first automatically localizes the regions of interest used in the Tanner-Whitehouse method, then an InceptionResNetV2 network extracts features from both the regions of interest and the whole image to estimate bone age, combining the region-based (TW3) and whole-image (Greulich-Pyle) approaches. It was trained and evaluated on the public RSNA bone age dataset and an in-house dataset.
study_design: technical development with retrospective benchmark validation
dataset_size: public RSNA bone age dataset plus an in-house dataset (exact case counts not stated)
headline_result: Localization precision of 99.1% on the public RSNA dataset; mean absolute error 0.38 years (males) and 0.45 years (females) on RSNA, and 0.41 years (males) and 0.44 years (females) on the in-house dataset.

title: Automatic Quantification of Serial PET/CT Images for Pediatric Hodgkin Lymphoma Using a Longitudinally Aware Segmentation Network.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, P.H.S.; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: longitudinally aware segmentation network with cross-attention between timepoints
patient_population: 297 children in two Children's Oncology Group trials (median age 15.4 and 15.8 years), 200 internal and 97 external
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: deciding from the interim PET whether a child's Hodgkin lymphoma is responding, which determines how much treatment they receive
model_description: Reads the baseline and interim PET together rather than separately, letting features from the first scan inform where to look on the second, which is how a physician actually reads a response study. It then produces the quantities that drive therapy decisions — metabolic tumor volume, total lesion glycolysis, qPET and the change in SUVmax — which correlated strongly with physician measurements. Trained and externally tested on cooperative group trial data.
study_design: retrospective study on clinical trial cohorts with external testing
headline_result: F1 0.61 for detecting residual lymphoma on interim PET, beating all comparators (P < .01); baseline segmentation Dice 0.77; Spearman correlation with physician measurements 0.78-0.96 across the four PET metrics

title: Deep Learning-based Brain Age Prediction Using MRI to Identify Fetuses with Cerebral Ventriculomegaly.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
patient_population: 317 fetuses with ventriculomegaly and 183 typically developing fetuses
clinical_problem: using a fetal brain age prediction model to identify fetuses with ventriculomegaly, its severity, and associated CNS abnormalities on fetal MRI
model_description: Input: multiplanar fetal brain MRI sections; output: a predicted fetal brain age, compared to gestational age (predicted age difference) to identify ventriculomegaly, its severity, and associated CNS abnormalities.
dataset_size: 317 fetuses with ventriculomegaly, 183 typically developing fetuses
headline_result: fetuses with VM had significantly larger absolute predicted age difference than typical fetuses (P<.001); severe VM larger than moderate VM (P=.004)

title: Enhancing task fMRI individual difference research with neural signatures.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

clinical_problem: improving the reliability of task-fMRI individual-difference measures of cognition and psychopathology in early adolescents
model_description: A machine-learning classifier ('neural signature') is trained on task-based fMRI to distinguish high versus low working-memory load; its prediction captures individual differences and is compared against standard regional brain activation estimates for reliability and association with cognition/psychopathology.
headline_result: Signature predictions more reliable and more strongly associated with task performance, cognition and psychopathology than standard regional activation estimates

title: SegFormer3D: Improving the Robustness of Deep Learning Model-Based Image Segmentation in Ultrasound Volumes of the Pediatric Hip.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

clinical_problem: Robustly segmenting bone anatomy from 3D hip ultrasound to automate measurement of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) metrics
model_description: A 3D extension of the SegFormer transformer architecture, with hierarchically structured encoders producing multi-scale features, segments hip bone anatomy from 3D ultrasound volumes to compute DDH diagnostic metrics more robustly than CNN/ViT baselines
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and robustness evaluation study
dataset_size: not stated exactly (clinical pediatric test set)
headline_result: Up to 0.9% improvement in Dice score and up to 3% smaller 95% Hausdorff distance vs. state of the art

title: A comprehensive dataset of germinoma on MRI/CT with clinical and radiomic data.
body_region: brain (pineal/suprasellar region, intracranial germ cell tumor)

release_evidence: there are no publicly available imaging datasets for germinoma. This study aimed to create a comprehensive dataset for germinoma...

title: Enhancing Pediatric Bone Age Assessment Using Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Orthopedic Surgery.

clinical_problem: automated pediatric bone age assessment from hand and wrist radiographs to guide orthopedic treatment decisions for growth-related disorders
model_description: A ResNet-50-based deep-learning model takes hand and wrist radiographs as input and outputs a predicted bone age in months, benchmarked against radiologist-determined ages.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study using a public benchmark dataset
headline_result: RMSE 11.07 months, MAE 8.54 months, R² 0.929

title: Graph Neural Network Learning on the Pediatric Structural Connectome.
model_family: graph neural networks (simple and residual graph convolutional networks), compared with multi-layer perceptron, random forest, and SVM
patient_population: adult BRIGHT dataset (147 Hodgkin lymphoma survivors, 162 age-matched controls) and pediatric HCP-Development dataset (135 healthy subjects)
clinical_problem: sex classification from pediatric and adult structural brain connectome data

Architecture experiments test network depth, pooling, and skip connections, with performance assessed by accuracy, AUC, and adversarial robustness; adult-trained models were also extended to and augmented with pediatric data.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort methodological and classification study
headline_result: Adult GNN models achieved 85.1% accuracy in sex classification on unseen adult participants; the best model using pediatric data augmentation achieved 83.0% accuracy on pediatric and 81.3% on adult participants

title: Deep Learning-Enhanced Ultra-high-resolution CT Imaging for Superior Temporal Bone Visualization.

clinical_problem: Improve image quality and diagnostic visualization of temporal bone structures on ultra-high-resolution CT using deep learning reconstruction, including in a pediatric-dose protocol
model_description: Applies a vendor-specific deep learning reconstruction algorithm (AiCE Inner Ear) to ultra-high-resolution temporal bone CT raw data, producing denoised images with improved contrast-to-noise and signal-to-noise ratios compared to hybrid iterative reconstruction, evaluated in both adult- and pediatric-dose protocols.
release_evidence: a novel, vendor-specific deep learning-based reconstruction (DLR) algorithm called AiCE Inner Ear
dataset_size: 57 temporal bones from 35 patients (30 adult protocol, 5 pediatric protocol)
headline_result: DLR significantly improved subjective image quality (p<0.024), reduced noise (p<0.001), increased CNR/SNR (p<0.001) in both adult and pediatric protocol subgroups

title: Diagnosis on Ultrasound Images for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip with a Deep Learning-Based Model Focusing on Signal Heterogeneity in the Bone Region.

clinical_problem: automated diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) in infants from ultrasound images

study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: AUC 0.92 for DDH detection in qualifying images, exceeding orthopedic resident accuracy

title: Automatic Evaluation of Bone Age Using Hand Radiographs and Pancorporal Radiographs in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.

model_description: A custom DenseNet201-based deep neural network estimates bone age from hand radiographs, with Score-CAM explainability, trained on the RSNA Bone Age dataset and tested on adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients; compared against the BoneXpert commercial system.

dataset_size: RSNA Bone Age dataset (training); >250 AIS patients (testing)
headline_result: MAE 4.87 months on clinical AIS test set

title: Deep Learning-based Aligned Strain from Cine Cardiac MRI for Detection of Fibrotic Myocardial Tissue in Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.

title: Artificial Intelligence Iterative Reconstruction for Dose Reduction in Pediatric Chest CT: A Clinical Assessment via Below 3 Years Patients With Congenital Heart Disease.
