clinical_problem: Can a physics-informed neural network reliably estimate cerebral blood flow from arterial spin labeling MRI in infants?
model_description: SUPINN, a spatial-uncertainty-based physics-informed neural network with a multi-branch architecture, estimates cerebral blood flow, bolus arrival time, and blood T1 from infant arterial spin labeling MRI data.
release_evidence: Source code is provided at: https://github.com/cgalaz01/supinn
study_design: technical method development and validation study
headline_result: CBF relative error -0.3±71.7% (outperforming least squares and standard PINNs)

title: Identifying texture features from structural magnetic resonance imaging scans associated with Tourette's syndrome using machine learning.
patient_population: pediatric MRI from National Taiwan University, ages 2-18
clinical_problem: Can texture features from structural brain MRI help diagnose Tourette syndrome in children and adolescents?
model_description: Texture features extracted from FreeSurfer-segmented structural brain MRI regions are classified using SVM and naive Bayes classifiers to distinguish Tourette syndrome from controls.

title: Feedback Attention to Enhance Unsupervised Deep Learning Image Registration in 3D Echocardiography.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: unsupervised deep learning image registration with spatial feedback attention
patient_population: fetal and adult 3D echocardiography datasets
clinical_problem: improving cardiac motion estimation accuracy in 3D echocardiography, applicable to fetal and adult hearts
model_description: A spatial feedback-attention module generates a co-attention map of residual registration error and feeds it back into an unsupervised 3D deep-learning image-registration network, improving cardiac motion estimation on both fetal and adult 3D echocardiography.
release_evidence: Codes and data are available at: https://github.com/kamruleee51/Feedback_DLIR
headline_result: Outperformed existing 3D deep-learning image-registration approaches

title: Development and validation of a deep learning algorithm for prediction of pediatric recurrent intussusception in ultrasound images and radiographs.
model_family: CNN ensemble (VGG11, ResNet18) with decision fusion (LightGBM)
patient_population: 3665 cases of pediatric intussusception, 2017-2022, single center
clinical_problem: predicting recurrence of intussusception in children
model_description: Deep learning models (VGG11 for ultrasound images, ResNet18 for abdominal radiographs) each predict probability of recurrent intussusception; predictions are combined via averaging and stacking (LightGBM meta-model) fusion.
headline_result: AUC 0.897 with stacking fusion (LightGBM), vs 0.669 (US alone) and 0.809 (radiograph alone)

title: A Case for Automated Segmentation of MRI Data in Milder Neurodegenerative Diseases.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: 16 juvenile and 8 late-infantile GM1 gangliosidosis patients and 11 neurotypical controls
clinical_problem: evaluating the accuracy of automated brain MRI segmentation pipelines in GM1 gangliosidosis (a neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorder), compared with manual segmentation
model_description: Input: brain MRI from juvenile and late-infantile GM1 gangliosidosis patients and neurotypical controls; output: automated volumetric segmentation of 7 brain structures compared against manual segmentation across 5 pipelines.
dataset_size: 75 MRI scans (45 juvenile GM1, 11 late-infantile GM1, 19 controls)
headline_result: volBrain's vol2Brain pipeline had strongest correlations with manual segmentation for whole brain, ventricles, and thalamus

title: The role of the dopamine system in autism spectrum disorder revealed using machine learning: an ABIDE database-based study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 551 children from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) database
clinical_problem: Evaluating whether functional connectivity of dopamine-related brain regions on fMRI can serve as a diagnostic biomarker and subtyping tool for autism spectrum disorder in children
model_description: Functional connectivity between dopamine-related regions of interest and across the whole brain, derived from resting-state fMRI, is analyzed with machine-learning clustering methods to predict autism spectrum disorder and identify functional-connectivity-based subtypes.
study_design: retrospective case-control study using a public multi-site neuroimaging database
headline_result: subtype clustering accuracy over 0.8

title: Deep learning models for early and accurate diagnosis of ventilator-associated pneumonia in mechanically ventilated neonates.
patient_population: 670 neonates with mechanical ventilation, 900 chest X-ray images (399 VAP, 501 non-VAP), Taiwan tertiary NICU
clinical_problem: diagnosing ventilator-associated pneumonia in mechanically ventilated neonates in the NICU from chest x-ray images, to guide antibiotic decisions
model_description: Deep neural network models (ResNet, VGG, DenseNet, RegNetX80, and an ensemble of ResNet50+RegNetX80) take neonatal chest X-ray images as input and output classification of ventilator-associated pneumonia versus no VAP, with explainable-AI heatmaps highlighting the left-lower lung region.
study_design: prospective observational cohort with retrospective deep learning model development
headline_result: Best specificity 0.8378 (RegNetX80); ensemble AUC 0.8023

title: A deep learning model for radiological measurement of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis using biplanar radiographs.
journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
venue_label: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
patient_population: 600 biplanar radiographs
clinical_problem: Automatically measuring coronal and sagittal spinal alignment parameters (Cobb angle and sagittal parameters) on biplanar radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: A deep-learning model using a ResNet34 backbone performs keypoint detection to automatically measure the coronal Cobb angle and sagittal spinal alignment parameters on biplanar radiographs, compared against manual measurement by two senior spinal surgeons.
study_design: retrospective model development with internal train/test split, compared against manual surgeon measurements
headline_result: mean absolute difference 2.15 degrees (coronal), 2.72 degrees (sagittal); ICC 0.985/0.927; diagnostic accuracy 97.2%, AUC 0.972

title: Modulation of cerebellar homotopic connectivity by modified electroconvulsive therapy at rest: Study of first-episode, drug-naive adolescent major depressive disorder.
model_family: support vector machine / support vector regression
patient_population: 30 first-episode, drug-naive adolescent MDD patients and 34 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Can resting-state fMRI connectivity of the cerebellum distinguish adolescents with depression from controls and predict response to electroconvulsive therapy?
model_description: SVM classification of cerebellar homotopic functional connectivity (VMHC) distinguishes adolescents with depression from controls, and support vector regression relates connectivity changes to symptom improvement after electroconvulsive therapy.
headline_result: 73.85% accuracy, AUC 0.7486 differentiating MDD from controls

title: Prediction of mental health risk in adolescents.
patient_population: over 11,000 children from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
clinical_problem: predicting future risk of general psychiatric illness in adolescents
model_description: Inputs are psychosocial questionnaire data and neuroimaging measures from the ABCD study; output is a stratified psychopathology risk score predicting conversion to the highest psychiatric-illness-risk group the following year. Neural networks were trained separately on current-symptom and etiology/neuroimaging feature sets.
study_design: prospective multi-site cohort study (ABCD) with neural network prediction models
headline_result: current-symptoms model AUC 0.84 for predicting conversion to highest psychiatric risk group; etiology/mechanism model (including neuroimaging) AUC 0.75; adding neuroimaging did not improve performance

title: Deep-Learning-Based Multi-Class Classification for Neonatal Respiratory Diseases on Chest Radiographs in Neonatal Intensive Care Units.
patient_population: 43,338 portable chest radiographs from newborns at 10 university hospitals in Korea (34,598 training, 4,370 validation, 4,370 testing)
clinical_problem: Classify neonatal respiratory diseases (RDS, TTN, air leak syndrome, atelectasis, BPD) versus healthy lungs on portable chest radiographs in the NICU
model_description: Takes portable supine neonatal chest radiographs (plus gestational age and birth weight) and, via a modified ResNet50 deep-learning model, classifies the image into one of six categories: healthy lung, RDS, TTN, air leak syndrome, atelectasis, or bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
study_design: retrospective multicenter deep learning model development study
headline_result: Overall test accuracy 83.96%, F1 83.68% (per-condition F1: BPD 92.19%, ALS 90.65%, RDS 90.30%, atelectasis 86.56%, healthy 87.38%, TTN 70.84%)

title: Artificial intelligence and perinatology: a study on accelerated academic production- a bibliometric analysis.
clinical_problem: What are the research trends and clinical focus areas of AI applications in perinatology imaging?
model_description: Bibliometric analysis of 382 perinatology articles indexed in Web of Science, characterizing AI research trends by imaging modality (ultrasound 59.8%, MRI 20.5%), evaluation purpose, and organ system.
dataset_size: 382 articles (121 highly cited analyzed in depth)
headline_result: Most common keyword 'deep learning' (115/382 articles); most frequent purpose 'prenatal screening'

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted approach to assessing bowel wall thickness in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease using intestinal ultrasound images.
patient_population: 260 pediatric patients contributing 4,565 intestinal ultrasound images
clinical_problem: measuring bowel wall thickness on intestinal ultrasound in children with inflammatory bowel disease, so that repeat endoscopy under sedation can be avoided
model_description: Delineates the bowel wall between the lumen-mucosa and muscularis-serosa interfaces on intestinal ultrasound, computes the average wall thickness, and classifies the segment as normal or abnormal at a chosen cutoff. The clinical prize is stated plainly: intestinal ultrasound could replace repeated endoscopy under sedation and cross-sectional imaging, but only if someone can interpret it, and interpretation is the bottleneck this addresses.
headline_result: at a 2 mm wall thickness cutoff, sensitivity 90.3% and specificity 93.7% on 3,953 test images; agreement with manual measurement 0.942

title: Hand X-rays findings and a disease screening for Turner syndrome through deep learning model.
patient_population: 101 pediatric patients with Turner syndrome (case-control)
clinical_problem: Can hand X-ray features and deep learning help screen for Turner syndrome in girls with short stature?
model_description: A ResNet50 deep learning model, combined with measured hand radiograph parameters (metacarpal ratio, ulnoradial distance, carpal angle, ulnar-radial angle), screens for Turner syndrome.
headline_result: ResNet50: 78.89% accuracy, 76.67% specificity, 83.33% sensitivity

title: Prediction of clinical risk factors in pregnancy using optimized neural network scheme.
model_family: recurrent neural network (augmented, with metaheuristic feature selection)
patient_population: pregnant women, fetal ultrasound
clinical_problem: Can AI-based analysis of ultrasound images improve prediction of estimated fetal weight and pregnancy risk factors?
model_description: An augmented recurrent neural network, with an optimized feature-selection algorithm, is applied to ultrasound-derived features to classify and predict fetal birth weight and related risk parameters.
study_design: model development study (methodology poorly specified in abstract)

title: Towards automatic US-MR fetal brain image registration with learning-based methods.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
patient_population: dataset of same-day intra-subject 3D US-MR fetal brain image pairs
clinical_problem: Can ultrasound and MRI images of the fetal brain be automatically aligned to combine their diagnostic strengths?
model_description: An atlas-assisted multi-task learning network registers fetal brain ultrasound to MRI by learning jointly from intra-subject US-MR pairs and image-to-atlas registration tasks.
study_design: retrospective method development and validation study
headline_result: Average target registration error <4 mm, outperforming conventional and other learning-based methods

title: Quantitative T1 mapping indicates elevated white matter myelin in children with RASopathies.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: 72 children (49 with RASopathies, 23 typically developing)
clinical_problem: distinguishing children with RASopathies from typically developing children using myelin content measures
model_description: Quantitative T1 mapping (macromolecular tissue volume in white matter, cortical R1) is combined with a support vector machine classifier to distinguish children with RASopathies from typically developing children based on myelination patterns.
headline_result: SVM classification accuracy 87%

title: Risk stratification in neuroblastoma patients through machine learning in the multicenter PRIMAGE cohort.
patient_population: 513 patients (discovery, PRIMAGE database) plus 22 patients external independent cohort, children with neuroblastoma
clinical_problem: predicting overall survival and risk stratification in children with neuroblastoma using MRI radiomics combined with clinical/molecular features at diagnosis
model_description: Combines radiomics features extracted from T2-weighted MRI of neuroblastoma primary tumors with clinical and molecular variables as input to a random survival forest model, outputting predicted overall survival and risk stratification (low/intermediate/high).
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation study
headline_result: External cohort: C-index 93.4, time-dependent AUC 95.4

title: Fetal Birth Weight Prediction in the Third Trimester: Retrospective Cohort Study and Development of an Ensemble Model.
model_family: ensemble of Ridge, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron
patient_population: 16,655 singleton live births without congenital anomalies (>28 weeks gestation)
clinical_problem: predicting third-trimester fetal birth weight using clinical and ultrasound biometry data with ensemble machine learning
model_description: Input: maternal/neonatal demographics, obstetric clinical data, and sonographic fetal biometry from electronic medical records; output: ensemble machine-learning prediction of third-trimester birth weight.
study_design: retrospective cohort study with model development
headline_result: few-feature ensemble model achieved 81% accuracy, exceeding traditional ultrasound formula methods

title: Alteration of cortical structure and functional connectivity in childhood trauma.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 215 participants (57 with childhood trauma, 158 without), including children, adolescents, and adults
clinical_problem: Can structural and functional brain MRI distinguish individuals with a history of childhood trauma?
model_description: A logistic regression model using cortical volume, surface area, and functional connectivity features from multi-modal MRI classifies individuals with vs. without a history of childhood trauma.
headline_result: Classification accuracy 78% (p<0.001)

title: Fast and Stable Neonatal Brain MR Imaging Using Integrated Learned Subspace Model and Deep Learning.
patient_population: neonates undergoing brain MRI (dHCP dataset plus four independent medical centers)
clinical_problem: accelerating neonatal brain MRI acquisition using deep learning with sparse k-space sampling
model_description: Input: sparsely sampled neonatal brain MRI k-space data; output: high-quality reconstructed brain images using a neonate-specific learned subspace model integrated with model-driven deep learning.
study_design: methods development and multicenter validation study

title: Optical Flow-Enhanced Mamba U-Net for Cardiac Phase Detection in Ultrasound Videos.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: fetal echocardiogram dataset and the public adult Echonet-Dynamic dataset
clinical_problem: automated detection of cardiac end-systolic and end-diastolic frames in fetal and adult echocardiography videos
model_description: Input: echocardiography video frames; output: regression-based identification of end-systolic/end-diastolic keyframes using optical flow for short-term motion and a Mamba layer for long-term dependencies.
headline_result: frame mismatch 1.465 (ES) and 0.842 (ED) frames on the fetal echocardiogram dataset; 2.444 and 2.072 frames on the adult Echonet-Dynamic dataset

title: Three-dimensional markerless surface topography approach with convolutional neural networks for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis screening.
model_family: convolutional neural network on surface deviation and depth maps
patient_population: 558 adolescents aged 10-18: 285 with confirmed adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (curves 10-45 degrees) and 273 with typically developing spines
clinical_problem: screening adolescents for scoliosis without the unnecessary referrals and radiographs that current screening generates
model_description: The input is a 3D surface scan of the torso rather than a radiograph, which is the point: it quantifies trunk asymmetry by mirroring the torso geometry against itself and feeding the deviation and depth maps to a network. Scans came from two different capture devices. Like the photograph-based screening work, its value is in deciding who needs a radiograph rather than in replacing one.
headline_result: classification of scoliotic from typically developing torsos with 10-fold cross-validation; accuracy figures not stated in the abstract

title: Enhanced U-Net for Infant Brain MRI Segmentation: A (2+1)D Convolutional Approach.
patient_population: 10 infant subjects (iSeg-2017 dataset)
clinical_problem: segmenting infant brain MRI into cerebrospinal fluid, gray matter, and white matter
model_description: Input: T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI; output: (2+1)D U-Net segmentation of CSF, gray matter, and white matter.
headline_result: average segmentation accuracy 92.2%, a 0.7 percentage-point improvement over previous methods

title: Optimized attention-enhanced U-Net for autism detection and region localization in MRI.
patient_population: public autism brain MRI dataset (ABIDE)
clinical_problem: Can deep learning detect autism spectrum disorder and localize the affected brain regions on MRI in children?
model_description: An attention-enhanced MobileNet classifier (SSM-AM) detects autism spectrum disorder from brain MRI, and an attention-based U-Net (MDA-AUnet) localizes abnormal brain regions, both optimized with a metaheuristic algorithm (RA-EBO).
headline_result: Accuracy 97.29%, sensitivity 97.27%, specificity 97.36%

title: Volume-based complete automation for ultrasound fetal biometry: A pilot approach to assess feasibility, reliability, and perspectives.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
venue_label: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
model_family: automated landmark detection algorithm on 3D ultrasound volumes
patient_population: 175 datasets from women attending standard third-trimester ultrasound follow-up (16-30 weeks gestation)
clinical_problem: automating fetal biometry measurement from 3D ultrasound volumes to reduce operator dependency
model_description: Input: 3D ultrasound volumes of the fetal head, abdomen, and thigh; output: fully automated software-driven fetal biometry measurements compared with standard 2D and human-driven 3D measurements.
headline_result: completion rates 94% (abdomen) to 100% (head); intra/inter-operator ICC 0.8-0.99

title: T2-weighted MRI radiomics for the prediction of pediatric and young adult rhabdomyosarcoma alveolar subtype and distant metastasis: a pilot study.
model_family: Lasso logistic regression, support vector machine (radiomics)
patient_population: 86 pediatric and young adult patients with rhabdomyosarcoma (median age 52-59 months)
clinical_problem: Can MRI radiomics predict alveolar histological subtype and distant metastasis at diagnosis in children with rhabdomyosarcoma?
model_description: T2-weighted MRI radiomics features are used to train Lasso and SVM classifiers that predict alveolar histological subtype and presence of distant metastasis in pediatric rhabdomyosarcoma at baseline imaging.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional pilot study with external holdout validation
headline_result: Alveolar subtype AUC 0.76 (Lasso); metastasis AUC 0.81 (Lasso)

title: Population-Driven Synthesis of Personalized Cranial Development From Cross-Sectional Pediatric CT Images.
patient_population: 2,014 subjects aged 0-10 years (cross-sectional training); 51 subjects (longitudinal validation)
clinical_problem: Can a generative AI model predict how an individual child's skull will grow over time, using only a single CT scan?
model_description: A GAN with a Siamese cyclic encoder-decoder and identity-preservation mechanism learns age- and sex-independent representations from single cross-sectional head CT scans, then synthesizes images predicting how that child's skull will look at other ages.
study_design: retrospective model development and longitudinal validation
headline_result: State-of-the-art performance on independent longitudinal dataset (no single number given)

title: Fetal Diagnostics using Vision Transformer for Enhanced Health and Severity Prediction in Ultrasound Imaging.
patient_population: 500 fetal ultrasound images from multiple hospitals
clinical_problem: Can a vision transformer classify fetal health status and severity of abnormalities from ultrasound images?
model_description: A Vision Transformer model is trained to classify fetal ultrasound images into health status categories (healthy/mild/moderate/severe) and to score abnormality severity.
headline_result: 90% classification accuracy, F1 0.87, MAE 0.30

title: Predicting infant brain connectivity with federated multi-trajectory GNNs using scarce data.
patient_population: infants during the first postnatal year, with brain connectivity data held across multiple hospitals
clinical_problem: predicting infant brain connectivity development trajectories across multiple imaging modalities from a single baseline scan while preserving data privacy across hospitals
model_description: Input: a single baseline brain connectivity graph per modality; output: federated graph neural network forecasting multi-trajectory brain connectivity evolution across hospitals with scarce, incomplete longitudinal data.
release_evidence: Our source code is available at https://github.com/basiralab/FedGmTE-Net-plus
headline_result: FedGmTE-Net++ outperformed benchmark methods in brain multi-trajectory prediction from a single baseline graph (no single summary metric stated)

title: Automated Detection of Hydrocephalus in Pediatric Head Computed Tomography Using VGG 16 CNN Deep Learning Architecture and Based Automated Segmentation Workflow for Ventricular Volume Estimation.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
patient_population: 105 head CT scans (6,300 slices), infants
clinical_problem: automated detection of hydrocephalus and ventricular volume estimation in infant head CT
model_description: A VGG16-based CNN combined with an automated segmentation pipeline (windowing, histogram equalization, thresholding) takes infant head CT images as input, segments the cerebral ventricles to estimate ventricular volume, and classifies the scan as hydrocephalus or normal.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Mean classification accuracy 90.4% ± 1.2%; segmentation R² 0.94-0.99 vs manual

title: Intersection-based slice motion estimation for fetal brain imaging.
model_family: machine-learning-based classifier for misaligned slice detection, combined with intersection-based motion estimation
patient_population: fetal MRI (simulated and real data)
clinical_problem: correcting inter-slice motion artifacts in fetal brain MRI to improve 3D reconstruction quality
model_description: Input: orthogonal fetal brain MRI slice stacks; output: motion parameters estimated from intersecting-slice intensity profiles, with a machine-learning classifier flagging misaligned slices for correction.
headline_result: very low registration errors on simulated datasets; qualitative improvement over state-of-the-art on real data

title: A machine learning model based on placental magnetic resonance imaging and clinical factors to predict fetal growth restriction.
model_family: logistic regression (radiomics-based, best of eight ML algorithms compared)
patient_population: 110 FGR cases and 158 healthy controls, 28-37 weeks gestation, two hospital campuses
clinical_problem: predicting fetal growth restriction using placental MRI radiomics combined with clinical factors
model_description: Combines radiomics features extracted from sagittal T2-weighted placental MRI with clinical variables as input to a logistic-regression-based model (best of eight ML algorithms tested), outputting a nomogram-based prediction of fetal growth restriction.
study_design: retrospective case-control study with internal and external validation
headline_result: AUC 0.941 training, 0.899 internal test, 0.861 external test

title: Machine learning-based radiomics using MRI to differentiate early-stage Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy in children.
patient_population: 62 patients aged 36-60 months (41 DMD, 21 BMD)
clinical_problem: Can MRI radiomics distinguish early-stage Duchenne from Becker muscular dystrophy in young children?
model_description: Radiomic features extracted from Dixon-sequence MRI (automatically segmented by a deep learning method) are used in machine learning classifiers to distinguish Duchenne from Becker muscular dystrophy in early-stage disease.
headline_result: ML models: accuracy 81.2-90.6% vs radiologists 69.4%

title: Development and validation of pan-cancer lesion segmentation AI-model for whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT in diverse clinical cohorts.
patient_population: 1014 whole-body FDG-PET/CT images (public, training); validated on pediatric osteosarcoma/neuroblastoma (n=13), pediatric solid tumor (n=14) and adult pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma (n=40) cohorts
clinical_problem: segmenting cancer lesions on whole-body FDG PET/CT regardless of tumor type or site
model_description: A 3D nnU-Net-based deep learning model, trained on a public whole-body FDG-PET/CT dataset, automatically segments cancer lesions agnostic to tumor type or site, and is evaluated on separate pediatric and adult tumor cohorts.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort model development and external validation
dataset_size: 1014 whole-body PET/CT (public); 13 osteosarcoma/neuroblastoma, 14 pediatric solid tumor, 40 adult pheochromocytoma cohorts
headline_result: Lesion-level sensitivity/Dice: 97.83%/0.73 (pediatric solid tumor), 40.15%/0.36 (osteosarcoma/neuroblastoma), 78.37%/0.50 (adult pheochromocytoma)

title: Formative research to optimize pre-eclampsia risk-screening and prevention (PEARLS): study protocol.
patient_population: pregnant women in Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa (formative qualitative/quantitative study)
clinical_problem: Validating and implementing an AI-based ultrasound tool for gestational age estimation as part of a broader pre-eclampsia risk-screening and prevention program in resource-limited settings
model_description: As part of the formative phase of the PEARLS trial, an artificial-intelligence ultrasound tool for estimating gestational age will be validated and implemented alongside a pre-eclampsia risk-screening algorithm; this protocol paper describes qualitative and quantitative feasibility research (interviews, focus groups, surveys) rather than the AI tool's technical performance.
study_design: mixed-methods formative research study protocol (trial registration PACTR202403785563823)

title: Automatic brain quantification in children with unilateral cerebral palsy.
patient_population: 35 patients (ages 5-15) for training; validated on 54 children with CP (ages 7-16) and an independent set of 36 children with congenital/acquired brain anatomy distortions (ages 1-17)
clinical_problem: Automatically quantify lesion-free brain volumes in children with unilateral cerebral palsy to relate brain structure to motor and visual outcomes
model_description: Trains deep learning models on T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI, using an automatic label generation workflow, to segment brain structures and lesions and compute lesion-free brain and regional volumes, correlated with lesion extent and motor/visual outcomes.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with independent external validation cohort
dataset_size: 35 training patients; 54 validation children with CP; independent set of 36 children with brain anatomy distortions
headline_result: Reduced affected-hemisphere volumes correlated with lesion extent (p<0.05); regional (e.g., thalamic) lesion-free volumes linked to motor/visual outcomes (p<0.05)

title: Optimized deep learning model for diagnosing tonsil and adenoid hypertrophy through X-rays.
model_family: YOLOv8n object detection with ResNet18 classification
patient_population: pediatric outpatients aged 2-12 years with respiratory obstruction symptoms
clinical_problem: diagnosing severity of tonsillar and adenoid hypertrophy from lateral nasopharyngeal X-rays in children
model_description: Input: lateral nasopharyngeal X-rays; output: YOLOv8n detection of tonsil/adenoid regions followed by CNN classification of hypertrophy severity.
dataset_size: 819 training/validation images, 484 test images (1,006 collected initially)

title: Recovering Image Quality in Low-Dose Pediatric Renal Scintigraphy Using Deep Learning.
patient_population: public dynamic renal scintigraphy database (pediatric)
clinical_problem: Recover image quality in low-dose pediatric renal scintigraphy to allow reduced radiation exposure
model_description: Applies denoising neural networks (DnCNN, UDnCNN, DUDnCNN, AttnGAN) to simulated half-dose (50% counts) pediatric renal scintigraphy images to restore image quality comparable to full-dose acquisitions.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study using a public dataset
headline_result: UDnCNN achieved the best balance of SNR and MS-SSIM among four networks; half-dose reconstructed images comparable to full-dose

title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Brain Volumetry Model Predicting Poor Psychomotor Outcomes in Preterm Neonates.
model_family: random forest and logistic regression on automated MRI volumetry (Infant FreeSurfer)
patient_population: 150 very low birth weight (<1500 g) preterm infants assessed at term-equivalent age MRI and 18-24 months corrected age
clinical_problem: predicting long-term psychomotor and mental developmental outcomes in very-low-birth-weight preterm infants from term-equivalent-age brain MRI volumetry
model_description: Input: automated brain volumetry (Infant FreeSurfer) and diffusion tensor imaging metrics from term-equivalent-age MRI plus clinical data; output: random forest/logistic regression prediction of low Psychomotor and Mental Development Index at 18-24 months.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
headline_result: AUROC 0.9297 (Psychomotor Development Index) and 0.7755 (Mental Development Index) using combined clinical and MRI volumetry model

title: A novel deep learning radiopathomics model for predicting carcinogenesis promotor cyclooxygenase-2 expression in common bile duct in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction: a multicenter study.
patient_population: 219 pediatric PBM patients (median age 2.2-3.4 years)
clinical_problem: Can a combined imaging and pathology AI model predict a molecular marker of cancer risk (COX-2) in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction?
model_description: A deep learning radiopathomics model integrates CT radiomics/deep-learning imaging features with histopathology image features to predict biliary COX-2 expression in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation
headline_result: AUC 0.851 (internal test), 0.841 (external test)

title: Revealing morphological fingerprints in perinatal brains using quasi-conformal mapping: occurrence and neurodevelopmental implications.
patient_population: 461 infants (cross-sectional), 41 infants with longitudinal scans
clinical_problem: Can individual infants be identified from morphological 'fingerprints' of their brain MRI, and do these predict later neurodevelopment?
model_description: A deep learning framework projects 3D cortical morphology (thickness, curvature, sulcal depth) onto 2D maps via quasi-conformal mapping and uses ResNet18 with contrastive learning to identify individual infants from brain MRI and relate morphological patterns to later cognitive/behavioral development.
headline_result: Top1 accuracy 85.90%, Top5 accuracy 92.20% for individual identification

title: Automated scan quality evaluation for DDH using transfer learning: Development of a novel ensemble system.
patient_population: 1,891 subjects (infants) from two hospitals in Korea
clinical_problem: Automatically evaluate the scan quality of pelvic ultrasound images used to diagnose developmental dysplasia of the hip by scoring five anatomical landmarks
model_description: Uses an ensemble of transfer-learning CNN models to score the quality/visibility of five anatomical landmarks on pelvic ultrasound images for DDH screening, with Grad-CAM verification and an accelerated sequence method for real-time use.
headline_result: Kappa >=0.6 for all models; AUC 0.89 for classifying standard images; processing time 0.20-0.35 s/image

title: PARADISE: Personalized and regional adaptation for HIE disease identification and segmentation.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
patient_population: term-born neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
clinical_problem: segmenting small, diffuse hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy lesions on neonatal brain MRI
model_description: ParadiseNet incorporates global-local learning, progressive uncertainty learning and self-evolution learning modules, inspired by clinical interpretation, to segment small and diffuse HIE lesions on neonatal brain MRI.
headline_result: Over 4% Dice and 6% NSD improvement for small (<1%) lesions versus U-Net and other general segmentation algorithms

title: Application of Radiomics in Predicting the Prognosis of Medulloblastoma in Children.
patient_population: 81 children diagnosed with medulloblastoma
clinical_problem: predicting prognosis (overall survival) of pediatric medulloblastoma using MRI radiomics combined with clinical features
model_description: Input: radiomics features extracted from T1-weighted MRI tumor regions of interest plus clinical/molecular features; output: risk stratification and survival prediction via a combined clinical-radiomics model.
headline_result: clinical-radiomics model C-index 0.860 vs. radiomics-only 0.762 vs. clinical-only 0.806

title: Automated Measurements of Spinal Parameters for Scoliosis Using Deep Learning.
patient_population: 1682 patients with scoliosis; internal testing set of 87 adolescents (7-16y) and 26 older adults (>=60y)
clinical_problem: Can an automated deep learning tool accurately measure spinal parameters (Cobb angle and others) for scoliosis diagnosis, in both adolescents and older adults?
model_description: A CNN pipeline (coarse segmentation, landmark localization, fine segmentation) automatically measures Cobb angle, T1 tilt, coronal balance, clavicular angle, shoulder height, T5-T12 Cobb angle, and sagittal balance from spinal radiographs.

The reader gain was modest, and in 2% of cases residents talked themselves out of a correct diagnosis because of the AI.

title: Transfer Learning of Deep Neural Networks Pretrained Using the ABCD Dataset for General Psychopathology Prediction in Korean Adolescents.
journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
venue_label: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
patient_population: 6,905 ABCD Study adolescents (US) for pretraining; 125 adolescents (healthy and with major depressive disorder) from Seoul National University Hospital for transfer
clinical_problem: Predicting general psychopathology risk, including major depressive disorder, in adolescents from resting-state functional MRI connectivity, and testing whether a model trained on US adolescents generalizes to Korean adolescents
model_description: A deep neural network trained to predict a general psychopathology factor from resting-state functional connectivity MRI in a large US adolescent cohort (ABCD Study) is transferred and fine-tuned to predict psychopathology scores in an independent Korean adolescent cohort, compared against kernel ridge regression and a baseline DNN.
study_design: retrospective model development with external transfer-learning validation across independent multi-site cohorts
headline_result: transferred DNN Pearson r=0.29±0.18, mean absolute error 0.59±0.09 (p<.005), outperforming kernel ridge regression and a baseline DNN

title: Pediatric chest X-ray diagnosis using neuromorphic models.
patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs from the public PediCXR benchmark dataset
clinical_problem: classifying prevalent thoracic diseases on pediatric chest X-rays using neuromorphic spiking neural networks
model_description: Input: pediatric chest X-rays (PediCXR dataset); output: spiking-neural-network classification across six thoracic illness categories using spatiotemporal, event-driven processing.
study_design: retrospective model development and benchmarking study
headline_result: Hierarchical Spiking Neural Network (HSNN) achieved 96% classification accuracy across six thoracic illness categories, F1 0.95, specificity 1.0 for pneumonia detection

title: Myo-Guide: A Machine Learning-Based Web Application for Neuromuscular Disease Diagnosis With MRI.
journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
venue_label: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 2,961 MRI samples from genetically confirmed cases of 20 pediatric and adult neuromuscular diseases
clinical_problem: differential diagnosis of neuromuscular diseases from patterns of muscle involvement on MRI
model_description: Input: muscle MRI fat-content maps (harmonized across studies), age at MRI, and sex; output: predicted neuromuscular disease diagnosis (ranked candidates) via an XGBoost ensemble, with SHAP-based explanation of disease-specific muscle involvement patterns; delivered as a free web application.
release_evidence: implemented as a free web platform, providing global access to the medical community
study_design: retrospective multi-study model development with reader comparison
dataset_size: 2,961 MRI samples from 20 pediatric and adult NMDs
headline_result: balanced accuracy 64.8%±3.4%; weighted top-3 accuracy 84.7%±1.8%; outperformed expert clinicians' top-3 accuracy (75.0%±4.8%)

title: The Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Echocardiographic Detection of Congenital Heart Defects in the Fetus: A Mini-Review.
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal echocardiography (review, no specific cohort)
clinical_problem: Reviewing how AI-enhanced echocardiography can improve detection of congenital heart defects in the fetus, including image quality control, cardiac function measurement, defect detection and classification
model_description: A mini-review of AI applications in fetal echocardiography, covering image quality control, cardiac function measurement, and defect detection/classification, noting AI-based congenital heart defect detection sensitivity above 90% as a potential prenatal screening tool, particularly for low-resource settings via tele-echocardiography.
headline_result: AI-based congenital heart defect detection sensitivity greater than 90% in the fetus, as reported across the reviewed literature

title: Neuroanatomical associations with autistic characteristics in those with acute anorexia nervosa and weight-restored individuals.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
body_region: brain (anterior cingulate, middle frontal gyrus, orbitofrontal cortex)
patient_population: 183 individuals (67 healthy controls, 68 acute anorexia nervosa, 48 weight-restored) from the BEACON study; adolescents (some young adults)
clinical_problem: Determine whether autistic characteristics and frontal-region brain morphology predict future social anhedonia and alexithymia in adolescents with acute or weight-restored anorexia nervosa
model_description: Uses structural MRI-derived volume and surface area of the anterior cingulate cortex, middle frontal gyrus, and orbitofrontal cortex, together with autistic-characteristic scores, as input to random forest regression models predicting future levels of social anhedonia and alexithymia.
study_design: retrospective case-control neuroimaging study with random forest regression
headline_result: RFR models showed moderate-to-weak predictive performance; autistic characteristics were not important predictive features

title: Preoperative CT-based radiomics nomogram for progression-free survival prediction in pediatric posterior mediastinal malignancies.
model_family: logistic regression radiomics signature combined with a clinical nomogram
patient_population: 306 patients with posterior mediastinal malignancies
clinical_problem: predicting progression-free survival in pediatric posterior mediastinal malignancies using preoperative CT radiomics
model_description: Input: preoperative contrast-enhanced CT radiomics features plus clinical data (Ki-67 index, metastasis); output: radiomics nomogram predicting progression-free survival.
headline_result: radiomics nomogram AUC 0.87 (Brier score 0.22) in the test set, outperforming the clinical model (AUC 0.82) and radiomics-only model (AUC 0.77)

title: The performance of sonographic antenatal birth weight assessment assisted with artificial intelligence compared to that of manual examiners at term.
patient_population: 300 fetuses at mean gestational age 38.7+-1.1 weeks scheduled for elective cesarean section
clinical_problem: Compare accuracy of AI-supported antenatal fetal weight estimation with that of sonographers of different experience levels near term
model_description: An AI-supported algorithm performs automated antenatal fetal weight estimation using the Hadlock formula 3 from ultrasound measurements, compared prospectively against a junior and a senior sonographer's manual estimates relative to actual birth weight.
headline_result: AI accurate in 48.3% of cases vs 62% (junior) and 70% (senior) sonographer; AI mean difference from birth weight -338.4+-606.2g (largest error of the three)

title: AI-powered automated X-ray bone age analyzer for assisting bone age assessment in Chinese children and adolescents: accuracy, consistency, and time efficiency.
patient_population: 1000 children aged 1-18 years across five centers in China
clinical_problem: assisting physicians in assessing bone age from hand radiographs in children with growth/endocrine concerns
model_description: A commercially available AI-powered X-ray bone-age analyzer estimates TW3-RUS and TW3-Carpal bone age from hand radiographs, used alone or as assistance to physicians of varying experience levels, in a multicenter prospective study.
release_evidence: commercially available AI-powered X-ray bone age analyzer
headline_result: Accuracy 88.2-96.8% (TW3-RUS) and 90.6-97.2% (TW3-Carpal) with AI assistance; evaluation time significantly reduced

title: Predicting the onset of mental health problems in adolescents.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
patient_population: discovery N=3236 (168-513 per group with MRI), validation N=3851 (84-231, no MRI), ABCD study children/adolescents
clinical_problem: predicting onset of future mental health problems in children/adolescents using subclinical symptoms and neuroimaging data (ABCD study)
model_description: Machine-learning models take demographic, symptom, and neuroimaging (MRI) data as input from children aged 9-10 years to predict onset of six different mental health problems by age 12 as output.
study_design: prospective cohort study with machine learning model development and validation
headline_result: AUCs 0.71-0.90 for predicting six mental health problems; neuroimaging added limited value over symptoms

title: Deep Learning Model for Real-Time Nuchal Translucency Assessment at Prenatal US.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 3959 NT images from 3153 fetuses (internal dataset); 267 ultrasound videos from 267 fetuses (external dataset)
clinical_problem: identifying the standard nuchal translucency imaging plane and measuring NT thickness in real time during prenatal ultrasound
model_description: A deep learning model (AIM-NT) identifies the nuchal translucency plane in real time and measures NT thickness on prenatal ultrasound, benchmarked against experienced radiologists on internal and external multicenter datasets.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external validation
dataset_size: 3959 images (3153 fetuses) internal; 267 videos (267 fetuses) external
headline_result: AUC 0.92 for NT plane identification; no significant difference from radiologists in accuracy (88.8% vs 87.6%) or thickness measurement

title: Multi-Parameter MRI for Evaluating Glymphatic Impairment and White-Matter Abnormalities and Discriminating Refractory Epilepsy in Children.
patient_population: 70 children with drug-sensitive epilepsy and 26 with refractory epilepsy
clinical_problem: Distinguishing refractory from drug-sensitive epilepsy in children using glymphatic-function and white-matter MRI markers
model_description: DTI-ALPS index, fractional anisotropy, mean diffusivity and nodal efficiency from multi-parameter MRI are combined into a machine-learning model, evaluated by five-fold cross-validation, to discriminate refractory from drug-sensitive pediatric epilepsy
headline_result: Cross-validated ROC AUC 0.83 (sensitivity 78.2%, specificity 84.8%)

title: Retrospective Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Effectiveness of a New Tanner-Whitehouse-Based Bone Age Assessment Algorithm Trained with a Deep Neural Network System.
patient_population: 560 Korean children and adolescents (280 female, 280 male), mean age 9.43±2.92 years
clinical_problem: How well does a commercial deep learning bone age system based on the Tanner-Whitehouse method agree with pediatric radiologists?
model_description: A commercialized deep learning system, built on a Rotated Single Shot MultiBox Detector and EfficientNet-B0, automatically assigns Tanner-Whitehouse (TW3) bone age from hand and wrist radiographs.
release_evidence: A commercialized AI solution built upon the Rotated Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) and EfficientNet-B0 was used
study_design: retrospective clinical trial comparing AI to pediatric radiologists
headline_result: r2=0.977 vs radiologists; RMSE 0.529 years, MAE 0.388 years; 82.3% within 0.6 years of radiologist assessment

title: Self-supervised denoising diffusion probabilistic models for abdominal DW-MRI.
patient_population: 120 pediatric subjects with liver tumors
clinical_problem: Can a deep learning denoising method improve image quality and lesion detection on single-repetition diffusion-weighted MRI of children's liver tumors, without needing longer scan times?
model_description: A self-supervised denoising diffusion probabilistic model (ssDDPM), constrained by the diffusion signal decay model, denoises single-repetition abdominal diffusion-weighted MRI images in pediatric patients to improve ADC accuracy and lesion visibility while shortening scan time.
study_design: retrospective method development and comparison study
headline_result: Superior image quality, lesion conspicuity, and ADC accuracy vs. non-local means and deep image prior denoising

title: Brain Age Prediction in Type II GM1 Gangliosidosis.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: 81 MRI scans from 41 Type II GM1 gangliosidosis patients (juvenile and late-infantile subtypes) and 897 MRI scans from 556 neurotypical controls
clinical_problem: Predict brain age and regional brain structure age gaps from MRI to serve as a neuroimaging biomarker of disease severity/progression in GM1 gangliosidosis
model_description: Applies a machine learning MRI analysis pipeline (BrainStructuresAges) to compute predicted brain age and regional Brain Structures Age Gap Estimation from structural MRI, showing accelerated brain aging rates in GM1 gangliosidosis patients that correlate with clinical severity, intended as a surrogate outcome measure for clinical trials.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional/longitudinal neuroimaging biomarker study (medRxiv preprint)
dataset_size: 81 MRI scans from 41 GM1 patients; 897 MRI scans from 556 neurotypical controls
headline_result: Whole-brain aging rate: 0.83/year (controls) vs 1.57/year (juvenile GM1) vs 12.25/year (late-infantile GM1); predicted brain age and BSAGE correlated with clinical assessments

title: Automatic ultrasound image alignment for diagnosis of pediatric distal forearm fractures.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
venue_label: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
model_family: deep learning bone-boundary delineation with optimization-based image alignment
patient_population: children with distal forearm injuries imaged with point-of-care ultrasound
clinical_problem: using AI-aligned point-of-care ultrasound instead of X-rays to diagnose pediatric distal forearm fractures and reduce radiation exposure
model_description: Input: paired point-of-care ultrasound images of the distal forearm; output: deep-learning-delineated bone boundaries and landmarks used to automatically align ultrasound image pairs for fracture classification and angulation measurement.

title: Brain tissue biomarker impact bone age in central precocious puberty more than hormones: a quantitative synthetic magnetic resonance study.
model_family: deep learning (TW3 bone age scoring) + quantitative synthetic MRI
patient_population: 84 children with central precocious puberty and 84 controls
clinical_problem: Determine whether brain tissue composition biomarkers from synthetic MRI relate more strongly to bone age development than reproductive hormones in central precocious puberty
model_description: Uses quantitative synthetic MRI (SyMRI) to derive brain tissue component volumes (myelin, white matter, gray matter, CSF) and a deep learning model to score Tanner-Whitehouse III bone age from hand-wrist X-rays, then correlates these with hormone levels in children with central precocious puberty.
headline_result: TW3-Carpal score positively correlated with myelin content (r=0.397, P<0.001); not correlated with hormone levels

title: Quantitative T1 Mapping Indicates Elevated White Matter Myelin in Children With RASopathies.
patient_population: 72 children (49 with RASopathies, 23 typically developing)
clinical_problem: distinguishing children with RASopathies from typically developing children using myelin content measures
model_description: Quantitative T1 mapping (macromolecular tissue volume in white matter, cortical R1) is combined with a support vector machine classifier to distinguish children with RASopathies from typically developing children based on myelination patterns.
headline_result: SVM classification accuracy 87%

title: Automated cervix biometry, volumetry and normative models for 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted 0.55-3T fetal MRI during 2nd and 3rd trimesters.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: 20 evaluation datasets (0.55T and 3T); 270 normal term pregnancies (16-40 weeks GA) for the normative model
clinical_problem: Can an automated deep learning pipeline measure cervical biometry on fetal MRI to track cervical remodeling during pregnancy?
model_description: A deep learning pipeline performs automated multi-layer segmentation and biometric measurement of the pregnant cervix on 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted fetal MRI, used to build normative growth models and population-averaged cervix atlases.
study_design: method development and normative modeling study (preprint)
headline_result: Good agreement with manual measurements; inlet diameter and length correlated most strongly with gestational age

title: Predicting Postoperative Prognosis in Pediatric Malignant Tumor With MRI Radiomics and Deep Learning Models: A Retrospective Study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: gradient boosting / deep learning (3D ResNet-18 features + radiomics)
patient_population: 260 pediatric patients with brain tumors who underwent R0 resection, age <=14 years
clinical_problem: Predict 3-year postoperative disease-free survival in pediatric malignant brain tumor patients by combining MRI radiomics, deep learning features, and clinical indices
model_description: Extracts 1,130 radiomics features (Pyradiomics) and 511 deep learning features (3D ResNet-18) from preoperative T1-enhanced MRI with manually delineated tumors, combines them with clinical indices via Lasso feature reduction, and trains machine learning models (SVM, random forest, LightGBM) to predict 3-year disease-free survival.
study_design: retrospective multimodal ML model development study
headline_result: Fusion model (LightGBM): AUC 0.859, accuracy 85.2%; combined with clinical indexes AUC improved to 0.909

title: A fully automatic Cobb angle measurement framework of full-spine DR images based on deep learning.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
venue_label: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
patient_population: children and adolescents undergoing full-spine DR for scoliosis (1,163 AP and 1,378 LAT view images)
clinical_problem: Automatically measure the Cobb angle from full-spine radiographs to assess scoliosis severity, replacing time-consuming manual measurement with variability
model_description: A deep learning framework (YOLOv8 with CBAM) classifies AP/LAT spine views, locates the region of interest, detects vertebral boundaries, types, and corner points, and automatically computes the Cobb angle from full-spine digital radiographs.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with reader study validation
dataset_size: 1,163 AP view and 1,378 LAT view DR images
headline_result: Mean Cobb angle error 2.56 deg (AP), 2.50 deg (LAT); ICC 0.956 (AP), 0.925 (LAT); reader study major curve error 3.92 deg, ICC 0.943

title: Integrating neuron-specific enolase and venous-phase enhanced computed tomography radiomics for improved survival prediction in high-risk neuroblastoma: a two-center study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: radiomics score (Cox regression) combined with a clinical biomarker (neuron-specific enolase)
patient_population: 140 patients with high-risk neuroblastoma (70 training, 30 test, 40 external validation) from two centers
clinical_problem: improving survival prediction in high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma by combining a clinical marker (neuron-specific enolase) with CT radiomics
model_description: Input: venous-phase enhanced CT radiomics features plus neuron-specific enolase; output: combined model predicting overall survival in high-risk neuroblastoma, externally validated.
study_design: two-center retrospective study with external validation
headline_result: combined model 5-year overall survival AUC 0.780 (train), 0.742 (test), 0.710 (external validation); concordance indices 0.730/0.707/0.690

title: Deep learning-based auto-contouring of organs/structures-at-risk for pediatric upper abdominal radiotherapy.
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
venue_label: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 189 in-house pediatric postoperative CTs (renal tumors/neuroblastoma) + 189 public thoracoabdominal CTs
clinical_problem: automated multi-organ segmentation of organs at risk for radiotherapy planning in pediatric patients with upper abdominal tumors (renal tumors, neuroblastoma)
model_description: CT-based deep-learning multi-organ segmentation models (Model-PMC-UMCU trained on in-house data; Model-Combined trained on combined in-house and public data) take pediatric upper abdominal CT scans as input and output contours of 17 organs at risk for radiotherapy planning.
study_design: retrospective multi-dataset deep learning segmentation model development and validation study
headline_result: Mean DSC >0.95 for 5/9 clinician-delineated OARs; stomach-bowel and pancreas DSC <0.90

title: Computed tomography based radiomics signature for predicting the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor in pediatric patients with nephroblastoma.
model_family: radiomics signature (logistic regression) combined with a clinical nomogram
patient_population: 73 pediatric patients with nephroblastoma
clinical_problem: predicting vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression in pediatric nephroblastoma (Wilms tumor) using CT radiomics
model_description: Input: CT radiomics features extracted from a manually marked tumor region of interest plus clinicopathological data; output: radiomics-based nomogram predicting VEGF expression level.
headline_result: logistic regression radiomics model AUC 0.761 (training), 0.791 (test)

title: Automatic segmentation and quantitative analysis of brain CT volume in 2-year-olds using deep learning model.
patient_population: 1,487 head CT scans of healthy 2-year-old children
clinical_problem: Can deep learning automatically segment and measure brain volumes on CT in healthy 2-year-old children to create normative reference values?
model_description: A ResU-Net deep learning model automatically segments brain regions on head CT of 2-year-old children, producing regional brain volume measurements used to build a normative reference database.
headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.96 (testing set) with ResU-Net (3,3,3) kernel

title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric osteopenia diagnosis: evaluating deep network classification and model interpretability using wrist X-rays.
model_family: CNN and transformer models (six networks compared; DenseNet201 with transfer learning best)
patient_population: pediatric wrist X-rays from the GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset
clinical_problem: Classifying osteopenia versus healthy bone from pediatric wrist X-rays as an alternative to bone mineral density assessment, with interpretable visual explanations
model_description: Six deep networks (CNNs and transformer models) are trained to classify osteopenia versus healthy bone from pediatric wrist X-rays in the public GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset, with two explainable-AI techniques used to visualize and interpret the networks' decisions.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation on a public pediatric wrist radiograph dataset
dataset_size: GRAZPEDWRI-DX pediatric wrist X-ray dataset (exact n not stated)
headline_result: DenseNet201 with transfer learning achieved the top classification accuracy of 95.2%

title: Computer-aided assessment for enlarged fetal heart with deep learning model.
model_family: YOLOv8 with CBAM attention module and ResNeXtBlock
patient_population: prenatal ultrasound video dataset (size not stated)
clinical_problem: automating detection of fetal heart enlargement on prenatal ultrasound as an indicator of possible congenital heart disease
model_description: A YOLOv8 object-detection model with a CBAM attention module and a ResNeXtBlock residual network automatically detects fetal heart enlargement from prenatal ultrasound videos, compared against a YOLOv11 self-attention variant.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and benchmark comparison

title: TIER-LOC: Visual Query-based Video Clip Localization in fetal ultrasound videos with a multi-tier transformer.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
patient_population: fetal ultrasound heart-sweep videos and the large-scale PULSE dataset for fetal anomaly detection
clinical_problem: Can an AI model automatically find relevant video clips (e.g., standard views) within fetal ultrasound sweep videos, to assist sonographer workflow and anomaly detection?
model_description: TIER-LOC is a multi-tier spatio-temporal transformer that retrieves the video clip in a fetal ultrasound sweep matching a given example (query) frame, used to detect standard-view clips in fetal heart sweeps and to support fetal anomaly detection.
study_design: retrospective method development and benchmark comparison
dataset_size: two ultrasound video datasets plus PULSE dataset
headline_result: Outperformed best prior state-of-the-art model by 7%, 4%, and 4% across three datasets

title: Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy Imaging Endophenotypes and Relationship With Cognition and Resting-State EEG.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: supervised machine learning classifier + K-means clustering
patient_population: 64 JME patients aged 12-25 and 41 age/sex-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: Explaining heterogeneous cortical-thickness findings in Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy by defining imaging-based endophenotypes and relating them to cognition and EEG
model_description: Data-driven comparison of cortical thickness and subcortical volumes between JME patients and controls; supervised machine learning confirms the classification power of these differences, and K-means clustering groups patients into imaging endophenotypes correlated with cognition and EEG
study_design: prospective cohort study (Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy Connectome Project)
headline_result: Three discrete imaging endophenotypes identified (left, right, symmetric), with left-hemisphere disease linked to lower general cognitive performance

title: A Medical Multimodal Large Language Model for Pediatric Pneumonia.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 163,999 outpatient and 8,684 inpatient pediatric cases; test set of 642 samples verified by pediatric pulmonology specialists
clinical_problem: Support differential diagnosis, treatment planning, and generation of medical records/radiology reports for pediatric pneumonia
model_description: A medical multimodal large language model trained on a three-stage strategy using plain-text clinical records and interleaved image-text pairs (2D chest X-ray, 3D chest CT, and radiology reports) to generate free-text medical records and radiology reports and support clinical decision-making for pediatric pneumonia.
study_design: retrospective large-scale multimodal model development and evaluation study
dataset_size: 163,999 outpatient and 8,684 inpatient cases (training); 642-sample test set
headline_result: Automated LLM scoring corroborated by manual specialist scoring on 642-sample test set demonstrating superiority of P2Med-MLLM (no single numeric headline given)

title: Machine Learning-Based Identification of Children With Intermittent Exotropia Using Multiple Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Features.
model_family: machine learning (logistic regression best; multiple classifiers compared)
patient_population: 41 children with intermittent exotropia and 36 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Can resting-state functional brain MRI distinguish children with intermittent exotropia from healthy peers?
model_description: Machine learning classifiers (best: logistic regression with ANOVA feature selection) use resting-state fMRI regional activity/connectivity features across 360 brain regions to distinguish children with intermittent exotropia from healthy controls.
headline_result: AUC 0.957 (training), 0.804 (validation), 0.818 (test)

title: MRI-based deep learning with clinical and imaging features to differentiate medulloblastoma and ependymoma in children.
patient_population: 201 patients across three study centers
clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children, tumors that are difficult to distinguish clinically
model_description: A fine-tuned AlexNet-based deep learning classifier applied to T2-weighted MRI is fused with clinical and imaging features via a decision-tree model to differentiate medulloblastoma from ependymoma.
headline_result: Fusion model AUC 0.987 (train) / 0.889 (test), versus 0.712/0.689 for the imaging-only DL model

title: Comparison of bone age assessment using manual Greulich and Pyle method versus automated BoneXpert method in South African children.
model_family: automated bone age software (image analysis algorithm)
patient_population: 260 left hand-wrist radiographs of South African children with various pediatric endocrinology diagnoses
clinical_problem: Compare automated (BoneXpert) versus manual (Greulich-Pyle) bone age assessment methods in children with pediatric endocrinology diagnoses
model_description: BoneXpert automatically analyzes hand-wrist radiographs to compute a composite (carpal + tubular bone) bone age score, compared against the manual Greulich-Pyle method performed by three independent readers.
release_evidence: BoneXpert software performed automated bone age assessment
headline_result: ICC between Manual BA and BoneXpert BA = 0.982; best-fit composite weighting: 50% carpal, 50% tubular bones

title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence noise reduction tool for conventional X-ray imaging - a visual grading study of pediatric chest examinations at different radiation dose levels using anthropomorphic phantoms.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: anthropomorphic phantoms simulating pediatric chest radiography, multiple dose levels
clinical_problem: improving image quality or allowing radiation dose reduction for pediatric chest radiography using an AI noise-reduction tool
model_description: An AI-based intelligent noise-reduction algorithm is applied to conventional pediatric chest radiographs across a range of radiation dose levels and graded by pediatric radiologists using visual grading characteristics analysis.
headline_result: Image quality significantly better with INR at dose levels >=80% versus standard-dose reference

title: CLIF-Net: Intersection-Guided Cross-View Fusion Network for Infection Detection From Cranial Ultrasound.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: cross-view fusion convolutional neural network (dual-branch with cross-attention)
patient_population: newborn infants undergoing cranial ultrasound at Mbale Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda
clinical_problem: detecting possible serious bacterial infection in newborns using multi-view cranial ultrasound images
model_description: Input: paired coronal and sagittal cranial ultrasound images; output: intersection-guided cross-view fusion network combining both views to classify possible serious bacterial infection vs. non-infection.
study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation study
headline_result: CLIF-Net demonstrated substantially enhanced performance over prevailing state-of-the-art infection detection techniques (no single numeric metric stated)

title: SegQC: a segmentation network-based framework for multi-metric segmentation quality control and segmentation error detection in volumetric medical images.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 198 fetal MRI scans
clinical_problem: Automatically estimate segmentation quality and detect segmentation errors in fetal MRI structures to support clinical QC and model development
model_description: SegQCNet, a deep network, takes a scan and its segmentation mask and outputs voxel-wise segmentation error probabilities, from which quality metrics and error-region localization are computed for fetal brain, fetal body, and placenta segmentations, compared against expert radiologist corrections.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and benchmarking study
headline_result: Segmentation error detection recall/precision: 0.77/0.48 (fetal body), 0.74/0.55 (fetal brain); outperformed TTA- and autoencoder-based QC methods

title: Validity of ChatGPT in Assisting Diagnosis of Periventricular-Intraventricular Hemorrhage via Cranial Ultrasound Imaging in Very Preterm Infants.
patient_population: 35 very preterm infants in a Vietnamese NICU
clinical_problem: Diagnose periventricular-intraventricular hemorrhage from cranial ultrasound images in very preterm infants
model_description: Takes cranial ultrasound images (coronal and sagittal views) with a standardized diagnostic prompt into ChatGPT-4o, which outputs a diagnosis of periventricular-intraventricular hemorrhage, compared against pediatric radiologist interpretation.
release_evidence: ChatGPT-4o (OpenAI, San Francisco, USA), an artificial intelligence model
dataset_size: 35 very preterm infants (16 PV-IVH cases, 19 controls)
headline_result: Sensitivity 75% (12/16), specificity 84.2% (16/19), AUC 0.796, kappa 0.595 vs pediatric radiologists

title: Impact of test set composition on AI performance in pediatric wrist fracture detection in X-rays.
patient_population: Children with wrist radiographs from the open-source GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset
clinical_problem: Whether AI models for pediatric wrist fracture detection perform as well on realistically difficult cases as on randomly sampled test cases
model_description: EfficientNet (classification) and YOLOv11 (detection) models trained on pediatric wrist radiographs are evaluated on two different test-set sampling strategies (random vs. difficulty-balanced) to measure real-world performance drop
headline_result: YOLOv11 precision dropped from 0.95 (random test set) to 0.83 (balanced, harder test set)

title: Potential of Artificial Intelligence for Bone Age Assessment in Iranian Children and Adolescents: An Exploratory Study.
patient_population: 555 hand radiographs (220 boys, 335 girls) of children aged 1-18 years at a tertiary research hospital
clinical_problem: Assessing skeletal maturity (bone age) from hand radiographs in children
model_description: A deep learning model takes left-hand radiographs as input and outputs an estimated bone age in years, benchmarked against Greulich-Pyle reference assessment.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal validation
headline_result: MAE 0.59y (boys) / 0.61y (girls); ICC 0.74 (boys) / 0.82 (girls)

title: Machine learning models for estimating fetal weight based on ultrasonographic biometry: Development and validation study.
model_family: machine learning (Gradient Boosting, SVM, Random Forest, TabPFN)
patient_population: 3,525 low-risk singleton pregnancies at the National Maternal Perinatal Institute of Peru, 2009-2022
clinical_problem: Estimate fetal weight from ultrasonographic biometric measurements using machine learning, compared to traditional Hadlock and Shepard formulas
model_description: Trains machine learning models (Gradient Boosting, SVM, Random Forest, TabPFN) on ultrasonographic biometric measurements (biparietal diameter, abdominal circumference, head circumference, femur length, gestational age) to estimate fetal weight, validated against actual outcomes and compared to Hadlock and Shepard formulas.
study_design: retrospective observational model development and temporal validation study

title: Evaluation of radiomics as an assistant tool for radiologists in the diagnosis of necrotizing enterocolitis.

headline_result: AUC 0.82 (train), 0.74 (test), 0.71 (temporal validation); more sensitive than radiologists in temporal validation (P=0.003)

title: Assessing fetal lung maturity: Integration of ultrasound radiomics and deep learning.
patient_population: 263 pregnancies
clinical_problem: Predicting fetal lung maturity from prenatal ultrasound
model_description: Combines radiomic features from prenatal ultrasound images with clinical data using deep learning (DenseNet121) to predict fetal lung maturity.

title: Evaluation of synthetic images derived from a neural network in pediatric brain magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Morphometric and radiomics analysis toward the prediction of epilepsy associated with supratentorial low-grade glioma in children.

venue_label: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society

title: Bone Age Estimation of Chinese Han Adolescents's and Children's Elbow Joint X-rays Based on Multiple Deep Convolutional Neural Network Models.

title: Multimodal MRI radiomics enhances epilepsy prediction in pediatric low-grade glioma patients.

title: An X-ray bone age assessment method for hands and wrists of adolescents in Western China based on feature fusion deep learning models.

clinical_problem: Estimating bone/skeletal age from hand-wrist radiographs to determine legal age boundaries in adolescents

title: An interpretable deep learning approach for autism spectrum disorder detection in children using NASNet-mobile.

clinical_problem: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder from structural brain MRI
model_description: A NASNet-Mobile deep learning model with LIME explainability takes structural brain MRI as input and classifies whether a child has autism spectrum disorder.
study_design: retrospective model development using a public dataset
headline_result: Accuracy 0.9607, F1 0.9614 (2-11y group)

title: Classification of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Curvature Using Contrastive Clustering.
patient_population: 1156 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis who underwent deformity correction surgery
clinical_problem: Classifying spinal curve patterns in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis to inform surgical planning

headline_result: interobserver kappa 0.701-0.731; silhouette score 0.308

title: Automated ventricular segmentation in pediatric hydrocephalus: how close are we?
model_name: FastSurfer and QuickNAT (existing whole-brain segmentation tools evaluated)
patient_population: 40 scans from 32 pediatric patients (age 0-18 years) with hydrocephalus
clinical_problem: Evaluating the accuracy of automated whole-brain segmentation tools for measuring lateral ventricle volume in children with hydrocephalus, compared to manual segmentation

headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.61 for both FastSurfer and QuickNAT; younger age and larger ventricular volume significantly associated with lower Dice scores

title: Deep Learning Image Reconstruction (DLIR) Algorithm to Maintain High Image Quality and Diagnostic Accuracy in Quadruple-low CT Angiography of Children with Pulmonary Sequestration: A Case Control Study.

model_description: A deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm reconstructs quadruple-low-dose CT angiography images to maintain diagnostic image quality while reducing radiation and contrast dose in children with suspected pulmonary sequestration.

title: Using machine learning models based on cardiac magnetic resonance parameters to predict the prognostic in children with myocarditis.

patient_population: 77 pediatric patients with myocarditis, 2020-2023

title: Alterations of white matter functional networks in pediatric drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy: A graph theory analysis study.

clinical_problem: Classifying children with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy from white matter functional connectivity

clinical_problem: Diagnosing acute bilirubin encephalopathy in neonates with hyperbilirubinemia

study_design: retrospective observational study using automated MRI segmentation, dHCP cohort

headline_result: AUC 0.819 (SVM classification)

title: Optimizing MRI sequence classification performance: insights from domain shift analysis.

clinical_problem: Provide an annotated dataset to support AI-based pelvic X-ray quality evaluation and developmental dysplasia of the hip diagnosis

study_design: prospective data collection, retrospective model development
headline_result: Accuracy 98%, Dice 0.97 (SegNet); 92.5%/91.2% accuracy vs industry experts for BPD/HC

title: Transforming 3D MRI to 2D Feature Maps Using Pre-Trained Models for Diagnosis of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder.

The best-performing LSTM model combined MRI-derived features with clinical attributes.
headline_result: LSTM model accuracy 0.86, AUC 0.90

title: Ensemble learning of deep CNN models and two stage level prediction of Cobb angle on surface topography in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis.

headline_result: MAE 6.13 degrees, RMSE 7.5 degrees (EfficientNetB0); severity classification precision 84.62%

headline_result: SGA detection 70% (DL) vs 58% (Hadlock); LGA detection 55% (DL) vs 41% (Hadlock), p<0.001

title: Efficient feature extraction using light-weight CNN attention-based deep learning architectures for ultrasound fetal plane classification.

dataset_size: largest benchmark fetal-plane ultrasound dataset (size not stated in abstract)
