dataset_size: 31 AIS patients, high-resolution CT covering cervical to lumbar spine
headline_result: U-Net Dice 92.2 ± 2.4% (HD 9.80 ± 1.34 mm); Attention U-Net Dice 92.3 ± 2.9% (HD 8.67 ± 3.38 mm), with Attention U-Net significantly better HD in mid-thoracic scoliosis sites (P = .027)

title: RNN-AHF Framework: Enhancing Multi-focal Nature of Hypoxic Ischemic Encephalopathy Lesion Region in MRI Image Using Optimized Rough Neural Network Weight and Anti-Homomorphic Filter.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Artificial Intelligence Model Assisting Thyroid Nodule Diagnosis and Management: Pilot Results for Evaluating Thyroid Malignancy in Pediatric Cohorts.

headline_result: AUROC 0.913-0.929, sensitivity 78.7-89.4%, specificity 79.8-91.7%; outperformed ACR-TIRADS and K-TIRADS (p<0.05)

title: Assessing the association between ADHD and brain maturation in late childhood and emotion regulation in early adolescence.
model_family: machine learning (brain age prediction algorithm, unspecified)

headline_result: Greater brain-PAD predicted greater expressive suppression (b=0.172, p_FDR=0.004); marginal R²=0.020

title: Upper Airway Volume Predicts Brain Structure and Cognition in Adolescents.
journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
venue_label: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

patient_population: large fetal ultrasound image collection (size not specified)

title: OSAM-NET: A multi-feature fusion model for measuring fetal head flexion during labor with transformer multi-head self-attention.

venue_label: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society

title: Radiomics-based prediction of pathological subtypes in peripheral neuroblastic tumors using 123I-MIBG SPECT/CT imaging: an observational study.

title: Comparative accuracy of two commercial AI algorithms for musculoskeletal trauma detection in emergency radiographs.
model_family: two commercial deep learning fracture detection algorithms
patient_population: 998 emergency musculoskeletal radiographs (585 normal, 413 abnormal) covering adults and children

The shared weakness is the useful finding: subtle abnormalities made up about two-thirds of both algorithms' false negatives but under a fifth of their true positives.

title: Machine learning-assisted classification of hip conditions in pediatric cerebral palsy patients using migration percentage measurements.

Regression activation mapping identifies brain regions, including the caudate, amygdala, parahippocampal gyrus, and hippocampus, most predictive of irritability.

title: Lightweight deep learning system for automated bone age assessment in Chinese children: enhancing clinical efficiency and diagnostic accuracy.

clinical_problem: Automated bone age assessment in Chinese children for growth disorder evaluation
model_description: A two-stage lightweight deep learning framework (YOLOv8 for epiphysis localization, modified EfficientNetB3 for grade classification) automatically assesses bone age from hand radiographs per the Chinese 05 standard.
headline_result: 80.3% train / 81.5% test accuracy; epiphysis localization mAP 99.5%

title: Longitudinal image-based prediction of surgical intervention in infants with hydronephrosis using deep learning: Is a single ultrasound enough?
patient_population: 794 patients (603 SickKids, 102 Stanford, 89 CHOP)
clinical_problem: Predicting need for pyeloplasty (surgery) in infants with hydronephrosis from renal ultrasound images
model_description: Deep learning models (single-visit and multi-visit, using convolutional pooling, LSTM, and temporal shift architectures) predict risk of surgical intervention (pyeloplasty) for hydronephrosis from kidney ultrasound images across multiple clinic visits.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional model development and external validation

title: Comparative Analysis of Atlas and Neural Network Autosegmentation Methods for Pediatric Craniospinal Irradiation With the Development of a Knowledge-Based Quality Assurance Tool.

model_description: Atlas-based, commercial AI, and in-house neural network autosegmentation methods take planning CT scans as input and output contours for 13 organs at risk in pediatric craniospinal irradiation; a companion kernel-density-estimation quality-assurance tool flags autosegmentation errors by comparing CT number distributions per organ to a baseline.
study_design: retrospective comparison study with a companion QA-tool development
dataset_size: 63 CSI patients for autosegmentation comparison; 100 CSI patients for QA tool baseline, tested on 50 cases
headline_result: In-house AI outperformed Atlas and commercial AI in overlap and distance metrics (e.g., overlap improvement of 0.01-0.02); QA tool achieved 100% agreement with baseline in 60.7% of in-house AI tests vs ~46% for Atlas/commercial AI

title: Toward a fair, gender-debiased classifier for the diagnosis of attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder- a Machine-Learning based classification study.

venue_label: BMC medical informatics and decision making
model_family: XGBoost classifier with AI Fairness 360 bias-mitigation/reweighing algorithms
patient_population: 400 children and adolescents with and without ADHD (98 females: 25 ADHD, 73 typically developing), a subsample of the Child Mind Institute dataset

Multiple bias-mitigation algorithms from the AI Fairness 360 toolbox reduce a previously reported gender disparity in ADHD diagnosis; a reweighed XGBoost model achieved the best accuracy and fairness, tested on an independently acquired test set from an earlier study.
study_design: retrospective classification study with an external test set
dataset_size: 400 children and adolescents (98 females: 25 ADHD, 73 typically developing)
headline_result: Reweighed XGBoost model achieved the best accuracy and highest fairness among tested bias-mitigation approaches on both fMRI and structural MRI datasets

title: Attend-and-Refine: Interactive keypoint estimation and quantitative cervical vertebrae analysis for bone age assessment.

patient_population: Pediatric orthodontic patients (cephalometric radiograph datasets)
clinical_problem: Estimating skeletal growth potential (cervical vertebral maturation) in pediatric orthodontic patients from lateral cephalometric radiographs
model_description: ARNet, a user-interactive deep learning model, identifies cervical vertebra keypoints on lateral cephalometric radiographs to assess cervical vertebral maturation and growth potential for orthodontic treatment timing.
study_design: retrospective model development, validated across multiple datasets

title: Multi-Modal and Multi-View Fusion Classifier for Craniosynostosis Diagnosis.
journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
venue_label: Studies in health technology and informatics
patient_population: 294 pediatric patients (882 X-ray images)
clinical_problem: Diagnosing craniosynostosis in infants using multi-view X-rays instead of CT, to reduce radiation exposure
model_description: A deep learning model with multi-view fusion and cross-attention combines three X-ray views (AP, lateral right, lateral left) and patient metadata (age, sex) to detect craniosynostosis, using Grad-CAM to localize relevant cranial-suture regions.
headline_result: AUROC 0.975, F1 0.882, sensitivity 0.878, specificity 0.937

title: Automatic Multi-Stage Classification Model for Fetal Ultrasound Images Based on EfficientNet.
journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
venue_label: Studies in health technology and informatics
patient_population: Fetal/newborn ultrasound images across early, midterm, and newborn stages (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: Improving automatic classification of fetal ultrasound images across pregnancy stages to support clinical workflow.
model_description: A convolutional neural network (EfficientNet) classifies fetal ultrasound images collected at different pregnancy stages (early, midterm, newborn) into diagnostic categories to support clinical workflow.
headline_result: EfficientNet showed the best classification performance, particularly at the newborn stage (no numeric accuracy given)

title: CLIF-Net: Intersection-guided Cross-view Fusion Network for Infection Detection from Cranial Ultrasound.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
model_name: CLIF-Net (intersection-guided Cross-view Local- and Image-level Fusion Network)
patient_population: 302 cranial ultrasound scans of newborn infants from Mbale Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda
clinical_problem: Detecting possible serious bacterial infection (sepsis) in newborns using cranial ultrasound imaging.
model_description: CLIF-Net uses two CNN branches with cross-attention-based multi-level fusion to combine coronal and sagittal cranial ultrasound views (exploiting their geometric intersection) and output a classification of possible serious bacterial infection (pSBI) versus non-pSBI in newborns.
headline_result: CLIF-Net demonstrated substantially enhanced performance over prevailing state-of-the-art infection detection techniques (numeric metrics not given)

title: A Cohort Study of Pediatric Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia Involving AI-Based CT Image Parameters and Electronic Health Record Data.
model_family: AI-derived imaging indices with logistic regression
patient_population: 230 children hospitalized with severe community-acquired pneumonia
clinical_problem: predicting respiratory failure in children with severe community-acquired pneumonia
model_description: AI-derived quantitative indices from chest CT (e.g., number and laterality of involved lung lobes) are combined with electronic health record data in logistic regression models to predict respiratory failure in children with severe pneumonia.
headline_result: Model 2 sensitivity 84.3%, specificity 59.8% at optimal cutoff (AUC not explicitly stated)

title: Brain ultrasound radiomics identify textural differences in basal ganglia and white matter between full term newborns HIV-exposed uninfected and HIV-unexposed in Botswana.
patient_population: 33 full-term newborns (20 HIV-exposed uninfected, 13 HIV-unexposed) in Botswana
clinical_problem: Identifying early neurodevelopmental imaging biomarkers in newborns using brain ultrasound texture (radiomic) analysis, comparing HIV-exposed-uninfected and HIV-unexposed infants
model_description: Radiomic texture features (first-order statistics, run-length, co-occurrence matrices) are extracted from basal ganglia and white matter regions on brain ultrasound and combined via logistic regression to distinguish HIV-exposed-uninfected from HIV-unexposed newborns as an early neurodevelopmental biomarker.
headline_result: white matter model AUC 0.76, sensitivity 0.86

title: Parental and carer views on the use of AI in imaging for children: a national survey.
body_region: not specified (general pediatric imaging, e.g. fractures)
patient_population: 146 parents/carers of children, UK national survey
clinical_problem: Exploring parent/carer acceptance and preferences regarding AI-assisted interpretation of pediatric imaging (e.g., fracture radiographs).
study_design: national online survey of parents/carers on AI in pediatric imaging
headline_result: 64% believed AI more accurate than clinicians at interpreting paediatric musculoskeletal radiographs; 71% wanted consent before AI use

title: Sex Differences in Functional Gradients and Dynamic Functional Connectivity in Preschool-Aged Children With ASD.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 54 children with ASD (40 boys, 14 girls) and 44 typically developing children (28 boys, 16 girls), aged 2-6 years
clinical_problem: characterizing sex differences in brain network organization in preschool autism spectrum disorder
model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional gradient and dynamic functional connectivity features from preschool-aged children are used to train multiple machine learning classifiers to distinguish ASD from typically developing children, separately for boys and girls.
headline_result: classification performance evaluated for ASD vs TD (specific accuracy not given in abstract)

title: Artificial intelligence-based prenatal ultrasound for diagnosing fetal lip and palate during the second trimester.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
venue_label: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
patient_population: 700 fetuses at 20-24 weeks gestation, single center
clinical_problem: automatically identifying standard ultrasound cross-sectional planes of the fetal lip and palate to aid second-trimester screening for cleft lip/palate
model_description: A YOLOv5-based object-detection AI model automatically classifies standard versus nonstandard ultrasound cross-sectional images of the fetal lip and palate, compared against sonographers of differing experience levels.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development with reader comparison
headline_result: AUC 0.971-0.988 (AI) vs 0.824-0.939 (sonographers) across standard fetal facial views

title: Brain-wide associations of reaction time variability in the ABCD study.
patient_population: 8,066 children aged 9-10 years from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
clinical_problem: Characterizing trial-level intra-individual variability in reaction time (a marker of impaired attention) from functional MRI during a Stop-Signal Task in children.
model_description: A hidden Markov model is applied to Stop-Signal Task fMRI data to compute, on a trial-by-trial basis, the probability of a child being in a 'good' versus 'poor' attentional state, as one of several methods for modeling intra-individual reaction-time variability and its associated brain activation patterns.
study_design: cross-sectional analysis of ABCD Study fMRI data
headline_result: Z-score-based modeling of IIVRT showed the strongest effect sizes in task-related networks (lower IIVRT associated with greater default mode network activation, higher IIVRT with greater dorsal attention network activation)

title: Streamline tractography of the fetal brain in utero with machine learning.
patient_population: fetuses (11 test subjects, gestational ages 23-36 weeks); additional generalization testing on Developing Human Connectome Project data
clinical_problem: fetal brain tractography for studying white matter development in utero
model_description: A deep neural network predicts streamline propagation for fetal brain tractography, taking as input diffusion tensor fiber orientation, prior propagation directions, spatial distance-to-cortex encodings, tissue segmentation, and an atlas-based orientation prior; anatomically constrained filtering rules prune implausible streamlines.
study_design: technical development with independent test-set validation
dataset_size: manually-refined whole-brain fetal tractograms for training; 11 independent test subjects (23-36 weeks GA)
headline_result: superior performance across all evaluated tracts vs comparison methods (no single metric given)

title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Pediatric Bone-Age Assessment: A Comparative Accuracy Analysis.
model_family: closed-source multimodal large language models, used without task-specific training
patient_population: 180 left-hand wrist radiographs of children aged 0-18 from the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age dataset
clinical_problem: whether a general-purpose chatbot can substitute for dedicated bone age software, which is expensive
model_description: A clean negative result, and a useful one. Three general multimodal chatbots were asked to read bone age directly from the radiograph with no fine-tuning. They can do it, in the sense of producing plausible numbers, but errors of two to three years and limits of agreement beyond four and a half years put them nowhere near clinical or medico-legal use. Worth citing whenever someone proposes a general chatbot in place of dedicated software.
dataset_size: 180 radiographs from the public RSNA dataset
headline_result: best model (Gemini 2.5 Pro) mean absolute error 28.5 months; all models had 95% limits of agreement exceeding ±4.5 years

title: MRI-Based Radiomics for Outcome Stratification in Pediatric Osteosarcoma.
patient_population: 63 pediatric osteosarcoma patients (plus 9 external validation cases), mean age 11.8+/-3.5 years
clinical_problem: Predicting progressive disease, therapy response, relapse, and survival in pediatric osteosarcoma using MRI-based radiomics
model_description: Machine learning classifiers combine MRI-based radiomic features (from whole-tumor, tumor-sampling, and bone/soft-tissue segmentations) with clinical features to predict progressive disease, therapy response, relapse, and survival in pediatric osteosarcoma.
headline_result: validation ROC AUC 0.94-1.0; testing ROC AUC 0.63-1.0

title: Equivariant spherical CNNs for accurate fiber orientation distribution estimation in neonatal diffusion MRI with reduced acquisition time.
patient_population: 43 neonatal diffusion MRI datasets from the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP)
clinical_problem: Estimating brain white-matter fiber orientation from diffusion MRI in neonates using fewer gradient directions, to enable faster, cheaper scans for identifying neurodevelopmental disorders.
model_description: A rotationally equivariant spherical CNN takes reduced-gradient-direction (30% of full protocol) multi-shell diffusion MRI signals from neonates as input and predicts the full Fiber Orientation Distribution (FOD), enabling faster acquisitions while preserving tractography quality.
study_design: retrospective methods-development study using dHCP data
headline_result: sCNN significantly outperformed an MLP baseline on MSE, PSNR, angular correlation coefficient, angular error, and peak match rate, with FODs/tractography comparable to a Hybrid-CSD ground truth using only 30% of the full acquisition

title: Improving skull-stripping for infant MRI via weakly supervised domain adaptation using adversarial learning.
model_family: adversarial domain adaptation network (weakly supervised, GAN-based)
patient_population: Newborn brain MRI from the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP), a private newborn dataset, and synthetic data (patient counts not stated)
clinical_problem: Improving skull-stripping (removing non-brain tissue) on newborn brain MRI, which is complicated by the strong domain shift between adult and newborn brain images.
model_description: A weakly supervised adversarial domain-adaptation network, expanded with dHCP data, a private newborn dataset, and GMM-generated synthetic data, takes newborn brain MRI as input and outputs a skull-stripped (brain-only) segmentation mask, generalizing across adult, synthetic, public and private newborn MRI domains.
headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.9509 ± 0.0055 and Hausdorff distance 3.0883 ± 0.1833 for newborn MRI, surpassing SynthStrip (Dice 0.9412 ± 0.0063, Hausdorff 3.1570 ± 0.1389)

title: MCBL-UNet: A Hybrid Mamba-CNN Boundary Enhanced Light-weight UNet for Placenta Ultrasound Image Segmentation.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
patient_population: Multiple medical ultrasound datasets (placenta, gestational sac, thyroid nodules); sizes not stated
clinical_problem: Accurately segmenting the placental contour on ultrasound, which is difficult due to image noise, fuzzy boundaries, and limited clinical resources.
model_description: MCBL-UNet, a compact 6-layer U-Net combining Mamba's long-range modeling with CNN local feature extraction, boundary-enhancement, global-context, and attention modules, takes ultrasound images as input and outputs a segmentation mask of the placenta (and gestational sac/thyroid nodules).
headline_result: MCBL-UNet outperformed 13 existing mainstream segmentation methods on Dice coefficient and mIoU using only 1.31M parameters and 1.26G FLOPs

title: Cumulative impacts of early life adversity and persistent/recurrent pain in children: A longitudinal normative modelling study from the ABCD Study cohort.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: 1,671 children from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study cohort, baseline and 2-year follow-up
clinical_problem: Whether early life adversity and persistent/recurrent pain have combined effects on brain structure in children, and whether these can be distinguished by structural MRI.
model_description: A support vector machine is applied to structural MRI measures (subcortical volume, cortical thickness, surface area) to classify children into control, persistent/recurrent-pain-only, early-life-adversity-only, and combined-exposure groups.
study_design: longitudinal normative modelling study using ABCD Study data (preprint)
headline_result: Support vector machine models classified group status with at best 66.8% accuracy using all brain measures

title: Deep learning approach for screening neonatal cerebral lesions on ultrasound in China.
patient_population: 8,757 neonatal cranial ultrasound images
clinical_problem: Automated screening and diagnosis of severe neonatal cerebral lesions on cranial ultrasound to support timely diagnosis.
model_description: A deep-learning system automatically extracts standard views from cranial ultrasound video and classifies whether severe cerebral lesions are present.
study_design: retrospective multi-center algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: AUC 0.982 (internal), 0.944 (external); sensitivity 0.875/0.962; outperforms junior radiologists, 55.11% faster

title: Detection of neonatal pneumoperitoneum on radiographs using deep multi-task learning.

patient_population: 204 neonates (546 radiographs) internal; 378 radiographs external (125 pneumoperitoneum cases) from 11 NICUs
clinical_problem: Diagnosing neonatal pneumoperitoneum on abdominal radiographs
model_description: A deep multi-task learning model combining classification and segmentation detects neonatal pneumoperitoneum on radiographs, evaluated with and without AI assistance for readers of varying experience.
release_evidence: All code is available at https://github.com/brody9512/NEC_MTL.
study_design: retrospective multicenter diagnostic study with reader study
dataset_size: 204 neonates (546 radiographs) internal; 378 radiographs external (11 NICUs)
headline_result: internal AUC 0.98, external AUC 0.89; AI assistance improved reader accuracy from 82.5% to 86.6%

title: DCE-UNet: a transformer-based fully automated segmentation network for multiple adolescent spinal disorders in x-ray images.
patient_population: Self-constructed large-scale multi-disease adolescent spinal X-ray dataset
clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting spinal lesions across multiple adolescent spinal disorders on X-ray to support computer-aided diagnosis
model_description: DCE-UNet, a hybrid CNN-Transformer segmentation network, automatically segments lesion regions across multiple adolescent spinal disorders in X-ray images.
headline_result: Dice 91.3%, mIoU 84.1, Hausdorff Distance 4.007

title: Validation of an artificial intelligence-based automated PRAGMA and mucus plugging algorithm in pediatric cystic fibrosis.
journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
venue_label: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
publication_types: Journal Article; Validation Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

clinical_problem: Automating chest CT scoring of structural airway damage (bronchiectasis, airway wall thickening, mucus plugging) in pediatric cystic fibrosis, replacing time-consuming visual PRAGMA-CF scoring
model_description: An automated AI algorithm (PRAGMA-AI) analyzes inspiratory chest CT scans of children with cystic fibrosis to quantify percent bronchiectasis, percent disease, airway wall thickening and mucus plugging, validated against the visual PRAGMA-CF reference score
headline_result: Strong correlation with visual PRAGMA-CF for %bronchiectasis, %disease and %mucus plugging; weak correlation for %airway wall thickening

title: Predictive model integrating deep learning and clinical features based on ultrasound imaging data for surgical intervention in intussusception in children younger than 8 months.

model_description: Deep transfer-learning features extracted from abdominal ultrasound images (via pretrained networks and LASSO feature selection) are combined with clinical variables in a logistic regression model to predict which infants with intussusception will require surgery after enema reduction, validated in an external-center and a prospective cohort.
study_design: retrospective model development with external and prospective validation
dataset_size: 415 cases: 280 from Centre 1 (training/internal validation), 85 external validation (Centre 2), 50 prospective validation
headline_result: combined model AUC 0.911 (internal), 0.871 (external), 0.890 (prospective)

title: Development and validation of a keypoint region-based convolutional neural network to automate thoracic Cobb angle measurements using whole-spine standing radiographs.

clinical_problem: automated thoracic Cobb angle measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis screening
model_description: A keypoint region-based CNN is trained on whole-spine standing radiographs to automatically identify landmark keypoints and calculate the thoracic Cobb angle, intended to support scoliosis screening where a trained radiologist may not be available.
dataset_size: 609 training radiographs; 83-patient institutional AIS registry (pre/postoperative) for validation
headline_result: MAE 2.22°, MSE 9.1, SMAPE 4.29%, ICC 0.98

title: Predicting pediatric age from chest X-rays using deep learning: a novel approach.
patient_population: 128,008 pediatric chest X-rays from two tertiary hospitals in Shanghai
clinical_problem: Estimating pediatric age from chest radiographs as a complement to bone age assessment, to help screen for abnormal growth and development
model_description: A ResNet-based deep neural network with a Coordinate Attention mechanism predicts pediatric age directly from chest radiographs, using heatmap visualization to identify the anatomic regions (spine, mediastinum, heart) driving the prediction.
study_design: retrospective model development with internal and external validation
headline_result: MAE 5.86 (M)/5.80 (F) months internal; 7.40/7.29 months external; Spearman r>0.98

title: Machine learning-based method for the detection of dextrocardia in ultrasound video clips.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
venue_label: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
patient_population: 142 pairs of Situs/4CH ultrasound images for training; 14 ultrasound videos (7 normal, 7 dextrocardia) for testing
clinical_problem: Automatically detecting dextrocardia (a congenital anomaly) from routine fetal ultrasound sweeps.

study_design: retrospective model development and internal test-set evaluation
dataset_size: 142 pairs of Situs/4CH images (training); 14 ultrasound videos, 2,916 frames total (testing)
headline_result: Dice scores 0.968/0.958/0.953/0.949 for chest/spine/stomach/heart segmentation; dextrocardia classification score (FBCS) of 0.99

title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Predicting Adverse Clinical Outcomes in Placenta Accreta Spectrum: A Multicenter Study.

patient_population: 125 clinically confirmed PAS patients from two centers
clinical_problem: Predicting adverse clinical outcomes (major hemorrhage, hysterectomy) in placenta accreta spectrum using MRI morphological indicators and clinical features

study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation
headline_result: CatBoost AUROC 0.90 internal, 0.84 external

title: Evaluation of Bladder Dysfunction Outcomes Among Standardized Bladder Shapes in Children With Spina Bifida.
patient_population: 417 pediatric and adolescent patients with spina bifida who underwent video urodynamics, median age 2.6 years
clinical_problem: Whether bladder shape on fluoroscopic imaging is associated with filling pressures and bladder dysfunction in children with spina bifida, and standardizing bladder-shape terminology.

title: TransSeg: Leveraging Transformer With Channel-Wise Attention and Semantic Memory for Semi-Supervised Ultrasound Segmentation.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: FH-PS-AoP transperineal ultrasound dataset (size not stated)

title: Deep adversarial learning identifies ADHD-specific associations between apoptotic genes and white matter microstructure in frontal-striatum-cerebellum circuit.

patient_population: 600 Chinese children with ADHD and typically developing controls
clinical_problem: identifying ADHD-specific gene-white matter microstructure associations using diffusion tensor imaging and genotype data

Interpretable deep learning analysis then identifies which white matter regions and genes contribute to ADHD-specific versus non-specific associations.
study_design: cross-sectional case-control cohort study, technical development
dataset_size: 600 children (ADHD and typically developing), Chinese cohort

title: Comparison of BoneXpert and IB-Lab-PANDA automated Bone Age Evaluation in Children With Growth and Puberty Disorders.
patient_population: 521 left-hand radiographs of children aged 2-19 years
clinical_problem: comparing agreement between two commercial automated bone-age assessment programs in children with growth and puberty disorders
model_description: Two commercially available AI bone-age assessment programs, BoneXpert and IB-Lab-PANDA, are compared against each other and against manual Greulich-Pyle ratings on hand radiographs, across age, sex, puberty and diagnosis subgroups.
release_evidence: BoneXpert(R) and IB-Lab-PANDA(R) described as commercially available AI bone age assessment programs
dataset_size: 521 radiographs (213 compared to manual Greulich-Pyle reference)

title: Machine Learning and Feature Selection in Pediatric Appendicitis.
model_family: random forest, logistic regression, LightGBM, GANDALF
patient_population: 781 pediatric patients aged 0-18, 2016-2023, single center (Germany)
clinical_problem: predicting diagnosis, management and severity of pediatric appendicitis using clinical and ultrasound data
model_description: Multiple machine learning models (random forest, logistic regression, LightGBM, and a tabular deep learner GANDALF), paired with various feature-selection methods, predict pediatric appendicitis diagnosis, management and severity, evaluated with and without ultrasound image-descriptive features.

title: A Fully Automated Analysis Pipeline for 4D Flow MRI in the Aorta.

dataset_size: 379 subjects, including 75 pediatric patients with hereditary aortic disease

title: Evaluating Hemodynamic Changes in Preterm Infants Using Recent YOLO Models.

title: Quantifying "Medical Renal Disease": A Pediatric Pilot Study Using Ultrasound Radiomics for Differentiating Acute Kidney Injury and Chronic Kidney Disease.

patient_population: 31 pediatric subjects: 8 with oliguric AKI, 14 with CKD, 9 healthy controls
clinical_problem: differentiating acute kidney injury from chronic kidney disease in children

release_evidence: 124 advanced texture features were extracted using the open-source ©PyFeats
headline_result: XGBoost macro-averaged F1 score 0.90

patient_population: early pregnancy fetal brain ultrasound images
clinical_problem: identifying key anatomical brain structures in early-pregnancy fetal ultrasound screening
model_description: FBStrNet, built on a lightweight YOLOv5 backbone with a decoupled detection head and clinical-knowledge-informed false-detection reduction, detects key fetal brain anatomical structures in early-pregnancy ultrasound images in real time (11.5 ms inference) to assist sonographers in anomaly screening.
headline_result: outperforms state-of-the-art methods; inference time 11.5 ms

title: Accuracy of Large Language Models in Detecting Cases Requiring Immediate Reporting in Pediatric Radiology: A Feasibility Study Using Publicly Available Clinical Vignettes.
patient_population: 71 publicly available pediatric clinical vignettes with images
clinical_problem: Using multimodal large language models to detect pediatric radiology cases requiring immediate/urgent reporting, to support worklist prioritization.
model_description: Seven vision-capable multimodal LLMs (e.g., Gemini-Flash) are given pediatric radiology clinical vignette images and classify whether the case requires immediate reporting, compared to human readers.
study_design: feasibility study comparing multimodal LLMs to human readers on public vignettes
headline_result: Gemini-Flash t1 highest accuracy 83.1%, comparable to expert pediatrician (84.5%)

title: Development of a Deep-Learning Model for Estimating Newborn Gestational Age via Lumbar Vertebral Segmentation on Plain Radiography.
model_family: DeepLabv3+ (ResNet50 backbone) for segmentation, AgeClassifier (dual ResNet18) for regression
patient_population: 423 newborns imaged with cross-table lateral radiographs within 24 hours of birth, from two hospitals
clinical_problem: estimating newborn gestational age from plain radiographs
model_description: Cross-table lateral radiographs of newborns are segmented for the five lumbar vertebral bodies using a DeepLabv3+/ResNet50 model, then a dual-ResNet18 AgeClassifier estimates gestational age from vertebral shape; the model was developed at one institution and externally tested at another.
study_design: retrospective model development with external testing
headline_result: segmentation Dice 0.801; GA estimation MAE 5.2±0.5 days; Bland-Altman bias -0.4 days

title: HarmonicEchoNet: Leveraging harmonic convolutions for automated standard plane detection in fetal heart ultrasound videos.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: fetal echocardiography from two private studies (PULSE and CAIFE)
clinical_problem: automated detection of standard fetal echocardiography views to identify congenital heart conditions
model_description: HarmonicEchoNet uses harmonic convolution blocks (DCT-based decomposition) and a harmonic spatial/channel squeeze-and-excitation module to automatically detect standard fetal heart views in transverse-sweep or freehand ultrasound video, aiding acquisition for congenital heart disease screening.
dataset_size: four datasets from two private studies (PULSE, CAIFE)
headline_result: 10-15x faster inference (3.9 ms) and 2-7% accuracy improvement over ConvNeXt/DeiT/VOLO baselines

title: Personalized MRI-based characterization of subcortical anomalies in Ataxia-Telangiectasia using deep-learning.
patient_population: Children and adolescents with ataxia-telangiectasia and healthy children (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: Characterizing basal ganglia and cerebellar abnormalities in ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T), a condition with under-studied extrapyramidal movement dysfunction, at an individual-patient level.
model_description: A normative self-supervised deep autoencoder, trained on diffusion (apparent diffusion coefficient) and perfusion (cerebral blood flow) MRI features from healthy children across seven brain regions, reconstructs these features; higher reconstruction error in A-T patients (interpreted via SHAP) identifies abnormal regions at an individual level.
headline_result: A-T participants showed significantly higher feature-reconstruction errors than controls, with extrapyramidal movement sub-scores correlating with reconstruction error in cerebellar/subcortical structures

title: Role of artificial intelligence in congenital heart disease.
patient_population: Not applicable (mini-review)
clinical_problem: Reviewing how AI can improve diagnosis, management, and long-term monitoring of congenital heart disease, from prenatal screening through postnatal management.
task: detection / diagnosis; outcome prediction; workflow / non-interpretive
model_description: A mini-review describing how AI algorithms applied to fetal echocardiography and postnatal diagnostic imaging can improve prenatal detection, postnatal classification of CHD subtype/severity, hemodynamic assessment, treatment decision support, and remote/wearable monitoring for congenital heart disease.

title: Automated system of analysis to quantify pediatric hip morphology.
model_family: U-Net (six coarse-model and four fine-model variants)
patient_population: Anteroposterior pelvic radiographs of juvenile hips (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: Objectively quantifying juvenile hip morphology to support diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), which currently lacks a reliable assessment metric.
model_description: A coarse-to-fine U-Net-based system detects 22 anatomical landmarks on anteroposterior pelvic radiographs of the juvenile hip, from which novel morphological measurements of hip joint shape are derived to support DDH assessment.
headline_result: Root-mean-square landmark-detection error of 3.79 mm, with bias/precision of 0.03 ± 17.6 mm (x) and 1.76 ± 22.5 mm (y); morphological metric errors comparable to clinical experts

title: FaithfulNet: An explainable deep learning framework for autism diagnosis using structural MRI.
model_family: explainable deep learning (CNN with gradient-based CAM and SHAP)
patient_population: Children from the publicly available ABIDE-II structural MRI repository
clinical_problem: Diagnosing autism from structural brain MRI while also explaining which brain regions drive the diagnosis and relate to academic performance.
model_description: FaithfulNet, a deep learning model trained on structural brain MRI, classifies scans as autistic or typically developing; gradient-based class activation maps and SHAP explanations are combined into a novel 'Faith_CAM' visualization to identify the brain regions (including memory regions linked to academic performance) driving each prediction.
study_design: retrospective model development study using a public dataset
dataset_size: ABIDE-II public structural MRI dataset (size not stated)
headline_result: Classification accuracy of 99.74% with AUC of 1

title: Using deep learning to predict internalizing problems from brain structure in youth.
model_family: deep learning model using structural MRI brain measures
patient_population: youth from four large-scale datasets: ABCD, Healthy Brain Network, HCP-Development, and Province of Ontario Neurodevelopmental network (N=14,523 cross-sectional; N=10,540 longitudinal)
clinical_problem: predicting current and future internalizing problems (anxiety and depression) in youth from structural brain MRI
model_description: Structural MRI measures of cortical thickness, surface area, and volume from four large pediatric neuroimaging datasets are input to deep learning models. One model predicts clinically significant internalizing problems cross-sectionally, and another predicts subsequent worsening of internalizing symptoms longitudinally, using stratified cross-validation and testing in independent held-out and external samples.
study_design: cross-sectional and longitudinal multi-dataset cohort study
headline_result: Cross-sectional model AUC 0.80 [95% CI 0.71-0.88]; longitudinal model AUC 0.66 [0.65-0.67] in the general population, AUC 0.80 [0.78-0.81] in an external test set of primarily neurodevelopmental conditions, AUC 0.73 [0.70-0.76] across all neurodevelopmental conditions

title: From brain to behavior: Psychological resilience mediates associations between whole-brain resting-state connectivity and NSSI.
patient_population: 89 adolescents (46 NSSI-positive, 43 NSSI-negative), age 15.39+/-1.77 years
clinical_problem: Identifying brain connectivity patterns and psychological resilience associated with non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents
model_description: Support vector machine analysis of whole-brain resting-state fMRI connectivity identifies neural correlates of non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents, examining psychological resilience as a mediating factor.

title: Classification of familial and non-familial ADHD using auto-encoding network and binary hypothesis testing.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: 438 children (129 ADHD-familial, 159 ADHD-non-familial, 150 controls)
clinical_problem: Distinguishing familial from non-familial ADHD in children using multimodal brain MRI and deep learning
model_description: An auto-encoder-based deep learning pipeline with feature selection classifies familial versus non-familial ADHD and controls using T1-weighted and diffusion-weighted MRI cortical and white-matter metrics.
headline_result: AUC 0.67 (ADHD-F vs controls), 0.70 (ADHD-NF vs controls), 0.67 (ADHD-F vs ADHD-NF)

title: Method for fetal ultrasound image classification using pseudo-labelling with PCA-KMeans and an attention-augmented MobileNet-LSTM model.
model_family: MobileNet backbone with multi-head attention and LSTM
patient_population: Fetal ultrasound image dataset (size not stated)
clinical_problem: Improving fetal ultrasound image classification for early diagnosis despite limited labeled data and high inter-class variability.
model_description: A hybrid deep learning model (MobileNet backbone with multi-head self-attention and LSTM layers) classifies fetal ultrasound images, trained with pseudo-labels generated by PCA dimensionality reduction and K-means clustering to address limited labeled data.
headline_result: Test accuracy of approximately 98% with a macro-F1 score of 0.98

title: An MRI Atlas of the Human Fetal Brain: Reference and Segmentation Tools for Fetal Brain MRI Analysis.
model_family: diffeomorphic deformable registration with kernel regression; deep learning multiclass segmentation models
patient_population: 160 fetuses with typically-developing brains, 21-37 gestational weeks
clinical_problem: providing a reference atlas and segmentation tools for studying typical/atypical in-utero brain development
model_description: A spatiotemporal (4D) fetal brain MRI atlas (CRL-2025) is built from 160 typically-developing fetal MRI scans via diffeomorphic registration and age-kernel regression, including detailed tissue segmentations and 126-region parcellation, released with deep-learning-based multiclass segmentation models for fine-grained fetal brain MRI segmentation.
release_evidence: these materials are publicly released to support the broader research community
study_design: technical development (atlas construction and tool release)

title: Neuroanatomy Reflects Individual Variability in Impulsivity in Youth.
patient_population: 9,099 youth at baseline, 6,432 at 2-year follow-up, from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
clinical_problem: Identifying neuroanatomical correlates of impulsivity in youth using structural MRI
model_description: Multivariate brain-based predictive models relate neuroanatomical features (cortical thickness, surface area, gray matter volume) from structural MRI to individual differences in impulsivity across behavioral scales in youth from the ABCD Study.

title: Prenatal diagnosis of cerebellar hypoplasia in fetal ultrasound using deep learning under the constraint of the anatomical structures of the cerebellum and cistern.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 302 cases of cerebellar hypoplasia and 549 normal pregnancies, Maternal and Child Health Hospital of Hubei Province, Sept 2019-Sept 2023
clinical_problem: Improving prenatal ultrasound diagnosis of fetal cerebellar hypoplasia, which is difficult due to ultrasound's limited resolution, artifacts, and skull shadowing.
model_description: ASC-Net, a dual-branch deep learning classification network, takes fetal brain ultrasound images and anatomical structure masks (skull, cerebellum, cerebellomedullary cistern boundaries) as separate inputs and outputs a classification of cerebellar hypoplasia versus normal.
release_evidence: ASC-Net is open-sourced and publicly available in a GitHub repository at https://github.com/Wwwwww111112/ASC-Net
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
dataset_size: 302 cerebellar hypoplasia cases and 549 normal pregnancies
headline_result: Classification accuracy 0.9778 and 0.9222, AUC 0.9986 and 0.9265, on two test sets

title: Multi-task learning for classification and prediction of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis based on fringe-projection three-dimensional imaging.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
venue_label: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
patient_population: Adolescents undergoing scoliosis screening/assessment
clinical_problem: Assessing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (Cobb angle, curve type, curve direction) without ionizing radiation
model_description: Multi-task deep learning model takes structured back-surface data from fringe-projection 3D imaging as input and jointly predicts Cobb angle, curve type, and curve direction.
study_design: Retrospective model development and evaluation study
headline_result: MAE 2.9° / RMSE 6.9° for Cobb angle (vs 5.4°/12.5° single-task baseline); R=0.96 vs radiographic measurement

title: Prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia using machine learning from chest X-rays of premature infants in the neonatal intensive care unit.
patient_population: 122 premature infants born ≤28 weeks and <1250 g, NICU, 2020-2021; 395 chest radiographs
clinical_problem: Predicting the severity of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) in premature infants from serial chest radiographs in the NICU.
model_description: A DenseNet121 deep-learning model takes chest radiographs obtained on postnatal day 1 and weeks 2-4 as input and predicts the likelihood of no, mild, moderate, or severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, compared against actual clinical outcomes.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study

title: Biophysically constrained dynamical modelling of the brain using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging.
patient_population: 20 healthy controls and 19 children with leukemia
clinical_problem: Modeling brain functional dynamics and connectivity disruption in children with leukemia using a biophysically constrained neural network derived from multimodal MRI
model_description: BRAINN, an analog electrical neural-network model constrained by biophysical parameters estimated from multimodal MRI (diffusion tractography and functional connectivity), simulates brain dynamics and connectivity to assess disruption before and during leukemia treatment in children.
dataset_size: 39 participants (20 healthy controls, 19 children with leukemia)

title: A Physics-Informed Deep Learning Deformable Medical Image Registration Method Based on Neural ODEs.
patient_population: not stated
clinical_problem: Quantifying fetal brain cortical expansion and growth via deformable image registration for developmental studies
model_description: Physics-informed deep learning registration method (using neural ODEs and growth/remodeling mechanics); one of several applications aligns longitudinal fetal brain MRI to quantify cortical expansion during development (also applied to adult brain atrophy and zebrafish fin regrowth).
study_design: Methods development study with benchmark comparisons across multiple non-clinical and clinical datasets

title: New frontiers in radiologic interpretation: evaluating the effectiveness of large language models in pneumothorax diagnosis.
patient_population: 172 pneumothorax cases (148 patients >12 years, 24 patients <=12 years)
clinical_problem: Diagnostic accuracy of multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, Claude 3.5) for identifying pneumothorax on chest radiographs, by age group and pneumothorax size.
model_description: Three multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, Claude 3.5) are given chest radiographs plus basic symptoms and classify pneumothorax presence, compared across age groups.
headline_result: Pediatric accuracy 12.5-20.8% vs adult 57.4-69.6% (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, Claude 3.5)

title: Visual and Predictive Assessment of Pneumothorax Recurrence in Adolescents Using Machine Learning on Chest CT.
model_family: neural network (best performer among machine learning models compared)
patient_population: 299 adolescents with conservatively managed spontaneous pneumothorax
clinical_problem: predicting recurrence of spontaneous pneumothorax in adolescents
model_description: Machine learning models, including a neural network, are trained on chest CT images from adolescents with spontaneous pneumothorax to predict recurrence, with Grad-CAM used to visually confirm that bleb/bulla presence and apical lung regions drive predictions.
headline_result: neural network AUC 0.970 (right), 0.958 (left)

title: Neurodevelopmental deviations in schizophrenia: Evidences from multimodal connectome-based brain ages.
patient_population: 80 antipsychotic-naive first-episode early-onset schizophrenia patients and 91 typically developing controls
clinical_problem: Characterizing abnormal brain developmental trajectories (brain age) in early-onset schizophrenia using multimodal MRI and machine learning
model_description: Machine learning brain-age estimation models trained on structural, diffusion, and functional MRI connectome features predict individual brain age; the gap between predicted and chronological brain age is compared between early-onset schizophrenia patients and typically developing controls.
headline_result: increased brain age gap in EOS vs TD using structural/morphometric connectome features, correlated with symptom severity

title: Artificial intelligence assisted ultrasound for selective screening of hip dysplasia at children's health care centers in the Netherlands.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
venue_label: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
patient_population: 105 infants (210 hips) at four Child Health Care centers in the Netherlands, May-Dec 2022
clinical_problem: Reducing unnecessary hospital referrals for hip ultrasound in selective screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), without missing cases.
model_description: An AI-assisted point-of-care hip ultrasound tool (CHC-US), usable by a Child Health Care physician, screens infant hips for developmental dysplasia of the hip, with results compared against a formal hospital ultrasound.
headline_result: CHC-US could reduce hip ultrasound referrals by approximately half without missing DDH cases (two apparent misses were reclassified as no DDH on re-evaluation)

title: Sex classification from hand X-ray images in pediatric patients: How zero-shot Segment Anything Model (SAM) can improve medical image analysis.
patient_population: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age dataset (hand X-ray images from pediatric patients)
clinical_problem: Classifying sex from pediatric hand radiographs for forensic and anthropological applications
model_description: Zero-shot Segment Anything Model (SAM) segments pediatric hand radiographs, and deep learning ensemble models classify sex from the segmented hand bone structure and silhouette, with attention-map explainability.
study_design: retrospective model development using a public dataset
headline_result: sex classification accuracy above 95%

title: External validation of predictive models for diagnosis, management and severity of pediatric appendicitis.
patient_population: 430 patients (Regensburg, Germany) for model development; 301 patients (Dusseldorf, Germany) for external validation
clinical_problem: Externally validating machine learning models for diagnosing, staging severity, and guiding management of pediatric appendicitis
model_description: Machine learning models combining demographic, clinical, scoring, laboratory, and ultrasound parameters predict the diagnosis, severity, and management (e.g., surgery) of pediatric appendicitis, externally validated across two independent European hospital cohorts.

title: Widespread associations between behavioral metrics and brain microstructure in ASD suggest age mediates subtypes of ASD.
patient_population: 273 participants (148 with ASD), ages 8-17, NIH Autism Centers of Excellence network
clinical_problem: Using neuroimaging-derived microstructural metrics and machine learning clustering to identify subtypes of autism spectrum disorder related to behavioral profiles.
model_description: Machine learning cluster analysis applied to diffusion MRI-derived microstructural metrics (g-ratio, axonal conduction velocity) and behavioral/cognitive scores identifies subtypes of autism spectrum disorder.
study_design: cross-sectional multi-site cohort study with ML cluster analysis

title: Limited generalizability of dynamic fMRI correlates of adolescent rumination.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
venue_label: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
model_family: dynamic resting-state fMRI predictive models (published adult model, linear DMN/connectome models, exploratory random forest)
patient_population: 443 adolescents (clinical and non-clinical)
clinical_problem: predicting adolescent rumination severity from dynamic resting-state fMRI connectivity
model_description: Dynamic resting-state fMRI connectivity, including default-mode network connections, is used with several predictive models, an adult-derived dynamic connectivity model, linear default-mode-network and whole-brain connectome models, and an exploratory random forest, to predict self-reported trait rumination in the largest adolescent sample studied to date (n=443). None of these models generalized well to held-out or external adolescent data.
release_evidence: Preprint (bioRxiv); no repository or product named, per RECHECK rule for preprints
headline_result: The adult dynamic connectivity model failed to generalize; linear DMN and whole-brain connectome models failed to generalize to held-out data; an exploratory random forest model did not generalize to an external sample with a distinct scanner protocol

title: [Dual-Channel Shoulder Joint X-ray Bone Age Estimation in Chinese Han Adolescents Based on the Fusion of Segmentation Labels and Original Images].
model_family: VGG16, ResNet18, ResNet50, DenseNet121 (CNN) with U-Net++ segmentation
patient_population: 1,286 shoulder joint radiographs from Chinese Han adolescents aged 12.0 to <18.0 years (708 male, 578 female)
clinical_problem: Estimating bone age from shoulder-joint radiographs (an alternative to hand-wrist films) in adolescents.
model_description: Four CNN architectures (VGG16, ResNet18, ResNet50, DenseNet121) estimate bone age from shoulder-joint radiographs, comparing single-channel (original image) versus dual-channel input (original image fused with a U-Net++-segmented shoulder-joint region), against manual bone-age estimation.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study
headline_result: Dual-channel DenseNet121 achieved MAE 0.54 years, RMSE 0.82 years, R² 0.76, PCC 0.88, outperforming manual estimation (MAE 0.82 years)

title: Brain functional connectivity predicts depression and anxiety during childhood and adolescence: A connectome-based predictive modeling approach.
patient_population: ABCD cohort n=3,718 children (9-11y) + BANDA n=150 adolescents (14-17y)
clinical_problem: predicting future depression and anxiety severity in children and adolescents from baseline resting-state brain functional connectivity
model_description: Connectome-based predictive modeling uses baseline whole-brain resting-state functional connectivity MRI as input to predict depression and anxiety symptom severity at 1-year follow-up as output, validated internally in a childhood cohort (ABCD) and externally in an adolescent cohort (BANDA).
study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with internal and external validation of a connectome-based predictive model
headline_result: ABCD internal: rho=0.058, p=0.040; BANDA external validation: rho=0.222, p=0.007

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Synthesizing Longitudinal Infant Brain MRI during Early Development.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: Infants from the Baby Connectome Project
clinical_problem: Generating missing infant brain MRI time points to study early brain developmental trajectories
model_description: Three-stage age- and modality-conditioned deep learning framework takes existing T1/T2-weighted infant brain MRI scans as input and synthesizes brain MRI at missing longitudinal time points, also performing tissue segmentation and cortical reconstruction.
dataset_size: 848 MRI scans from 139 infants (119 training, 20 test)
headline_result: SSIM 0.87-0.90 (T1), 0.87-0.89 (T2); Dice 0.85 gray matter, 0.86 white matter segmentation

title: Deep learning model using cross-sequence learning to identify orbital fractures in radiographs of patients under 20 Years.
model_family: multi-input deep learning with cross-sequence learning (CNN)
patient_population: Patients under 20 years old with facial trauma from two hospitals (n = 904 and n = 910 development datasets)
clinical_problem: Detecting orbital fractures on radiographs in patients under 20 years old to reduce unnecessary CT scans and radiation exposure.
model_description: A multi-input deep learning model with a novel cross-sequence learning method takes orbital rim view radiographs as input and outputs a prediction of orbital fracture presence, evaluated with and without model assistance for a radiology resident, pediatric radiologist, and ophthalmic surgeon.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic study with reader study
dataset_size: development datasets of 904 and 910 patients from two hospitals; internal test set drawn from a 7:1:2 split
headline_result: Model AUROC 0.802 (sensitivity 65.8%, specificity 86.5%, PPV 70.9%, NPV 83.5%); with model assistance, specificity improved significantly for both the ophthalmic surgeon and the radiology resident (P < 0.001)

title: Predicting pediatric diagnostic imaging patient no-show and extended wait-times using LLMs, regression, and tree based models.
patient_population: Pediatric patients undergoing diagnostic and interventional radiology appointments at a children's hospital (Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto)
clinical_problem: Predicting which pediatric diagnostic/interventional radiology outpatients will miss their appointment (no-show) or face long wait times, to guide scheduling accommodations.
model_description: Inputs are patient demographic and appointment-related features (20 total); XGBoost, random forest, SVM, logistic regression, a neural network, and a pretrained large language model output a predicted probability of appointment no-show or of wait time exceeding 1 hour.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study of appointment scheduling data
headline_result: XGBoost AUC 0.96 / F1 0.62 for no-show prediction; random forest AUC 0.83 / F1 0.61 for wait-time prediction

title: Modification of Brain Connectome on Association Between Adverse Childhood Experiences and Development of Mental Disorders in Preadolescence.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
patient_population: 6,813 children aged 9-11 years at baseline from the ABCD Study, 21 US sites
clinical_problem: Whether whole-brain functional connectivity from resting-state MRI modifies the relationship between adverse childhood experiences and later psychiatric diagnoses
model_description: Input is baseline resting-state functional MRI data; a machine-learning-based latent connectome variate score is derived and tested as a moderator of the association between adverse childhood experiences and psychiatric diagnoses over 2-year follow-up.
headline_result: Connectome variate score significantly modified association between ACEs and psychiatric diagnoses (beta -0.02, 95% CI -0.03 to -0.01, p<.001)

title: Dynamic functional connectivity variability in the thalamocortical circuit: Insights from Self-Limited Epilepsy with Centrotemporal Spikes (SeLECTs).
patient_population: 45 SeLECTs patients and 55 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Understanding the neural dynamics of Self-Limited Epilepsy with Centrotemporal Spikes (SeLECTs), a common childhood epilepsy, and whether connectivity variability can distinguish affected children from controls.
model_description: A support vector machine classifier uses dynamic functional connectivity variability (sliding-window analysis of 16 thalamic seed regions) from resting-state fMRI to distinguish children with SeLECTs from healthy controls.
headline_result: Significant dFC variability differences found in 9 of 16 thalamic seeds between groups (SVM used for classification, accuracy not numerically stated)

title: FetalDenseNet: multi-scale deep learning for enhanced early detection of fetal anatomical planes in prenatal ultrasound.
model_family: CNN (comparison of VGG16, ResNet50, InceptionV3, DenseNet169, MobileNetV2)
patient_population: 12,400 ultrasound images from 1,792 patients
clinical_problem: Improving classification of fetal anatomical planes on prenatal ultrasound to enhance interpretation accuracy.
model_description: Five CNN architectures (VGG16, ResNet50, InceptionV3, DenseNet169, MobileNetV2) are trained and compared on a large clinically validated dataset to classify fetal anatomical planes on prenatal ultrasound images.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study
dataset_size: 12,400 ultrasound images from 1,792 patients (80/20 train/test split)
headline_result: DenseNet169 achieved the highest classification accuracy of 92%

title: AI Model Integrating Imaging and Clinical Data for Predicting CSF Diversion in Neonatal Hydrocephalus: A Preliminary Study.
patient_population: Neonates with suspected raised intracranial pressure/hydrocephalus, including myelomeningocele and post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus
clinical_problem: Predicting which neonates with hydrocephalus will need CSF diversion surgery, using MRI and clinical data
model_description: Combines multimodal MRI features with clinical data to predict, at the individual-neonate level, future need for CSF diversion (shunt or ETV).
study_design: Retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: 116 neonates (development cohort, China); 21 neonates (external validation cohort, USA)
headline_result: AUC 0.824 development cohort (vs 0.528 clinical-only, 0.685 imaging-only); AUC 0.808 external validation cohort

title: Population-specific calibration and validation of an open-source bone age AI.
model_family: deep learning bone age model (Deeplasia) with sex-specific linear recalibration
patient_population: Georgian children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment (retrospective cohort of 381 pediatric hand radiographs)
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity / bone age assessment
model_description: The model takes a hand radiograph and outputs an estimated bone age. The existing open-source deep learning tool Deeplasia was recalibrated with a sex-specific linear correction fit on 121 Georgian children's hand radiographs, rated by seven local pediatric radiologists and endocrinologists, to produce Deeplasia-GE, then tested on a held-out set of 260 images.
dataset_size: 381 pediatric hand radiographs (121 used for calibration, 260 held out for testing)
headline_result: Calibration reduced mean absolute difference from 6.57 to 5.69 months on the held-out test set (n=260); Deeplasia-GE had smaller error than any of the individual human raters.

title: CurriMAE: curriculum learning based masked autoencoders for multi-labeled pediatric thoracic disease classification.
patient_population: pretrained on CheXpert and ChestX-ray14 (adult datasets), fine-tuned and evaluated on PediCXR (pediatric chest radiograph dataset)
clinical_problem: multi-labeled classification of pediatric thoracic diseases on chest radiographs
model_description: CurriMAE is a masked-autoencoder self-supervised pretraining approach that progressively increases the image masking ratio across four training stages; pretrained on adult chest radiograph datasets (CheXpert, ChestX-ray14) and fine-tuned on the pediatric PediCXR dataset for multi-label pediatric thoracic disease classification.
dataset_size: pretraining on CheXpert and ChestX-ray14; fine-tuning/evaluation on PediCXR
headline_result: CurriMAE outperforms ResNet, ViT-S, and standard MAE on PediCXR (specific metric not given)

title: Detection of pneumonia in children through chest radiographs using artificial intelligence in a low-resource setting: A pilot study.
patient_population: Children with suspected pneumonia; 5,232 open-source pediatric CXRs plus 190 prospectively collected Nigerian CXRs
clinical_problem: Automated detection of pneumonia on chest radiographs in children, validated in a low-resource African setting.
model_description: An AI model trained on an open-source pediatric CXR dataset classifies chest radiographs as normal or pneumonia, externally tested on prospectively collected Nigerian pediatric CXRs.
study_design: prospective cross-sectional pilot validation study, multi-center (Nigeria)
dataset_size: 5,232 open-source pediatric CXRs (training/internal test); 190 external Nigerian CXRs
headline_result: Internal AUC 0.93 (86% accuracy); external (Nigeria) AUC 0.65 (58% accuracy)

title: Development and temporal validation of a deep learning model for automatic fetal biometry from ultrasound videos.
journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
venue_label: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
patient_population: Pregnant patients with healthy fetuses undergoing routine ultrasound
clinical_problem: Automatically measuring fetal biometry (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length) and estimating fetal weight from ultrasound
model_description: Classifies ultrasound video frames into standard fetal biometry planes (HC/AC/FL), then automatically measures each parameter; fetal weight estimated via the Hadlock 3 formula.
dataset_size: 16,626 training images; prospective validation on 281 ultrasound videos
headline_result: Mean absolute error vs expert: 0.96% HC, 1.56% AC, 1.77% FL, 3.10% fetal weight

title: NeoCLIP: a self-supervised foundation model for the interpretation of neonatal radiographs.
patient_population: Infants admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (4,629 infants, Boston, 2008-2023)
clinical_problem: Detecting pathologies and identifying medical device placement on neonatal radiographs in the NICU
model_description: Self-supervised contrastive-learning foundation model trained on neonatal radiographs paired with radiology reports; detects 15 radiological features and 5 medical devices.
study_design: Retrospective model development and internal validation
headline_result: Higher AUROC than controls for all labels except portal venous gas

title: An exploratory study on ultrasound image denoising using feature extraction and adversarial diffusion model.
model_family: adversarial diffusion model with feature-extraction network (GAN + diffusion model, U-Net structure)
body_region: fetal head (HC18), heart (CAMUS), and nerve (Ultrasound Nerve) — public benchmark images
patient_population: public benchmark ultrasound datasets: fetal head circumference (HC18), cardiac (CAMUS), and peripheral nerve (Ultrasound Nerve); not a specific clinical cohort
clinical_problem: reducing speckle noise in ultrasound images to improve image quality for analysis
model_description: ADM-ExNet replaces the reverse process of a diffusion denoising model with a GAN (U-Net generator/discriminator) and incorporates a structural feature-extraction network into the loss function, to remove simulated Gaussian speckle noise from ultrasound images (including fetal head circumference images) while preserving structural detail.

title: Segmentation-free pretherapeutic assessment of BRAF-status in pediatric low-grade gliomas.
model_family: deep learning segmentation (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) and CNN classification with segmentation-informed pretraining
patient_population: 455 patients with pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) treated 1999-2023 at a children's hospital
clinical_problem: noninvasive pretreatment prediction of BRAF mutation status in pediatric low-grade glioma
model_description: Whole-brain FLAIR MRI is segmented by one of three tested networks (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) and then classified by a deep learning model to predict BRAF status without relying on manual tumor segmentation. A pretraining step embeds segmentation knowledge into the whole-brain classification model to improve accuracy without needing a tumor mask at inference.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and comparison
dataset_size: 455 patients with molecularly characterized pLGG and whole-brain FLAIR MRI
headline_result: AUC 0.741 without segmentation knowledge, improved to 0.772 with segmentation pretraining (vs 0.756 for segmentation-based baseline)

title: Precise diagnosis of pediatric posterior cranial fossa neoplasms based on 2.5D MRI deep learning.
model_family: 2.5D deep learning combining Residual Network and Swin Transformer
patient_population: 309 pediatric patients with pathology-confirmed posterior fossa tumors
clinical_problem: preoperative differentiation of pediatric posterior fossa tumor type (pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma)
model_description: ResSwinT takes five-sequence MRI (T1WI, T1C, T2WI, FLAIR, ADC) constructed as 2.5D images and outputs a three-way classification among pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, and ependymoma. SHAP analysis is used to show which tumor regions drive each prediction.

title: Characteristics of fetal facial expression changes using artificial intelligence: a pilot study.
patient_population: 47 singleton pregnancies at 28-37 weeks of gestation
clinical_problem: characterize fetal facial expression patterns using AI to indirectly infer fetal brain activity
model_description: an original AI model classifies frames of fetal facial expression video into categories (e.g., neutral, mouthing) to quantify duration, transitions, and correlation dimensions, proposed as an indirect proxy for fetal brain activity
dataset_size: 57,208 frames (95.27 minutes) from 47 singleton pregnancies, 28-37 weeks gestation
headline_result: neutral and mouthing expressions had the longest durations (median 71.0 s and 53.3 s)

title: MRI-based radiomics model for differentiating focal cortical dysplasia from dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor in epileptic children.
patient_population: 169 children with epilepsy (96 FCD, 73 DNET)
clinical_problem: preoperatively differentiate focal cortical dysplasia from dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor in children with epilepsy using MRI radiomics
model_description: radiomics features are extracted from T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and T2-FLAIR MRI, selected via LASSO, and used to build SVM classifiers (individual-sequence and fusion models) to differentiate FCD from DNET preoperatively, compared with radiologists
headline_result: fusion radiomics model AUC 0.894 (95% CI 0.799-0.968), accuracy 82.0%, superior to junior radiologist and comparable to senior radiologist

title: Automated cervix biometry, volumetry and normative models for 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted 0.55-3T fetal MRI during 2nd and 3rd trimesters.
patient_population: 270 normal-term pregnancies, 16-40 weeks gestation; pipeline validated on 20 datasets (0.55T and 3T)
clinical_problem: Automated measurement of cervical length and volume on fetal MRI to study cervical remodeling before birth
model_description: 3D T2-weighted motion-corrected fetal MRI is input to a deep learning pipeline that automatically performs multi-layer segmentation of the pregnant cervix and derives biometric measurements (e.g., inlet diameter, length), compared with manual measurement and used to build normative growth curves.
dataset_size: 270 normal term cases (16-40 weeks GA); pipeline validated on 20 datasets
headline_result: Automated cervix biometry showed good agreement with manual measurements; inlet diameter and length correlated most strongly with gestational age

title: Detection of leptomeningeal angiomas in brain MRI of Sturge-Weber syndrome using multi-scale multi-scan Mamba.
patient_population: Patients with Sturge-Weber syndrome (congenital disorder presenting in early childhood)
clinical_problem: Automated detection of leptomeningeal angiomas on brain MRI in children with Sturge-Weber syndrome to speed diagnosis.
model_description: Input: T1-enhanced brain MRI. Output: segmentation/detection of leptomeningeal angiomas via a multi-scale multi-scan Mamba encoder-decoder, pretrained on public BraTS data and fine-tuned on the SWS cohort.
study_design: Retrospective model development study with 5-fold cross-validation.
headline_result: Dice score 91.53% (BraTS pretraining set) and 78.67% (SWS test set), outperforming two neurologists.

title: Predicting congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in prenatal hydronephrosis via machine learning.
patient_population: Infants diagnosed with prenatal hydronephrosis
clinical_problem: Predicting congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) from prenatal/postnatal urinary tract dilation ultrasound findings to guide need for advanced imaging.
model_description: Input: ultrasound urinary-tract-dilation parameters (central/ureteral dilation, AP diameter) and age at first ultrasound. Output: predicted probability of CAKUT diagnosis.
study_design: Retrospective cohort study, ML model development.
headline_result: AUC 0.915-0.922 across Random Forest, LightGBM and XGBoost models.

title: Accurate Cobb Angle Estimation via SVD-Based Curve Detection and Vertebral Wedging Quantification.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: HRNet + Swin-Transformer deep learning framework with SVD-based curve analysis
patient_population: patients aged 10-18 years with full-spine anteroposterior radiographs for scoliosis
clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement and vertebral wedging assessment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis severity
model_description: The model takes full-spine anteroposterior radiographs and predicts superior and inferior endplate angles and vertebral midpoints for each vertebra, combining an HRNet/Swin-Transformer backbone with singular value decomposition to compute Cobb angle and a new Vertebral Wedging Index without assuming a predefined curve pattern.
study_design: retrospective model development with dual-rater annotation
dataset_size: 630 full-spine radiographs from patients aged 10-18 years
headline_result: 83.45% diagnostic accuracy, 2.55-degree mean absolute error for Cobb angle

title: Development and validation of a novel prediction model for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy based on maternal cardiovascular function and placental blood flow metrics at 22 to 24 gestational weeks using machine learning.
publication_types: Journal Article; Validation Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: Normotensive pregnant women at 22-24 weeks' gestation
clinical_problem: Predicting hypertensive disorders of pregnancy using mid-gestation maternal hemodynamics and Doppler ultrasound placental blood flow measures.
model_description: Input: noninvasive maternal cardiovascular (impedance cardiography) and Doppler ultrasound placental/uteroplacental blood-flow measures. Output: predicted probability of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
study_design: Cross-sectional cohort study, ML model development.
headline_result: AUC 0.82 (95% CI 0.65-0.95) on independent test set; sensitivity 70%, specificity 79%.

title: Benchmarking Vision LLMs in fetal ultrasound interpretation: a five-point expert evaluation of standard vs. custom prompts.
patient_population: 9 fetal ultrasound images evaluated by 6 Vision LLMs and 3 expert sonographers
clinical_problem: Whether vision-capable large language models can interpret fetal ultrasound images for prenatal care
model_description: Fetal ultrasound images are input to six Vision Large Language Models (via a chatbot platform) with standard vs. tailored prompts; outputs are assessed by expert sonographers on anatomical recognition, biometric potential, image quality, normalcy assessment, and clinical recommendations.
headline_result: Custom prompts improved performance; best models (Claude Sonnet 3.5, ChatGPT-4o) achieved median scores of 19 and 18 out of 25

title: The value of AI-assisted multiple bone age assessment methods for evaluating efficacy in idiopathic short stature: A retrospective study of traditional Chinese medicine treatment for girls in China.
patient_population: Female pediatric patients with idiopathic short stature undergoing traditional Chinese medicine treatment, and healthy children controls
clinical_problem: Using AI-assisted bone age assessment methods (Greulich-Pyle, TW3, TW China) to evaluate treatment efficacy in girls with idiopathic short stature.
model_description: Input: left-hand X-rays at baseline and follow-up. Output: AI-assisted bone age estimates via G&P, TW3 and TW-China atlas methods, tracked over 6/9/12-month follow-up to gauge treatment efficacy.
dataset_size: 388 healthy children (control) and 190 female ISS patients
headline_result: Bone-age difference on follow-up was significantly higher in the treatment-effective group (P<.01); TW3/TW-China methods detected efficacy as early as 6 months versus 12 months for G&P.

title: Preoperative noninvasive prediction of Rex vs. Warren shunt selection in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction: a machine learning model based on serology and ultrasound.
model_family: XGBoost (gradient boosting; best of five ML algorithms compared)
patient_population: Pediatric patients with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO) undergoing shunt surgery
clinical_problem: Preoperative noninvasive prediction of optimal surgical shunt (Rex vs. Warren) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction, using ultrasound and serology instead of invasive portography.
model_description: Input: ultrasound imaging features and serological markers selected via LASSO. Output: predicted probability guiding Rex vs. Warren shunt selection, deployed as an online prediction tool.
study_design: Retrospective diagnostic model development study with internal and external validation.
headline_result: XGBoost AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.79-0.99) training, 0.75 (95% CI 0.54-0.97) external validation.

title: Automated and accurate view classification of fetal echocardiography using convolutional neural networks.
