journal: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine Update
venue_label: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine Update
model_family: Spider Wasp Optimization (SWO) feature selection combined with K-Nearest Neighbor classifier, using features from a ResNet50V2 residual learning architecture
patient_population: pediatric patients with brain tumors (brain MRI from King Abdullah Hospital)
clinical_problem: classification of pediatric brain tumor type
model_description: The model classifies pediatric brain tumor type from MRI images. Features are extracted with a ResNet50V2 deep learning architecture, then a Spider Wasp Optimization metaheuristic algorithm selects the most informative features, which are fed into a K-Nearest Neighbor classifier for binary and multiclass tumor classification. It was compared against other deep learning architectures (MobileNetV2, ResNet50V2) and machine learning classifiers (KNN, SVM, Random Forest).
study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy / technical development
dataset_size: brain MRI images from King Abdullah Hospital (exact n not stated)
headline_result: SWO+KNN achieved 97.5% accuracy for binary classification and 95.5% for multiclass classification, outperforming other deep learning and machine learning models compared.

title: Artificial Intelligence enhanced R1 maps can improve lesion detection in focal epilepsy in children
patient_population: paediatric focal epilepsy patients (17 MRI-lesion-positive, 14 MRI-negative; 26 evaluable after exclusions), plus 10 healthy volunteers used for network training
clinical_problem: detection of subtle cortical lesions in pediatric focal epilepsy surgery evaluation
model_description: A 3D U-Net, trained on paired 3T and 7T MRI from 10 healthy volunteers, enhances quantitative R1 relaxation maps acquired at standard 3T field strength to approximate the image quality of ultra-high-field 7T MRI. It was applied to 3T R1 maps from a separate cohort of pediatric focal epilepsy patients scanned at a different site, and radiologists compared lesion visibility and detection on the AI-enhanced maps versus original 3T maps and 3D-FLAIR.
study_design: retrospective technical development with radiological review
dataset_size: 10 healthy volunteers for training; 17 MRI-positive and 14 MRI-negative pediatric epilepsy patients for application
headline_result: Lesions detected on AI-enhanced R1 maps in 14/15 (93%) MR-positive and 4/11 (36%) MR-negative patients, with superior image quality compared to original 3T R1 maps and 3D-FLAIR

title: Boundary and channel double calibrated CT segmentation network for pneumonia in children
model_family: dual-encoder CNN segmentation network with boundary feature enhancement and channel recalibration modules
patient_population: children with pneumonia undergoing chest CT
clinical_problem: segmentation of pneumonia-infected lung regions on chest CT in children
model_description: A dual-encoder deep learning network segments pneumonia-infected regions on pediatric chest CT. A boundary feature enhancement module uses prior contour labels and multi-directional edge detectors with cross-attention to sharpen lesion boundaries, while a channel recalibration module suppresses background noise, together improving segmentation of small, low-contrast infected regions; the network also generalized to adult COVID-19 CT images.
headline_result: Dice, Jaccard index, sensitivity and Matthews correlation coefficient improved by 2.99%, 4.76%, 2.56% and 3.03% respectively versus the best-performing comparison network on pediatric pneumonia CT

title: Correlations of artificial intelligence measured parameters on anteroposterior and lateral spinal X-ray films with severity of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
patient_population: adolescents with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)
clinical_problem: quantifying spinal deformity severity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: The uAI DR scoliosis analysis system automatically measures multiple spinal alignment parameters (Cobb angle, coronal balance distance, T1 slope, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, apical vertebral translation, thoracic trunk shift, thoracic kyphosis, sagittal vertical axis) from anteroposterior and lateral spinal radiographs. The study correlated these AI-measured parameters with AIS severity and coronal/sagittal balance status in a large retrospective cohort.
release_evidence: Parameters were measured using the named 'uAI DR scoliosis analysis System' software product.
headline_result: Cobb angle, coronal balance distance, apical vertebral translation and thoracic trunk shift increased significantly with AIS severity (all P<0.001); T1 slope, apical vertebral translation and thoracic trunk shift were independent predictors of severity.

title: Domain shifts in infant brain diffusion MRI: Quantification and mitigation for fODF estimation
model_family: MLP-based, Transformer-based, and U-Net/CNN-based deep learning architectures (compared)
patient_population: 488 infant subjects from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) and Baby Connectome Project (BCP)
clinical_problem: estimation of fiber orientation distributions from diffusion MRI to study early brain development, addressing generalizability across scanners and protocols
model_description: Three deep learning architectures (MLP-based, transformer-based, and U-Net/CNN-based) were trained to estimate fiber orientation distribution functions from infant diffusion MRI, and their robustness to domain shifts (scanner/protocol differences, age, number of input gradient directions) was systematically evaluated. Two adaptation strategies, method-of-moments and fine-tuning, were tested to correct inter-site domain shift, with fine-tuning giving the best results.
headline_result: U-Net outperformed other models with fewer diffusion gradient directions; performance plateaued from 28-45 input directions across all models; fine-tuning outperformed method-of-moments for correcting inter-site domain shift

title: PW-GAN: Pseudo-Warping Field Guided GAN for Unsupervised Denoising of Fetal Brain MRI Images
patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal brain MRI (simulated and in vivo data)
clinical_problem: image-quality improvement for reconstructed fetal brain MRI to support prenatal neural disorder diagnosis
model_description: PW-GAN is an unsupervised generative adversarial network that denoises 3D fetal brain MRI volumes reconstructed from motion-corrupted thick-slice scans. It treats denoising as an unpaired style-transfer problem between low- and high-quality MRI domains and adds a pseudo-deformation-field module, based on optical flow, to keep structures consistent between adjacent slices while removing residual noise and interpolation artifacts.
dataset_size: not stated precisely (simulated and in vivo data)
headline_result: Outperforms existing unsupervised denoising models and achieves performance on par with several state-of-the-art supervised methods

title: Intersecting effects of social circumstances and transcendent thinking on mid-adolescents’ longitudinal functional connectome development
model_family: machine learning predictor analysis on graph-theoretic functional connectome measures
patient_population: Mid-adolescents from low-socioeconomic-status contexts followed longitudinally with fMRI (n=65)
clinical_problem: predicting longitudinal functional brain network development in mid-adolescents from social circumstances and psychological disposition
model_description: Longitudinal (2-year) resting-state fMRI graph-theory metrics were computed to characterize functional brain network (FBN) development in mid-adolescents. Machine learning analysis identified transcendent thinking (a psychological disposition) and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as the principal predictors of FBN change, with effects differing by parental education and violence exposure subgroup.
study_design: longitudinal resting-state fMRI study with machine learning predictor analysis
headline_result: Machine learning identified transcendent thinking and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as principal predictors of functional brain network change.

title: Recognition of normal fetal echocardiogram based on an explainable denosing deep learning model
model_name: GSCAViT (grouped sharing convolutional attention - vision transformer)
model_family: vision transformer with denoising group-sharing convolutional attention module
patient_population: 358 fetuses undergoing cardiac ultrasound examinations
clinical_problem: classification of standard fetal echocardiographic views
model_description: GSCAViT is a deep learning model that classifies seven standard fetal echocardiogram view types (e.g., three-vessel and trachea, four-chamber, aortic arch, bicaval, outflow tracts) from ultrasound images. It combines a denoising group-sharing convolutional attention module with a vision transformer, and uses SHAP explainability to visualize which image features drive classification.
headline_result: Accuracy 97.1%, precision 97.1%, recall 97.0%, F1-score 97.0% in validation; AUCs of 0.994, 0.928, and 0.932 on three separate test sets

title: Improving Pneumonia Diagnosis with Radimagenet: A Deep Transfer Learning Approach
patient_population: children aged 1-5 years
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection on chest X-ray
model_description: Two ResNet-50 models pretrained on different source datasets - ImageNet (14 million natural images) versus RadImageNet (1.4 million medical images) - were fine-tuned to detect pneumonia on chest X-rays of children aged 1-5 years. Performance was compared across six evaluation metrics to test whether a medically pretrained backbone improves classification on a small pediatric imaging dataset.
dataset_size: not stated precisely (chest X-ray images of children aged 1-5)
headline_result: RadImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 outperformed ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 across six evaluation metrics for pediatric pneumonia detection

title: PIOFSF: A deep learning-based pediatric inferior orbital fracture screening framework
model_family: 3D diffusion and symmetrical attention-based frequency-domain adaptive global feature network (DSA-FAGFNet), CNN-based
patient_population: children undergoing head/orbital CT for suspected orbital fracture
clinical_problem: screening for pediatric orbital fractures
model_description: PIOFSF is a deep learning pipeline for screening pediatric orbital fractures on CT: it performs 3D reconstruction, corrects for head tilt so the orbits are symmetrically aligned, localizes the orbits using clustering and a Hough transform, then classifies fracture presence with a 3D network (DSA-FAGFNet) combining diffusion-based orbital position coding, symmetrical attention and frequency-domain feature extraction, aiming to catch subtle fractures that are often missed or misdiagnosed as other conditions in children.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: F1 score 82.50%

title: Comparison of three artificial intelligence-assisted bone age assessment methods for predicting adult height in girls
journal: Chinese Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism
model_family: AI-assisted bone age assessment (architecture not stated), applied to three established prediction formulas (Bayley-Pinneau, Tanner-Whitehouse 3, China 05)
patient_population: 278 female children undergoing pubertal development assessment at Shenzhen Children's Hospital, 2014-2020, followed until adult height was reached
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment for adult height prediction in girls with pubertal disorders
model_description: AI-assisted bone age assessment of left-hand-wrist radiographs was used to apply three adult-height prediction methods (Bayley-Pinneau, Tanner-Whitehouse 3, and China 05) in girls followed to adult height, comparing which method most accurately predicted final adult height and how errors varied by age, bone age delay/advancement, and pubertal stage.
headline_result: TW3 and BP methods overestimated adult height by 2.6+-3.0 cm and 1.7+-3.7 cm; China 05 underestimated by 2.3+-3.5 cm; proportion of predictions within +-5 cm of final height: TW3 80.0%, BP 77.0%, China 05 74.2% (P=0.038)

title: Towards automated multi-regional lung parcellation for 0.55-3T 3D T2w fetal MRI
patient_population: 104 normal-anatomy fetal controls and 45 congenital diaphragmatic hernia cases; 290 controls used for growth charts, across 0.55T, 1.5T and 3T scanners
clinical_problem: fetal lung volume and lobar segmentation for prediction of neonatal outcomes, including congenital diaphragmatic hernia
model_description: A 3D Attention U-Net automatically segments the fetal lungs into five standard lobes on 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted fetal body MRI, replacing time-consuming manual 2D slice-by-slice segmentation. It was trained on normal-anatomy and congenital diaphragmatic hernia cases across 0.55T, 1.5T and 3T scanners, and used to generate normal fetal lung volumetry growth charts.
dataset_size: 104 normal controls and 45 CDH cases for the training dataset; 18 cases for evaluation; 290 controls for growth charts
headline_result: Good Dice performance for normal lung anatomy on 18 evaluation cases, with expectedly lower Dice values for the ipsilateral lung in congenital diaphragmatic hernia cases

title: A Novel Real-Time Deep Learning Screening for Prenatal and Neonatal Biliary Atresia Diagnosis for Ghost Gallbladders: Better Interpretation and More Novice-Friendly
model_name: NRDLS (Novel Real-time Deep Learning method for Ultrasound Screening)
model_family: ensemble deep learning model with transfer learning; two-stage detection and classification
patient_population: neonates aged 25-77 days with obstructive jaundice at first diagnosis; also addresses prenatal fetal gallbladder screening
clinical_problem: screening and diagnosis of biliary atresia via gallbladder localization ('ghost gallbladder') in prenatal and neonatal jaundice
model_description: NRDLS is a two-stage deep learning system that localizes the fetal or neonatal gallbladder (including difficult-to-find 'ghost' gallbladders) on ultrasound and then classifies the images to diagnose biliary atresia. It was built via transfer learning from an ensemble deep learning model and evaluated on data from hospitals different from the training site, then deployed for frontline screening in several primary care hospitals.
study_design: retrospective multicenter cohort study with prospective clinical deployment
dataset_size: derivation cohort from Guangzhou Women and Children Medical Center PACS records, 2010-2024; external validation cohorts of 118 and 72 patients with neonatal jaundice
headline_result: Detection mean average precision 92.8%, AUC 0.917-0.944; external validation AUC 82% and 85%; after deployment, novice physicians achieved mean AUC 0.92, specificity 0.93, F1-score 0.83

title: DVVDNet: A dual-view vertebra detection network with anatomical constraints for automatic scoliosis assessment
model_family: dual-view vertebra detection deep learning network with gated multi-scale attentive fusion and an anatomical constraint loss
patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing anteroposterior and lateral spine radiographs
clinical_problem: vertebra detection to support assessment of spinal curvature in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: DVVDNet takes paired anterior-posterior and lateral spine radiographs and detects vertebrae to support automated scoliosis assessment. It fuses information from both views with a gated multi-scale attentive fusion module and applies an anatomical constraint loss reflecting vertebral geometry to stabilize predictions. It was evaluated on the public AASCE challenge dataset and a private hospital dataset, showing high agreement with radiologists' assessments.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: public AASCE challenge dataset plus a private hospital dataset (sizes not stated)
headline_result: high agreement with radiologists' assessments (no single numeric accuracy metric reported)

title: Establishment and validation of an artificial intelligence model for ultrasound image quality control in early pregnancy
model_family: deep learning-based image quality assessment system
patient_population: fetuses at 11 to 13+6 weeks gestation undergoing routine first-trimester ultrasound at a single hospital, 2018-2024
clinical_problem: quality control and standardization of first-trimester ultrasound screening planes
model_description: PSAIS is a deep-learning system trained on 17,910 static first-trimester ultrasound images across 8 quality-control planes to automatically recognize anatomical structures and assess image quality/standardization, split into training (12,536), test (3,582) and validation (1,792) sets. Its output was compared against two expert sonographers using intraclass correlation and Kappa statistics, and its processing speed was compared to manual quality control.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and reader-comparison study
dataset_size: 17,910 images from first-trimester ultrasound exams (First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, 2018-2024)
headline_result: mAP >0.800 for anatomical structure recognition on all 8 planes; ICC 0.678-0.843 and Kappa 0.530-0.768 agreement with two experts; total processing time 413s vs. 77,008-94,918s for manual QC (P<0.001)

title: Application of a hybrid artificial intelligence model integrating view detection and structural segmentation in evaluating cardiac function of anemic fetuses
model_family: hybrid AI model combining view detection and structural segmentation (deep learning)
patient_population: 47 fetuses: 15 anemic (diagnosed via umbilical venous puncture) and 32 normal controls, 2018-2024
clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of fetal cardiac size, morphology and function in fetal anemia
model_description: A hybrid AI model combining four-chamber view detection with structural segmentation extracts a panel of fetal cardiac size, shape, and function measurements (chamber lengths, ventricular diameters, sphericity indices, strain, fractional area change and shortening) and their Z-scores from four-chamber echocardiographic ultrasound videos. It was used to compare anemic and normal fetuses, and its measurement agreement with conventional fetal HQ software was assessed by intraclass correlation.
dataset_size: 47 fetuses (15 anemic: 44 videos/1,056 segments; 32 control: 46 videos/1,104 segments)
headline_result: AI-based measurements agreed well with conventional fetal HQ technology (ICC 0.788 control, 0.837 anemia); anemic fetuses showed larger right ventricular dimensions, lower ventricular sphericity indices, and reduced LVGLS/LVFAC (P<0.05 to P<0.001)

title: Value of artificial intelligence in assisting ultrasound residents training for the identification，measurement and diagnosis of fetal nuchal translucency thickness
patient_population: fetuses undergoing first-trimester nuchal translucency ultrasound; retrospective images used to train ultrasound resident sonographers
clinical_problem: nuchal translucency measurement and screening for fetal abnormality
model_description: An AI model automatically identifies the nuchal translucency (NT) plane on fetal ultrasound images and measures NT thickness. In this study it was used as a training aid: after an initial round of independent NT identification, measurement and diagnosis, two resident sonographers received additional AI-assisted training, then all sonographers performed a second independent round that was compared to a fetal medicine expert's blinded review. The AI model itself was not the subject of an accuracy evaluation here, only its effect on trainee performance.
headline_result: AI-assisted training significantly improved NT measurement standardization rate in both resident sonographers (chi2=25.768 and 17.035, both P<0.05) and diagnostic accuracy in one resident (chi2=10.180, P<0.05); traditional lecture-only training produced no significant improvement in the middle-age sonographer

title: AI-Powered Segmentation and Prognosis with Missing MRI in Pediatric Brain Tumors
model_family: dropout-trained nnU-Net (3D CNN) with modality-dropout training, compared to generative image synthesis and heuristic imputation
patient_population: children with pediatric brain tumors: 715 patients from the Children's Brain Tumor Network and BraTS-PEDs, plus 43 patients with longitudinal MRI from PNOC003/007 clinical trials
clinical_problem: pediatric brain tumor segmentation and prognosis when MRI sequences are missing from the exam
model_description: An nnU-Net tumor segmentation model was trained with random dropout of FLAIR and/or non-contrast T1-weighted sequences to simulate incomplete pediatric brain tumor MRI exams. It was compared against a generative image-synthesis model and simple copy-substitution/zeroing heuristics for handling missing sequences. Tumor volumes from each method fed into time-varying Cox regression models to estimate survival risk.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional cohort study, technical development
dataset_size: 715 patients (CBTN and BraTS-PEDs) plus 43 patients with 157 longitudinal MRI timepoints (PNOC003/007)
headline_result: Dropout-trained segmentation model showed only up to 0.04 Dice drop under missing MRI and a stable survival C-index of 0.65 versus complete-input performance; image synthesis achieved SSIM > 0.90

title: Automated Right Ventricular Assessment in Pediatric Echocardiography via Deep Learning Improves Measurement Reliability and Reduces Variability
model_family: FCBFormer (deep learning segmentation architecture, best of several trained)
patient_population: 664 pediatric echocardiograms
clinical_problem: quantification of right ventricular function in pediatric cardiac evaluation
model_description: A deep-learning segmentation model (best-performing architecture: FCBFormer) was trained on 664 pediatric echocardiograms to automatically segment the right ventricle and compute right ventricular fractional area change (RVFAC), a measure of RV function. Its segmentations and measurements were compared to manual ground truth and to four blinded human experts to assess whether it reduces inter-observer variability in RV assessment. (Duplicate SSRN posting of the same study as record emb:L2040562547.)
study_design: retrospective technical development and reader study
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.926, MAE 5.913% for RVFAC prediction; model-generated segmentation preferred over human segmentation in 57.3% of blinded expert comparisons

title: Predicting Anatomical Brain Tumor Growth by Guided Denoising Diffusion Models
patient_population: adult (n=1,251) and pediatric (n=144) patients from the BraTS23 challenge for training; validated on a multi-institutional pre-radiotherapy pediatric diffuse midline glioma dataset (n=178 paired slices)
clinical_problem: predicting spatial tumor growth in pediatric diffuse midline glioma
model_description: A guided denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM), trained on multiparametric MRI from the BraTS23 challenge (adult and pediatric cases), generates probabilistic maps of future anatomical tumor growth conditioned on a baseline scan, focused on pediatric diffuse midline glioma. Repeated generation of synthetic follow-up T2-FLAIR images produced growth-probability maps validated against real longitudinal MRI from a separate multi-institutional pediatric dataset; trained radiologists could not reliably distinguish synthetic from real scans.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 1,251 adult + 144 pediatric training cases (BraTS23); 178 paired slices for validation (pediatric diffuse midline glioma)
headline_result: radiologists could not reliably distinguish synthetic from real MRI (accuracy 0.53±0.03); tumor growth maps matched observed follow-up growth with mean continuous Dice score 0.79±0.13

title: Neural Timescale of Adolescents Major Depressive Disorder
patient_population: Adolescents with major depressive disorder and healthy controls
clinical_problem: predicting depression and anxiety severity in adolescents from resting-state fMRI intrinsic neural timescale
model_description: Resting-state fMRI was used to compute cortical intrinsic neural timescale (INT), a measure of temporal stability of neural activity, in adolescents with major depressive disorder and healthy controls. An SVR-based machine learning model used INT patterns to predict individual depression and anxiety severity scores; INT alterations were also linked to suicidal ideation and childhood trauma.
study_design: cross-sectional resting-state fMRI case-control study with SVR-based prediction
headline_result: SVR-based machine learning showed altered intrinsic neural timescale patterns predicted individual depression and anxiety severity.

title: Using deep learning methods to shorten acquisition time in children’s renal cortical imaging
model_family: diffusion-based generative model (SR3), compared to U-Net, U2-Net, Restormer, and PoissonSR3
patient_population: pediatric patients with suspected urinary tract infection undergoing 99mTc-DMSA renal scintigraphy; training cohort 94 (mean age 5.16 years), test cohort 36 (mean age 6.39 years)
clinical_problem: reconstructing diagnostic-quality renal cortical scintigraphy images from reduced-acquisition-time scans to shorten scan time
model_description: A diffusion-based generative model (SR3) was trained to reconstruct standard-quality pediatric 99mTc-DMSA renal cortical scintigraphy images from simulated reduced-count (accelerated) acquisitions, aiming to shorten scan time while preserving diagnostic image quality. It was benchmarked against U-Net, U2-Net, Restormer, and a Poisson-noise variant of itself using image-quality metrics and measures of renal contrast and anatomic fidelity (Dice coefficient).
headline_result: SR3 achieved best performance: PSNR 30.976, SSIM 0.760, FID 25.687, LPIPS 0.055 (all P<.001 vs. comparators); Dice 0.749 (left kidney), 0.745 (right kidney), supporting 4-fold accelerated acquisition

title: Predicting coronary artery abnormalities in Kawasaki disease: Model development and external validation
model_family: logistic regression and machine learning models (LightGBM, XGBoost) using clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and treatment variables
patient_population: children with Kawasaki disease from two prospective multicenter Japanese registries; 4,973 (development, PEACOCK) and 2,438 (external validation, Post-RAISE)
clinical_problem: predicting coronary artery abnormality development in Kawasaki disease to guide the need for follow-up echocardiography
model_description: Using 29 clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and treatment variables collected within the first week after Kawasaki disease diagnosis (including the peak coronary artery Z-score, Zmax), the authors compared a simple single-predictor model, logistic regression, and machine learning models (LightGBM, XGBoost) to predict which children will develop a coronary artery abnormality (Zmax >= 2) at the one-month follow-up echocardiogram. Models were developed and internally validated on one Japanese multicenter registry and externally validated on a second.
study_design: prospective multi-center registry-based model development and external validation study
dataset_size: 4,973 patients (development, PEACOCK registry), 2,438 patients (external validation, Post-RAISE registry)
headline_result: simple model using week-1 Zmax alone achieved AUC 0.79 on external validation; additional variables or complex ML models improved AUC by less than 0.02, and no model reduced echocardiography need by more than 30% while keeping missed-CAA cases below 10

title: Automated biometry for assessing cephalopelvic disproportion in 3D 0.55T fetal MRI at term
model_family: 3D U-Net models (MONAI framework) for landmark localization
patient_population: late-gestation pregnancies (36-40 weeks) from the MiBirth study, imaged with low-field 0.55T MRI
clinical_problem: assessment of cephalopelvic disproportion / risk of obstructed labor via fetal and pelvic biometry
model_description: A fully automated pipeline uses deep-learning (3D U-Net, MONAI framework) landmark localization on 3D-reconstructed T2-weighted low-field (0.55T) fetal MRI to compute 12 standard linear and circumference measurements of the fetal head and maternal pelvis used to assess cephalopelvic disproportion. The pipeline was trained on 57 semi-manually annotated datasets, quantitatively validated on 10 test cases, and applied to 206 scans from the MiBirth study investigating prediction of delivery mode.
study_design: prospective technical development and feasibility study
dataset_size: 57 training datasets, 10 test cases, applied to 206 additional scans
headline_result: quantitatively validated on 10 test cases (specific metric values not given); applied to 206 clinical scans to demonstrate feasibility

title: Evaluation of Deep Learning Models with Spatial Attention for Fetal Head and Pubic Symphysis Segmentation in Intrapartum Ultrasound Images
model_family: U-Net, PSPNet, LinkNet, FPN, SegNet, each with and without a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM)
body_region: fetal head and maternal pubic symphysis (intrapartum pelvis)
patient_population: intrapartum ultrasound images from a public dataset
clinical_problem: assessment of fetal head descent during labor via angle of progression and head-symphysis distance
model_description: Five segmentation architectures (U-Net, PSPNet, LinkNet, FPN, SegNet), each with and without a Convolutional Block Attention Module, were trained on a public intrapartum ultrasound dataset to segment the fetal head and pubic symphysis. The segmentations support automated calculation of the angle of progression and head-symphysis distance, measurements otherwise made manually and prone to observer variability.
study_design: retrospective technical development / model comparison study
dataset_size: public intrapartum ultrasound dataset (size not stated)
headline_result: U-Net + CBAM achieved the best performance, 99.88% accuracy

title: Automated right ventricular assessment in pediatric echocardiography via deep learning improves measurement reliability and reduces variability
model_family: FCBFormer (deep learning segmentation architecture, best of several trained)
patient_population: 664 pediatric echocardiograms
clinical_problem: quantification of right ventricular function in pediatric cardiac evaluation
model_description: A deep-learning segmentation model (best-performing architecture: FCBFormer) was trained on 664 pediatric echocardiograms to automatically segment the right ventricle and compute right ventricular fractional area change (RVFAC), a measure of RV function. Its segmentations and measurements were compared to manual ground truth and to four blinded human experts to assess whether it reduces inter-observer variability in RV assessment.
study_design: retrospective technical development and reader study
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.926, MAE 5.913% for RVFAC prediction; model-generated segmentation preferred over human segmentation in 57.3% of blinded expert comparisons

title: Artificial intelligence in evaluating the fetal heart. The first stages of development of the Moscow Kulakov National Medical Research Center for Obstetrics, Gynecology and Perinatology
model_family: AI algorithm for fetal echocardiography (zone detection, view classification, pathology detection)
patient_population: fetuses at 18-21 weeks gestation undergoing fetal echocardiography
clinical_problem: screening for congenital heart disease on fetal echocardiography
model_description: An AI algorithm was developed to support fetal heart examination from five standard cardiac ultrasound video projections (at least 25 frames per slice). The pipeline localizes the fetal chest and heart, classifies which standard heart view a frame shows, and flags whether the heart structure on that slice appears normal or abnormal, producing a 'normal' or 'not normal' (possible CHD, recommend extended echocardiography) opinion. Results were verified against expert diagnosis and postnatal confirmation.
dataset_size: not stated (cases from Moscow Kulakov National Medical Research Center)
headline_result: Accuracy was 98% for locating the chest/heart zone, 82% for classifying the cardiac view, and 77% for detecting pathology on a slice.

title: Clinical value of a deep learning multi-view fusion model for diagnosing fetal conotruncal defects
model_family: deep learning-based multi-view fusion recognition model
patient_population: fetuses at 20-32 weeks gestation with suspected conotruncal defects and matched normal controls
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of fetal conotruncal defects
model_description: A deep learning model takes one standard image each from four fetal cardiac ultrasound views (four-chamber, left ventricular outflow tract, right ventricular outflow tract, three vessels and trachea) and fuses them to classify the conotruncal anatomy as normal or defective. Three fusion strategies requiring positivity on two, three, or four views were compared; the best model was validated against post-abortion pathology or postnatal echocardiography and against sonologists of varying experience.
dataset_size: 88 CTD cases and 176 controls (82 CTD and 161 controls after exclusions); 60/22 CTD and 120/41 control train/validation split
headline_result: Optimal fusion model (Fusion Model 1) had 86% sensitivity and 76% specificity, statistically comparable to senior sonologists (91%, P>0.999) and significantly better than intermediate (55%, P=0.049) and junior sonologists (32%, P=0.003).

title: A Hybrid Image Enhancement and Deep Learning Approach to Pneumonia Detection
model_family: denoising autoencoder (DDAE) + CLAHE + edge-aware fusion enhancement, followed by ResNet18/ResNet50/DenseNet121 transfer learning classifiers
patient_population: publicly available pediatric chest X-ray dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection on chest radiographs
model_description: A hybrid image-enhancement pipeline combines a denoising autoencoder with CLAHE contrast enhancement and edge-aware fusion to improve pediatric chest radiograph quality before classification. Enhanced images are then classified for pneumonia using ResNet18, ResNet50, and DenseNet121 with transfer learning; Grad-CAM visualizations showed the models focusing on lung regions.
dataset_size: publicly available pediatric chest X-ray dataset (size not stated)
headline_result: classification accuracy increased by up to 3.8% after enhancement, with improved sensitivity; image quality improved (PSNR +3 dB, SSIM 0.74 to 0.86)

title: Explainability of Models Applied to Obstetric Medical Imaging
model_family: convolutional neural networks and a Vision Transformer, with Grad-CAM/Grad-CAM++/HiRes-CAM explainability
patient_population: pregnant women undergoing induction of labor, imaged with third-trimester obstetric ultrasound
clinical_problem: predicting mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean) after induction of labor
model_description: A range of deep learning architectures, including CNNs and a Vision Transformer, were trained on third-trimester obstetric ultrasound images to predict delivery mode after induction of labor. Explainable AI methods (Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, HiRes-CAM) generated saliency heatmaps of model attention, which experts judged to show clinically meaningful patterns, though there is no established ground truth for this task and model performance was modest.
headline_result: modest performance overall; no specific accuracy/AUC number given in the abstract

title: Claustrum volume in humans – lifespan trajectory and effect of age, hemisphere, and sex
model_family: deep learning-based automated segmentation with normative modeling
patient_population: 3,474 healthy participants aged 1-80 years, including children and adolescents as part of a lifespan cohort
clinical_problem: normative claustrum volume trajectory across the lifespan by age, hemisphere, and sex
model_description: Deep learning-based automated segmentation was applied to T1-weighted 3T MRI scans from 3,474 healthy participants aged 1 to 80 to measure claustrum volume, followed by normative modeling to map lifespan trajectories by hemisphere and sex, and regression analysis of age, hemisphere, and sex effects. Claustrum volume increased rapidly from infancy to adolescence, plateaued in early-to-middle adulthood, then declined into old age.
headline_result: rapid claustrum volume growth from ~1-15 years (39.300 mm3/year), plateau 15-40 years, decline 40-80 years; right claustrum larger than left across ages

title: Application of multimodal deep learning in identifying autism spectrum disorder in children with global developmental delay
model_family: multimodal deep learning (multi-channel model using DTI metrics)
patient_population: 357 children (79 ASD, 278 GDD)
clinical_problem: differentiating autism spectrum disorder from global developmental delay
model_description: Deep learning models were trained on T1-weighted and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) MRI from young children to classify autism spectrum disorder versus global developmental delay. A nested cross-validation with propensity score matching controlled for sex and age; the best multi-channel model using all DTI metrics achieved the strongest performance, with saliency maps highlighting white-matter tract and cortical gray-matter regions driving classification.
headline_result: mean AUROC 0.648, accuracy 57.1% on balanced test sets

title: AI-Based Quality Control for Fetal Ultrasound Image in Low-Resource Settings: A Real-World Multicenter Evaluation from West China
model_family: AI-based image quality scoring system (architecture not specified)
patient_population: pregnant women undergoing fetal ultrasound across 49 hospitals in Guizhou Province, China; 72,373 examinations performed, 61,959 analyzed
clinical_problem: quality control of fetal ultrasound images / standard plane acquisition
model_description: An independent, post-examination AI quality-control system scores uploaded fetal ultrasound images from 0-100 and classifies them as standard, basic-standard, or non-standard, for first-trimester, basic biometry, limited anomaly, and standard anomaly scan types. Deployed prospectively across district- and county-level hospitals in a low-resource province of China, it was used to track examination- and plane-level standardization rates by sonographers over 36 months.
study_design: prospective multi-center real-world implementation and evaluation study
dataset_size: 61,959 examinations (551,144 images) from 186 sonographers at 34 hospitals
headline_result: full-standard examination rate roughly doubled to tripled across scan categories over 36 months (e.g., first-trimester scan 39.5% to 82.1%, P<0.05)

title: A Sequential Fetal Growth Machine Learning Model for Predicting Birth Weight
model_family: machine learning model using sequential ultrasound biometry (compared against 15 existing formulae)
patient_population: singleton pregnancies across four hospitals in China; development cohort 10,277, external validation 4,014
clinical_problem: prediction of birth weight from serial fetal ultrasound biometry
model_description: A machine-learning model integrates fetal ultrasound biometric measurements from up to four prenatal ultrasound examinations across pregnancy (11-13+6, 18-23+6, 28-31+6 weeks and 1-2 weeks before birth) to predict birth weight. It was developed on 10,277 singleton pregnancies and externally validated on 4,014 pregnancies from three additional hospitals, compared against 15 existing sonographic birth-weight formulae.
study_design: retrospective multi-center cohort study with model development and external validation
headline_result: internal MAE 193.29 g, Acc250 71.30%, Acc500 95.91%; external MAE 178.67-206.99 g; outperformed existing formulae by 4-5 percentage points in Acc250

title: Multimodal Fusion of fMRI and Clinical Data for ADHD Diagnosis: A Spatiotemporal Attention ResNet Approach
model_family: spatiotemporal attention ResNet (multimodal fusion of fMRI and clinical data)
patient_population: children and adolescents in the public ADHD-200 dataset
clinical_problem: diagnosis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
model_description: A spatiotemporal attention residual network fuses resting-state functional MRI data with clinical data to classify ADHD versus non-ADHD. It was evaluated on the public ADHD-200 dataset, and model weights were used to identify functional brain network regions most associated with the classification, including at the NYU site subset.
dataset_size: ADHD-200 dataset (size not stated in abstract)
headline_result: classification accuracy of 75.6%, outperforming other benchmark methods

title: Expert review: current applications and future directions of artificial intelligence in obstetrics
patient_population: expert review of the obstetric AI literature (no single study population)
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis, monitoring and prediction of pregnancy complications such as pre-eclampsia
model_description: This expert review synthesizes AI applications in obstetrics from a literature search (January 2020-July 2025) of PubMed, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore. It covers AI-assisted prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, electronic fetal monitoring, and obstetric surgical assistance, noting that predictive models for pregnancy complications such as pre-eclampsia have achieved AUC greater than 0.9. It also discusses data privacy, interpretability, algorithmic bias and liability challenges.
headline_result: predictive models for pre-eclampsia reported AUC >0.9

title: PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF THE RADIOMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF 18F-FDG PET/CT IN CHILDREN WITH HODGKIN'S LYMPHOMA
model_family: radiomic quantitative parameters (Dmax/DmaxVox) extracted with LIFEx software and manual measurement
patient_population: pediatric patients with newly diagnosed Hodgkin lymphoma undergoing baseline and interim 18F-FDG PET/CT
clinical_problem: prognostic risk stratification in pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma
model_description: Two novel quantitative PET/CT parameters, Dmax and DmaxVox (the distance between the two most distant hypermetabolic foci or voxels within a lesion), were measured on baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT using the LIFEx software and by manual measurement, then normalized to body surface area or height. The normalized values were tested for association with event-free survival in children with Hodgkin lymphoma.
headline_result: Height-normalized SDmaxVox was significantly associated with event-free survival (P=0.03); negative predictive value exceeded 95% for both LIFEx- and manually-derived SDmaxVox at optimal cut-offs (0.123 and 0.086).

title: Development and validation of a prediction model for repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation efficacy in adolescents with major depressive episodes based on pre-treatment and early-treatment functional MRI
model_family: SVM-RBF (support vector machine, radial basis function) on ALFF features selected by LASSO regression
patient_population: adolescent inpatients with major depressive episode; discovery cohort 62 (mean age 15.2), external validation cohort 26 (mean age 15.5)
clinical_problem: predicting response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) treatment for major depressive episode
model_description: Resting-state functional MRI amplitude-of-low-frequency-fluctuation (ALFF) features, measured before and early in treatment and selected by LASSO regression, were fed into a support-vector-machine (SVM-RBF) classifier. The model predicts whether an adolescent with major depressive episode will respond to a course of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, measured by Hamilton Depression Rating Scale reduction. It was built on a discovery cohort with internal validation and tested on an independent external cohort.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development with external validation
headline_result: AUC 0.996 (modeling set), 0.786 (internal validation), 0.825 (external validation)

title: Feasibility study on deep learning for thigh muscles automatic segmentation on axial T(1)WI in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy
patient_population: 60 children with genetically confirmed Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD)
clinical_problem: quantifying thigh muscle fat infiltration / segmentation in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
model_description: A TransUNet deep-learning model was trained on axial T1-weighted MRI to automatically segment 11 thigh muscles bilaterally in children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. It was trained on 48 patients and tested on 12, with performance measured by Dice similarity coefficient, intersection over union, and average symmetric surface distance against manual delineation by physicians, intended to speed up assessment of muscle fat infiltration.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: test set DSC 0.944, IoU 0.900, ASSD 0.58; training set DSC 0.971, IoU 0.948; no significant difference in performance across fat-infiltration severity groups

title: Advanced Deep Learning Architecture for the Early and Accurate Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Neuroimaging
patient_population: 1,112 participants (539 ASD, 573 controls) from 17 sites, ABIDE-1 dataset
clinical_problem: diagnosis and classification of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children
model_description: A VGG20 deep-learning architecture was applied to region-based summaries of resting-state functional MRI from the public ABIDE-1 dataset to classify children as having autism spectrum disorder or not. Model performance was evaluated using recall, precision, F1-score and accuracy.
headline_result: accuracy of 61%

title: Adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury exhibit increased pain empathic neural reactivity and personal distress to physical but not affective pain
model_family: machine learning whole-brain pattern classification (alongside standard univariate fMRI analysis)
patient_population: unmedicated adolescents with NSSI (n=29) and healthy adolescent controls (n=33)
clinical_problem: identifying neural signatures of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) via pain-empathy processing
model_description: Functional MRI was collected while adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury and healthy controls performed a validated pain-empathy paradigm (observing physical versus affective pain). Machine learning was applied to whole-brain activation patterns to distinguish NSSI participants from controls, in addition to standard univariate group-difference analysis; a physical-pain empathic pattern gave the best discrimination between groups.
dataset_size: 29 adolescents with NSSI, 33 healthy adolescent controls
headline_result: machine learning revealed distinguishable whole-brain signatures, with a physical-pain empathic pattern giving the best discrimination (no single accuracy/AUC number reported)

title: Level II Ultrasound Standard Plane Recognition for Mid Pregnancy by a Specific ResNet20
model_family: custom seven-layer ResNet with bottleneck residual modules
patient_population: second-trimester fetuses from 200 pregnant women
clinical_problem: standard plane recognition during second-trimester (Level II) fetal ultrasound screening
model_description: A custom seven-layer ResNet20 model with bottleneck residual modules classifies second-trimester fetal ultrasound images into 10 standard anatomical sections using a softmax output. It was trained on 1,869 images from 200 pregnant women (90%/10% train-test split) and compared against AlexNet and VGG16.
release_evidence: "The code is open-source at https;// github. com/Chenan7/Resnet-19" (as printed in the abstract)
headline_result: overall recognition accuracy 88.2% vs. AlexNet 80.2% and VGG16 73.3% (P<0.001); 100% precision for cerebellar transverse, bilateral eye transverse, and spinal sagittal sections

title: Intelligent recognition of prenatal ultrasound standard sections based on VMamba model
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: standardized identification of prenatal ultrasound screening planes
model_description: A VMamba-based model was trained to automatically recognize 21 standard prenatal ultrasound screening planes/sections from 2D images. Its classification performance was compared against ResNet-50, Swin-Transformer, ConvNeXtV2, RepViT, and MSPANet, with Grad-CAM heat maps and t-SNE plots used to check whether the model attended to the correct anatomical structures.
headline_result: VMamba achieved the best performance among compared models: sensitivity 94.54%, specificity 99.72%, accuracy 94.42%, AUC 0.997, F1 0.944.

title: Intelligent auxiliary model based on Swin-Transformer for diagnosing fetal ocular malformations
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
patient_population: fetuses with prenatally screened ocular malformations and normal controls
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of fetal ocular malformations
model_description: A Swin-Transformer-based model was trained on fetal ophthalmic ultrasound images to distinguish normal fetal eyes from ocular malformations. Its diagnostic performance was compared against MobileNet-V2, ResNet-50, VGG-16 and Vision-Transformer models, with heat maps and confusion-matrix/t-SNE analysis used to assess interpretability.
dataset_size: 1,282 ophthalmic ultrasound images of malformed fetal eyes and 526 images of normal fetal eyes (8:1:1 train/validation/test split)
headline_result: The Swin-Transformer model achieved sensitivity 88.31%, specificity 97.37%, AUC 0.990, precision 87.31%, F1 87.71% in the test set, outperforming the four comparison models.

title: The Comparison of Convolutional Neural Networks and the Manual Measurement of Cobb Angle in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
patient_population: 500 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis individuals (200 training, 300 validation)
clinical_problem: automatically measuring Cobb angle from whole-spine radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, compared to manual measurement
model_description: A fully automated deep learning framework identifies vertebral boundaries and landmarks on whole-spine radiographs to automatically calculate Cobb angles (proximal thoracic, main thoracic, thoracolumbar/lumbar curves) in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
headline_result: mean absolute error 2.92 degrees (major curve), ICC 0.967, r=0.972; 88.7% within +/-5 degrees

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Fully Automated Assessment of Left Ventricular Volume, Ejection Fraction and Strain: Experience in Pediatric and Young Adult Echocardiography.
model_family: machine learning (vendor automated software, deep learning-based border detection)
patient_population: 50 normal volunteers (children and young adults)
clinical_problem: Can fully automated machine learning-based echocardiographic analysis reliably measure left ventricular volumes, ejection fraction, and strain in children and young adults compared to manual measurement?
model_description: Takes echocardiographic images as input; AutoLV and AutoSTRAIN (TomTec) software automatically detect endocardial borders and output LV volumes, ejection fraction, and myocardial strain.
release_evidence: AutoLV and AutoSTRAIN (TomTec) were employed for the fully automated LV analysis
headline_result: Strong correlation with manual EF (r=0.8373) and GLS (r=0.9766); analysis time significantly shorter with automated methods

title: A YOLOX-Based Deep Instance Segmentation Neural Network for Cardiac Anatomical Structures in Fetal Ultrasound Images.
journal: IEEE/ACM transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics
venue_label: IEEE/ACM transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: YOLOX-based deep instance segmentation neural network
patient_population: fetal echocardiography (congenital heart disease screening)
clinical_problem: automated localization and segmentation of cardiac anatomical structures in the fetal four-chamber view, to support congenital heart disease diagnosis and growth-parameter measurement
model_description: Input: fetal four-chamber-view ultrasound images; output: instance segmentation of 13 types of cardiac anatomical structures.
study_design: methods development and comparison against baseline segmentation methods
headline_result: Outperforms nine competitive baseline methods (no single summary metric reported)

title: Novel AI-Based Algorithm for the Automated Computation of Coronal Parameters in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Patients: A Validation Study on 100 Preoperative Full Spine X-Rays.
model_family: anatomical landmark detection with automated parameter computation
patient_population: 100 preoperative full spine radiographs of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
clinical_problem: computing the coronal parameters that classify an adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curve and guide surgical planning
model_description: Detects clavicles, cervical, thoracic and lumbar spine and sacrum and computes T1 tilt, clavicle angle, coronal balance, lumbar modifier and the regional Cobb angles, with no human input, on every image attempted. Agreement with two experienced raters was excellent, and the pattern of which parameters are hardest matched the humans' — proximal thoracic Cobb angle worst, coronal balance and clavicle angle best.
headline_result: intraclass correlation with human raters 0.78-0.98 across all parameters, computed on 100% of images; mean error 4.7 degrees for proximal thoracic Cobb angle and 0.2 degrees for clavicle angle

title: The Multiscale Surface Vision Transformer.
model_family: hierarchical (shifted-window) vision transformer for cortical surface meshes
patient_population: neonates (preterm and term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP); also tested on adult UK Biobank and MindBoggle datasets
clinical_problem: neonatal brain phenotyping and cortical parcellation from surface MRI data
model_description: A transformer backbone processes cortical surface meshes by applying self-attention within local mesh windows and merging patches hierarchically, producing representations usable for multiple downstream tasks. It was evaluated for predicting neonatal phenotypes from dHCP surface data and, built into a segmentation architecture, for cortical parcellation on adult datasets.
release_evidence: Code and trained models are publicly available at https://github.com/metrics-lab/surface-vision-transformers
dataset_size: dHCP neonatal dataset; UK Biobank and MindBoggle datasets for parcellation
headline_result: Outperforms existing surface deep learning methods for neonatal phenotyping prediction; competitive results on cortical parcellation on UK Biobank and MindBoggle

title: A Deep Learning Pipeline Using Prior Knowledge for Automatic Evaluation of Placenta Accreta Spectrum Disorders With MRI.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
venue_label: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 540 pregnant women with suspected placenta accreta spectrum from two institutions (409 training, 103 internal test, 28 external test)
clinical_problem: diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum antenatally from MRI to assist radiologists, especially less experienced ones
model_description: An nnU-Net segments the placenta on T2-weighted MRI, then DenseNet-based classifiers analyze the utero-placental border region and placental position to diagnose placenta accreta spectrum, using histopathology as ground truth.
study_design: retrospective multi-institution diagnostic model development study
dataset_size: 540 pregnant women (409 training, 103 internal test, 28 external test) from two institutions
headline_result: AUC 0.860 (internal test), 0.897 (external test), exceeding 3 radiologists (AUC 0.737-0.770)

title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Placenta Accreta Spectrum Disorders: Deep Learning Radiomics of Pelvic MRI.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
