clinical_problem: Detecting congenital heart disease (atrial and ventricular septal defects) on pediatric transthoracic echocardiograms across multiple views and modalities to assist less experienced sonographers
model_description: Input: 2D and Doppler transthoracic echocardiogram images across 5 standard views; output: cardiac view classification and prediction of normal vs. ASD vs. VSD status with high-risk region visualization, via a multi-view multi-modal deep learning framework
study_design: retrospective model development with cross-center external testing
headline_result: CHD screening AUC 0.996 within-center, 0.990 cross-center; accuracy 0.994/0.993

title: Artificial intelligence-powered early identification of refractory constipation in children.
patient_population: children with functional constipation (n=77), refractory constipation (n=63), or no constipation (n=65)
clinical_problem: early identification of refractory constipation in children
model_description: Standardized colon size ratios measured on barium enema (sigmoid, descending, transverse, rectum, rectosigmoid) were used to train a linear support vector machine that classifies children into functional constipation, refractory constipation, or non-constipation groups, aiming to flag refractory disease earlier.
headline_result: 81% accuracy (95% CI 79.17-83.19%) distinguishing refractory constipation from the other groups

title: Development of a CT-based radiomics-clinical model to diagnose acute pancreatitis on nonobvious findings on CT in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction.
patient_population: Children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction evaluated for acute pancreatitis
clinical_problem: Diagnosing acute pancreatitis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction when CT findings are nonobvious, using a radiomics-clinical nomogram.
model_description: Input: pancreatic CT radiomics features plus clinical parameters. Output: nomogram predicting presence of acute pancreatitis in children with nonobvious CT findings.
study_design: Single-center retrospective radiomics-clinical nomogram development study.
headline_result: Combined radiomics-clinical nomogram AUC 0.938 (training), 0.864 (validation).

title: AI supported fetal echocardiography with quality assessment.
patient_population: 5,363 images from 2,551 pregnancies (training/validation); 100 patients prospective validation (192 images)
clinical_problem: Automated quality assessment and view/plane segmentation for fetal echocardiography to support the 18-22 week anomaly scan.
model_description: A deep learning model auto-captures and segments fetal echocardiography images, assigning a quality score that determines segmentation reliability, validated prospectively against clinician review.
study_design: retrospective model development with prospective clinical validation
dataset_size: 5,363 images from 2,551 pregnancies; prospective validation of 192 images from 100 patients
headline_result: Overall segmentation accuracy 0.91 (SD 0.09); 0.97 for above-average quality images

title: Transformer based multi-modal MRI fusion for prediction of post-menstrual age and neonatal brain development analysis.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 592 neonates (478 term-born, 114 preterm-born), developing Human Connectome Project
clinical_problem: Estimating post-menstrual age and assessing brain maturity from neonatal brain MRI to help identify preterm-related developmental risk
model_description: A transformer-based multi-modal deep learning model fuses T2-weighted structural MRI and diffusion MRI features via a two-stream dense network and self-attention to estimate post-menstrual age and classify preterm versus term birth, with saliency maps for interpretability.
headline_result: MAE 0.5 weeks for PMA estimation; 95% accuracy for term/preterm classification

title: BOOSTING SKULL-STRIPPING PERFORMANCE FOR PEDIATRIC BRAIN IMAGES.
patient_population: multi-institutional pediatric brain MRI data across scan types and age cohorts
clinical_problem: removing non-brain tissue from pediatric brain MRI scans to enable downstream image analysis
model_description: input pediatric brain MRI of varying scan types; output a skull-stripped brain-only image via a model trained on highly variable synthetic images derived from label maps
release_evidence: We distribute our model at https://w3id.org/synthstrip.
study_design: methods development study evaluated across multiple pediatric datasets
headline_result: substantially outperforms pediatric baselines across scan types and age cohorts; runtime <1 minute (no single summary metric reported)

title: Automating the Human Action of First-Trimester Biometry Measurement from Real-World Freehand Ultrasound.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: hybrid CNN (classification-regression guidance network + confident-frame detector + segmentation network)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing first-trimester ultrasound
clinical_problem: automating standard-plane selection and crown-rump length measurement from freehand first-trimester ultrasound video
model_description: input freehand first-trimester ultrasound video; output automatically detected standard planes, segmented fetal landmarks, and a crown-rump length/gestational age estimate
headline_result: Pearson r=0.92, R2=0.84 vs. expert CRL measurement; mean absolute error 0.834 weeks for fetal age

title: Pulmonary vascular reactivity in growth restricted fetuses using computational modelling and machine learning analysis of fetal Doppler waveforms.
model_family: machine learning clustering plus computational hemodynamic model
patient_population: 97 growth-restricted and 111 normally grown singleton fetuses, 24-37 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: characterizing pulmonary vascular reactivity in growth-restricted fetuses using Doppler ultrasound
model_description: Doppler ultrasound waveforms of the pulmonary vessels, taken before and after maternal hyperoxygenation, are classified into clusters by machine learning and fed into a computational model that estimates the ratio of pulmonary vascular resistance before and after oxygenation, distinguishing responsive from non-responsive growth-restricted fetuses.
headline_result: cluster A PVR ratio 0.98±0.33 vs cluster B 0.78±0.28, p=0.0156

title: Deep learning-based automated lesion segmentation on pediatric focal cortical dysplasia II preoperative MRI: a reliable approach.
patient_population: 65 pediatric patients with pathology-confirmed focal cortical dysplasia type II
clinical_problem: detecting and segmenting focal cortical dysplasia lesions on preoperative MRI in children with epilepsy
model_description: Takes a high-resolution 3D T1-MPRAGE brain MRI as input and outputs an automatic voxel-level detection map and segmentation of focal cortical dysplasia lesions, using a 3D full-resolution nnU-Net.
study_design: retrospective pilot study with algorithm development and internal validation
headline_result: sensitivity 0.73; mean Dice-Sørensen coefficient 0.57 on the testing dataset

title: Evaluating the Robustness of a Deep Learning Bone Age Algorithm to Clinical Image Variation Using Computational Stress Testing.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 1,425 pediatric hand radiographs (RSNA internal test set), 1,202 (Digital Hand Atlas external test set)
clinical_problem: testing the robustness of an automated bone age assessment algorithm to real-world image variations in pediatric hand radiographs
model_description: The award-winning deep learning bone age model from the 2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge takes pediatric hand radiographs and outputs a predicted bone age; this study computationally stress-tests it against image transformations (rotation, flips, brightness, contrast, inversion, laterality marker, resolution).
dataset_size: 1,425 pediatric hand radiographs (RSNA internal test set), 1,202 (Digital Hand Atlas external test set)
headline_result: mean absolute difference 6.8 months (RSNA), 6.9 months (DHA); clinically significant error proportions differed for 57% (19/33) of image transformations

title: Application of artificial neural networks to evaluate femur development in the human fetus.
patient_population: Human fetuses aged 17-30 weeks from spontaneous miscarriages and preterm deliveries
clinical_problem: Assessing fetal femur development (ossification center parameters) using AI to aid prenatal detection of skeletal anomalies.
model_description: Input: gestational age and femur length. Output: an MLP (2-3-2-5 architecture) predicts five parameters of the femoral shaft primary ossification center (linear dimensions, cross-sectional areas, volume) derived from CT/digital image analysis.
headline_result: Correlation between predicted and actual values: R=0.955 (training), 0.942 (validation), 0.953 (testing).

title: Gated cardiac CT in infants: What can we expect from deep learning image reconstruction algorithm?
patient_population: Anthropomorphic pediatric (infant) phantom study (not real patients)
clinical_problem: Reducing radiation dose in ECG-gated cardiac CT for infants with congenital heart disease using deep learning image reconstruction while preserving image quality.
model_description: A Deep Learning Image Reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm processes low-dose ECG-gated cardiac CT phantom images and reconstructs images with improved vessel detectability and spatial resolution compared to iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V), enabling dose reduction.
headline_result: DLIR-H improved detectability 2.4% and discrimination 20.9% vs ASIR-V50; enabled 64% dose reduction

title: Enhancing pediatric pneumonia diagnosis through masked autoencoders.
patient_population: pediatric chest X-ray dataset (children, particularly under 5), pretraining on adult chest X-rays then fine-tuning on pediatric pneumonia dataset
clinical_problem: improving diagnosis of pediatric pneumonia (and distinguishing bacterial vs viral) from chest X-rays despite scarce labeled pediatric data
model_description: Input: pediatric chest X-ray images; output: classification of normal vs. pneumonia, and further into bacterial vs. viral pneumonia, using a Masked Autoencoder pretrained (self-supervised) on adult chest X-rays and fine-tuned on a pediatric pneumonia dataset.
study_design: retrospective model development with self-supervised pretraining and internal evaluation
headline_result: AUC 0.996, accuracy 95.89% (normal vs pneumonia); accuracy 93.86% for 3-class (normal/bacterial/viral)

title: Cognitive Impairment Is Related to Glymphatic System Dysfunction in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis.
patient_population: 65 pediatric MS patients (median age 15.5) and 23 age/sex-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: predicting cognitive impairment in pediatric multiple sclerosis from glymphatic-system MRI markers
model_description: Inputs are MRI-derived diffusion metrics (DTI-ALPS glymphatic index, lesion volume, white matter diffusivity/anisotropy) and IQ; output is a random forest prediction of cognitive impairment status, with feature-importance ranking of MRI predictors.
dataset_size: 65 pediatric MS patients and 23 healthy controls
headline_result: out-of-bag AUC 0.762 for predicting cognitive impairment; DTI-ALPS index was the top predictor (relative importance 100%)

title: Predicting event-free survival after induction of remission in high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma: combining 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT radiomics and clinical factors.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 172 patients with high-risk neuroblastoma reviewed; 87 met inclusion criteria (training/validation 7:3)
clinical_problem: predicting event-free survival after remission induction in high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma from 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT images of the lumbar vertebral bodies are combined with clinical risk factors in a Cox-regression nomogram to predict event-free survival after remission induction.
study_design: retrospective radiomics-nomogram development and validation study
headline_result: Nomogram C-index 0.819 (training), 0.712 (validation); 1-year AUC 0.899/0.748

title: Noise suppression of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy improves paediatric brain tumour classification.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: adaptive wavelet noise suppression (AWNS) plus supervised machine learning classifier (Naive Bayes)
patient_population: 83/42 children (two cohorts) with ependymoma, medulloblastoma, or pilocytic astrocytoma across four UK centres
clinical_problem: classifying pediatric brain tumor type (ependymoma, medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma) from proton MR spectroscopy
model_description: Clinical 1H-MR spectroscopy is denoised with adaptive wavelet noise suppression before metabolite concentrations are extracted as features and classified with supervised machine learning (with SMOTE oversampling) to distinguish three pediatric brain tumor types; noise suppression improved classification accuracy.
dataset_size: 83 children (1.5T cohort) and 42 children (3T cohort) from four UK centres
headline_result: classification accuracy improved from 81% to 88% (overall, 1.5T) and 62% to 76% (overall, 3T) after noise suppression

title: High Resolution Multi-delay Arterial Spin Labeling with Transformer based Denoising for Pediatric Perfusion MRI.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: Typically developing children undergoing test-retest perfusion MRI
clinical_problem: Improving image quality of pediatric cerebral perfusion MRI (multi-delay arterial spin labeling) to more reliably quantify cerebral blood flow and arterial transit time in children.
model_description: Input: multi-delay arterial spin labeling perfusion MRI images. A Transformer-based deep-learning model, trained using k-space-weighted-image-average denoised references, denoises images to improve SNR and repeatability of cerebral blood flow and arterial transit time maps.
dataset_size: 21 typically developing children aged 8-17 years, test-retest scans

title: Deep Learning Model for Prediction of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in Preterm Infants Using Chest Radiographs.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
venue_label: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
model_family: transfer learning deep learning model (segmentation + image fusion)
patient_population: 1,491 chest radiographs for lung segmentation dataset; 1,021 chest radiographs of preterm infants for BPD prediction dataset
clinical_problem: early prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants from chest radiographs
model_description: Input: chest radiographs of preterm infants (as early as ≤24 hours postnatal age); output: automated lung region segmentation (transfer learning) followed by image-fusion-based prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia risk, compared against expert diagnostic accuracy.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal evaluation
dataset_size: 1,491 CXRs (segmentation) + 1,021 CXRs (BPD prediction) of preterm infants
headline_result: lung segmentation Dice 0.960; BPD prediction model exceeded diagnostic accuracy of experts

title: Development of a diagnostic support system for distal humerus fracture using artificial intelligence.
patient_population: 4,931 elbow radiographs from patients aged 7 years and older with suspected traumatic distal humerus fracture
clinical_problem: Detecting distal humerus fractures on anteroposterior and lateral elbow radiographs in patients seven years and older, to reduce missed or delayed fracture diagnoses
model_description: Input: AP and lateral elbow radiographs cropped around the capitellum; output: binary classification (fractured vs. normal), via a ResNet18 deep learning model
headline_result: accuracy 69.14%, specificity 95.89%, sensitivity 61.49%, AUC 0.787 (vs. 0.580 for senior surgeon reference)

title: Automated body organ segmentation, volumetry and population-averaged atlas for 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted fetal body MRI.
model_family: neural network organ segmentation with a population-averaged atlas
patient_population: 91 normal control fetal 3T MRI datasets across 22-38 weeks gestational age
clinical_problem: volumetry of fetal organs, which is currently done by slice-by-slice manual segmentation of motion-corrupted stacks
model_description: Supplies the two things missing before fetal organ volumetry can be automated: a parcellation protocol defining ten organ regions, which did not previously exist in any standard form, and the first population-averaged T2-weighted atlas of the fetal body. The network trained on that protocol then produced organ growth charts across gestation that behaved as expected, which is the sanity check for a normative tool.
headline_result: robust segmentation across gestational ages, with organ growth charts from 22-38 weeks showing the expected volume increase

title: Multiparametric MRI-Based Interpretable Radiomics Machine Learning Model Differentiates Medulloblastoma and Ependymoma in Children: A Two-Center Study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: radiomics with machine-learning classifiers (XGBoost, Bernoulli naive Bayes, logistic regression, SVM, linear SVC)
patient_population: 135 children with medulloblastoma or ependymoma from two centers
clinical_problem: distinguishing medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children on brain MRI
model_description: Takes radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI as input and outputs a machine-learning classification distinguishing medulloblastoma from ependymoma, benchmarked against human expert diagnosis.
study_design: retrospective two-center model development with external validation
headline_result: XGBoost AUC 0.92 on test set and 0.80 on external validation; human expert diagnosis AUC 0.66 (test) and 0.69 (external)

title: A novel center-based deep contrastive metric learning method for the detection of polymicrogyria in pediatric brain MRI.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
venue_label: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
patient_population: Children with polymicrogyria and controls from the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (PPMR dataset)
clinical_problem: Detecting polymicrogyria, a subtle cortical malformation, on pediatric brain MRI
model_description: A center-based deep contrastive metric learning anomaly-detection method flags pediatric brain MRIs likely to show polymicrogyria, intended as a computer-aided screening tool for radiologists; code and a new open pediatric MRI dataset (PPMR) are released publicly.
release_evidence: Our code is available at: https://github.com/RichardChangCA/... ; dataset available at kaggle.com/datasets/lingfengzhang/pediatric-polymicrogyria-mri-dataset
study_design: Retrospective model development study, first ML application to detect polymicrogyria from MRI
dataset_size: Small, imbalanced pediatric MRI dataset (PPMR; exact N not stated in abstract)
headline_result: 88.07% recall at 71.86% precision

title: [The diagnostic value of lung ultrasound in children with community-acquired pneumonia].
journal: Zhonghua er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of pediatrics
venue_label: Zhonghua er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of pediatrics
model_family: LASSO feature selection with random forest classifier
patient_population: 422 hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia
clinical_problem: diagnostic value of lung ultrasound for community-acquired pneumonia and severity prediction in hospitalized children
model_description: Lung ultrasound signs (consolidation, confluent B-lines, pleural effusion) are selected by LASSO regression and fed into a random forest classifier to diagnose pneumonia (against chest CT) and to predict severe disease in hospitalized children.
dataset_size: 422 children with CAP (110 with chest CT)
headline_result: AUC 0.87 (full variables) / 0.84 (LASSO-selected) for CAP diagnosis; AUC 0.76 for severe CAP using consolidation size/body surface area

title: Exploring the diagnostic value of ultrasound radiomics for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
model_family: random forest (best of RF, LR, KNN, SVM, MLP)
patient_population: 150 neonates with lung disease (60 NRDS, 30 each pneumonia/meconium aspiration/transient tachypnea) at a maternity and children's hospital
clinical_problem: Objectively diagnosing neonatal respiratory distress syndrome from lung ultrasound, reducing reliance on operator-dependent visual interpretation
model_description: Texture features extracted from lung ultrasound images using PyRadiomics are used to train random forest, logistic regression, KNN, SVM and MLP classifiers to distinguish neonatal respiratory distress syndrome from other neonatal lung diseases
headline_result: Random forest AUC 0.99, not significantly different from experienced physicians (AUC 0.98, P=0.24) but significantly better than junior physicians (AUC 0.85, P<0.0001)

title: Menarche, pubertal timing and the brain: female-specific patterns of brain maturation beyond age-related development.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: machine learning classification model and brain-age prediction model
patient_population: age-matched adolescent females from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) cohort; brain-age model trained on the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort
clinical_problem: classifying pubertal status (pre- vs post-menarche) from structural brain MRI and comparing it to brain-age-based markers of neurodevelopment in adolescent girls
model_description: Machine learning model trained on cortical and subcortical structural MRI features to classify pre- versus post-menarche status, compared against a separately trained brain-age prediction model applied to the same data
study_design: cross-sectional machine learning classification study using cohort MRI data
headline_result: machine learning model achieved moderate but statistically significant accuracy in classifying menarche status

title: AI-Assisted X-ray Fracture Detection in Residency Training: Evaluation in Pediatric and Adult Trauma Patients.
model_family: machine learning fracture detection algorithm used as a reading aid
patient_population: 200 radiographs from patients aged 1 to 95 (mean 40.7 years), half containing at least one fracture, read by four residents of differing experience
clinical_problem: whether AI assistance helps radiology residents find fractures, and what that means for training
model_description: A reader study framed around residency training rather than around the algorithm. Residents gained 19 points of sensitivity with the aid, at essentially no cost in specificity, with the largest gains for the least experienced. The authors raise the training question directly: a tool that lifts a trainee to expert-level detection also removes the errors trainees learn from.
headline_result: resident sensitivity rose from 58% to 77% with AI (p < 0.001) with specificity unchanged; stand-alone AI sensitivity 93% at 77% specificity; interpretation time fell and confidence rose

title: Supervised contrastive learning enhances graph convolutional networks for predicting neurodevelopmental deficits in very preterm infants using brain structural connectome.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: graph convolutional network (GCN) with supervised contrastive learning (SCL)
patient_population: ~280 very preterm infants (CINEPS cohort), MRI at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: early prediction of neurodevelopmental deficits (cognition, language, motor) at 2 years corrected age in very preterm infants using brain structural connectome from MRI at term-equivalent age
model_description: A graph convolutional network trained with supervised contrastive learning takes the brain structural connectome (derived from diffusion MRI at term-equivalent age) as a graph input and outputs predicted risk of neurodevelopmental deficits (cognitive, language, motor) at 2 years corrected age in very preterm infants.
study_design: prospective single-cohort study with deep learning model development
headline_result: Mean AUCs 0.72-0.75 for predicting three neurodevelopmental deficits

title: Correlative Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Cobb Angle Measurements and Human-Based Measurements in Adolescent Idiopathic and Congenital Scoliosis.
journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
venue_label: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
patient_population: 130 patients with 3-foot standing spine radiographs for idiopathic or congenital scoliosis over a 10-year period
clinical_problem: automatic Cobb angle measurement for idiopathic and congenital scoliosis in children and adolescents
model_description: A segmentation-based Augmented U-Net model with non-square kernels automatically measures Cobb angles on 3-foot standing spine radiographs, compared with manual radiologist measurements in idiopathic and congenital scoliosis cohorts.
headline_result: SMAPE 11.82% combined cohort; 13.02% idiopathic, 11.90% congenital

title: Sensorless volumetric reconstruction of fetal brain freehand ultrasound scans with deep implicit representation.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: fetal freehand 2D ultrasound video sequences from multiple manufacturers
clinical_problem: reconstructing 3D fetal brain volumes from freehand 2D ultrasound sweeps without external tracking, to improve prenatal brain assessment
model_description: ImplicitVol takes a set of untracked 2D freehand fetal brain ultrasound images, predicts their 3D spatial locations, and reconstructs a continuous 3D volumetric representation of the fetal brain.

title: Neuroanatomical Predictors of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS)-Induced Modifications in Neurocognitive Task Performance in Typically Developing Individuals.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
venue_label: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: machine learning (unspecified algorithms; general linear models + ML)
patient_population: 57 typically developing male and female children who received tDCS
clinical_problem: predicting individual children's behavioral response to transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) from neuroanatomical MRI measures (cortical thickness, surface area), to inform future personalized neuromodulation treatment in neurodevelopmental disorders
model_description: Machine-learning algorithms use structural MRI-derived cortical thickness and surface area measures as input to predict individual children's task-performance response to transcranial direct current stimulation as output.
study_design: prospective experimental (sham-controlled) study with machine learning model development
headline_result: Highest ML accuracy: 65% of behavioral variance in N-back task performance explained by surface area (DLPFCleft stimulation)

title: Supervised representation learning based on various levels of pediatric radiographic views for transfer learning.
patient_population: ~70,000 pediatric X-ray images collected over 24 years at Asan Medical Center
clinical_problem: building pediatric-specific pretrained radiograph models to improve downstream pediatric radiology AI tasks such as fracture classification and bone age assessment, addressing the mismatch of natural-image pretrained models for grayscale medical images
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; foundation model / vision-language
model_description: PedXnets are Inception V3-based models pretrained on ~70,000 pediatric radiographs classified by radiographic view (7, 30, or 68 classes) to serve as domain-specific backbones for transfer learning; validated on downstream tasks of pediatric fracture classification and bone age assessment.
study_design: retrospective single-center pretraining and transfer-learning validation study
dataset_size: ~70,000 pediatric X-ray images (24 years, single center)

title: Deep-learning computer vision can identify increased nuchal translucency in the first trimester of pregnancy.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 560 fetuses between 11 and 13 weeks 6 days gestation, 88 with NT >3.5mm
clinical_problem: Automatically detecting an increased nuchal translucency, a marker of genetic/structural fetal anomalies, on first-trimester ultrasound
model_description: A U-Net convolutional neural network segments the fetus and the nuchal translucency region on standardized mid-sagittal first-trimester ultrasound images, computing an NT:fetus ratio to flag thickened (anomalous) NT
headline_result: AUROC 0.96 for detecting thick NT on model segmentation; 94% sensitivity at 91% specificity

title: A deep learning framework for identifying and segmenting three vessels in fetal heart ultrasound images.
model_family: YOLOv5 (detection) and modified DeepLabv3 with an Attentional Multi-scale Feature Fusion (AMFF) module (segmentation)
body_region: fetal heart (three-vessel view: pulmonary artery, aorta, superior vena cava)
patient_population: 511 fetal heart three-vessel-view ultrasound images
clinical_problem: automatically detecting and segmenting the three great vessels on the fetal heart ultrasound three-vessel view to assist prenatal congenital heart disease screening
model_description: Two-stage deep learning framework: YOLOv5 detects and localizes the three vessels on fetal heart ultrasound images, then a modified DeepLabv3 with an attentional multi-scale feature fusion module segments each vessel within the localized region
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal evaluation
headline_result: Dice coefficients of 85.55%, 89.12%, and 77.54% for pulmonary artery, aorta, and superior vena cava respectively

title: From 2D to 3D: automatic measurement of the Cobb angle in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis with the weight-bearing 3D imaging.
journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
venue_label: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 53 AIS patients, 88 spinal curves
clinical_problem: comparing traditional 2D Cobb angle measurement to automated 3D Cobb angle measurement methods using weight-bearing 3D imaging in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: Input: weight-bearing 3D spine imaging; output: automated 3D segmentation of the spine and femoral heads using a 3D-UNet deep learning model, from which Cobb angles are automatically calculated by three different 3D geometric methods and compared to manual 2D measurement.
headline_result: Plane Projection Method values not significantly different from 2D method; Analytical and Plane Intersecting Methods gave significantly larger estimates

title: Bridging the gap: improving correspondence between low-field and high-field magnetic resonance images in young people.
patient_population: 70 individuals, mean age 20.39 years (range 9-26 years)
clinical_problem: improving correspondence between low-field and high-field brain MRI in young people
model_description: T1- and T2-weighted images from a 64mT low-field portable MRI system are processed by SynthSR, a convolutional-neural-network super-resolution method, to produce images with improved correspondence to matched 3T high-field images; performance is compared against a multi-orientation averaging alternative.
headline_result: SynthSR improved correspondence to high-field images to r=0.85-0.97 for most brain volume measures (vs. r=0.60-0.88 uncorrected); cortical thickness correspondence remained poor (r=0.14)

title: Voxelwise Multivariate Analysis of Brain-Psychosocial Associations in Adolescents Reveals 6 Latent Dimensions of Cognition and Psychopathology.
journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
venue_label: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
patient_population: 11,288 children ages 9-10, ABCD Study cohort (baseline)
clinical_problem: Identifying latent brain-behavior dimensions linking gray matter density patterns to psychopathology symptoms in children, using machine learning.
model_description: A sparse partial least squares machine learning framework takes voxelwise structural MRI gray matter density and psychosocial questionnaire data as input and identifies six latent brain-behavior dimensions related to cognition and psychopathology.
headline_result: 6 latent dimensions identified, 4 related to mental health (all p<.03)

title: The application of machine learning based on computed tomography images in the identification of renal tumors in children.
model_family: radiomics-based machine learning (feature selection with ANOVA/RFE, multiple classifier pipelines)
patient_population: 82 children with renal tumors at a single pediatric urology department
clinical_problem: preoperative differentiation of Wilms tumor from non-Wilms renal tumors in children using CT
model_description: input CT radiomics texture features extracted from the tumor region of interest; output a machine-learning classification distinguishing Wilms from non-Wilms renal tumors
headline_result: best internal-validation AUC 0.792 (corticomedullary phase) and 0.655 (nephrogenic phase)

title: Clinical-functional correlation with brain volumetry in severe perinatal asphyxia: a case report.
patient_population: A single term infant with perinatal asphyxia (case report)
clinical_problem: Correlating longitudinal brain volumetric changes, measured with 3D machine learning models, with clinical/neurodevelopmental outcome in a case of severe perinatal asphyxia.
model_description: Input: longitudinal 3D brain MRI. Output: ML-based volumetric analysis of basal ganglia, thalamus and cerebellar structures over time in a newborn with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, correlated with clinical neurodevelopmental outcome.
study_design: Case report with longitudinal 3D volumetric MRI analysis.

title: The maternal-fetal neurodevelopmental groundings of preterm birth risk.
patient_population: 31 singleton pregnancies, 28-34 weeks gestation (19 low-risk, 12 high-risk for preterm birth)
clinical_problem: using fetal brain functional connectivity from resting-state fMRI combined with maternal risk factors to improve prediction of preterm birth risk
model_description: A random forest model (MaFra-Neuro) combines the Maternal Frailty Inventory score with fetal brain functional connectivity features derived from resting-state fMRI (estimated using the Greedy Equivalence Search algorithm) as input to predict preterm birth risk, gestational age at birth, and related perinatal outcomes.

title: High sensitivity methods for automated rib fracture detection in pediatric radiographs.
patient_population: 1,109 pediatric chest radiographs, manually labeled by 7 pediatric radiologists
clinical_problem: Automated detection and localization of rib fractures on pediatric chest radiographs to improve sensitivity for identifying non-accidental trauma in children under 3.
model_description: Ensembled CNN object detectors (RetinaNet, YOLOv5) with a dynamic 'avalanche decision' threshold scheme take pediatric chest radiographs as input and detect/localize rib fractures to flag possible non-accidental trauma.
headline_result: F2 score 0.725±0.012 (best ensembled model) vs expert inter-reader F2 0.732

title: Predicting depression risk in early adolescence via multimodal brain imaging.

title: The value of radiomics features of the spleen as surrogates for differentiating subtypes of common pediatric lymphomas.

title: Applying machine learning in screening for Down Syndrome in both trimesters for diverse healthcare scenarios.

title: Radiomic study of antenatal prediction of severe placenta accreta spectrum from MRI.

headline_result: Clinical-radiomic model AUC 0.713, accuracy 0.695, sensitivity 0.843, specificity 0.447

title: Regional brain structural network topology mediates the associations between white matter damage and disease severity in first-episode, Treatment-naïve pubertal children with major depressive disorder.

headline_result: Diagnostic model achieved AUROC 0.88 and F1 score 0.80

title: Beyond hand-crafted features for pretherapeutic molecular status identification of pediatric low-grade gliomas.
patient_population: 336 patients treated for pediatric low-grade glioma (1999-2018)
clinical_problem: non-invasively determining the molecular/genetic status of pediatric low-grade glioma from MRI to guide use of targeted therapy

headline_result: Mean AUC 0.824 (combined model) vs 0.802 (radiomics) vs 0.764 (CNN)

title: Subject-specific atlas for automatic brain tissue segmentation of neonatal magnetic resonance images.
model_family: random forest classifier atlas-based segmentation with expectation-maximization Markov random field
patient_population: 40 neonatal MR images, gestational age 37-44 weeks
clinical_problem: segmenting gray matter, white matter and CSF on neonatal brain MRI

headline_result: overall accuracy 94.3%, Dice 0.945 (GM), 0.947 (WM), 0.912 (CSF); up to 4% improvement over comparator methods

title: Fetal-BET: Brain Extraction Tool for Fetal MRI.
journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
venue_label: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology

headline_result: accurate brain extraction on heterogeneous test data from different scanners, pathological brains, and various gestational stages (no single summary metric stated)

title: Using machine learning to automatically measure kyphotic and lordotic angle measurements on radiographs for children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.

title: FLUEnT: Transformer for detecting lung consolidations in videos using fused lung ultrasound encodings.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: transformer combining variational autoencoder embeddings, ResNet-18 features, and patient metadata
patient_population: pediatric lung ultrasound pneumonia patients (video-level dataset, size not specified in abstract)
clinical_problem: detecting lung consolidations on pediatric lung ultrasound video for pneumonia diagnosis
model_description: FLUEnT combines frame-level embeddings from a variational autoencoder, spatial features from a ResNet-18, and encoded patient metadata into fused encodings that are passed to a transformer for binary classification of lung consolidation presence in pediatric lung ultrasound videos.

title: nnU-Net-based Segmentation of Tumor Subcompartments in Pediatric Medulloblastoma Using Multiparametric MRI: A Multi-institutional Study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, P.H.S.

study_design: retrospective multi-institutional segmentation model development and cross-site evaluation
headline_result: Dice scores for tumor habitat 0.80-0.86 across three test sites

title: Deep generative model of the distal tibial classic metaphyseal lesion in infants: assessment of synthetic images.
model_family: mask conditional diffusion model (generative deep learning)
patient_population: 39 infants (mean age 4.1 months) with distal tibia radiographs, used to derive real and synthetic test images
clinical_problem: generating synthetic training images of classic metaphyseal lesions, a fracture highly specific to infant abuse, to augment limited training data
model_description: A mask conditional diffusion model (MaC-DM) generates synthetic distal tibia radiographs with and without classic metaphyseal lesions to augment a limited training dataset for automated fracture detection; three blinded radiologists then assessed whether the synthetic images correctly showed the lesion and whether they could distinguish real from synthetic images.
study_design: retrospective single-center generative model development with reader study
dataset_size: 100 real images tested (from 177 normal/73 CML dataset); 100 synthetic images generated
headline_result: radiologists diagnosed CML with kappa 0.90, accuracy 92%, but could not distinguish real from synthetic images (kappa 0.05, accuracy 53%)

title: Multimodal Model for Predicting Fetal Acidosis in Delivery Room.
journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
venue_label: Studies in health technology and informatics
body_region: fetal heart / whole fetus (delivery room monitoring)
patient_population: 2,266 deliveries at a tertiary hospital delivery room
clinical_problem: prediction of fetal acidosis at delivery
model_description: Inputs are features extracted from electronic medical records, biosignals (cardiotocography) and imaging data (including fetal echocardiography), concatenated into a single feature vector; a classifier trained on this multimodal input outputs a predicted probability of post-delivery fetal acidosis.
headline_result: AUROC 0.752 on the test dataset

title: Separating group- and individual-level brain signatures in the newborn functional connectome: A deep learning approach.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 464 neonates and 100 adults from public rs-fMRI datasets
clinical_problem: Can individual-specific brain functional connectivity patterns be identified in newborns using resting-state fMRI, similar to what is seen in adults?
model_description: Takes resting-state fMRI-derived functional connectivity matrices as input; a variational autoencoder outputs latent representations used to predict age and identify individual subjects across repeat scans.
study_design: retrospective methods development using public neonatal and adult rs-fMRI datasets
headline_result: Individual identification accuracy ~45% with VAE vs. ~10-30% with linear models; age prediction r~0.7

title: Learning from the few: Fine-grained approach to pediatric wrist pathology recognition on a limited dataset.
model_family: fine-grained deep convolutional neural network architecture with LION optimizer and Grad-CAM
patient_population: children and adolescents with wrist trauma radiographs (limited dataset)
clinical_problem: recognizing pediatric wrist pathologies, particularly fractures, on trauma X-rays
model_description: A fine-grained deep convolutional neural network automatically identifies discriminative regions in pediatric wrist X-rays to classify wrist pathologies, refined via ablation analysis and the LION optimizer, with Grad-CAM used to visualize the regions driving each prediction.
dataset_size: limited dataset (exact size not stated in abstract)
headline_result: accuracy 86% (augmented) and 84% (original) test sets; fracture sensitivity 97%

title: Identifying developmental changes in functional brain connectivity associated with cognitive functioning in children and adolescents with ADHD.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: machine learning models on movie-watching fMRI connectivity
patient_population: children and adolescents aged 6-16 (373 with ADHD, 106 neurotypical) undergoing movie-watching fMRI
clinical_problem: predicting cognitive abilities (IQ and related measures) in children and adolescents with ADHD from functional connectivity
model_description: Functional connectivity patterns recorded while children and adolescents watched a short movie during fMRI were used to train machine learning models that predict IQ and other cognitive measures (visual-spatial, verbal comprehension, fluid reasoning), evaluated with out-of-sample cross-validation. The models successfully predicted these measures in younger children (6-11) with ADHD but not in adolescents (12-16) with ADHD.
dataset_size: 373 children/adolescents with ADHD, 106 neurotypical controls, ages 6-16
headline_result: Machine learning models predicted IQ and cognitive measures in early/middle childhood (ages 6-11) with ADHD but failed to generalize to adolescents (12-16)

title: Assessment of deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) on image quality in pediatric cardiac CT datasets type of manuscript: Original research.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

clinical_problem: Improving image quality of pediatric cardiac CT while managing radiation dose, comparing deep-learning reconstruction to conventional iterative reconstruction

title: Machine learning approach for the prediction of macrosomia.

clinical_problem: predicting fetal macrosomia in the third trimester using ultrasound examination data to guide delivery planning

study_design: retrospective single-center predictive model development study

title: Development and testing of a deep learning algorithm to detect lung consolidation among children with pneumonia using hand-held ultrasound.

clinical_problem: Detecting pulmonary consolidation on point-of-care lung ultrasound to diagnose pneumonia in hospitalized children
model_description: Input: point-of-care lung ultrasound video clips from a handheld transducer across 12 lung zones; output: detection and localization of pulmonary consolidation, via a deep learning algorithm trained on annotated video/frame-level features enriched with adult data
study_design: prospective multicenter algorithm development and testing
dataset_size: 107 pediatric participants, 117 exams, 604 positive/589 negative consolidation videos
headline_result: accuracy 88.5%, sensitivity 88%, specificity 89%

headline_result: 50/86 features highly correlated (PCC>=0.8) SmartSpeed vs C-SENSE; only 15/86 for SmartSpeed-SuperRes

title: High-level feature-guided attention optimized neural network for neonatal lateral ventricular dilatation prediction.

title: Comparative analysis of brain age prediction using structural and diffusion MRIs in neonates.

title: AIDA (Artificial Intelligence Dystocia Algorithm) in Prolonged Dystocic Labor: Focus on Asynclitism Degree.

title: High-quality expert annotations enhance artificial intelligence model accuracy for osteosarcoma X-ray diagnosis.

clinical_problem: Detecting osteosarcoma on knee X-rays at initial consultation to improve early diagnosis in pediatric and young adult patients
model_description: Input: knee X-ray images; output: binary classification of osteosarcoma vs. normal, via a U-Net-based AI model trained on expert-annotated data with data-centric augmentation techniques
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with independent test-set evaluation
dataset_size: 468 osteosarcoma + 378 normal training images; independent test of 268 osteosarcoma + 554 normal images
headline_result: sensitivity 95.52%, specificity 96.21%, AUC 0.989

title: EchoAGE: Echocardiography-based Neural Network Model Forecasting Heart Biological Age.

clinical_problem: estimating heart biological age from echocardiographic parameters to assess cardiac health status beyond chronological age, including in children with progeria syndrome

title: Accuracy of CAD4TB (Computer-Aided Detection for Tuberculosis) on paediatric chest radiographs.

title: Detecting pediatric appendicular fractures using artificial intelligence.

clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicular fractures in pediatric emergency department trauma patients
model_description: Input: pediatric limb radiographs; output: detection of acute fractures, evaluated both as a standalone model and as assistive support for emergency physicians.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with reader study comparing physicians with and without AI assistance
headline_result: Model: mAP50 89%, sensitivity 90%, specificity 92%, F1 90%; AI assistance improved physician sensitivity from 93.7% to 97.0% and accuracy from 88% to 94.9%

clinical_problem: enhancing low-field MRI image quality to improve visualization of epileptogenic lesions in children, for use in resource-limited settings

title: Assessment of supervised longitudinal learning methods: Insights from predicting low birth weight and very low birth weight using prenatal ultrasound measurements.

title: Deep learning for detecting prenatal alcohol exposure in pediatric brain MRI: a transfer learning approach with explainability insights.

title: Conditional generative adversarial network-assisted system for radiation-free evaluation of scoliosis using a single smartphone photograph: a model development and validation study.

title: Streamline tractography of the fetal brain in utero with machine learning.

title: A deep learning model for differentiating paediatric intracranial germ cell tumour subtypes and predicting survival with MRI: a multicentre prospective study.

title: Functional imaging derived ADHD biotypes based on deep clustering: a study on personalized medication therapy guidance.

headline_result: mean SUV relative difference -2.6±5.8%; lesion overlap Dice 0.92±0.08

headline_result: AUC 0.883 (YOLOv7+UNet3+) vs 0.749 (residents), 0.808 (fellows)

title: Assessing the Diagnostic Performance of Automated Pituitary Gland Volume Measurement for Idiopathic Central Precocious Puberty.

title: MRI Application in Quantification of Epiphyseal Development in the Wrist and Bone Age Estimation of Han Male Adolescents in East China.

model_description: Input is wrist MRI (T1WI/T2WI) with graded and measured epiphyseal development at the distal radius/ulna and metacarpals, combined with height and weight; a support vector machine (best of several models tested) outputs a predicted bone age.
headline_result: SVM accuracy within 1.0 year of true age 88.7%, within 1.5 years 96.0%

title: An accurate pediatric bone age prediction model using deep learning and contrast conversion.
model_family: CNN (ResNet50, VGG19, Inception V3, Xception compared)

model_description: input left-hand radiographs with various contrast-conversion preprocessing techniques; output a predicted bone age via CNN models, best performance from Xception

title: Diffusion deep learning for brain age prediction and longitudinal tracking in children through adulthood.
patient_population: healthy children and adolescents aged 3-30, 16 multisite datasets
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: brain age / neurodevelopmental biomarker estimation from MRI

dataset_size: 32,851 T1-weighted MRI scans from 16 multisite datasets
headline_result: MAE 2.78 years (first external validation), 1.97 years (second external validation)

title: Motion-invariant variational autoencoding of brain structural connectomes.

clinical_problem: Remove motion-induced artifacts from brain structural connectomes derived from diffusion MRI to more accurately relate brain networks to cognition

headline_result: Motion-adjusted connectomes more strongly associated with cognition-related traits than competing approaches (no single number given)

title: Generative AI for rapid diffusion MRI with improved image quality, reliability, and generalizability.

age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult

study_design: retrospective method development with out-of-domain fine-tuning across multiple pediatric and adult cohorts
dataset_size: HCP training n=1021; fine-tuning/eval cohorts of children (n=40), adults with TBI (n=40), adolescents with ICH (n=8)

title: Gray matter correlates of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder in boys versus girls with sensory processing dysfunction.

clinical_problem: characterize gray matter volume/density differences associated with ADHD comorbidity in children with sensory processing dysfunction, by sex

study_design: retrospective case-control neuroimaging study using deep learning segmentation

title: Explainable Multimodal Graph Isomorphism Network for Interpreting Sex Differences in Adolescent Neurodevelopment.
patient_population: adolescents undergoing multi-task fMRI
clinical_problem: characterizing sex-related differences in adolescent brain functional connectivity (neurodevelopment)
model_description: Takes multi-task fMRI-derived brain connectivity graphs as input and outputs a sex classification, with GNNExplainer identifying the sub-networks driving the prediction.

headline_result: 81.67% improvement in classification accuracy versus competing models

title: Consistency between artificial intelligence and expert Greulich-Pyle atlas method for bone age assessment
journal: Chinese Journal of Tissue Engineering Research
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Tissue Engineering Research
model_family: artificial intelligence Greulich-Pyle (GP) bone age assessment system (domestically developed)
patient_population: children and adolescents aged 6-15 years undergoing wrist radiography
clinical_problem: bone age assessment using the Greulich-Pyle method
model_description: A domestically developed AI system that applies the Greulich-Pyle atlas method to wrist radiographs was compared against manual GP bone-age assessment by an expert, in a cohort of boys and girls aged 6-15 years, to check whether the AI system's readings agree closely enough with expert readings for clinical use.
dataset_size: 1,322 wrist radiographs from children/adolescents 6-15 years (672 male, 650 female)
headline_result: Mean absolute difference from expert GP assessment was 0.39 years (male) and 0.32 years (female); Pearson correlation r=0.991 (male) and r=0.992 (female); overall Kappa 0.603 (male) and 0.659 (female).

title: Automatic axial vertebral rotation estimation on radiographs for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis by deep learning
model_family: deep learning landmark detection and segmentation (coordinate-convolution + Polarized Self-Attention feature extraction on a High-Resolution Network)
patient_population: 37 spine radiographs (481 vertebrae) from adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
clinical_problem: measurement of axial vertebral rotation for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)
model_description: Spine radiographs are input. An improved feature-extraction module (coordinate convolution plus Polarized Self-Attention) built on a High-Resolution Network outputs vertebral landmark locations and pedicle segmentation, from which an automatic algorithm calculates axial vertebral rotation (AVR), a measurement used in treatment decisions and progression prediction for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
dataset_size: 37 spine radiographs, 481 vertebrae, 962 AVR measurements (two observers)
headline_result: mean radial error of landmark detection 2.70mm (2.13mm improvement over baseline); pedicle segmentation Dice 72.45% (4.61% improvement); average AVR measurement error under 5°, within clinical standard

title: Trustworthiness of Four-dimensional Ultrasound and Artificial Intelligence in Improving KANET Test for Detection of Fetuses at Neurorisk
journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
venue_label: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
patient_population: fetuses undergoing the Kurjak Antenatal Neurodevelopmental Test (KANET) via 4D ultrasound during the third trimester
clinical_problem: early detection of fetal neurological impairment risk via fetal movement analysis (KANET test)
model_description: 3D ultrasound image frames extracted from 4D recordings of fetal movement during the KANET test are input. A custom CNN classifies characteristic fetal neurobehavioral movements (e.g., facial vs hand-to-face movements) to assist early detection of fetal neurological impairment disorders (e.g., cerebral palsy, epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder), with results shown via a graphical interface as each recorded frame is parsed.
headline_result: overall classification accuracy 93.83%

title: Hand bone extraction and segmentation based on a convolutional neural network
model_family: two-stage CNN pipeline: YOLOv5-based detection network with polarized self-attention (OSA-YOLOv5), followed by a GRU-UNet segmentation network
patient_population: adolescents undergoing left-hand X-ray, mixed with the RSNA public bone age dataset
clinical_problem: hand bone segmentation to support skeletal bone age assessment
model_description: Left-hand X-ray images are input. OSA-YOLOv5, a detection network enhanced with a coordinate-convolution and Polarized Self-Attention feature-extraction module, first extracts (localizes) the hand bones; GRU-UNet then separates and segments the individual bones, using spatial-sequence modeling. The pipeline is intended as a preprocessing step for automated bone age assessment.
dataset_size: 2000 left-hand X-ray images (1000 from adolescents at licensed local hospitals, 1000 from the RSNA public bone age dataset)
headline_result: OSA-YOLOv5 training efficiency 28% higher than the traditional network with higher extraction accuracy; GRU-UNet segmentation accuracy 14.70% higher than UNet

title: Postnatal age-related change of brain volume and its association with neurobehavior outcome in term neonates
journal: Journal of Xi'an Jiaotong University (Medical Sciences)
venue_label: Journal of Xi'an Jiaotong University (Medical Sciences)
patient_population: 75 full-term newborns (gestational age 39.38±1.22 weeks, postnatal age 11.11±6.67 days) with no MRI abnormalities
clinical_problem: postnatal brain regional volume growth and its association with neurobehavioral outcome in term neonates
model_description: 3D T1-weighted neonatal brain MRI is input. VB-Net, a deep learning segmentation model, divides the brain into 87 template-defined regions and computes each region's volume; these volumes are then related to postnatal age and neurobehavioral scores by correlation and regression analysis.
headline_result: 66.7% of regional brain volumes (58/87) significantly increased with postnatal age (r 0.2-0.7, P<0.05); right occipital lobe gray matter volume grew fastest (slope 100.67) and correlated with behavioral scores (r=0.324, P<0.01)

title: Analysis of the current situation and development trend of bone age assessment of children in China based on questionnaires
clinical_problem: bone age assessment practice patterns and adoption of AI-assisted bone age assessment
model_description: Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 450 radiologists and pediatricians across 162 Chinese medical institutions, on current pediatric bone age assessment practices. Found left-wrist radiography and the ATLAS method predominate, that 98.4% of respondents agreed AI technology should be used to assist bone age assessment, but that only 9.3% of institutions currently use AI-assisted technology.
dataset_size: 450 valid questionnaires from 162 medical institutions across 26 provinces
headline_result: 98.4% (443/450) of respondents agreed AI should assist bone age assessment, but only 9.3% (15/162) of institutions currently use AI-assisted technology

title: Automatic characterization of cerebral MRI images for the detection of autism spectrum disorders
