patient_population: 1114 T1-weighted MRI scans from 521 individuals with ASD and 593 controls, age range 6-64 years, divided into three broad age groups
clinical_problem: detection/characterization of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) via structural brain MRI texture analysis
model_description: T1-weighted brain MRI scans are input, from which automatically labeled subcortical and cortical regions have texture features computed using Riemannian geometry descriptors and Haralick texture quantifiers. The most discriminative features are selected and used to train an artificial neural network to classify ASD versus typically developing controls.
dataset_size: 1114 MRI scans (521 ASD, 593 controls), ages 6-64 years

title: XRAInet: AI-based decision support for pneumothorax and pleural effusion management
patient_population: pediatric patients admitted between 2005 and 2022 with pneumothorax or pleural effusion
clinical_problem: deciding whether tube thoracostomy is needed for pediatric pneumothorax or pleural effusion
model_description: XRAInet is a deep learning decision-support system trained on chest X-rays to identify pediatric patients with pneumothorax or pleural effusion and to localize the abnormal region, supporting the decision of whether tube thoracostomy intervention is warranted versus conservative management.
headline_result: XRAInet achieved a mean average precision of 0.918; on an independent test set, sensitivity was 64.00% and specificity was 96.15%.

title: Impact of reconstruction algorithms on the success rate and quality of automatic airway segmentation in children under ultra-low-dose chest CT scanning
model_family: commercial deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm evaluated against filtered back-projection and ASIR-V, with automatic airway segmentation via VCAR software
patient_population: 52 children undergoing ultra-low-dose chest CT, divided into three age groups (1-2 years, 3-6 years, 7-13 years)
clinical_problem: impact of CT reconstruction algorithm on automatic airway segmentation success and image quality in ultra-low-dose pediatric chest CT
model_description: Ultra-low-dose chest CT raw data are reconstructed with six different algorithms (filtered back-projection, 50%/100% adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction, and low/medium/high-strength deep learning image reconstruction). Automatic airway segmentation software is then applied to each reconstruction, and segmentation success rate plus subjective and quantitative image quality are compared across pediatric age groups and tracheal sizes.
release_evidence: DLIR (deep learning image reconstruction) and VCAR are named, commercially available CT reconstruction/segmentation software
headline_result: segmentation success rate in the youngest group improved from 7.69% (100% ASIR-V) to 38.64% with DLIR-medium/high (P=0.03); DLIR-high gave the lowest image noise and highest subjective quality score

title: Radiomics analysis on blood-pool phase of bone scintigraphy for the diagnosis of Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
model_family: radiomics with recursive feature elimination and a random forest classifier
patient_population: 190 patients with suspected juvenile idiopathic arthritis
clinical_problem: diagnosis of active knee arthritis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA)
model_description: Blood-pool phase bone scintigraphy images (technetium-99m-methyl diphosphonate) are input, with the region of interest defined as the area between the knee growth plates. Quantitative radiomic features are extracted from original and filtered images, recursive feature elimination selects the most informative features, and a random forest classifier outputs a diagnosis of active JIA-related knee arthritis.
headline_result: AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.88-0.92) using 14 selected radiomic features (4 original, 10 filtered)

title: A familial modeling framework for advancing precision medicine in neuropsychiatric disorders: A study in children with RASopathies
model_family: univariate regression and multivariate machine learning
patient_population: 53 families of children with Noonan syndrome, ages 4-12.9 years (mean 8.48, SD 2.12), 34 female
clinical_problem: predicting child neuroanatomical and neuropsychiatric outcomes in Noonan syndrome (a RASopathy) from parent traits
model_description: Non-carrier parent cognitive and behavioral trait measures are input. Univariate regression and multivariate machine learning models output predicted child cognitive, behavioral, and neuroanatomical outcomes (via structural brain MRI), providing an individualized expected-outcome estimate for children with Noonan syndrome relative to traditional case-control comparisons.
dataset_size: 53 families of children with Noonan syndrome
headline_result: parent cognition (especially visuospatial/motor abilities), depression, anxiety and ADHD symptoms were significantly associated with child neuroanatomical variability, particularly in temporal, parietal, subcortical regions and the amygdala (no single summary statistic given)

title: Predicting gestational age at birth in the context of preterm birth from multi-modal fetal MRI
model_family: machine learning pipeline (data imputation, feature selection, regression models)
patient_population: 176 control pregnancies and 67 preterm birth cases, using comprehensive multi-modal fetal MRI
clinical_problem: predicting gestational age at birth in the context of preterm birth risk
model_description: Multi-modal morphological and functional fetal MRI features (including cervical length and placental T2* values) are input to a machine learning regression pipeline with data imputation and feature selection. The pipeline outputs a predicted gestational age at birth, which is then classified into term versus preterm categories.
headline_result: R2 0.51, mean absolute error 2.22 weeks; term/preterm classification accuracy 0.88, sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.89

title: Ultra-low-field paediatric MRI in low- and middle-income countries: super-resolution using a multi-orientation U-Net
patient_population: infants scanned with paired ultra-low-field and high-field MRI
clinical_problem: improving image resolution/quality of ultra-low-field MRI for pediatric neurodevelopmental research in low- and middle-income countries
model_description: Multiple low-resolution, anisotropic T2-weighted images acquired in orthogonal orientations on an ultra-low-field MRI scanner are input. A multi-orientation U-Net outputs a high-resolution, isotropic super-resolved T2-weighted reconstruction, trained on paired ultra-low-field and high-field infant MRI data to improve accessibility of MRI for neurodevelopmental research in resource-limited settings.
headline_result: caudate volume estimates: linear correlation r=0.94 vs 0.84 for existing methods; concordance correlation 0.94 vs 0.80; mean error 0.05 cm3 vs 0.36 cm3

title: Radiomics combined with CT features for distinguishing mycoplasma and non-mycoplasma pneumonia in children
journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
model_family: radiomics combined with CT features, using logistic regression, SVM, random forest, LDA, and SGD classifiers
patient_population: 153 children with pneumonia (101 mycoplasma, 52 non-mycoplasma)
clinical_problem: distinguishing mycoplasma from non-mycoplasma pneumonia in children
model_description: Chest CT images are input, from which radiomic features and selected qualitative CT features (lobar involvement, bronchial wall thickening, tree-in-bud sign, edge-retraction sign) are extracted. Multiple machine learning classifiers are trained on the combined CT and radiomic features to output a probability of mycoplasma versus non-mycoplasma pneumonia.
headline_result: best combined CT-radiomics model (SVM) AUC 0.823 in validation (vs CT-only 0.710 and best radiomics-only 0.715, not significant); training-set AUC 0.840, significantly higher than CT-only or radiomics-only (P<0.05)

title: Detection of hidden pediatric elbow fractures in X-ray images based on deep learning
journal: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
venue_label: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
patient_population: 1370 pediatric patients undergoing elbow X-ray, from multiple healthcare centers
clinical_problem: detection of hidden (occult) pediatric elbow fractures
model_description: Preprocessed (normalized, resized) elbow radiographs are input. A DenseNet-201 convolutional neural network, trained with a 70/30 train-validation split and data augmentation, outputs a classification of whether a pediatric elbow fracture is present, intended to assist diagnosis of fractures that are difficult to detect.
dataset_size: 1370 pediatric patients, X-ray images from multiple healthcare centers
headline_result: accuracy 94.1%, AUC 98.7%, sensitivity 93.2%, specificity 94.8% on the training dataset

title: Sensorless volumetric reconstruction of fetal brain freehand ultrasound scans with deep implicit representation
patient_population: fetuses imaged with freehand 2D ultrasound sweeps, natively-acquired and volume-sampled video sequences from different ultrasound manufacturers
clinical_problem: 3D reconstruction of fetal brain anatomy from freehand, non-sensor-tracked 2D ultrasound sweeps
model_description: A set of freehand 2D ultrasound images (without external position tracking) is input. ImplicitVol, a deep neural network, predicts each image's location in 3D space, jointly refines these locations, and represents the reconstructed anatomy as a continuous implicit function rather than a discrete voxel grid, producing a 3D fetal brain volume reconstructable to arbitrarily high resolution.
headline_result: reconstructions show significantly better visual and semantic quality than existing interpolation-based reconstruction approaches (no single numeric metric given)

title: Radiomics of fetal magnetic resonance imaging in congenital diaphragmatic hernia
model_family: radiomics feature extraction (pyradiomics) with statistical correlation analysis
patient_population: 72 pregnant women: 35 with congenital fetal diaphragmatic hernia, 37 without fetal lung pathology
clinical_problem: assessing fetal lung structural maturity/pathology in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH)
model_description: Frontal/co-frontal T2-weighted fetal MRI images at the level of the lungs are input, with the lung region of interest manually segmented in 2D and 3D. 107 radiomic features are extracted using pyradiomics, and statistical correlation analysis relates these features to the presence of fetal lung pathology in congenital diaphragmatic hernia, as a potential source of additional diagnostic information on lung structural maturity.
headline_result: 14 significant 2D features and 73 significant 3D features (p<0.05); after removing cross-correlated features, 6 (2D) and 8 (3D) features retained; 20 3D features with correlation coefficient r>0.4 (p<0.05) vs 3 for single-slice

title: Repurposing Clinical MRI Archives for Multiple Sclerosis Research with a Flexible, Single-Modality Approach: New Insights from Old Scans
body_region: brain (white matter lesions, cortical and deep gray matter)
patient_population: training: 2934 multiple sclerosis patients (4247 scans) across 592 scanners; external validation: 1001 patients (14,952 scans) from three cohorts, including 161 adolescent patients
clinical_problem: quantifying multiple sclerosis lesion and brain volumes from heterogeneous, single-modality clinical MRI archives
model_description: A single MRI modality/sequence from a clinical brain scan is input (rather than a full multimodal protocol). MindGlide, a deep learning model, outputs volumes of white-matter lesions, cortical gray matter, and deep gray-matter structures, trained on a large multi-scanner multiple sclerosis dataset and externally validated including an adolescent subgroup, to enable analysis of incomplete or heterogeneous clinical archives.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort technical development and external validation
dataset_size: 4247 scans from 2934 patients (training); 14,952 scans from 1001 patients across 3 external validation cohorts (incl. 161 adolescents)
headline_result: MindGlide-derived volumes correlated with EDSS disability (|r| 0.1-0.2, p<0.05) and outperformed an established tool; robustly detected treatment effects (lesion accrual, brain tissue loss) across clinical trials

title: Prediction of Autism Antenatally via Fetal Ultrasound and Postnatally via MRI Studies
journal: Journal of Population Therapeutics and Clinical Pharmacology
venue_label: Journal of Population Therapeutics and Clinical Pharmacology
model_family: statistical and machine learning prediction models
patient_population: fetuses (via prenatal ultrasound) and their offspring followed postnatally with MRI at 6 and 12 months
clinical_problem: early prediction of autism spectrum disorder from prenatal and early postnatal brain imaging
model_description: In a prospective cohort of pregnant women and their offspring, fetal head circumference, corpus callosum thickness and ventricle size were assessed with 3D/4D ultrasound, and postnatal brain structure (amygdala size, frontal cortical volume) was assessed with MRI at 6 and 12 months. Statistical tests and machine learning algorithms were used to evaluate how well these prenatal and postnatal imaging markers predicted later autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
headline_result: Prediction accuracy for autism spectrum disorder was 70% using antenatal ultrasound alone, 85% using postnatal MRI alone, and 90% combining both.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Framework: Decoding Brain Task and Prediction of Individual Performance in False-Belief Task at Early Childhood Stage
model_name: Ex-stGCNN (explainable spatiotemporal connectivity-based Graph Convolutional Neural Network); also an Explainable Convolutional Variational Auto-Encoder
model_family: graph convolutional neural network with SHAP explainability; variational autoencoder
patient_population: 155 participants, age range 3-12 years and adults, watching a short animated film during fMRI
clinical_problem: decoding brain states (Theory of Mind/pain) and predicting individual task performance in early childhood development
model_description: Static and inter-subject functional connectivity matrices, derived from fMRI acquired while participants watched an animated film, are input. Ex-stGCNN, an explainable graph convolutional network, classifies brain states (Theory-of-Mind vs pain), and a separate explainable variational autoencoder predicts an individual's pass/fail/inconsistent performance on a subsequent false-belief task; SHAP is used to identify the most contributing brain regions.
headline_result: brain-state decoding accuracy 94% (inter-subject connectivity) / 85% (static connectivity), 92% average with five-fold cross-validation; false-belief performance prediction accuracy 90%

title: Multiparametric MRI Along with Machine Learning Informs on Molecular Underpinnings, Prognosis, and Treatment Response in Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma
patient_population: pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) patients, treatment-naive, in discovery and replication cohorts
clinical_problem: prognostication (immunological profiling, progression-free survival, treatment response) in pediatric low-grade glioma
model_description: Treatment-naive multiparametric MRI, combined with RNA sequencing, is used to build a radiomic signature. The signature predicts immunological cluster membership (derived from XCell enrichment scores), and a combined clinicoradiomic model predicts progression-free survival and correlates with treatment response, to support early risk stratification in pediatric low-grade glioma.
headline_result: radiomic signature balanced accuracy 81.5% (discovery) and 84.4% (replication); progression-free survival concordance index 0.71 and 0.77; clinicoradiomic score correlated with treatment response (p=0.001)

title: Scanner-based real-time 3D brain+body slice-to-volume reconstruction for T2-weighted 0.55T low field fetal MRI
model_family: deep learning-based deformable/rigid slice-to-volume (D/SVR) reconstruction pipeline integrated with the Gadgetron scanner framework
patient_population: 12 prospectively acquired fetal MRI datasets (22-40 weeks gestational age) plus 83 retrospective 0.55T datasets
clinical_problem: real-time, scanner-based 3D reconstruction of motion-corrupted fetal MRI at ultra-low field
model_description: Motion-corrupted 2D T2-weighted single-shot Turbo Spin Echo stacks from a 0.55T low-field MRI scanner are input. An automated deformable/rigid slice-to-volume reconstruction pipeline (SVRTK), integrated into the scanner's Gadgetron workflow, outputs a super-resolved 3D reconstruction of fetal brain and body available on the scanner console during the ongoing scan.
dataset_size: 12 prospective fetal datasets (22-40 weeks GA); 83 retrospective 0.55T datasets
headline_result: reconstructions available on average 6:42±3:13 minutes after acquisition of the final stack; image quality rated good to acceptable for interpretation; stable reconstruction quality on retrospective testing

title: Ultrasound imaging based recognition of prenatal anomalies: a systematic clinical engineering review
clinical_problem: recognition of prenatal structural anomalies on ultrasound
model_description: Systematic clinical-engineering review of AI-based prenatal ultrasound anomaly screening, including multimodal data fusion with circulating biomarkers and explainable AI (XAI) approaches. Proposes a deep-learning-based explanatory framework that would chart anomaly-screening results from ultrasound video and link them to probable structural deformations, to increase clinician trust; no specific trained model's performance is reported.

title: Construction and Validation of A Deep Learning-based Bone Age Prediction Model for Children Living in Both Plain and Highland Regions
journal: Medical Journal of Peking Union Medical College Hospital
venue_label: Medical Journal of Peking Union Medical College Hospital
model_family: deep learning bone age prediction model
patient_population: children undergoing left-hand radiography, including Han and Tibetan children from plain and highland regions
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in children from different ethnicities and altitudes
model_description: EVG-BANet is a deep learning model that predicts bone age from a left-hand radiograph. It was trained on the public RSNA and RHPE bone-age datasets plus a self-established dataset of Han and Tibetan children from a plain-region and a highland-region hospital, then evaluated on an independent external test set of Tibetan children from a third hospital.
study_design: retrospective multi-center diagnostic accuracy / external validation study
dataset_size: RSNA dataset (train 12,611/val 1,425/test 200), RHPE dataset (train 5,491/val 713/test 79), self-established dataset (train 825/test 351 from 1,176 children), external test 256 children
headline_result: Mean absolute difference from reference bone age ranged 0.34-0.53 years and accuracy within 1 year ranged 89.45%-97.72% across the RSNA, RHPE, self-established, and external test sets.

title: The role of machine learning in detecting primary brain tumors in Saudi pediatric patients through MRI images
journal: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
venue_label: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
patient_population: pediatric patients with primary brain tumors imaged at King Abdullah Specialist Children's Hospital
clinical_problem: detection of primary brain tumors in children
model_description: MRI images of pediatric patients with primary brain tumors (glioma, primitive neuro-ectodermal tumor, pituitary tumor) and normal images were retrieved from the hospital's PACS. Machine learning algorithms, including an artificial neural network, were trained on 70% of the images and tested on the remaining 30% to classify and detect brain tumors.
headline_result: The artificial neural network method accurately detected pediatric primary brain tumors, with results reported to match the radiologist's report (no single summary accuracy figure given).

title: Development and external validation of an ultrasound image-based deep learning model to estimate gestational age in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy using data from Garbh-Ini cohort: a prospective cohort study in North Indian population
model_name: GAUGE (Garbh-Ini Ultrasound image-based Gestational age Estimator)
model_family: deep learning image-based regression model with a conformal prediction algorithm for distribution-shift detection
patient_population: 2207 pregnant women in the Garbh-Ini cohort, North India, imaged at 18-32 weeks of pregnancy; external test set of 311 participants from a separate ultrasound lab in New Delhi
clinical_problem: estimation of gestational age in the second and third trimesters
model_description: Fetal head ultrasound images (rather than standard fetal biometry measurements) are input. A deep learning model, GAUGE, directly learns image features associated with gestational age and outputs a gestational age estimate; a conformal prediction algorithm flags and rejects images affected by data distribution shift.
study_design: prospective cohort study with external validation
dataset_size: 9647 images from 2207 participants (development); internal test N=204; external test N=311
headline_result: mean absolute error 2.8 days (internal test, N=204) and 5.9 days (external test, N=311); 44% and 35% more accurate than the Hadlock and INTERGROWTH-21st biometry-based models respectively

title: Automated Neuroprognostication via Machine Learning in Neonates with Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
model_family: elastic net regression model on MRI-derived shape and radiomic features
patient_population: 286 infants treated with therapeutic hypothermia for hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
clinical_problem: neuroprognostication (neurodevelopmental outcome prediction) in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
model_description: Newborn brain MRI, labeled for deep gray-matter structures using a custom anatomical template, is input. Shape-related and radiomic features are extracted from these structures, and an elastic net model, trained on MRI features alone, clinical data alone, or both, outputs predicted Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development cognitive, language, and motor scores at 18 months.
headline_result: MRI-based models predicted Bayley scores with correlations more than double, and explained more than four times the variance of, clinical-data-only models; combined models were similar to or marginally better than MRI alone

title: Artificial Intelligence to Assist in the Screening Fetal Anomaly Ultrasound Scan (PROMETHEUS): A Randomised Controlled Trial
model_family: deep learning models (image-plane identification and biometry measurement)
body_region: fetal anatomy (standard anomaly-screening planes, including heart)
patient_population: 78 pregnant participants (26 with fetal congenital heart disease, 52 healthy fetuses), scanned by 58 sonographers at a single teaching hospital
clinical_problem: screening fetal anomaly ultrasound, including fetal congenital heart disease
model_description: Live 2D fetal ultrasound video is input during a routine anomaly scan. The AI tool identifies and saves 13 standard fetal image planes and automatically measures four biometric parameters in real time, to assist the sonographer. It was tested in a randomized controlled trial against standard (non-AI-assisted) scanning, blinded to fetal CHD status.
headline_result: AI-assisted sensitivity/specificity 88.9%/98.0% vs standard 81.5%/92.2% (not significant); AI scans significantly shorter (median 11.4 vs 19.7 min, p<0.001); lower sonographer cognitive load (NASA TLX 35.2 vs 46.5, p<0.001); superior AI repeatability/reproducibility for biometry

title: Predicting task-related brain activity from resting-state brain dynamics with fMRI Transformer
model_family: transformer-based deep learning model (shifted-window self-attention with contrastive learning)
patient_population: adults from UK Biobank (n=7038) and children from the ABCD study (n=4944)
clinical_problem: predicting task-related brain activation from resting-state fMRI, potentially reducing the need for task-based fMRI
model_description: Resting-state fMRI scans are input. SwiFUN, a transformer model using shifted-window self-attention and contrastive learning, outputs predicted 3D task-activation maps for an emotion-processing task (FACES-PLACES contrast), without requiring an actual task-based fMRI acquisition. It was evaluated in both an adult cohort (UK Biobank) and a pediatric cohort (ABCD).
study_design: retrospective technical development using public cohort data
headline_result: consistently higher prediction accuracy than existing methods across all contrasts, with up to 27% improvement for the FACES-PLACES contrast in ABCD data

title: 胸部 X 线片人工智能联邦学习系统用于病原学诊断儿童社区获得性肺炎
journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
model_family: attention-mechanism deep learning classification model with federated learning deployment (compared against DenseNet)
patient_population: 900 children with community-acquired pneumonia (300 each bacterial, viral, mycoplasma) from 2 hospitals, plus 5856 children from the public GWCMCx dataset
clinical_problem: pathogen diagnosis (bacterial vs viral vs mycoplasma) of community-acquired pneumonia in children
model_description: Posteroanterior chest X-rays are input, optionally combined with clinical data. An attention-mechanism-based deep learning model, trained with federated deployment across two hospitals plus a public dataset, outputs binary (CAP vs healthy) or ternary (bacterial/viral/mycoplasma) pathogen classification for pediatric community-acquired pneumonia.
dataset_size: 6756 chest X-ray images (900 from 2 hospitals + 5856 from public GWCMCx dataset), split 5359 training / 1397 validation
headline_result: overall accuracy 97.00%, AUC 0.990; hospital-only data AUC 0.858 (imaging) and 0.836 (imaging+clinical), both better than DenseNet (AUC 0.740, P<0.05)

title: Automated Pediatric Brain Tumor Imaging Assessment Tool from CBTN: Enhancing Suprasellar Region Inclusion and Managing Limited Data with Deep Learning
body_region: brain (whole brain, sellar/suprasellar region, and tumor)
patient_population: 527 pediatric patients with various pediatric brain tumor (PBT) histologies (336 for skull-stripping, 489 for tumor segmentation), multi-institutional
clinical_problem: automated skull-stripping and tumor segmentation for monitoring pediatric brain tumors
model_description: Multi-institutional, multi-parametric MRI (single-sequence T2/FLAIR, or multi-sequence T1-Gd plus T2/FLAIR) is input. Separate nnU-Net-based deep learning models output a whole-brain/sellar-suprasellar skull-stripping mask, and whole-tumor and enhancing-tumor segmentation masks. The models are designed to generalize to rare sellar/suprasellar tumors and to work with missing MRI sequences in limited-data, real-world clinical scenarios.
dataset_size: 527 pediatric patients (336 for skull-stripping, 489 for tumor segmentation)
headline_result: skull-stripping Dice 0.98±0.01 (median 0.98); whole-tumor Dice 0.84±0.17 (T2) / 0.82±0.19 (FLAIR); enhancing-tumor Dice 0.65±0.35 (T1-Gd+FLAIR) / 0.64±0.36 (T1-Gd+T2)

title: A machine learning approach to predict mortality and pulmonary hypertension severity in newborns with congenital diaphragmatic hernia
model_family: supervised machine learning model (algorithm not specified)
patient_population: 50 patients with isolated left-sided CDH from singleton pregnancies
clinical_problem: predicting postnatal mortality and pulmonary hypertension severity in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH)
model_description: Prenatal fetal ultrasound imaging variables and MRI-derived lung shape features, combined with gestational age and birth weight, are input. A supervised machine learning model outputs predicted postnatal mortality and severity of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN) in fetuses with isolated left CDH.
headline_result: mortality prediction: 88% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, AUC 0.88; PPHN prediction: 82% accuracy, 85% sensitivity, AUC 0.82

title: Optimized Pyramidal Convolution Shuffle attention neural network based fetal cardiac cycle detection from echocardiograms
model_family: Optimized Pyramidal Convolution Shuffle Attention Neural Network
patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography (Shenzhen Maternal and Child Health Hospital)
clinical_problem: identifying end-systolic and end-diastolic cardiac cycle frames on fetal echocardiography
model_description: OPCSANN-FCCD detects the end-systolic and end-diastolic frames within fetal echocardiogram video clips, a step needed for automated cardiac biometric assessment. Ultrasound frames are first denoised with an anisotropic diffusion filter, texture features are extracted with a window-adaptive gray-level co-occurrence matrix, and a pyramidal convolution shuffle-attention neural network classifies frames as end-systolic or end-diastolic.
dataset_size: Shenzhen Maternal and Child Health Hospital fetal echocardiogram dataset (exact n not stated)
headline_result: OPCSANN-FCCD improved accuracy by 22.4-27.6% and reduced computational load by 26.6-31.2% compared with three existing fetal cardiac-cycle detection methods (FCCD-ME-HCF, FCUSD-ML-MAM, HFSCCD-UV).

title: Novel AI-Driven Infant Meningitis Screening from High Resolution Ultrasound Imaging
model_family: three-stage deep learning framework (quality-control CNN, WBC-threshold classification CNN, GradCAM/statistical XAI)
patient_population: 30 infants with suspected meningitis and a permeable fontanelle, from three Spanish University Hospitals (2021-2023)
clinical_problem: non-invasive screening for infant meningitis
model_description: High-resolution transfontanellar ultrasound images (Neosonics technology) are used as input. A three-stage deep learning pipeline first performs quality control (vessel/non-vessel filtering), then classifies images as control or meningitis based on a CSF white blood cell count threshold, with GradCAM and image-statistic explainability layered on top. It is intended as a non-invasive alternative/adjunct to lumbar puncture for infant meningitis screening.
dataset_size: 2194 images screened; final cohort 16 patients (6 meningitis cases/336 images, 10 controls/445 images), 781 images used for stage-2 classification
headline_result: 96% accuracy in quality control; 93% precision and 92% accuracy at image level; 94% patient-level accuracy; 100% sensitivity and 90% specificity (6 meningitis, 10 controls)

title: AmygdalaGo-BOLT: an open and reliable AI tool to trace boundaries of human amygdala
model_family: boundary-aware deep learning segmentation model (multiscale features, spatial priors, self-attention, encoder-decoder)
patient_population: children and adolescents undergoing structural brain MRI for developmental neuroimaging studies
clinical_problem: automated amygdala segmentation for developmental neuroimaging
model_description: Structural brain MRI scans are input. The model is a boundary-aware deep learning network that integrates multiscale image features, spatial priors and self-attention to trace amygdala boundaries, trained and validated on manually labeled pediatric scans from multiple imaging centers. It is intended as an open, reliable, and efficient alternative to manual amygdala tracing in developmental neuroimaging research.
release_evidence: "we publicly release both the labeled datasets and the full source code"
dataset_size: 854 manually labeled MRI scans from pediatric datasets, with independent samples for generalizability testing
headline_result: closely matches expert manual labels, improves processing efficiency, and outperforms existing tools in accuracy across imaging centers and age groups (no single numeric metric given)

title: Automatic part segmentation for full newborn skeleton-articulated geometries using geometric deep learning and 3D point cloud
journal: International Journal of Biomedical Engineering and Technology
venue_label: International Journal of Biomedical Engineering and Technology
patient_population: 124 newborns undergoing CT
clinical_problem: automatic segmentation of the newborn skeleton for maternal pelvis / fetal skeletal modeling
model_description: The model takes 3D point clouds reconstructed from CT scans of newborn skeletons as input and outputs an automatic segmentation of skeletal parts. It was trained using PointNet++, a geometric deep learning architecture, on manually segmented CT scans from 124 newborns, and compared against a k-means clustering baseline. It is intended to speed up creation of articulated newborn skeleton models for maternal pelvis / fetal biomechanical modeling.
headline_result: PointNet++ accuracy 95.7 ± 4.7% and IoU 91.7 ± 7.9%, vs 74.6 ± 3.7% accuracy and 59.8 ± 4.7% IoU for k-means clustering

title: Pediatric brain tumor classification using deep learning on MR-images with age fusion
model_family: vision transformer (pretrained on ImageNet, fine-tuned) with age-fusion; convolutional network compared
patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade astrocytoma, ependymoma, or medulloblastoma from the Children's Brain Tumor Network (age range 0.01-36.49 years)
clinical_problem: classification of pediatric brain tumor type
model_description: Deep learning models were trained to classify pediatric brain tumor type (low-grade astrocytoma, ependymoma, medulloblastoma) from transversal MRI slices showing tumor, using T1-weighted post-contrast, T2-weighted, or ADC sequences separately. Patient age was fused with image features (joint fusion), and two pre-training strategies were compared; Grad-CAM and PCA were used to visualize model attention and the learned feature space.
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 178 subjects (T1w post-contrast n=94, T2w n=160, ADC n=66) from the Children's Brain Tumor Network
headline_result: The best model (vision transformer pretrained on ImageNet, fine-tuned on ADC images with age fusion) achieved MCC 0.77±0.14 and accuracy 0.87±0.08, outperforming models trained on T2w (MCC 0.58) and T1w post-contrast (MCC 0.41) data.

title: Research of intelligent model for automatically counting the number of vertebral ossification center below the end of conus medullaris
model_family: YOLOv8-based segmentation model with post-processing fitting/counting algorithm
patient_population: fetuses undergoing sacrococcygeal spinal midsagittal ultrasound, retrospectively selected 2021-2022 from two hospitals
clinical_problem: counting vertebral ossification centers to support fetal spina bifida screening
model_description: Midsagittal sacrococcygeal ultrasound images are input. A YOLOv8-based network segments the vertebral ossification centers and the spinal conus medullaris, and a post-processing step fits and automatically counts the ossification centers below the conus medullaris. It is intended to speed up and standardize prenatal screening for fetal spina bifida.
dataset_size: 3000 ultrasound images (2800 for segmentation training, 200 for testing)
headline_result: AI counting accuracy 95.00% vs attending physician 94.50% (P=0.823) and junior physician 88.50% (P=0.012); AI counting time 0.09s vs 5.00s (attending) and 7.00s (junior), P<0.001

title: A Graph Neural Network Approach to Investigate Brain Critical States Over Neurodevelopment
model_family: Graph Neural Network trained on Ising-model networks
patient_population: typically developing children and children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
clinical_problem: characterizing brain functional maturation using resting-state fMRI
model_description: A Graph Neural Network trained on simulated 2D Ising-model networks was used to estimate an 'Ising temperature' from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity, a marker of how close brain dynamics are to a critical state. The method was applied to children to study how this measure changes with age in typical development and in ADHD.
headline_result: Ising temperature correlated negatively with age in both typically developing children (r=-0.48, P<0.0001) and children with ADHD (r=-0.49, P<0.0001), suggesting the brain moves away from criticality with age.

title: Evaluation of Liver Fibrosis on Grayscale Ultrasound in a Pediatric Population Using a Cloud-based Transfer Learning Artificial Intelligence Platform
journal: Advanced Ultrasound in Diagnosis and Therapy
venue_label: Advanced Ultrasound in Diagnosis and Therapy
model_family: Google Vision AutoML (transfer learning image classification)
patient_population: 190 pediatric patients referred for liver biopsy and ultrasound
clinical_problem: noninvasive detection of liver fibrosis
model_description: B-mode ultrasound images of the liver (about 14 per patient) were used to train a supervised image-classification model on a cloud-based AI platform (Google Vision AutoML) via transfer learning, to classify liver appearance as fibrotic or non-fibrotic. The model's output was compared against biopsy-proven fibrosis status and against blinded pediatric radiologist reads on an external validation cohort.
release_evidence: built using a commercial cloud platform (Google Vision AutoML), but the resulting model itself is not stated to be released
dataset_size: 190 patients; 2,324 images (development, 154 cases) and 360 images (external validation, 36 cases)
headline_result: External validation: AI sensitivity 70.56% vs radiologists' mean sensitivity 42.04%; AI accuracy 57.78% vs radiologists' mean accuracy 46.11%

title: De-Coupling Connectivity: A Cognitive Biomarker in Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury
model_family: graph-theory connectivity coupling metrics with regression models
patient_population: children with traumatic brain injury (aged 9-18 years) and healthy controls
clinical_problem: predicting cognitive outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury
model_description: Structural and functional brain connectivity were derived from MRI using graph theory in children with traumatic brain injury and healthy controls, scanned in the acute and post-acute phases. A 'coupling connectivity' measure (correlation between structural and functional graph-theory metrics) was calculated, and regression models used acute-phase coupling connectivity to predict post-acute executive function test outcomes.
dataset_size: 45 children with TBI and 47 healthy controls, aged 9-18 years
headline_result: TBI patients showed disrupted structural-functional connectivity coupling versus controls, and acute-phase coupling connectivity significantly predicted post-acute executive function outcomes.

title: Automatic Diagnosis of Early Pregnancy Fetal Nasal Bone Development Based on Complex Mid-Sagittal Section Ultrasound Imaging
model_name: FNB-ADS (Fetal Nasal Bone Automated Diagnostic System)
model_family: YOLOv8 detection + lightweight segmentation network + ResNet34 classifier
patient_population: fetuses undergoing early prenatal mid-sagittal ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: early prenatal screening for fetal nasal bone abnormality (chromosomal abnormality marker)
model_description: FNB-ADS is an automated pipeline for early-pregnancy fetal nasal bone ultrasound. It uses YOLOv8 to localize the nasal bone region on mid-sagittal plane images, a lightweight segmentation network to segment the nasal bone, nasal tip and prenasal skin, and a ResNet34 classifier to diagnose developmental abnormalities from the segmented structures. The authors also released the FNB-UDV dataset of annotated images and videos used to develop and test the system.
release_evidence: The FNB-UDV image/video dataset is stated to be publicly released, but the abstract does not say whether the model code or weights are released.
study_design: technical development / retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 1,007 2D ultrasound images and 12 ultrasound videos (FNB-UDV dataset)
headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy was 92.37% on images (0.14 s/image) and 98.69% on video (0.37 s/frame inference speed).

title: Using Convolutional Neural Networks for the Classification of Suboptimal Chest Radiographs
model_family: DenseNet121 and YOLOv8 convolutional neural networks
patient_population: patients undergoing chest radiography, median age 67 years (range 0-102), including pediatric and adult cases
clinical_problem: identifying technically suboptimal chest radiographs to reduce repeat imaging
model_description: DenseNet121 and YOLOv8 convolutional neural networks were trained to classify chest radiographs (both PA and lateral views) as optimal or suboptimal quality, a task intended to flag images likely to need repeat acquisition. Model classifications were compared with radiologists' classifications, and this was the first such study to include lateral views and pediatric cases.
dataset_size: 3,587 patients; 10,000 CXRs total (4,000/4,000 training, 400/400 validation, 25/25 test)
headline_result: DenseNet121 achieved AUROC 0.97 and YOLOv8 AUROC 0.95 for distinguishing optimal from suboptimal chest radiographs; agreement with radiologists varied but differences were not statistically significant.

title: Deep learning super-resolution of paediatric ultra-low-field MRI without paired high-field scans
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing ultra-low-field brain MRI
clinical_problem: improving image quality of affordable ultra-low-field brain MRI for pediatric neuroimaging
model_description: A deep learning model generates a super-resolved brain MRI from a single ultra-low-field scan, without requiring paired high-field training data or the three orthogonal ultra-low-field acquisitions used by prior multi-resolution registration methods. Output quality was assessed by image quality metrics, correlation of derived tissue volumes, and Dice overlap of tissue segmentations, including an exploratory test of generalization across scanning sites.
headline_result: The single-scan deep learning approach significantly improved image quality metrics, tissue volume correlations, and Dice overlap of tissue segmentations compared with the single ultra-low-field input; an exploratory external site evaluation suggested site-specific retraining may be needed to address domain shift.

title: Pedvision: A Manual-Annotation-Free and Age Scalable Segmentation Pipeline for Bone Analysis in Hand X-Ray Images
model_family: segmentation pipeline: ROI detection network + foundation model instance translation + instance classifier network, with curriculum learning
patient_population: children aged 4 to 228 months undergoing hand radiography
clinical_problem: automated bone segmentation for pediatric bone analysis across ages
model_description: PedVision is a segmentation pipeline for hand X-rays that first localizes regions of interest, then uses a foundation model to translate each region into instance-level candidates, which an instance classifier network maps to one of 19 bones across five classes. A semi-automated, foundation-model-assisted annotation workflow with iterative human-in-the-loop review builds the training data across successive rounds, avoiding fully manual annotation, and is designed to scale across a wide pediatric age range including low-quality images.
release_evidence: "The project is open source at github.com/mohofar/PedVision."
study_design: technical development / retrospective segmentation accuracy study
dataset_size: hand X-ray images from children aged 4-228 months, segmenting 19 bones into 5 classes (exact image count not stated)
headline_result: Compared with DeepLabV3+ (ResNet34/ResNet101 backbones), the pipeline improved Dice scores by up to 6.19% in subjects over 14 years and 17.01% in subjects under 7 years, particularly in low-quality images.

title: Does Restrictive Anorexia Nervosa Impact Brain Aging? A Machine Learning Approach to Estimate Age Based on Brain Structure
model_family: machine learning brain-age estimation model (377 neuroanatomical features from structural MRI)
patient_population: female patients aged 10-40 years with acute or weight-restored anorexia nervosa and age-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: brain age gap as a biomarker of anorexia nervosa's effect on brain structure
model_description: A machine learning model was trained on 3,487 healthy-control T1-weighted MRI scans (ages 5-45, ten datasets) using 377 neuroanatomical features to estimate brain age. It was then applied to structural MRI from acute anorexia nervosa, weight-restored anorexia nervosa, and matched healthy-control groups from two institutions to compute the brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) as a biomarker of accelerated brain aging.
dataset_size: acute AN n=113, weight-restored AN n=35, healthy controls n=90 (model trained on 3,487 healthy-control scans)
headline_result: Model mean absolute error was 2.37 years in healthy controls; brain age was overestimated by 2.25 years in acute AN, normalizing after weight restoration (difference from HC not significant, P=0.98); brain-PAD correlated with BMI in acute AN (r=-0.291, P=0.005).

title: Validation of Artificial Intelligence for Bone Age Assessment in Hong Kong Children
patient_population: children referred for left hand and wrist radiographs for bone age assessment at a tertiary centre in Hong Kong, Jan-Dec 2019, mean chronological age 9.8 years
clinical_problem: skeletal (bone age) maturity assessment
model_description: Left hand and wrist radiographs were analyzed by BoneXpert 3.0, an automated AI bone-age software using the Greulich and Pyle method, and compared against bone ages assessed manually by two experienced pediatric radiologists in 99 studies.
headline_result: Strong correlation between BoneXpert and manual assessment (r = 0.98, R2 = 0.97); mean difference -0.08 year (SD 0.73); accuracy 0.74 year overall

title: CT findings of mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children
journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
model_family: AI pneumonia CT image-assisted diagnostic analysis software
patient_population: 85 children with mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia confirmed by nucleic acid test
clinical_problem: quantification of pneumonia lesion extent on chest CT in mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
model_description: AI-assisted chest CT image analysis software automatically quantified lesion volume, percentage of lesion volume relative to total lung volume, and CT attenuation value on CT scans of children with confirmed mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. These quantitative parameters were then correlated with clinical laboratory markers of inflammation.
headline_result: Lesion volume and lesion volume percentage positively correlated with serum sialic acid, CRP, D-dimer, FDP and fibrinogen (r=0.232-0.439)

title: Prediction of Motor Developmental Outcomes Based on MRI Radiomics in Premature Infants
model_family: radiomics-based binary classification model (ANOVA feature selection, ten-fold cross-validation)
patient_population: preterm infants imaged with brain MRI at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: prediction of motor neurodevelopmental outcome in preterm infants
model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from T1-weighted, T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR brain MRI obtained at term-equivalent age in preterm infants. A classification model combining these radiomic features with perinatal clinical variables was trained to predict motor developmental delay, defined using Bayley Scales assessment at 12-24 months corrected age, and compared to a clinical-variables-only model.
dataset_size: 218 preterm infants (90 with motor developmental delay)
headline_result: AUC for the combined radiomics + clinical model was 0.94 versus 0.87 for the clinical-only model and up to 0.85 for radiomics from combined MRI sequences alone.

title: Detection of Pneumonia in Children through Chest Radiographs using Artificial Intelligence in a Low-Resource Setting: A Pilot Study
model_family: deep learning classification model (architecture not specified)
patient_population: children in Nigeria undergoing chest radiography, prospectively sampled across two radiology departments
clinical_problem: detection of childhood pneumonia on chest radiographs in a low-resource setting
model_description: An AI model was developed on an open-source US pediatric chest radiograph dataset to classify images as normal or pneumonia, then externally tested on prospectively collected Nigerian pediatric chest radiographs read by two blinded radiologists as the reference standard, to evaluate generalizability to a low-resource clinical setting.
dataset_size: 5,232 open-source pediatric chest radiographs for development (1,349 normal/3,883 pneumonia training; 234/390 internal test) and 190 Nigerian radiographs for external testing (93 normal/97 pneumonia)
headline_result: The model achieved 86% accuracy and 0.93 AUC on the internal test set, but only 58% accuracy and 0.65 AUC on the external Nigerian test set.

title: NeoCLIP: A Self-Supervised Foundation Model for the Interpretation of Neonatal Radiographs
model_family: self-supervised deep contrastive learning foundation model
body_region: chest and abdomen (neonatal intensive care radiographs)
patient_population: infants who received a radiograph while admitted to a large neonatal intensive care unit
clinical_problem: interpretation of neonatal intensive care radiographs (multiple pathologies and device placement)
model_description: NeoCLIP is a self-supervised contrastive learning model trained on neonatal intensive care radiographs paired with findings automatically extracted from radiology reports using a large-language-model-based pipeline. It identifies 15 pathologies and 5 medical devices relevant to neonatal intensive care from a plain radiograph, with an option to incorporate patient demographics.
dataset_size: 20,154 radiographs and 15,795 reports from 4,629 infants (3,731 training, 419 validation, 479 test)
headline_result: NeoCLIP's AUROC exceeded all baseline methods for every radiographic finding except portal venous gas, and outperformed similar models developed for adult populations; adding demographics improved AUROC without reaching statistical significance.

title: Aperiodic parameters of the fMRI power spectrum associate with preterm birth and neonatal age
model_family: machine learning regression model on fMRI aperiodic power-spectrum parameters
patient_population: neonates (preterm and full-term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project
clinical_problem: assessing brain maturation and effect of preterm birth using functional MRI
model_description: Using task-free fMRI from the Developing Human Connectome Project, the aperiodic (non-oscillatory) parameters of the BOLD signal power spectrum were extracted from cortical/subcortical regions. A machine learning regression model using aperiodic parameters from 90 brain regions of interest was trained to predict post-menstrual age and postnatal age, and associations with preterm birth were examined.
dataset_size: Developing Human Connectome Project neonatal fMRI cohort (exact n not stated)
headline_result: The regression model predicted post-menstrual and postnatal age with mean test R² of 0.20-0.41; clear differences in aperiodic parameters were found between preterm and full-term infants and between sexes.

title: Imaging Clusters of Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma are Associated with Distinct Molecular Characteristics
model_family: K-means clustering on radiomic features with elastic net logistic regression
patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade glioma (pLGG) from the Children's Brain Tumor Network
clinical_problem: linking imaging appearance to molecular subtype in pediatric low-grade glioma
model_description: 881 radiomic features plus clinical variables (age, sex, tumor location) were extracted from MRI of pediatric low-grade glioma and grouped into three imaging clusters using principal component analysis and K-means clustering. A useful cautionary reference for any pediatric AI procurement discussion.

title: Machine learning for accurate estimation of fetal gestational age based on ultrasound images.
model_family: machine learning image analysis of standard ultrasound planes, using no measurement inputs
patient_population: two independent ultrasound datasets, one for training and internal validation and one for external validation, with gestational age ground truth from a reliable last menstrual period date confirmed by first-trimester crown-rump length
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy in the second and third trimesters, where biometry assumes an average fetal size at each gestational age and its error widens to at least two weeks as growth deviates from that average
model_description: Attacks the assumption rather than the measurement. Conventional dating converts size to age through a population growth curve, so any fetus off the average is mis-dated - which is exactly the growth-restricted fetus whose dating matters most. Reading the image directly, with no measurements at all, sidesteps that and the paper shows it holds up in intrauterine growth restriction. Blinded external validation against first-trimester-confirmed dates is the right standard and rarely met in this literature.
study_design: retrospective model development with blinded external validation
dataset_size: two independent datasets, sizes not stated in the abstract
headline_result: mean absolute error 3.0 days (95% CI 2.9-3.2) in the second trimester and 4.3 days (95% CI 4.1-4.5) in the third, better than current ultrasound-based clinical biometry at those ages

title: Deep learning based synthetic CT from cone beam CT generation for abdominal paediatric radiotherapy.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: cycle-consistent generative adversarial network with global-residuals-only learning and a structural consistency term in the loss
patient_population: paediatric patients treated for thoracic, abdominal and pelvic malignancies, with a development dataset and a separate unseen evaluation dataset
clinical_problem: adaptive radiotherapy needs CT-quality images to recalculate dose, but the image taken on the treatment couch is a cone beam CT - and in children's abdomens, bowel gas moves between fractions and the patient numbers are small
model_description: Three adaptations, each aimed at a specific difficulty of the pediatric setting. Structural consistency is written into the loss because a cycleGAN will otherwise hallucinate anatomy - fatal when the change you are trying to capture is where the bowel gas moved. Slice selection on a common abdominal field of view turns scans from children treated for any thoracic, abdominal or pelvic malignancy into weakly paired training data, which is how a small population yields enough. Evaluation goes beyond image similarity to segmentation and proton-therapy-specific metrics, since the images exist to compute dose.
headline_result: mean absolute error 55.0 +/- 16.6 HU versus 58.9 +/- 16.8 HU for a baseline cycleGAN, with better structural agreement for gastrointestinal gas

title: A multi-institutional pediatric dataset of clinical radiology MRIs by the Children's Brain Tumor Network.
