clinical_problem: enabling AI-based clinical decision support in pediatric neuro-oncology via large-scale imaging data
model_description: Describes a multi-institutional, longitudinal, multi-parametric MRI imaging dataset (23,101 exams, with linked clinical, digital pathology, and genomic/omics data) for 1,526 pediatric brain tumor patients, released to accelerate AI model development in pediatric neuro-oncology.
release_evidence: "treatment-naive images for 370 subjects were processed and released through the NCI Childhood Cancer Data Initiative via the Cancer Data Service"
dataset_size: 23,101 multi-parametric MRI exams, 1,526 patients (370 subjects with processed images released)

title: Early diagnosis and meta-agnostic model visualization of tuberculosis based on radiography images.
model_family: CNN (Deep Fused Linear Triangulation + residual network)
patient_population: 3500 TB and 3500 normal chest radiographs (ages not clearly specified as pediatric-only, mesh indicates Child)
clinical_problem: early diagnosis of tuberculosis from chest radiographs
model_description: Takes posterior-anterior chest radiographs as input, applies a Deep Fused Linear Triangulation preprocessing method to highlight infected regions, and outputs a classification of tuberculosis versus normal using a deep residual learning network.
headline_result: Accuracy 99.2%, sensitivity 98.9%, specificity 99.6%, AUC 99.4%

title: Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Recursive Feature Elimination-Graph Neural Network (RFE-GNN) and Phenotypic Feature Extractor (PFE).
model_family: graph neural network (GNN) with recursive feature elimination
patient_population: ABIDE dataset subjects (children with ASD and controls)
clinical_problem: Can a graph neural network using resting-state fMRI connectivity and phenotypic data accurately diagnose autism spectrum disorder in children?
model_description: Takes fMRI-derived functional connectivity features (selected via recursive feature elimination) and phenotypic data as input; a graph neural network with a phenotypic feature extractor outputs ASD vs. control classification.
headline_result: 78.7% and 80.6% accuracy on ABIDE dataset

title: Selectively predicting the onset of ADHD, oppositional defiant disorder, and conduct disorder in early adolescence with high accuracy.
model_family: deep learning optimized with a custom AI algorithm for joint training and automated feature selection
patient_population: children aged 9-10 and their parents, Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) cohort, followed to age 11-12
clinical_problem: predicting onset of ADHD, oppositional defiant disorder, and conduct disorder in early adolescence using multimodal predictors including structural and functional MRI
model_description: Input: 5777 multimodal candidate predictors including structural and functional MRI metrics, psychosocial measures, and parent-reported traits; output: individual-level prediction of onset of ADHD, ODD, and CD at 2-year follow-up.
study_design: prospective cohort with deep-learning prediction, tested on held-out unseen data
headline_result: Multimodal models: ~86-97% accuracy, AUROC 0.919-0.996; neural-metrics-only models: ~80% accuracy and AUROC

title: DraiNet: AI-driven decision support in pneumothorax and pleural effusion management.
patient_population: pediatric CT scans (n not stated)
clinical_problem: detecting pneumothorax and pleural effusion on pediatric CT to help decide whether tube thoracostomy is needed
model_description: Takes pediatric chest CT scans as input and outputs detected and localized regions of pneumothorax and pleural effusion using an object-detection deep learning model, to support decisions about tube thoracostomy.

title: Automated deep bottleneck residual 82-layered architecture with Bayesian optimization for the classification of brain and common maternal fetal ultrasound planes.
clinical_problem: Automatically classifying standard maternal-fetal and fetal brain ultrasound planes to assist prenatal screening, particularly in resource-limited settings
model_description: An 82-layer deep residual bottleneck CNN with Bayesian-optimized hyperparameters and moth-flame-optimized feature selection classifies fetal brain and common maternal-fetal ultrasound planes.
headline_result: accuracy 78.5% (brain planes), 79.4% (maternal-fetal planes)

title: Development and optimization of AI algorithms for wrist fracture detection in children using a freely available dataset.
patient_population: 6,091 patients, 10,643 studies, 20,327 images (GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset)
clinical_problem: Detecting wrist fractures in children on radiographs using an optimized object detection algorithm.
model_description: A YOLOv7 object detection model, optimized through data preprocessing and configuration tuning, detects wrist fractures on pediatric radiographs; Grad-CAM used to visualize model attention.
study_design: retrospective model development and optimization study using a public dataset
headline_result: mAP@0.5 improved up to +25.51%, mAP@[0.5:0.95] improved up to +39.78% from preprocessing optimization

title: Identifying immunodeficiency status in children with pulmonary tuberculosis: using radiomics approach based on un-enhanced chest computed tomography.
patient_population: 173 children with pulmonary tuberculosis (72 with primary immunodeficiency, 101 without)
clinical_problem: identifying primary immunodeficiency status in children with pulmonary tuberculosis using CT
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from segmented lung lesions on unenhanced chest CT feed a logistic regression model that classifies immunodeficiency status (PID vs. non-PID) in children with pulmonary tuberculosis.
study_design: retrospective single-center radiomics study with training/testing split
headline_result: AUC 0.837 training set, 0.746 test set

title: Machine Learning Algorithm: Texture Analysis in CNO and Application in Distinguishing CNO and Bone Marrow Growth-Related Changes on Whole-Body MRI.
model_family: nine classic ML classifiers plus a deep learning neural network
patient_population: 66 patients with confirmed CNO and 28 with suspected extra-skeletal disease (pediatric population)
clinical_problem: distinguishing chronic non-bacterial osteomyelitis lesions from normal bone marrow growth changes on whole-body MRI
model_description: Input: texture features (Pyradiomics) from STIR-sequence whole-body MRI regions of interest; output: classification distinguishing CNO lesions from bone marrow growth-related changes using multiple ML classifiers and a deep neural network, with SHAP explanation.
headline_result: best deep neural network: accuracy 0.91, AUC 0.93 (95% CI 0.91-0.94), F1 0.94

title: Neuroquantification enhances the radiological evaluation of term neonatal hypoxic-ischaemic cerebral injuries.
patient_population: 297 children imaged for suspected HIBI; 96 children over age 3 with clinically diagnosed cerebral palsy and abnormal MRI underwent volumetric analysis
clinical_problem: quantifying regional brain volume loss in term neonatal hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury (HIBI) and cerebral palsy
model_description: Input is brain MRI of children with cerebral palsy due to hypoxic-ischaemic injury; the NeuroQuant(R) AI-based volumetric analysis software segments and quantifies brain substrate volumes (intracranial volume, thalami, brainstem, hippocampi, putamina, amygdala), compared against a normative NeuroQuant database, across HIBI subtypes.
release_evidence: Described as "NeuroQuant(R) software solution", a named, trademarked vendor product
dataset_size: 297 children screened; 96 children with cerebral palsy analyzed volumetrically
headline_result: Average intracranial volume reduced to the 1st percentile of the NeuroQuant normative database in all patient groups (p<0.001); significant volume differences among HIBI subtypes

title: Deep Learning for Automated Measurement of Total Cardiac Volume for Heart Transplantation Size Matching.
patient_population: 314 subjects aged 0-30 years (270 training, 44 validation: 36 normal, 8 heart disease)
clinical_problem: Automatically measuring total cardiac volume from CT to match donor and recipient heart size for pediatric heart transplantation
model_description: A custom 3D convolutional neural network (DenseNet + ResNet architecture) that takes cardiac CT scans as input and outputs an automatic segmentation used to calculate total cardiac volume for donor-recipient size matching in pediatric heart transplantation.
study_design: Retrospective algorithm development and validation study (preprint, Research Square)
headline_result: Dice 0.94 +/- 0.03; mean absolute percent error in TCV 5.5%

title: Is the diagnostic model based on convolutional neural network superior to pediatric radiologists in the ultrasonic diagnosis of biliary atresia?
patient_population: 4,887 gallbladder ultrasound images from infants with biliary atresia, non-BA hyperbilirubinemia, and healthy infants
clinical_problem: diagnosing biliary atresia from gallbladder ultrasound images in infants, compared to pediatric radiologists
model_description: Takes gallbladder ultrasound images as input and outputs a classification of biliary atresia versus non-BA hyperbilirubinemia versus healthy, using two Mask R-CNN models with different backbone networks, compared against four pediatric radiologists.
study_design: retrospective model development and reader comparison study
headline_result: Model 2 diagnostic performance exceeded two radiology experts at patient level (p<0.05)

title: Neuro-environmental interactions: a time sensitive matter.
patient_population: 124 typically developing participants (53% female), ages 13-25 years, PHIME study
clinical_problem: Determining whether recent environmental metal exposure affects resting-state brain functional connectivity in typically developing adolescents
model_description: An interpretable XGBoost-SHAP gradient boosting model that takes biomarker concentrations of six metals (from saliva, hair, nails, blood, urine) as input and predicts global efficiency of resting-state brain functional connectivity (fMRI graph-theory metric) as output.
study_design: Prospective cohort study (PHIME) with cross-sectional machine-learning prediction analysis
headline_result: Predicted vs measured global efficiency correlated at r=0.36, p<0.001 (~13% of variability explained)

title: The expert's knowledge combined with AI outperforms AI alone in seizure onset zone localization using resting state fMRI.
patient_population: 52 children with refractory epilepsy (25 underwent surgery)
clinical_problem: Localizing the seizure onset zone from resting-state fMRI connectomics in children with refractory epilepsy to guide surgical planning
model_description: A deep network trained on resting-state fMRI functional connectomics data, integrated with expert epileptologist annotations of seizure-onset-zone-indicative connectivity patterns, localizes the seizure onset zone; compared with a deep-learning-only model.
headline_result: accuracy 84.8 ± 4.5%, F1 91.7 ± 2.6% (expert+DL) vs. <50% accuracy (DL alone)

title: Automated motion artifact detection in early pediatric diffusion MRI using a convolutional neural network.
patient_population: 121 exams (2,276 dMRI volumes) at 1 and 24 months of age; second dataset of 26 exams (2,349 volumes), ages 2-36 months
clinical_problem: Automate detection of motion artifacts in diffusion MRI data from infants and young children for quality control
model_description: Takes individual diffusion MRI volumes as input; a simple 3D convolutional neural network classifies each volume as motion-artifact-affected or not, for automated quality control.
study_design: retrospective model development with generalizability testing on a second dataset
dataset_size: 2,276 dMRI volumes (121 exams); 2,349 volumes (26 exams) for generalizability testing
headline_result: 95% classification accuracy on 4-fold cross-validation; 98% accuracy on a second dataset with different acquisition parameters

title: Aberrant single-subject morphological brain networks in first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder.
model_family: support vector machine on graph-based morphological network features
patient_population: 25 first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with MDD and 19 healthy controls
clinical_problem: distinguishing adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls using structural brain network topology
model_description: T1-weighted MRI is used to build single-subject morphological brain networks (based on cortical thickness, fractal dimension, gyrification index, sulcus depth); graph-based topological features from the cortical-thickness network are fed into a support vector machine that outputs a binary MDD-vs-healthy-control classification.
study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: 87.6% accuracy distinguishing adolescent MDD from healthy controls using cortical-thickness network topology

title: Deep learning model for prenatal congenital heart disease (CHD) screening generalizes to the community setting and outperforms clinical detection.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
venue_label: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
patient_population: 42 normal fetuses and 66 fetuses with isolated severe CHD at birth, Netherlands 2015-2016
clinical_problem: Detecting congenital heart disease on second-trimester fetal anomaly-scan ultrasound images in a community (low-risk population) setting
model_description: A previously trained deep learning model, originally developed on tertiary-center images, applied to fetal cardiac ultrasound images from a community second-trimester anomaly scan to classify normal versus congenital heart disease.
study_design: Retrospective external validation study in a community low-risk population (preprint, medRxiv)
headline_result: Model sensitivity 91%, specificity 93%, vs clinical detection sensitivity 53%; blinded experts sensitivity 55+/-10%, specificity 71+/-13%

title: Elbow trauma in children: development and evaluation of radiological artificial intelligence models.
journal: Research in diagnostic and interventional imaging
venue_label: Research in diagnostic and interventional imaging
model_family: deep convolutional neural network (two models compared)
patient_population: 1956 pediatric elbow radiographs from 935 patients aged 0-18; external test set 120 patients
clinical_problem: detect post-traumatic injuries on pediatric elbow radiographs and assess impact of AI assistance on radiologist interpretation
model_description: Deep convolutional neural networks trained on pediatric elbow trauma radiographs to detect post-traumatic injuries, evaluated on an external test set both in silico and as decision support for eight radiologists reading with versus without AI assistance.
study_design: retrospective model development with external test set and multi-reader reader study
headline_result: model 1 external test accuracy 82.5%, AUROC 0.916; radiologist sensitivity improved 0.82->0.88 with AI

title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning-Based Prediction Model for Detection of Biliary Atresia.
patient_population: 1,605 neonates under 100 days with cholestasis (145 with biliary atresia); external validation n=912 (118 with biliary atresia)
clinical_problem: detecting biliary atresia in neonates with cholestasis
model_description: XGBoost models combine demographic, laboratory, and imaging features (abdominal ultrasonography and hepatobiliary scintigraphy) in a stepwise diagnostic pipeline to detect biliary atresia in neonates with cholestasis, integrated into a web-based diagnostic tool.
study_design: retrospective multi-center model development with external validation
dataset_size: 1,605 neonates (145 biliary atresia); external validation n=912 (118 biliary atresia)
headline_result: AUC 0.97-0.999 across stepwise XGBoost models

title: Shape-aware Segmentation of the Placenta in BOLD Fetal MRI Time Series.
journal: The journal of machine learning for biomedical imaging
venue_label: The journal of machine learning for biomedical imaging
patient_population: 91 subjects (healthy fetuses, fetal growth restriction, high-BMI mothers)
clinical_problem: segmenting the placenta across BOLD MRI time series to measure placental oxygenation and function, including in fetal growth restriction
model_description: Takes BOLD MRI time series volumes of the placenta as input and outputs a temporal placental segmentation mask using a machine learning framework with a placental-boundary-weighted loss.
headline_result: Boundary-weighting improved Dice by 8.3% (cross-entropy) and 6.0% (signed distance transform)

title: FetusMapV2: Enhanced fetal pose estimation in 3D ultrasound.
patient_population: large-scale fetal 3D ultrasound dataset
clinical_problem: estimating 3D fetal pose (anatomical landmarks) from 3D ultrasound to support biometric measurement, plane localization and fetal movement monitoring
model_description: Input: 3D fetal ultrasound volumes; output: estimated 3D positions of 22 fetal anatomical landmarks (pose), supporting biometric measurement, plane localization, and movement monitoring.
study_design: methods development and comparison against other pose-estimation methods

title: Characterizing White Matter Changes along Fibers in Treatment-Naive Pediatric Posttraumatic Stress Disorder.
patient_population: 48 participants under age 18: 24 treatment-naive PTSD patients and 24 trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls, matched for age, sex, and education
clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric PTSD from trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls using diffusion tensor imaging white matter microstructure
model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging metrics (fractional anisotropy, axial and radial diffusivity) along major white matter tracts are measured in treatment-naive pediatric PTSD patients and trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls under age 18. Support vector machine analyses are trained to distinguish PTSD from non-PTSD using pointwise microstructural measurements, with axial diffusivity providing the best classification performance.
dataset_size: 48 participants under 18 (24 PTSD, 24 trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls)
headline_result: Pointwise axial diffusivity measurements gave the best PTSD vs. trauma-exposed non-PTSD classification performance; white matter abnormalities correlated with PTSD symptom severity

title: Predicting neurodevelopmental outcomes from neonatal cortical microstructure: A conceptual replication study.
model_family: machine learning prediction pipeline (replication of Ouyang et al. 2020)
patient_population: Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) third release cohort; largest sample 295 neonates, gestational age 29-42 weeks
clinical_problem: Predict neurodevelopmental (language and cognitive) outcomes at 18-24 months from neonatal diffusion MRI cortical microstructure
model_description: Takes neonatal diffusion MRI-derived cortical fractional anisotropy maps as input to a predictive pipeline (replicating Ouyang et al. 2020) intended to predict Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development composite scores.
headline_result: Prediction results did not outperform random/chance levels (negative replication finding, in contrast to the original study)

title: Accelerated two-dimensional phase-contrast for cardiovascular MRI using deep learning-based reconstruction with complex difference estimation
model_family: unrolled neural network (modified DL-ESPIRiT) with Complex Difference estimation
patient_population: 155 fully sampled pediatric clinical 2D phase-contrast MRI datasets for training; prospective pediatric clinical patients for feasibility testing
clinical_problem: accelerating cardiac MRI flow quantification (peak velocity, total flow) to reduce scan time in children
model_description: A deep learning reconstruction framework (CD-DL) was trained on 155 fully sampled pediatric 2D phase-contrast cardiac MRI datasets to reconstruct highly undersampled (6-11x accelerated) flow images. It takes undersampled k-space data as input and outputs reconstructed images with quantitative peak velocity and total flow measurements, evaluated against a parallel imaging/compressed sensing method and tested prospectively in pediatric patients.
study_design: retrospective and prospective technical validation study
dataset_size: 155 fully sampled pediatric 2D phase-contrast MRI datasets (training); prospective pediatric cohort for feasibility testing (N not stated)
headline_result: 9x accelerated CD-DL reconstruction was accurate and precise for peak velocity (bias 2.8 vs 3.9 for PICS) and total flow (1.8 vs 2.9 for PICS)

title: Motion artifact correction in fetal MRI based on a Generative Adversarial network method
model_family: Generative Adversarial Network (autoencoder generator with residual/SE blocks, CNN discriminator)
patient_population: fetal MRI; trained on a synthetically created motion-artifact dataset and validated on real motion-degraded fetal MRI scans (exact number not stated)
clinical_problem: correcting motion artifacts in fetal MRI to avoid repeat scanning
model_description: A GAN-based deep learning network, trained on a synthetically generated motion-artifact fetal MRI dataset created by modifying k-space data, reduces and removes motion artifacts. It takes a motion-degraded fetal MR image as input and outputs a corrected image, and was also evaluated on real motion-affected scans.
dataset_size: synthetic motion-artifact training set (N not stated); validated on real motion-degraded fetal MRI scans
headline_result: average SSIM 93.7% and PSNR 33.5 dB on the synthetic dataset; average BRISQUE score 21.1 on real motion-affected images; outperformed BM3D, RED-Net, NLM filtering, and WGAN-VGG

title: Deep learning-based real time detection for cardiac objects with fetal ultrasound video
patient_population: 40 fetal echocardiography videos
clinical_problem: real-time detection of fetal cardiac substructures on ultrasound for prenatal cardiac assessment
model_description: A YOLOv7-based end-to-end neural network was trained on 40 fetal echocardiography videos to simultaneously detect nine fetal cardiac substructures (e.g. atria, ventricles, valves, aorta) as bounding boxes in real time from 2D ultrasound video, aiming to support real-time interpretation of fetal cardiac anatomy.
headline_result: highest mean average precision 82.10% at 17 frames per second (0.3 ms per frame) across nine cardiac substructures

title: Deep learning reconstruction for brain CT images in children
journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
model_family: vendor deep learning reconstruction (DLR) compared with ASIR-V iterative reconstruction
patient_population: 61 children undergoing brain CT
clinical_problem: improving image quality / reducing radiation dose for pediatric brain CT
model_description: Brain CT data from 61 children were reconstructed with six levels of adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V) and three levels of deep learning reconstruction (DLR: low, middle, high). Signal-to-noise ratio, contrast-to-noise ratio, noise, and subjective 5-point image quality scores were compared to determine which reconstruction level best preserves diagnostic image quality.
headline_result: DLR-high noise reduction rate exceeded ASIR-V100% (supratentorial 0.62 vs 0.59, infratentorial 0.61 vs 0.59, both P<0.001); DLR-middle and DLR-high had higher subjective scores than all ASIR-V levels

title: Data-driven characterization of Preterm Birth through intramodal Diffusion MRI
model_family: support vector machine classification on HARDI diffusion MRI features, with TBSS and canonical correlation analysis
patient_population: 46 preterm infants imaged at term-equivalent age and 23 control neonates born at term
clinical_problem: identifying white matter alterations associated with preterm birth
model_description: Advanced diffusion MRI (HARDI) measures from preterm and term-born neonates were analyzed with a traditional voxel-wise statistical method (TBSS) and a support vector machine classifier to identify white matter regions that discriminate preterm from term birth, with canonical correlation analysis relating findings across imaging measures.
headline_result: SVM classification on skeletonized HARDI measures produced satisfactory accuracy, especially for fiber-directionality parameters (no single summary number reported)

title: Deeplasia: prior-free deep learning for pediatric bone age assessment robust to skeletal dysplasias
patient_population: public RSNA bone age dataset (12,611 train / 1,425 validation / 200 test hand radiographs) plus a retrospectively collected cohort of 189 patients (568 x-rays) with molecularly confirmed genetic skeletal dysplasias
clinical_problem: bone age assessment, including in patients with skeletal dysplasia
model_description: Deeplasia is an open-source ensemble of convolutional neural networks that takes a hand radiograph as input and outputs an estimated bone age. It was trained on the public RSNA bone age dataset and additionally validated on hand x-rays from children with skeletal dysplasias, a population usually excluded from prior bone-age models, including a longitudinal subset for test-retest precision.
release_evidence: We design and present Deeplasia, an open-source prior-free deep-learning approach for pediatric bone age assessment specifically validated on patients with skeletal dysplasias.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 12,611/1,425/200 RSNA hand radiographs (train/val/test); 568 x-rays from 189 patients with skeletal dysplasias
headline_result: mean absolute difference 3.87 months on the RSNA test set; 5.84 months on dysplastic hands; longitudinal test-retest precision 2.74 months, at least at human expert level

title: Extracting low-dose (18)F-FDG PET/CT images with list mode based on deep learning reconstruction in children
journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
model_family: deep learning (DL) PET image reconstruction platform
patient_population: 93 pediatric patients undergoing whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT
clinical_problem: reducing scan time/radiotracer dose for pediatric 18F-FDG PET/CT while preserving image quality
model_description: In 93 children, standard full-dose (120 s/bed) and fast (20 s/bed) whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT scans were acquired, and 20 s/bed images were also extracted in list mode from the full-dose acquisition. All short-duration images were processed through a deep learning reconstruction platform to produce full-dose-equivalent images, and image-quality metrics and standardized uptake values were compared across the resulting image sets.
study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic performance comparison study
headline_result: no significant differences in subjective quality score, TBR, CNR, CV, SUVmax, or SUVmean between standard 120s and DL-reconstructed 20s images (all P>0.05)

title: The future of neonatal lung ultrasound: Validation of an artificial intelligence model for interpreting lung scans. A multicentre prospective diagnostic study
patient_population: 62 newborns, gestational age >=33+0 weeks, with early tachypnea/dyspnea/oxygen requirement, multicentre
clinical_problem: assessment of neonatal respiratory status and need for respiratory support using lung ultrasound
model_description: Lung ultrasound scans obtained at defined early time points in newborns with respiratory distress were processed to extract regions of interest and used to train a neural network to interpret lung ultrasound and generate an AI-based score analogous to an established neonatal lung ultrasound score (nLUS). The AI score's ability to predict need for CPAP and surfactant therapy was compared with the established nLUS score.
release_evidence: described as a research model with no stated public release
dataset_size: 62 newborns, three lung ultrasound scans each
headline_result: AUROC 0.88 (T0) and 0.80 (T1) for predicting need for CPAP; AUROC 0.84 (T0) and 0.89 (T1) for predicting need for surfactant therapy

title: Estimating cortical thickness trajectories in children across different scanners using transfer learning from normative models
model_family: hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model with transfer learning
patient_population: reference model from N=40,435 individuals across the lifespan and dozens of sites; transferred to a longitudinal developmental cohort of children aged 6-17 years (N=5,985) with three measurement waves on two scanners
clinical_problem: charting individual cortical thickness development, including detecting abnormal development in children born preterm, across scanners
model_description: A large reference normative model of cortical thickness was estimated with hierarchical Bayesian regression from over 40,000 individuals across the lifespan, then transferred to a longitudinal cohort of children aged 6-17 scanned on two scanners not seen during model estimation. The model produces an individual deviation score for cortical thickness that is independent of scanner effects, and was shown to detect morphological heterogeneity in individuals born preterm.
study_design: retrospective multi-site longitudinal normative modeling study
dataset_size: reference model N=40,435 (all ages); transfer cohort N=5,985 children aged 6-17, three waves, two scanners
headline_result: a transfer set of as few as 25 samples per site gave good performance; deviation scores detected morphological heterogeneity in individuals born pre-term

title: Incremental improvements in tractometry-based brain-age modeling with deep learning
model_family: deep learning models (including recurrent neural networks) for tractometry-based brain-age prediction, compared to a linear baseline
patient_population: large sample of children and adolescents (exact number not stated)
clinical_problem: predicting brain maturation (brain age) from diffusion MRI white matter measurements in children and adolescents
model_description: Diffusion MRI-derived white matter tract properties (tractometry) from children and adolescents were used as input to several deep learning architectures, including recurrent neural networks, to predict chronological brain age, compared against a linear regression baseline. Deep learning models, especially recurrent architectures, gave a modest accuracy improvement over the linear baseline. Open-source software implementing the models was released.
release_evidence: We provide open-source software that fits DL models to dMRI data (https://yeatmanlab.github.io/AFQ-Insight).
dataset_size: large sample of children and adolescents (exact N not stated)
headline_result: recurrent neural network architectures gave up to ~6% improvement in accuracy over the linear baseline

title: A primary and secondary feature interactive learning network for bone age assessment
model_family: primary and secondary feature interactive learning network (CNN with attention erasure module)
patient_population: adolescents undergoing hand radiography (RSNA bone age dataset)
clinical_problem: bone age assessment
model_description: Hand radiographs are processed end-to-end by PSILNet, which locates important bone-age-related regions using an attention erasure module and lets primary and secondary features learn from each other, without requiring additional manual region annotation, to estimate bone age.
headline_result: Mean absolute error of 4.09 months on the RSNA bone age dataset

title: Improvement of Bone Age Assessment Using a Deep Learning Model in Young Children: Significance of Carpal Bone Analysis
model_family: hybrid Greulich-Pyle and modified Tanner-Whitehouse deep learning model
patient_population: 453 hand radiographs from a single institution (external validation), young children
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in young children
model_description: A hybrid Greulich-Pyle / modified Tanner-Whitehouse deep-learning model for bone age assessment was trained on an open dataset with an added carpal-bone analysis module (M1), and compared with a version without carpal-bone analysis (M2). Both were externally validated against a reference standard set by three human experts on 453 hand radiographs from a single institution, stratified by sex and pubertal developmental stage.
headline_result: M1 (with carpal bone analysis) showed lower mean absolute difference (0.366y) than M2 (without, 0.388y) vs reference standard, p<0.001; greater improvement in pre-pubertal patients

title: Pediatric brain tumor classification using deep learning on MR-images from the children’s brain tumor network
model_family: off-the-shelf deep learning models and a custom shallow CNN, pretrained on adult MRI, with joint image-age fusion
patient_population: 181 subjects from the Children's Brain Tumor Network (CBTN), infratentorial and supratentorial tumors, mainly low-grade astrocytoma, ependymoma, and medulloblastoma
clinical_problem: classification of pediatric brain tumor type
model_description: T1w-Gd, T2-weighted, and ADC MRI sequences from children with brain tumors were used, separately, to classify tumor type using four off-the-shelf deep learning models and a custom shallow network, all pretrained on adult MRI. Image and age data were combined with joint fusion, and tumor-type prediction was computed per tumor volume; model attention was assessed with Grad-CAM.
headline_result: Best performance (custom shallow network with age fusion): MCC 0.71 (ADC) / 0.64 (T2-w) for infratentorial tumors; MCC 0.70 (ADC) / 0.57 (T2-w) for combined infra- and supratentorial tumors

title: Uncovering the effects of model initialization on deep model generalization: A study with adult and pediatric chest X-ray images
model_family: deep convolutional neural networks (Cold-start, Warm-start, Shrink-and-Perturb initialization) with weight-level ensembling
patient_population: adult and pediatric chest X-ray datasets, including external validation cohorts
clinical_problem: generalizability of chest X-ray classification models across adult and pediatric populations
model_description: The study compares three deep-learning model initialization strategies (Cold-start, Warm-start, Shrink-and-Perturb) for chest X-ray classification models trained on periodically arriving data, evaluating generalizability on external adult and pediatric chest X-ray datasets, and proposes two weight-level ensembling methods to combine multiple trained models.
headline_result: ImageNet-pretrained initialization showed superior generalizability over random initialization; weight-level ensembles showed significantly higher recall (p<0.05) than individual models

title: Clinical application differences between TW3‑Carpal and TW3‑RUS based artificial intelligence‑assisted bone age assessment system: a real‑world pilot study
model_family: AI-assisted TW3 (Tanner-Whitehouse 3) bone age assessment system
patient_population: 262 children who underwent left wrist radiography, stratified into six 3-year age groups spanning 1-18 years
clinical_problem: bone age assessment using TW3-Carpal vs TW3-RUS scoring criteria
model_description: Left wrist radiographs from 262 children were assessed for bone age with an AI-assisted system using two different scoring criteria, TW3-Carpal and TW3-RUS, and compared against the averaged assessment of two senior pediatric radiologists as reference, across six age strata.
headline_result: ICC 0.983 (TW3-RUS) and 0.976 (TW3-Carpal) vs reference; TW3-RUS criteria performed better for ages 10-15, TW3-Carpal better for ages 4-9

title: Accuracy of bone age assessment system based on deep learning in children with abnormal growth and development
model_family: deep learning bone age prediction software
patient_population: 717 children with abnormal growth and development (266 male, 451 female), aged 2-18 years
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in children with abnormal growth and development
model_description: Left wrist radiographs from 717 children with abnormal growth and development were evaluated for bone age using the Dr. Wise AI bone age prediction software (TW3-RUS and TW3-Carpal methods), compared against a reference standard (mean of three senior radiologists) and against two junior radiologists.
release_evidence: the AI system (Dr. Wise bone age prediction software)
headline_result: AI accuracy within 0.5 year: 75.3% (TW3-RUS) and 80.9% (TW3-Carpal); lower mean absolute error than junior radiologists (e.g. 0.360 vs 0.565/0.496 years, P<0.001), comparable agreement with senior radiologists (ICC>0.95)

title: Application and development of artificial intelligence in bone age imaging assessment of children
clinical_problem: bone age assessment using artificial intelligence

title: Super-Resolution Cine Image Enhancement for Fetal Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

model_description: T2-weighted brain MRIs from very preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus are automatically segmented into lateral ventricles, external CSF, white and cortical gray matter, brainstem, and cerebellum using a Bayesian U-Net with 3D spatial concrete dropout, which also produces a voxel-wise uncertainty map. Performance was compared against DenseNet, a standard U-Net, and an ensemble of both, using manual segmentations as ground truth, to support more objective 3D monitoring of ventricle size for treatment decisions.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation
headline_result: Bayesian U-Net gave the best lateral-ventricle segmentation (mean Dice 0.948) versus DenseNet (0.814), U-Net (0.944), and ensemble (0.942), with mean uncertainty-estimation AUC 0.949

title: An artificial intelligence powered platform for auto-analyses of spine alignment irrespective of image quality with prospective validation.
model_family: hybrid model combining an HRNet landmark detector with rule-based post-processing
patient_population: 1542 consecutive patients with scoliosis at two Hong Kong clinics from December 2019 to November 2020 for development, then prospective validation in a further 337 patients; biplanar EOS radiographs recaptured with smartphones or screenshots
clinical_problem: automatic measurement of spine alignment in scoliosis, where existing auto-analysis is unreliable and where the image a clinician has is often a phone photo or a screenshot rather than the original radiograph
model_description: Two things set it apart. First, it is deliberately trained on degraded images - smartphone photographs and screenshots of radiographs - because that is what gets sent between clinics, and robustness to that is the difference between a research tool and a usable one. Second, rules are layered on the network's landmarks so the output can be explained and checked, rather than emerging from an opaque regression. Prospectively validated on 337 further patients, which is rare in this literature.
dataset_size: 1542 development patients plus 337 prospective validation patients
headline_result: mean landmark error 2.78 pixels posteroanterior and 5.52 lateral; mean angle error 3.18 degrees coronal and 6.32 degrees sagittal; curve detection sensitivity 95.7% and specificity 88.1%; all predicted alignments strongly correlated with ground truth (R2 > 0.97)

title: Deep Learning-Assisted Diagnosis of Pediatric Skull Fractures on Plain Radiographs.
model_family: deep learning detection model for plain radiographs
patient_population: children with head trauma who had both skull radiography and cranial CT: development sets of 149 and 264 from two hospitals, external test set of 95 from a third; cranial CT was the reference standard
clinical_problem: detecting skull fractures on plain radiographs in children with head trauma, the film that is often taken first and read by whoever is on shift
model_description: One of the cleaner pediatric AI evaluations in the literature: multi-center development, a genuinely external test hospital, CT as the reference standard, and a two-session reader study with the crossed design that shows who the tool is for. The answer is the one that keeps recurring in pediatric AI - it significantly helped radiology residents and emergency physicians and did nothing measurable for the pediatric radiologist. That is an argument about staffing and coverage, not about accuracy.
study_design: retrospective multi-center model development with a crossed reader study
dataset_size: 413 development cases from two hospitals, 95 external test cases from a third
headline_result: AUROC 0.922 internal and 0.870 external; with AI assistance AUROC rose by 0.094 for radiology residents (p = 0.012) and 0.069 for emergency physicians (p = 0.043), but by only 0.008 for the pediatric radiologist (p = 0.850)

title: Bone suppression on pediatric chest radiographs via a deep learning-based cascade model.

venue_label: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
patient_population: 129 pediatric digitally reconstructed radiographs used for training data generation
clinical_problem: producing bone-suppressed images from pediatric chest radiographs to improve detection of pulmonary disease, since dual-energy subtraction cannot safely be used in children
model_description: Takes standard pediatric chest radiographs as input and outputs a bone-suppressed image using a cascaded deep-learning model, trained via adult CT-derived digitally reconstructed radiographs adapted to pediatric anatomy with a U-Net.
study_design: retrospective model development and reader evaluation study
headline_result: Radiologist effectiveness score 3.31 ± 0.48 (scale 1-5)

title: Forensic bone age estimation of adolescent pelvis X-rays based on two-stage convolutional neural network.

headline_result: RMSE 0.93-1.14 years; MAE 0.67-0.88 years (with segmentation-based augmentation)

title: Deep learning fetal ultrasound video model match human observers in biometric measurements.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: multi-task convolutional network doing spatio-temporal feature extraction and standard plane detection on ultrasound video
patient_population: 50 freehand fetal ultrasound video scans, compared against five experienced sonographers measuring at two time points at least two weeks apart
clinical_problem: fetal biometry - head circumference, biparietal diameter, abdominal circumference, femur length - and the gestational age and weight estimates derived from it, in settings short of sonographers who can interpret fetal ultrasound
model_description: Works from video rather than from a frozen frame, so the model chooses the measuring plane as well as the caliper positions - the part of biometry that actually takes skill. The evaluation is the strongest form available short of a trial: five sonographers measured twice, weeks apart, establishing both intra- and inter-observer variability, and the model's disagreement with each expert fell inside that band. Six minutes of expert time becomes a few seconds.
study_design: retrospective model development with a multi-reader repeatability study
headline_result: automated measurements comparable to five experienced sonographers, with differences within inter- and intra-observer variability and not statistically significant against any individual expert; seconds versus an average of six minutes

title: Denoising of pediatric low dose abdominal CT using deep learning based algorithm.

clinical_problem: reducing noise in low-dose pediatric abdominal CT to approximate standard-dose image quality
model_description: a generative adversarial network trained on unpaired low-dose and standard-dose CT images takes low-dose CT as input and outputs a denoised virtual standard-dose CT image
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and technical validation
dataset_size: LDCT n=83 (plus 33 test from another scanner), SDCT n=42
headline_result: virtual images had lowest noise and SNR/CNR similar to or higher than standard-dose CT (all p<0.001)

title: Automatic Placenta Localization From Ultrasound Imaging in a Resource-Limited Setting Using a Predefined Ultrasound Acquisition Protocol and Deep Learning.

dataset_size: 280 pregnant women, 6,574 training images; 148 holdout test cases
headline_result: Median test Dice 0.84; sensitivity 81%, specificity 82%

headline_result: validation AUC 0.92, test accuracy 0.875 (95% CI 0.81-0.94)

title: Detecting abnormal placental microvascular flow in maternal and fetal diseases based on flow-compensated and non-compensated intravoxel incoherent motion imaging.

headline_result: classification accuracy 73.5% (GDM), 66.7% (FGR) combining fb and vb features

title: Pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis and abdomen-pelvis CT images with expert organ contours.
model_family: annotated dataset release rather than a model
patient_population: 359 pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis or abdomen-pelvis CT exams (180 male, 179 female) from three scanners at Children's Wisconsin, ages 5 days to 16 years (mean 7 years), with expert contours of up to 29 organ structures
clinical_problem: organ autosegmentation has been developed almost entirely on adults for want of pediatric training data, and children's organs differ in shape and size across age in ways adult models do not anticipate
model_description: The pediatric counterpart to the adult organ-contour collections that autosegmentation was built on, and the reason it is needed is stated plainly - organ shape and size vary across childhood in ways an adult-trained model will not handle. Deliberately unselected: random routine clinical cases across three scanner models with varying acquisition, contrast and reconstruction protocols, which is what makes it a generalization test rather than a curated benchmark. Released publicly on The Cancer Imaging Archive.
release_evidence: available on The Cancer Imaging Archive under the collection Pediatric-CT-SEG, images in DICOM and contours in DICOM RTSTRUCT
dataset_size: 359 exams with up to 29 contoured organ structures each
headline_result: 359 pediatric CT exams spanning 5 days to 16 years with expert contours of up to 29 organs, released to enable pediatric organ autosegmentation development

title: Efficient Claustrum Segmentation in T2-weighted Neonatal Brain MRI Using Transfer Learning from Adult Scans.
model_family: deep learning segmentation model with transfer learning from adult scans
patient_population: 558 T2-weighted neonatal brain MRIs from the developing Human Connectome Project; trained/evaluated on 30 manual annotations, applied to 528 scans
clinical_problem: automatically segmenting the claustrum in neonatal brain MRI, a structure linked to subplate neuron development affected by prematurity, using knowledge transferred from adult claustrum segmentation
model_description: Deep learning-based claustrum segmentation model for T2-weighted neonatal brain MRI, using transfer learning from claustrum segmentation models trained on T1-weighted adult scans, requiring only a small number of neonatal annotations
release_evidence: The easy to use models and codes are made publicly available.

dataset_size: 558 neonatal MRIs (dHCP); trained on 30 manual annotations; applied to 528 scans
headline_result: median volumetric similarity 95.9%, robust Hausdorff distance 1.12 mm, Dice 80.0%; significantly superior to interrater reliability (p=0.047 volumetric similarity, p<0.005 Dice); reliable segmentation in 97.4% of 528 scans

title: Segmenting pediatric optic pathway gliomas from MRI using deep learning.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

clinical_problem: Can optic pathway gliomas, a common pediatric brain tumor, be segmented automatically and reproducibly on MRI to assess tumor burden, avoiding the difficult and error-prone manual segmentation process?
model_description: A fully automatic deep learning algorithm detects and segments optic pathway gliomas (and other brain tumors) from multi-modal MRI, using training strategies designed to generalize well despite limited ground-truth data.
release_evidence: 'our deep architectures have been made open-sourced to ensure full reproducibility of the method'
study_design: retrospective multi-dataset model development and validation
headline_result: High agreement between automatically calculated and ground-truth volumetric tumor measurements; fast operation (specific Dice/error numbers not given in abstract)

title: External validation of deep learning-based bone-age software: a preliminary study with real world data.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; Validation Study

clinical_problem: How does a commercially available deep-learning bone-age software perform against radiologist and pediatric endocrinologist readers, using real-world clinical data?
model_description: A commercially available deep-learning software takes a hand radiograph as input and outputs an estimated bone age, compared against three human reviewers (musculoskeletal radiologist, radiology resident, pediatric endocrinologist) using the Greulich-Pyle method.
release_evidence: 'a commercially available deep learning (DL)-based software for BA assessment'
study_design: retrospective external validation study with real-world clinical data
headline_result: RMSE (MAE) vs chronological age: DL software 13.54 (11.06) months, radiologist 15.18 (12.11), resident 16.19 (12.78), endocrinologist 19.53 (17.71) months; overall inter-rater ICC 0.93

title: Toward MR-only proton therapy planning for pediatric brain tumors: Synthesis of relative proton stopping power images with multiple sequence MRI and development of an online quality assurance tool.
patient_population: 195 pediatric brain tumor patients
clinical_problem: generating synthetic proton-stopping-power images from MRI alone, without CT, to plan proton radiotherapy in pediatric brain tumor patients

study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal test-set validation
dataset_size: 195 pediatric brain tumor patients (150 training, 45 testing)
headline_result: mean absolute error 42±13 HU (best T2W-based synthetic CT with preprocessing); QA gamma analysis correlated with true error (r=-0.89 T1W, r=-0.93 T2W)

title: Attention-guided deep learning for gestational age prediction using fetal brain MRI.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 741 developmentally normal fetal brain images from 19 to 39 weeks gestation for training, with independent validation at four academic institutions across the United States and Turkey
clinical_problem: judging whether fetal neural development is age-appropriate, which is hard because the brain's appearance changes constantly, image quality varies and motion artifact is common
model_description: Attention is what makes this workable on real clinical fetal MRI - it lets the network ignore the motion-corrupted and off-anatomy parts of an image rather than requiring clean input. The generalization evidence is stronger than usual: four independent institutions on two continents, with R2 of 0.81-0.90 after minimal fine-tuning, against 0.945 internally. That gap is the honest cost of leaving the training site, and reporting it is the paper's virtue.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: 741 training images plus four independent institutional datasets
headline_result: R2 0.945, mean absolute error 6.7 days and concordance correlation 0.970 internally; R2 0.81-0.90 at four external institutions after minimal fine-tuning

journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

study_design: retrospective multi-center model development and validation study
headline_result: AUC 0.88 and 0.87 on two independent clinical datasets

title: Intelligent Segmentation Medical Assistance System for MRI Images of Osteosarcoma in Developing Countries.
journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
venue_label: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
model_family: depthwise-separable U-shaped network with a conditional random field boundary refinement and Mean Teacher noisy-data training
patient_population: more than 80 000 osteosarcoma MRI images from three hospitals in China; osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor of children and adolescents
clinical_problem: segmenting osteosarcoma on MRI and computing tumor area in settings where radiologist time is the binding constraint and outcomes are worst
model_description: Explicitly engineered for a low-resource deployment rather than for a leaderboard: separable convolutions keep the model cheap to run, a Mean Teacher stage lets noisy studies be used rather than discarded, and a conditional random field cleans up boundaries that a light network gets wrong. The stated objective is a balance of speed, accuracy and cost, which is an unusual and honest framing for a segmentation paper.
dataset_size: more than 80 000 MRI images from three hospitals
headline_result: improved segmentation accuracy while holding the balance of speed and cost, tested across three hospitals

title: Automated segmentation of magnetic resonance bone marrow signal: a feasibility study.

model_description: A convolutional neural network, trained on 85 examinations, segments knee bone marrow signal on T2-weighted Dixon water-only MRI into three color-coded intensity levels, evaluated against a four-reader consensus ground truth.
headline_result: Median Dice 0.68 for level-1 (mildly increased) signal, 0.40 for level-3 (highest) signal, particularly poor when that signal was sparse

title: Effects of age, gender, and hemisphere on cerebrovascular hemodynamics in children and young adults: Developmental scores and machine learning classifiers.

model_description: Protocol describing planned use of brain MRI and clinical data as input to machine learning algorithms that will output abnormality detection, lesion-symptom mapping, and prediction of seizure onset by age 2.

title: Interobserver Variability of Hip Dysplasia Indices on Sweep Ultrasound for Novices, Experts, and Artificial Intelligence.

headline_result: alpha-angle ICC=0.87 (sweeps)/0.90 (single images) vs. subspecialists; DDH diagnosis agreement kappa=0.47 (AI) vs. 0.72 (subspecialists) on sweeps

title: Facilitating MR-Guided Adaptive Proton Therapy in Children Using Deep Learning-Based Synthetic CT.

clinical_problem: generating synthetic CT from MRI acquired during proton therapy to guide adaptive replanning in children with brain tumors, avoiding repeat CT
model_description: Input: T1-weighted MRI acquired during proton therapy; output: synthetic CT (sCT) for adaptive replanning, compared against a repeat 'ground truth' replanning CT.

headline_result: HU mean absolute error 65.3±13.9 (self-attention cycle-GAN) vs. 88.9±19.3 (conventional cycle-GAN); 3D gamma passing rates 97.6%±1.2% and 98.9%±0.9%

title: Technical note: Evaluation of a V-Net autosegmentation algorithm for pediatric CT scans: Performance, generalizability, and application to patient-specific CT dosimetry.
model_family: modified fully convolutional 3D V-Net, one autosegmentation model per organ
patient_population: 359 pediatric CT datasets with expert organ contours, with an independent 60-patient test set; separate models trained by scanner model protocol and by pediatric age group

model_description: Asks the generalizability questions a physicist would: does a model trained on some scanner protocols work on others (yes), and do age-group-specific models beat one model trained across all ages (no - pooling heterogeneous ages was as good). That second answer is practically important, because it means pediatric autosegmentation does not need to be fragmented by age band. The dosimetry endpoint is what validates the segmentations that matter: mean organ dose error stayed within 5% of expert contours for 18 of 19 organs, even where Dice was mediocre (0.52 for duodenum).
headline_result: median Dice from 0.52 (duodenum) to 0.96 (heart) across 19 organs, with mean dose error within 5% of expert segmentations for every organ except the spinal canal (6.31%)

title: Classification of suicidal thoughts and behaviour in children: results from penalised logistic regression analyses in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study.

title: No sonographer, no radiologist: New system for automatic prenatal detection of fetal biometry, fetal presentation, and placental location.
model_family: U-Net segmentation of the fetal head and placenta applied to volume sweep imaging acquisitions
patient_population: obstetric volume sweep imaging examinations performed in Peru by an operator with no previous ultrasound experience after eight hours of training
clinical_problem: obtaining fetal biometry, presentation and placental position where there is neither a sonographer to scan nor a radiologist to interpret
model_description: The title states the design goal exactly. Both halves of the expertise requirement are removed at once: a standardized sweep protocol keyed to external body landmarks replaces the sonographer's judgment about where to put the probe, and a U-Net replaces the interpreting provider. Eight hours of operator training is the whole input. Placental location is the weak point - substantial rather than near-perfect agreement - which is the finding a deployment plan would have to build around.
study_design: prospective diagnostic study in an under-resourced setting
headline_result: 100% agreement for fetal presentation (kappa 1, p<0.0001) and 76.7% for placental location (kappa 0.59); relative error 5.6% for biparietal diameter and 7.9% for head circumference; gestational age within 2 weeks of standard of care in up to 89%

title: Convolutional mesh autoencoders for the 3-dimensional identification of FGFR-related craniosynostosis.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 3D photographs of the general population (LSFM, LYHM datasets), CT scans of healthy infants, and patients with Muenke, Crouzon and Apert syndromes

study_design: retrospective model development and testing across photographic and medical imaging modalities
dataset_size: not stated precisely (3D photo datasets plus CT scans of healthy and syndromic infants)

headline_result: outperformed SVR, elastic-net/random-forest, spatio-temporal graph convolution, and BrainNetCNN baselines (no single summary number given); robust across independent ABCD sites

clinical_problem: Can a machine learning tool help radiologists identify distal tibial classic metaphyseal lesions on infant skeletal surveys, a fracture pattern highly specific for infant abuse?

title: Correlation of histopathology and multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging in childhood osteosarcoma: Predicting tumor response to chemotherapy.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: multi-feature fuzzy clustering with weighted majority ruling over conventional, diffusion-weighted and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI features
patient_population: 15 patients with newly diagnosed high-grade appendicular osteosarcoma enrolled in a single-center observational study, of whom 13 contributed usable data
clinical_problem: predicting tumor necrosis - and thus response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy - in childhood osteosarcoma, a cancer whose systemic treatment has been essentially unchanged for 30 years for want of a biomarker

Fifteen patients, so this is a proof of principle for a testable biomarker rather than a biomarker.
headline_result: MRI-estimated necrosis compared against pathologist estimates and deep-learning quantification of digitized histologic sections, through direct histologic-MR co-registration

title: Autonomous artificial intelligence in pediatric radiology: the use and perception of BoneXpert for bone age assessment.

BoneXpert was built as an AI-replace tool; asked how they actually use it, only 18% of radiologists let it replace them, 60% still review the radiograph themselves to exclude underlying disease, and 40% have never overruled it. Reporting time fell sharply. The authors' conclusion is the general lesson: bone age rating is not the whole of reading a bone age radiograph, so a tool validated for one task cannot autonomously own the examination.

patient_population: 2168 children aged 2.00-18.99 years (1125 female, 1043 male; mean age 12.3 +/- 4.3) who had abdominal CT at Cincinnati Children's Hospital between January 2009 and January 2019, screened to exclude abnormal BMI, medical conditions, medications, support devices and surgery

Automation is what makes the exclusion criteria affordable - screening 8817 scans down to 2168 by BMI percentile, medication, device and surgery status is only practical if the measurement itself is free. The finding that muscle index correlates only weakly with age and BMI, while raw area correlates strongly, is what makes the normative curves necessary.

title: Prediction of MYCN Amplification, 1p and 11q Aberrations in Pediatric Neuroblastoma via Pre-therapy 18F-FDG PET/CT Radiomics.

clinical_problem: noninvasively predicting MYCN amplification and 1p/11q chromosomal aberrations in pediatric neuroblastoma to guide risk stratification

headline_result: combined clinical-radiomic model AUC 0.98 (MYCN), 0.91 (1p), 0.93 (11q) in training set; 0.96, 0.88, 0.89 in test set

title: Fetal Organ Anomaly Classification Network for Identifying Organ Anomalies in Fetal MRI.

clinical_problem: Can a deep learning classification network automatically detect and classify anomalies in fetal brain, spinal cord, and heart on fetal MRI to make prenatal diagnosis more accurate and observer-independent?

headline_result: Classification accuracy 85.06% (brain), 85.27% (normal), 89.29% (spinal cord), 82.20% (heart)

title: Deep Neural Networks Predict the Need for CT in Pediatric Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Corroboration of the PECARN Rule.
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
venue_label: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR

clinical_problem: predict need for head CT in pediatric patients with mild traumatic brain injury to reduce unnecessary imaging, corroborating the PECARN clinical decision rule

title: Generative learning approach for radiation dose reduction in X-ray guided cardiac interventions.
patient_population: pediatric cardiac intervention patients; validated on 56 simulated and 52 patients' X-ray angiography sequences
clinical_problem: Reducing radiation dose during pediatric cardiac catheterization by predicting X-ray angiography frames instead of acquiring every frame
model_description: A model-free motion estimation network (LSTM) paired with a CNN content predictor estimates coronary artery motion and predicts future X-ray angiography frames, reducing the number of pulses required while preserving image quality.
dataset_size: 56 simulated and 52 patients' X-ray angiography sequences
headline_result: structural similarity index 97% (simulated), 82% (patient) data; pulse count reduced by up to 3 frames, about 30% dose reduction per second

title: Radiomics signature for the prediction of progression-free survival and radiotherapeutic benefits in pediatric medulloblastoma.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
venue_label: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
model_family: radiomics feature selection and machine learning modelling over 1294 features from T1-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI, combined into a nomogram
patient_population: 253 consecutive children with medulloblastoma from two hospitals, with a training set and two held-out test sets
clinical_problem: predicting progression-free survival in pediatric medulloblastoma and identifying which children benefit from postoperative radiotherapy
model_description: Larger than most pediatric radiomics studies at 253 children, with two separate held-out test sets rather than one, and the concordance index holds steady across all three - which is the main reason to trust it. The clinically actionable part is the last result: children with a low radiomics score did better after postoperative radiotherapy, which turns a prognostic score into a possible treatment-selection tool. The gain over clinicopathological factors alone is real but modest.
headline_result: concordance index 0.711, 0.707 and 0.717 on training and the two test sets; the nomogram reached 0.723 and 0.722 versus 0.665 and 0.677 for clinicopathological factors alone

title: MRI-based radiomics in distinguishing Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) and fibro-adipose vascular anomaly (FAVA) in extremities: A preliminary retrospective study.

clinical_problem: Can MRI-based radiomics distinguish Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma from fibro-adipose vascular anomaly in pediatric extremities before treatment, given their similar imaging and pathologic appearance?
model_description: Takes regions of interest from fat-suppressed T2-weighted MRI as input; radiomic features selected via LASSO are classified by a support vector machine to output a KHE vs. FAVA prediction.
headline_result: SVM AUC 0.807 (training), 0.846 (testing)

title: RDHCformer: Fusing ResDCN and Transformers for Fetal Head Circumference Automatic Measurement in 2D Ultrasound Images.
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (HC18 public dataset)
clinical_problem: Automatically measuring fetal head circumference from prenatal ultrasound to monitor fetal growth

study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation on the public HC18 benchmark
dataset_size: HC18 public dataset (exact n not stated)

title: Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Pediatric Lung POCUS: A Pilot Study of Novice Learners.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
venue_label: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
model_family: AI-assisted software generating panoramic lung views from a pleural sweep
patient_population: 32 previously healthy patients aged 0-17 years presenting to a pediatric emergency department with a cardiopulmonary complaint, scanned by seven novice learners after one hour of training; two POCUS-trained experts served as the criterion standard
clinical_problem: diagnosing pneumonia with point-of-care lung ultrasound in the pediatric emergency department, where the technique beats chest radiography but depends heavily on who is holding the probe
model_description: The AI does not read for pneumonia so much as build the image - stitching a pleural sweep into a complete panoramic view of the lung, which is the part a novice cannot reliably produce. One hour of training and seven novices is a deliberately hard test of that idea. The result should be read as a feasibility signal only: three pneumonias among 32 patients gives a sensitivity confidence interval spanning almost the entire range, and the mean image quality rating was under 3 out of 5.
headline_result: novice sensitivity 66.7% (CI 9.4-99.1%), specificity 96.5% and accuracy 93.7% with AI augmentation; expert interrater kappa 0.8; median scan time 7 minutes

title: Automated Multiclass Artifact Detection in Diffusion MRI Volumes via 3D Residual Squeeze-and-Excitation Convolutional Neural Networks.
patient_population: children and adolescents from the ABCD and Healthy Brain Network cohorts
clinical_problem: Automatically identifying the type of artifact present in diffusion MRI scans to flag poor-quality scans before further analysis
model_description: A two-step 3D residual squeeze-and-excitation CNN predicts the artifact type present in sub-volumes of a diffusion MRI scan, then a voting step outputs the overall artifact class for the whole volume.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation across two independent large-scale pediatric MRI cohorts
dataset_size: 2,494 poor-quality dMRI volumes (ABCD) and 4,226 (Healthy Brain Network)
headline_result: average accuracy 96.61% (ABCD) and 97.52% (Healthy Brain Network) test sets

title: Functional Brain Connections Identify Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Predict the Outcome of Cochlear Implantation.
model_family: support vector machine, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (voting ensemble)

clinical_problem: diagnosing sensorineural hearing loss and predicting cochlear implantation outcome from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity in children
model_description: Machine learning classifiers (SVM, logistic regression, KNN, and a voting ensemble) use resting-state fMRI functional connectivity features to diagnose sensorineural hearing loss and predict cochlear implantation outcome (category of auditory performance) in children.
dataset_size: 102 children (68 SNHL, 34 controls); 52 children with SNHL for CI outcome prediction
headline_result: classification AUC 0.84 (voting ensemble); CAP prediction accuracy 82.7%

title: A mutual promotion encoder-decoder method for ultrasonic hydronephrosis diagnosis.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: Children with UPJO/hydronephrosis (cohort size not stated in abstract)
clinical_problem: Automatically diagnose ureteropelvic junction obstruction (UPJO)/hydronephrosis severity from ultrasound images in children
model_description: Takes renal ultrasound images as input; a mutual-promotion encoder-decoder model first segments then classifies UPJO severity, sharing a transformation structure between segmentation and classification branches.
headline_result: Accuracy 0.891, F1-score 0.895

title: MRI Radiogenomics of Pediatric Medulloblastoma: A Multicenter Study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: two-stage sequential radiomics classifier selected from six candidate models
patient_population: 263 children with newly diagnosed medulloblastoma at 12 international pediatric sites, mean age 87 months
clinical_problem: identifying the molecular subgroup of a medulloblastoma from the preoperative MRI, which determines risk group and therapy
model_description: Extracts 1,800 texture and intensity features from preoperative T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 MRI and assigns the tumor to one of the four clinically actionable molecular subgroups, in two stages: first separating non-WNT/non-SHH tumors, then splitting WNT from SHH. A separate classifier distinguishes high-risk group 3 from group 4. If it held up prospectively it would let subgroup-directed decisions be made before surgery, and narrow who needs targeted genetic testing.
headline_result: microaveraged F1 88% across subgroups, 95% for WNT specifically, and AUC 98% for group 3 versus group 4

title: Validation of Convolutional Neural Networks for Fast Determination of Whole-Body Metabolic Tumor Burden in Pediatric Lymphoma.
patient_population: 102 pediatric lymphoma patients (76 analyzed after exclusions), mean age 11 years, IAEA multi-country dataset
clinical_problem: Can CNN-based software rapidly and accurately quantify whole-body metabolic tumor burden on 18F-FDG PET/CT in pediatric lymphoma compared to standard semiautomatic methods?
model_description: Takes whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT images as input; CNN-based software outputs automated calculation of whole-body metabolic tumor volume and total lesion glycolysis.
headline_result: ICC 0.993 (wbMTV) and 0.999 (wbTLG) vs. semiautomatic method; CNN mean 19 s vs. semiautomatic mean 21.6 min

title: Automatic measurement of fetal head circumference using a novel GCN-assisted deep convolutional network.

clinical_problem: automatically measuring fetal head circumference from ultrasound to monitor fetal growth
model_description: GAC-Net, a CNN with a graph convolutional network attention module, automatically segments the fetal skull boundary in ultrasound images to measure head circumference.
headline_result: Hausdorff distance 1.22+/-0.71mm, Dice similarity coefficient 98.21+/-1.16%

title: Multi-Contrast MRI Image Synthesis Using Switchable Cycle-Consistent Generative Adversarial Networks.
patient_population: large set of publicly accessible pediatric structural brain MRI images
clinical_problem: synthesizing an unacquired MRI contrast (e.g., T1-weighted from T2-weighted) when not all sequences are available
model_description: Takes one MRI contrast (e.g., T2-weighted) as input and outputs a synthesized image of another contrast (e.g., T1-weighted), using a single switchable CycleGAN generator instead of the two separate generators required by the original CycleGAN.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and comparative evaluation study
headline_result: switchable CycleGAN outperforms original CycleGAN on pediatric brain MRI contrast synthesis, quantitatively and qualitatively

title: A Principal Neighborhood Aggregation-Based Graph Convolutional Network for Pneumonia Detection.
patient_population: Real-world pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset (India)
clinical_problem: Detect pneumonia in children from chest X-rays
model_description: Takes chest X-ray images as input; transfer learning constructs a graph representation of images, and a principal-neighborhood-aggregation graph convolutional network classifies pneumonia presence.
headline_result: Best performance vs state-of-the-art baseline methods on a real-world dataset (exact figures not given)

title: CT-based morphologic and radiomics features for the classification of MYCN gene amplification status in pediatric neuroblastoma.

patient_population: 4,031 training cases (370,057 images); independent test set of 229 cases (203,619 images: 105 with ASD, 124 with intact septum)
clinical_problem: automatically detecting secundum atrial septal defect in children from color Doppler echocardiographic images across four standard views
model_description: Three-stage fully automatic CNN-based system that identifies the four clinically relevant echocardiographic views, segments cardiac structures and detects ASD candidates, then infers a final ASD diagnosis from color Doppler echocardiograms in children
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with independent test set
dataset_size: 4,031 training cases (370,057 images); independent test set of 229 cases (203,619 images)
headline_result: on independent test set: accuracy 0.8833, recall 0.8545, precision 0.8577, specificity 0.9136, F1 0.8546 (image-level averages across four views)

title: Clinical target segmentation using a novel deep neural network: double attention Res-U-Net.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: Double Attention Res-U-Net (deep neural network with residual blocks and multi-scale attention gates)
body_region: multiple (colonoscopy polyps, multi-site MRI, and fetal ultrasound structures including crown-rump length and fetal foot)
patient_population: three datasets: CVC-ClinicDB colonoscopy images, a multi-site MRI dataset, and a collected fetal ultrasound dataset
clinical_problem: developing a general-purpose medical image segmentation architecture, evaluated in part on fetal biometry structures (crown-rump length, fetal foot) from ultrasound

dataset_size: not specified for the fetal ultrasound dataset

title: Deep learning-based plane pose regression in obstetric ultrasound.

venue_label: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery

title: Ultrasound image denoising using generative adversarial networks with residual dense connectivity and weighted joint loss.

body_region: multiple (lymph nodes, fetal head, brachial plexus)

title: Density map estimation with convolutional neural networks to count radiopaque markers on colonic transit studies.

clinical_problem: Automatically counting radiopaque markers on abdominal radiographs to determine colonic transit time for work-up of pediatric constipation

study_design: Retrospective single-center model development and validation study
headline_result: Mean absolute error 2.6 markers; RMSE 3.9 markers (test set)

title: Automated detection of acute appendicular skeletal fractures in pediatric patients using deep learning.

age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicular fractures in children
model_description: An independent external validation of a marketed fracture-detection product on pediatric extremity radiographs, deliberately balanced across five anatomical regions with 60 examinations each. Avulsions are a characteristically pediatric injury, which makes that the finding to carry into a procurement discussion.
release_evidence: external validation of an existing commercial AI software program (BoneView)
headline_result: sensitivity per patient 91.3%, specificity 90.0%, AUC 0.93; sensitivity for avulsion fractures only 72.7%

title: Automated segmentation of whole-body CT images for body composition analysis in pediatric patients using a deep neural network.

clinical_problem: automated body composition analysis (fat, muscle, bone, organs) from whole-body CT in children
model_description: Input: whole-body CT/PET-CT images in children; output: automated segmentation of skin, bone, muscle, visceral fat, subcutaneous fat, internal organs, and CNS using a deep neural network fine-tuned via transfer learning from an adult model.

dataset_size: 31 patients (development, institution 1) plus 14 patients (external validation, institution 2)
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 99.28% after transfer learning vs 98.23% before (p<0.001)

title: U-Net-based image segmentation of the whole heart and four chambers on pediatric X-ray computed tomography.

study_design: retrospective model development and validation study using multiple public and custom datasets
dataset_size: three datasets: custom dCBP2021, public NBAtlas, public dHCP2017
headline_result: Dice 0.91-0.94 across three datasets for gray matter/white matter/CSF

title: Comparison of automatic liver volumetry performance using different types of magnetic resonance images.

headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.94, normalized RMSE 4.2% (best model, water+fat images)

title: PTNet3D: A 3D High-Resolution Longitudinal Infant Brain MRI Synthesizer Based on Transformers.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: pyramid transformer network using transformer and performer attention layers for 3D MRI synthesis
patient_population: the high-resolution Developing Human Connectome Project and the longitudinal Baby Connectome Project datasets
clinical_problem: infants sleep irregularly, cannot follow instructions and will not stay still, so a large share of scans in longitudinal infant studies are corrupted or missing - which breaks the developmental trajectories those studies exist to model
