Generalized across two independent large infant datasets.
headline_result: consistently superior synthesis accuracy and generalization to CNN-based GANs on two independent infant MRI datasets, with significant improvement in whole-brain segmentation when corrupted scans were replaced by synthesized ones

title: Comparing the Effectiveness of Brain Structural Imaging, Resting-state fMRI, and Naturalistic fMRI in Recognizing Social Anxiety Disorder in Children and Adolescents.

title: Chest Radiographs Using a Context-Fusion Convolution Neural Network (CNN): Can It Distinguish the Etiology of Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) in Children?

title: Automatic detection of pneumonia in chest X-ray images using textural features.

clinical_problem: automating Graf standard plane detection and angle measurement for infant hip ultrasound (DDH diagnosis)
model_description: Hip ultrasound images or video are processed by a three-module deep-learning framework (anatomical-structure detection, standard-plane scoring, angle measurement) that automatically identifies the Graf standard plane and measures alpha/beta angles to classify Graf type I/II hips, in both static-image and dynamic-video modes.
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: static mode: mean absolute error α 1.71°, β 2.40°, classification accuracy 94.71%; dynamic mode: accuracy 89.51% at 31 fps

title: FetalGAN: Automated Segmentation of Fetal Functional Brain MRI Using Deep Generative Adversarial Learning and Multi-Scale 3D U-Net.
model_family: generative adversarial network with multi-scale 3D U-Net

title: Resting-state functional connectivity identifies individuals and predicts age in 8-to-26-month-olds.

title: Influences of Magnetic Resonance Imaging Superresolution Algorithm-Based Transition Care on Prognosis of Children with Severe Viral Encephalitis.

title: Analyzing Transfer Learning of Vision Transformers for Interpreting Chest Radiography.

title: Deep learning accurately classifies elbow joint effusion in adult and pediatric radiographs.

headline_result: combined clinical+radiomics AUROC 0.84 for motor outcome at 4.5 years (vs. 0.8 clinical alone)

title: SynthStrip: skull-stripping for any brain image.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: CNN trained on synthetically generated images
patient_population: subjects from newborn to adult, across a range of acquisitions including clinically common thick-slice fast spin-echo
clinical_problem: removing non-brain signal (skull-stripping) as a first step in any brain MRI analysis
model_description: Takes any brain MRI, of any contrast or resolution, and returns a brain mask. It is trained entirely on synthetic images whose anatomy, intensities and artifacts are deliberately pushed beyond the realistic range, so that a single model generalizes to acquisitions it never saw, including neonatal and clinical thick-slice scans that defeat conventional tools.
release_evidence: our method and labeled evaluation data are available at https://w3id.org/synthstrip
headline_result: substantial accuracy improvement over popular skull-stripping baselines with a single trained model

title: Systematic evaluation of machine learning algorithms for neuroanatomically-based age prediction in youth.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: multiple ML algorithms (tree-based, kernel-based, linear, Bayesian)
patient_population: 2,105 typically developing individuals aged 5-22 years (five cohorts) for training; tested on 4,078 individuals aged 9-10 and 594 individuals aged 5-21
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult

title: Deep Learning to Predict Neonatal and Infant Brain Age from Myelination on Brain MRI Scans.
model_family: three-dimensional regression convolutional neural network with layer-wise relevance propagation attention maps
patient_population: 518 neonates and infants aged 0-25 months with reported normal myelination scanned at one academic center between January 1995 and June 2019 (mean gestationally corrected age 67 weeks +/- 33), with an external test set from the National Institutes of Health
clinical_problem: judging whether an infant's myelination is appropriate for age, which today means a radiologist visually inspecting T1 and T2 images against remembered milestones and comparing to gestationally corrected age
model_description: Automates an assessment that is already part of every pediatric brain MRI report, rather than inventing a new biomarker - the output is the age the brain looks like, which is exactly what the radiologist is estimating by eye. The attention maps are the convincing part: the network attended to cerebellum, posterior white matter and basal ganglia in the youngest infants and to anterior white matter in the oldest, which is the known caudal-to-rostral, posterior-to-anterior order of myelination. Combining T1 and T2 beat either alone, and it held up on an external NIH set.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: mean absolute error 9.8 +/- 2.3 weeks (T1), 9.1 +/- 1.9 (T2) and 7.7 +/- 1.7 (both) internally; 9.1 weeks on the external NIH test set

headline_result: 2D ultrasound more studied (88 studies) than 3D/4D (19); classification most common method (42 studies), followed by segmentation (31)

title: AI Denoising Improves Image Quality and Radiological Workflows in Pediatric Ultra-Low-Dose Thorax Computed Tomography Scans.

model_description: Takes ultra-low-dose pediatric chest CT data as input and outputs a denoised reconstructed image, compared against weighted filtered back projection and iterative reconstruction for objective noise, subjective quality, diagnostic accuracy, and time to diagnosis across 8 blinded readers.

title: Automated Machine Learning Segmentation and Measurement of Urinary Stones on CT Scan.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: deep learning algorithm segmenting renal anatomy and stones and computing stone features
patient_population: 94 children and adults with kidney stones identified on non-contrast CT, compared against three independent human reviewers
clinical_problem: measuring stone burden on non-contrast CT, which drives management decisions and which humans do inconsistently

title: Multi-Scale Deep Learning of Clinically Acquired Multi-Modal MRI Improves the Localization of Seizure Onset Zone in Children With Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: multi-scale residual neural network classifying cortical nodes from laminar surface sampling of multi-modal MRI intensities and diffusion tractography edge strengths
patient_population: children with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing clinically acquired multi-modal MRI, with an independent validation cohort split into lesional and non-lesional MRI groups
clinical_problem: localizing the seizure onset zone non-invasively in children with drug-resistant epilepsy, especially those whose MRI shows no lesion and who currently need intracranial electrodes to find it
model_description: The output is framed as a marker rather than a verdict - a per-node probability of seizure onset - which is how it can be combined with intracranial EEG rather than competing with it. The finding that justifies the whole exercise is in the non-lesional group, where MRI is by definition unhelpful: adding the marker to interictal intracranial EEG markers improved discrimination between resected epileptogenic and preserved non-epileptogenic sites by up to 15%. Uses clinically acquired sequences rather than a research protocol.
study_design: retrospective model development with independent validation
headline_result: Cohen's d of 1.21 between seizure onset and non-onset nodes, balanced accuracy 0.75 in lesional and 0.67 in non-lesional MRI groups, improving intracranial EEG-based discrimination by up to 15% in the non-lesional group

study_design: case-control retrospective study with a prospective validation cohort
dataset_size: 2196 images from 1098 women (training); two test sets of 136 patients/272 images each
headline_result: AUC 0.857 (retrospective test), 0.885 (prospective test); accuracy 80.32%/78.1%; manual CRL+FHR AUC only 0.687

patient_population: 583 subjects from four National Database of Autism Research studies spanning infants (median 7 months, n=155), toddlers (32 months, n=102), adolescents (13.1 years, n=230) and young adults (19.1 years, n=96)

The classifier reached AUC 0.70 in an independent validation cohort - a realistic figure that sits well below the ABIDE literature.

Training and validation performance are close, which is reassuring for a radiomics model of this size.

model_description: End-to-end deep learning framework using two CNNs to segment liver parenchyma and liver trauma regions on contrast-enhanced CT, automatically computing liver volume, trauma volume, and the liver parenchymal disruption index to grade pediatric blunt hepatic trauma severity
study_design: retrospective single-center study with temporal train/test split
headline_result: liver segmentation Dice 94.75%; trauma segmentation Dice 72.91%; liver parenchymal disruption index and trauma volume correlated with AAST grade (rho 0.823/0.831, p<0.001); AUC 0.942 (LPDI) and 0.952 (trauma volume) for distinguishing high- versus low-grade trauma

title: Pediatric radius torus fractures in x-rays-how computer vision could render lateral projections obsolete.
patient_population: Children with isolated distal radius torus fractures vs normal controls
clinical_problem: Could a single (posteroanterior-only) x-ray view, read by AI, safely rule out a distal radius torus fracture in children, avoiding the routinely obtained lateral view?
model_description: Three CNNs take a single posteroanterior wrist radiograph as input and classify it as fractured (distal radius torus fracture) or non-fractured.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and testing
dataset_size: 2,474 images (1,237 fractured, 1,237 normal); 200-image held-out test set
headline_result: CNN AUC up to 98% (95% CI 96.6-99.5%), exceeding human expert mean AUC of 93.5% (95% CI 89.9-97.2%)

title: Preoperative visualization of congenital lung abnormalities: hybridizing artificial intelligence and virtual reality.
journal: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
venue_label: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
patient_population: 5 asymptomatic, non-operated pediatric congenital lung abnormality cases
clinical_problem: Preoperatively identifying eligible cases for anatomical lung segmentectomy (vs. lobectomy) in children with congenital lung abnormalities using AI-based segmentation combined with virtual reality visualization
model_description: Input: chest CT scans; output: semi-automated segmentation of bronchovascular structures and lung lesions, visualized in 3D virtual reality to support surgical planning, combining AI segmentation and VR technology
study_design: retrospective feasibility study with specialist evaluation
headline_result: CT-based lesion-to-segment localization matched between specialists in 1/5 cases vs. 3/5 cases with 3D VR

title: Assessing atypical brain functional connectivity development: An approach based on generative adversarial networks.
patient_population: 377 neurotypical and 126 atypical children and adolescents from a community-based cohort
clinical_problem: Building a predictive neurotypicality score from brain functional connectivity to help identify atypical neurodevelopment in children and adolescents
model_description: An ensemble of GAN discriminators trained on neurotypical resting-state fMRI functional connectivity patterns produces a predictive neurotypicality score three years after scanning, with LIME used to identify explanatory functional hubs.
study_design: prospective community-based cohort with retrospective GAN-based modeling

title: A radiomics-based study of deep medullary veins in infants: Evaluation of neonatal brain injury with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy via susceptibility-weighted imaging.
patient_population: 190 infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and 89 controls, full-term (37+ weeks gestation)
clinical_problem: evaluating neonatal brain injury and predicting neurologic outcome in hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy using susceptibility-weighted imaging
model_description: Input: radiomic features of the deep medullary veins from susceptibility-weighted MRI plus clinical factors; output: nomogram predicting presence of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and neurologic outcome after perinatal asphyxia.
headline_result: combined nomogram AUC 0.97 (training)/0.95 (validation) for HIE; 0.91/0.88 for neurologic outcome

title: Application of deep-learning-based artificial intelligence in acetabular index measurement.
patient_population: 10,219 pediatric anteroposterior pelvic radiographs, April 2014-December 2018
clinical_problem: automated measurement of acetabular index on pelvic radiographs for developmental dysplasia of the hip assessment
model_description: Input: standard anteroposterior pelvic radiographs; output: automated acetabular index measurement, compared against expert committee and clinician measurements.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and reader-comparison study
headline_result: system 95% limits of agreement -0.93 to 2.86 degrees vs expert committee; accuracy closer to a senior clinician than most clinicians

title: Comparison of Parameters of Fetal Doppler Echocardiography Between Mothers with and Without Diabetes.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism
venue_label: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism
patient_population: 100 pregnant women (50 with diabetes, 50 controls), second/third trimester
clinical_problem: diagnosing fetal cardiac dysfunction in pregnancies complicated by maternal diabetes using Doppler echocardiography
model_description: Decision tree algorithms analyze fetal Doppler echocardiography parameters (isovolumic relaxation time, myocardial performance index, E/A ratio, ventricular wall thickness) to classify fetal cardiac dysfunction associated with maternal diabetes.
study_design: prospective case-control study with decision-tree analysis

title: Detection of coronary lesions in Kawasaki disease by Scaled-YOLOv4 with HarDNet backbone.
model_family: object detection CNN (YOLOv4 variant with HarDNet backbone)
patient_population: infants and young children with suspected Kawasaki disease
clinical_problem: Can AI detect coronary artery lesions from cardiac ultrasound in children with Kawasaki disease, to enable faster diagnosis and treatment and reduce the risk of coronary complications from delayed diagnosis?
model_description: Scaled-YOLOv4-HarDNet, an object-detection framework combining Scaled-YOLOv4 with a CSPHarDNet backbone, detects coronary artery dilatation and assesses coronary artery brightness on cardiac ultrasound images to identify Kawasaki disease coronary lesions.
headline_result: Mean average precision 72.63%, higher than Scaled-YOLOv4 (70.05%) and YOLOv5 (69.79%)

title: Application of TBSS-based machine learning models in the diagnosis of pediatric autism.
model_family: SVM / back-propagation neural network / logistic regression
patient_population: 32 children with autism, 27 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Classify pediatric autism using diffusion kurtosis imaging-derived white matter microstructure metrics
model_description: Takes diffusion kurtosis imaging metrics (FAK, MK, KA, RK, FA, DA, MD, DR) from tract-based spatial statistics regions as input; SVM, back-propagation neural network, and logistic regression classifiers distinguish autism from healthy controls.
headline_result: Back-propagation neural network accuracy 86.44%; SVM (RBF) 81.36%, SVM (linear) 84.75%; logistic regression 76.27% (leave-one-out cross-validation)

title: AI Estimation of Gestational Age from Blind Ultrasound Sweeps in Low-Resource Settings.
model_family: neural network on ultrasound cineloop sweeps
patient_population: 4,695 pregnant volunteers in North Carolina and Zambia, with separate test sets of IVF pregnancies and of sweeps collected by untrained users on low-cost devices
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy where there is no sonographer and no high-end ultrasound machine
model_description: Estimates gestational age from blind sweeps of the pregnant abdomen: the operator simply passes the probe along predefined lines without needing to find any standard plane. The model was more accurate than a trained sonographer's standard biometry, and the accuracy held when the sweeps were collected by untrained providers in Zambia using battery-powered devices. This is one of the clearest demonstrations in the corpus that AI can move an imaging capability to where the expertise is not.
headline_result: mean absolute error 3.9 days for the model versus 4.7 days for standard biometry (P < 0.001); 4.9 versus 5.4 days for sweeps collected by untrained users on low-cost devices

title: Deep Learning for Synthetic CT from Bone MRI in the Head and Neck.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: encoder-decoder networks (a 2-million-parameter Light_U-Net against VGG-16 U-Nets with and without transfer learning), trained on coregistered MR-CT slice pairs
patient_population: 39 pediatric and adult patients with both bone MRI and CT of the head and neck, four-fold cross-validation
clinical_problem: generating CT-equivalent images from bone MRI so that cortical bone can be visualized and processed without ionizing radiation - which matters most in the head and neck of children
model_description: The smaller network beat the larger one, which is worth noting for anyone assuming capacity is the constraint at 39 patients. The loss function choice is presented as a clinical trade rather than a technical detail: mean absolute error gives higher bone precision, mean squared error higher recall, and which you want depends on whether a missed or a hallucinated bone edge is worse downstream. Generalizability was tested by training and validating across hospitals, vendors and MRI techniques, and augmenting local data with outside data helped.
headline_result: Light_U-Net outperformed the VGG-16 models on Pearson correlation, error and bone precision/recall, with performance improving when local training data were augmented with data from other hospitals, vendors or MRI techniques

title: Automated seizure onset zone locator from resting-state functional MRI in drug-resistant epilepsy.
patient_population: 52 children with drug-resistant epilepsy; 24 underwent surgical resection/ablation with EEG and anatomical MRI correlation
clinical_problem: Can the seizure onset zone be localized automatically from resting-state fMRI in children with drug-resistant epilepsy, to reduce reliance on expert manual review before epilepsy surgery?
model_description: EPIK is a phased algorithm that uses fMRI noise biomarkers to eliminate noise independent components, then a maximum-likelihood classifier to identify which independent components localize the seizure onset zone from resting-state fMRI, benchmarked against expert IC sorting and surgical (Engel) outcomes.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development validated against surgical outcomes
headline_result: Mean accuracy 84.7% (4% higher than comparators), precision 74.1%, specificity 81.9%, sensitivity 88.6%; ~5-fold reduction in components needing expert review

title: Local Spatiotemporal Representation Learning for Longitudinally-consistent Neuroimage Analysis.
journal: Advances in neural information processing systems
venue_label: Advances in neural information processing systems
patient_population: longitudinal neurodegenerative adult MRI and developing infant brain MRI cohorts (sizes not stated)
clinical_problem: improving downstream segmentation of longitudinal brain MRI, including developing infant brain MRI, by better pretraining
model_description: A local, multi-scale spatiotemporal self-supervised pretraining method for image-to-image architectures takes longitudinal MRI scans as input and learns representations later fine-tuned for segmentation tasks with a self-supervised consistency regularization.
study_design: retrospective method-development study benchmarked across segmentation tasks
headline_result: Outperformed randomly-initialized baselines and existing self-supervised techniques on segmentation benchmarks (no single number reported in abstract)

title: Automatic detection and delineation of pediatric gliomas on combined [18F]FET PET and MRI.
patient_population: 66 pediatric patients, 109 [18F]FET PET/MRI scans
clinical_problem: Can a deep learning model automatically delineate pediatric brain tumors on combined [18F]FET PET and MRI as accurately as manual expert delineation, to reduce inter-rater variability in tumor volume and treatment response assessment?
model_description: Takes combined [18F]FET PET and MRI images as input; an ANN outputs automatic delineation (segmentation) of pediatric CNS tumors, from which biological tumor volume and tumor-to-background ratios are calculated.
headline_result: Median Dice 0.93; clinical metrics correlation r>=0.99 vs. manual reference

title: Faster Region-Convolutional Neural network oriented feature learning with optimal trained Recurrent Neural Network for bone age assessment for pediatrics
model_family: Faster R-CNN feature learning with an optimally-trained Recurrent Neural Network (Sun Flower Optimization)
patient_population: children (hand radiographs collected manually and from public sources)
clinical_problem: bone age assessment (Tanner-Whitehouse 3 based)
model_description: Takes hand radiographs as input. The region of interest is segmented with adaptive Otsu thresholding, a Faster R-CNN learns features from the segmented region, and a recurrent neural network, whose training weights are tuned by a Sun Flower Optimization algorithm, uses those features to predict the child's Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age. Evaluated on a mix of manually collected and publicly available hand radiograph images.
dataset_size: images collected manually and from public sources (exact count not stated)
headline_result: superior performance compared to state-of-the-art bone age assessment techniques (no specific metric value given)

title: An age-dependent Connectivity-based computer aided diagnosis system for Autism Spectrum Disorder using Resting-state fMRI
model_family: functional/effective connectivity features (group ICA, dual regression, Granger causality) classified with WEKA classifiers
patient_population: children, adolescents and adults, analyzed as separate age groups
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
model_description: Uses resting-state fMRI to build a computer-aided diagnosis system for autism spectrum disorder. Group independent component analysis identifies resting-state networks, dual regression obtains individualized components, and functional (full/partial correlation) and effective (Granger causality) connectivity features are extracted between networks. Because connectivity differs by age, features and classifiers were selected separately for children, adolescent and adult groups and evaluated with a suite of classifiers to distinguish ASD from typically developing individuals.
headline_result: 95.23% classification accuracy in the children age group using a classification-via-clustering classifier

title: ECAU-Net: Efficient channel attention U-Net for fetal ultrasound cerebellum segmentation
model_family: U-Net with efficient channel attention (ECA) modules
patient_population: fetuses in the second trimester of pregnancy
clinical_problem: fetal cerebellum segmentation for CNS assessment
model_description: Takes 2D fetal ultrasound images as input and outputs a segmentation mask of the fetal cerebellum, using a U-Net backbone with efficient channel attention modules that replace fully connected layers with shared-parameter 1D convolutions to reduce parameters. Trained on an in-house database (JSUAH-Cerebellum) of second-trimester fetal ultrasound images with Gaussian blur and random flipping augmentation, intended to automate a step in fetal CNS ultrasound evaluation.
study_design: technical development / retrospective segmentation accuracy study
dataset_size: JSUAH-Cerebellum database of second-trimester fetal ultrasound images (exact case count not stated)
headline_result: Mean Jaccard Score 86.01% and Dice Similarity Coefficient 91.35%, 2.86% and 3.73% higher than baseline U-Net

title: Automated atlas-based multi-label fetal cardiac vessel segmentation in Congenital Heart Disease
model_family: deep learning label propagation combined with a 3D residual U-Net
patient_population: 40 fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease (coarctation of the aorta) via cardiac vessel segmentation
model_description: Takes T2-weighted black-blood fetal cardiac MRI as input and produces a multi-label segmentation of the fetal heart and great vessels. The network combines deep-learning label propagation from a multi-label anatomical atlas with a 3D residual U-Net, trained using single-label manual segmentations from routine clinical practice plus the atlas, to give more detailed anatomical labeling than the single-label approach for assessing coarctation of the aorta and other congenital heart disease.
study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation accuracy study
dataset_size: 40 fetal subjects with suspected coarctation of the aorta
headline_result: Dice score 0.79 ± 0.02 for the fetal cardiac vessels region, statistically equivalent to a 3D residual U-Net trained solely on manual single-label data (p>0.05)

title: 3D MRI atlases of congenital aortic arch anomalies and normal fetal heart: application to automated multi-label segmentation
model_family: atlas-guided registration and deep learning segmentation
patient_population: fetuses with normal hearts and with congenital aortic arch anomalies
clinical_problem: fetal cardiovascular anomaly assessment (congenital aortic arch anomalies)
model_description: Presents the first 3D fetal cardiac MRI atlases of normal and abnormal (congenital aortic arch anomaly) fetal heart anatomy, built from black-blood T2-weighted fetal MRI reconstructed into 3D via slice-to-volume registration. Evaluates the feasibility of atlas-guided registration and deep learning methods for automated multi-label vessel segmentation from these images.

title: Coarse-to-fine segmentation and ensemble convolutional neural networks for automated pediatric bone age assessment
model_family: coarse-to-fine U-Net hand segmentation + stacking ensemble of five convolutional neural networks
patient_population: children and adolescents undergoing hand radiography
clinical_problem: bone age assessment
model_description: Takes a hand radiograph as input. A coarse-to-fine step (density-based clustering followed by a U-Net) segments and cleans the hand region, and the resulting clean hand image is passed to a stacking ensemble of five convolutional neural networks that outputs an estimated skeletal (bone) age. Evaluated on a mix of public and clinical hand radiograph datasets.
dataset_size: public and clinical hand radiograph datasets (exact count not stated)
headline_result: Mean absolute error of 5.42 months (males) and 5.98 months (females)

title: Structural differences in adolescent brains can predict alcohol misuse
model_family: machine learning (algorithm not specified) on structural MRI and DTI features
patient_population: adolescents assessed at ages 14, 19, and 22 from the IMAGEN cohort (n≈1182)
clinical_problem: prediction of adolescent alcohol misuse from structural and diffusion brain MRI
model_description: T1-weighted structural and diffusion tensor imaging from adolescents at ages 14, 19, and 22 in the IMAGEN cohort were used to train a machine-learning model predicting adolescent alcohol misuse (AAM) at age 22, tested on independent data; earlier-age scans (14, 19) were also used to predict later AAM.
release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
headline_result: Balanced accuracy 78% predicting alcohol misuse at age 22 from age-22 brain structure; 73% and 75% using age-14 and age-19 data respectively.

title: Atypical functional connectivity of the left fusiform gyrus in infants at familial risk for developmental dyslexia
model_family: multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) classifier on functional connectivity
patient_population: infants with (n=35) and without (n=63) a familial history of dyslexia, mean age ~8-9 months, recruited at Boston Children's Hospital
clinical_problem: classification of familial risk for developmental dyslexia from infant resting-state functional connectivity of the left fusiform gyrus
model_description: Structural and resting-state functional MRI were acquired in infants with and without familial risk for dyslexia. Multivariate pattern analysis was trained to classify infants by familial risk status using whole-brain functional connectivity to 20 predefined language/reading regions; connectivity of the left fusiform gyrus gave the strongest discrimination.
release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
headline_result: Classification accuracy 0.55 (p_corrected < 0.001, Cohen's d = 0.76) distinguishing familial risk status from left fusiform gyrus connectivity.

title: Applying a Convolutional Neural Network Based Iterative Algorithm to Automatically Measure Spinal Curvature on Radiographs for Children with Scoliosis
journal: Journal of Medical and Biological Engineering
venue_label: Journal of Medical and Biological Engineering
model_family: convolutional neural networks with an iterative vertebra-localization algorithm
patient_population: adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients; 110 and 272 radiographs used to train two CNNs, 100 new radiographs used for evaluation
clinical_problem: automated measurement of Cobb angle for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: Two convolutional neural networks, trained on 110 and 272 posteroanterior spine radiographs, segment the spinal column and individual vertebrae; combined with an iterative vertebra-localization algorithm, they automatically calculate the Cobb angle for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. Automatic measurements on 100 new radiographs were compared with manual measurements.
dataset_size: 110 and 272 training radiographs for the two CNNs; 100 additional radiographs for evaluation
headline_result: mean absolute difference 2.8°±2.8° vs manual measurement; 88% of measurements within 5° of manual measurement; average processing time 90 seconds per image

title: An open, analysis-ready, and quality controlled resource for pediatric brain white-matter research
model_family: neural network trained on expert- and community-scored examples
patient_population: children and adolescents from the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) study (N=2,747)
clinical_problem: automated quality control of diffusion MRI scans
model_description: Curates and preprocesses diffusion MRI data from the Healthy Brain Network study (N=2,747) into a standardized, analysis-ready open resource, including denoising and correction for motion, susceptibility distortion, and eddy currents. A neural network, trained using a small expert-scored subset plus a larger community-scored set, automatically scores the quality of every scan, intended to replace manual visual quality review for large-scale pediatric brain imaging research.
release_evidence: Preprocessed, analysis-ready data was made openly available
headline_result: Neural network QC concordant with expert ratings on a held-out set (ROC-AUC = 0.947)

title: VinDr-PCXR: An open, large-scale chest radiograph dataset for interpretation of common thoracic diseases in children
patient_population: 9,125 pediatric chest radiograph studies from a major pediatric hospital in Vietnam (2020-2021)
clinical_problem: interpretation of common thoracic diseases on pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: Releases VinDr-PCXR, a large open pediatric chest radiograph dataset of 9,125 studies, each manually annotated by an experienced pediatric radiologist for 36 critical findings and 15 diseases, with abnormal findings marked by bounding boxes. Split into a training set of 7,728 and a test set of 1,397 studies to support development of computer-aided diagnosis algorithms for pediatric chest radiograph interpretation, a task under-served relative to adult chest radiography due to a lack of annotated pediatric datasets.
release_evidence: the dataset was ... made publicly available on https://physionet.org/

title: Predicting Transdiagnostic Social Impairments in Childhood using Connectome-based Predictive Modeling
model_family: connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM), a machine-learning regression approach on functional connectivity
patient_population: transdiagnostic sample of youths with neurodevelopmental/psychiatric diagnoses (ASD, ADHD, mood, anxiety), mean age 11.68 years, from the Healthy Brain Network
clinical_problem: prediction of transdiagnostic social impairment (SRS-2 score) from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity during movie-watching
model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity was acquired during a social movie-watching task in a transdiagnostic youth sample. Connectome-based predictive modeling was trained via cross-validation to predict Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2) scores from connectivity data, with prediction confirmed in an independent replication sample.
release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
study_design: retrospective machine-learning prediction study with independent replication
dataset_size: N=144 (transdiagnostic Healthy Brain Network sample); replication sample n=41
headline_result: 10-fold cross-validation predicted SRS-2 (q2=0.32, r=0.57, p<.001); replicated in an independent sample (r=0.33, p<.035).

title: Anatomical prior based vertebra modelling for reappearance of human spines
model_family: deep learning object detection for vertebral landmark localization
patient_population: adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients (phantom and in vivo validation; exact N not stated)
clinical_problem: monitoring spinal curvature (Cobb angle) in scoliosis without radiation exposure
model_description: A deep learning object-detection method locates vertebral landmarks from freehand tracked ultrasound B-scan sequences of the spine; the landmarks are clustered to estimate the size, location, and posture of each vertebra, with missing vertebrae interpolated using anatomical priors, reconstructing a 3D model of the whole spine and measuring the Cobb angle without radiographs. The method was tested with phantom and in vivo experiments in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients.
study_design: technical development and phantom/in vivo validation study
headline_result: Cobb angle measurement correlation R2=0.978 (P<0.001) against reference

title: EVALUATION OF FETEL HEAD CIRCUMFRENECE (HC) AND ULTRASOUND IMAGES USING CNN
model_family: convolutional neural network for automated segmentation
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (110 labeled training images, 80 test images)
clinical_problem: fetal biometry (head circumference / biparietal diameter) for gestational age and growth assessment
model_description: Takes 2D fetal head ultrasound images as input and automatically segments the fetal head, fitting an ellipse by minimizing a cost function combining Dice score and ellipticity error, from which head circumference and biparietal diameter are calculated. Trained on 110 labeled images and tested on 80 ultrasound images, aiming to reduce the operator dependence and time cost of manual measurement.
dataset_size: 110 labeled training images, 80 test ultrasound images
headline_result: 94.31% success rate for HC/BPD measurement; 89.14% accuracy on plane acceptance check

title: Linking brain maturation and puberty during early adolescence using longitudinal brain age prediction in the ABCD cohort
model_family: convolutional neural network (deep learning brain-age prediction)
patient_population: children aged 9-12 years from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, assessed longitudinally at two timepoints
clinical_problem: linking pubertal development to brain maturation via brain-age prediction
model_description: A convolutional neural network deep learning brain-age model was trained on minimally processed T1-weighted structural MRI from the large longitudinal ABCD cohort (children aged 9-12) to predict each child's brain age at two timepoints. Predicted brain age was related to pubertal stage using linear mixed-effects models to test whether pubertal development is associated with accelerated brain maturation.
dataset_size: ABCD cohort, children aged 9-12, two longitudinal timepoints (exact N not stated in excerpt)
headline_result: brain-age prediction mean absolute error 0.7 and 1.4 years at the two timepoints, ICC 0.65; each pubertal-stage advance associated with 2.4 months higher brain age (β=0.10, P<.001), with steeper brain-age increases at higher pubertal development rates (P<.001)

title: Evaluation of Fetal Head Circumference (HC) and Biparietal Diameter (BPD (Biparietal Diameter)) in Ultrasound Images Using Multi-Task Deep Convolutional Neural Network
patient_population: 102 labeled training images and 70 test ultrasound images
clinical_problem: measuring fetal head circumference and biparietal diameter for gestational age estimation and CNS assessment
model_description: A multi-task deep convolutional neural network was trained to simultaneously segment the fetal head and fit an ellipse for head circumference and biparietal diameter estimation from ultrasound images, jointly optimizing a segmentation dice score and an ellipse-parameter error term. The model takes a 2D fetal head ultrasound image as input and outputs the head boundary and biometric measurements.
headline_result: success rate 92.31% for HC/BPD estimation; 87.14% accuracy for standard-plane acceptance check

title: Towards robust and generalizable super-resolution generative adversarial networks for magnetic resonance neuroimaging: a cross-population approach
patient_population: three cohorts: older subjects, newborns, and patients with brain tumor- or treatment-induced tissue changes
clinical_problem: improving MRI spatial resolution without longer scan times, tested for generalizability across populations including newborns
model_description: Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks (SRGANs) were trained on T1-weighted MRI from three cohorts (older adults, newborns, and brain tumor patients) to upsample image resolution, and tested for generalizability when applied across cohorts and when trained on a combined multi-cohort dataset, using synthetic and anatomical quality metrics.
headline_result: no artifacts were introduced when SRGANs were applied across cohorts or trained on a combined dataset; high image quality and anatomical fidelity were maintained

title: Attention-based multiple-instance learning for Pediatric bone age assessment with efficient and interpretable
model_family: attention-based multiple-instance learning convolutional neural network
patient_population: children (RSNA 2017 pediatric bone age dataset)
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
model_description: Takes a whole hand radiograph, cropped into small patches, as input. A feature extraction network computes patch features, and an attention mechanism ranks and aggregates the patches by importance (multiple-instance learning) without requiring manual region-of-interest annotation; the aggregated image features are combined with sex to predict bone age, and the attention weights produce an interpretable heatmap of the regions used. Validated on the Radiological Society of North America 2017 pediatric bone age dataset.
headline_result: Mean absolute error of 4.17 months

title: Temporal bone CT-based deep learning models for differential diagnosis of primary ciliary dyskinesia related otitis media and simple otitis media with effusion
model_family: deep learning CNNs (GoogLeNet, VGG16_bn, VGG19_bn, ResNet18/34/50)
patient_population: 31 children with primary ciliary dyskinesia and 30 age-matched children with otitis media with effusion
clinical_problem: differentiating primary ciliary dyskinesia-related otitis media from simple otitis media with effusion
model_description: Takes temporal bone CT images from children as input and classifies them as primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)-related otitis media versus simple otitis media with effusion. Several deep learning architectures (GoogLeNet, VGG16_bn, VGG19_bn, ResNet18/34/50) were trained on retrospective CT data and compared, with GoogLeNet performing best, intended to help screen for PCD, a cause of otitis media that is easy to miss clinically.
dataset_size: 31 children with PCD, 30 age-matched children with OME
headline_result: GoogLeNet model accuracy of 0.99 for PCD screening

title: Detection of pneumonia using convolutional neural networks and deep learning
model_family: convolutional neural network with dropout in the convolutional layers (custom architecture)
patient_population: pediatric patients aged 1-5 years from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center (public dataset)
clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia on chest radiographs
model_description: A convolutional neural network using dropout within its convolutional layers was trained and tested on 5,856 labeled pediatric anterior-posterior chest radiographs (a public dataset originally from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center, ages 1-5) to automatically detect pneumonia.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
headline_result: 97.2% accuracy, 97.3% recall, 97.4% precision, AUC 0.982, competitive with current state-of-the-art solutions

title: MTSE U-Net: an architecture for segmentation, and prediction of fetal brain and gestational age from MRI of brain
journal: Network Modeling Analysis in Health Informatics and Bioinformatics
venue_label: Network Modeling Analysis in Health Informatics and Bioinformatics
clinical_problem: fetal brain segmentation, classifying pathological vs neurotypical brain, and estimating gestational age from fetal brain MRI
model_description: MTSE U-Net is a multi-tasking single-encoder U-Net that, from an already-extracted fetal brain MRI, simultaneously segments the brain into seven structures (intracranial/extra-axial CSF spaces, gray matter, white matter, ventricles, cerebellum, deep gray matter, brainstem and spinal cord), classifies the brain as pathological or neurotypical, and predicts gestational age, all with a single shared model.
headline_result: Jaccard similarity 77% and Dice score 82% for segmentation; 89% accuracy for pathological/neurotypical classification; mean absolute error 0.83 weeks for gestational age prediction

title: Automated diagnosis of hip dysplasia from 3D ultrasound using artificial intelligence: A two-center multi-year study
patient_population: infants with clinical suspicion of DDH, mean age 87 days (range 4-267 days), at two tertiary pediatric hospitals (Edmonton, Canada and Melbourne, Australia)
clinical_problem: developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) detection and classification
model_description: Analyzes 3D ultrasound of the infant hip and automatically calculates two standard DDH indices (alpha angle and femoral head coverage) without user input, classifying each hip as normal or dysplastic. The commercial, FDA-cleared algorithm, trained on data from one site, was tested retrospectively on hips from that site and an independent site it had not seen before, and compared against conventional clinical diagnosis made from concurrent 2D ultrasound.
dataset_size: 2,492 hips from 1,563 patients (1,294 hips Edmonton, 1,198 hips Melbourne)
headline_result: Sensitivity 0.90 for dysplasia; correctly categorized 90% (148/165) of dysplastic hips and 86% (2,006/2,327) of other hips; kappa = 0.79 agreement with clinical diagnosis

title: An automated BIDS-App for brain segmentation of human fetal functional MRI data
model_family: 3D convolutional neural network (U-Net) within a BIDS-App Snakemake workflow
patient_population: 159 fetuses (1,103 volumes) from open-access data for training/testing; 19 fetuses (82 scans, over 2,300 volumes) from a local cohort for generalizability testing
clinical_problem: automated brain masking/segmentation for fetal functional MRI analysis
model_description: Funcmasker-flex is an open-source BIDS App that uses a 3D U-Net convolutional neural network to automatically segment (mask) the fetal brain from functional MRI volumes, removing the need for manual segmentation. It was trained and tested on open-access fetal fMRI data from 159 fetuses and further validated for generalizability on a separate local cohort of 19 fetuses.
release_evidence: The tool is freely available and can be applied to any BIDS dataset containing fetal bold sequences.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 159 fetuses / 1,103 volumes (training/testing); 19 fetuses / 82 scans / >2,300 volumes (generalizability testing)
headline_result: Dice metrics consistently ≥0.74 across both datasets compared to manual segmentation

title: Language and Social Regions Are Affected in Toddlers with Autism and Predict Later Language Outcome

title: Learning to map 2D ultrasound images into 3D space with minimal human annotation.

model_family: convolutional network with a learned pairwise attention module, trained self-supervised by inverting a slice-sampling process
patient_population: 2D slices sampled from 3D fetal brain volumes at 18-22 weeks gestational age, then real 2D transthalamic plane images and freehand scan video

title: Brain MRI radiomics analysis may predict poor psychomotor outcome in preterm neonates.

Adding gestational age or diffusion parameters did not improve it. Forty-six neonates with 13 events is small and the model is cross-validated rather than externally tested, so the effect size should be treated as provisional - but the premise, that the injury is subvisual, is the interesting claim.
headline_result: AUC 0.925 from T1-weighted, 0.834 from T2-weighted and 0.902 from both, with sensitivity 84.6% and specificity 78.8%, despite 45 of 46 scans showing no significant white matter injury on visual assessment

title: S3Reg: Superfast Spherical Surface Registration Based on Deep Learning.

title: Machine Learning-Based Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics for Prediction of H3K27M Mutation in Midline Gliomas.

headline_result: combined model AUC 0.89 (training), 0.87 (internal validation), 0.73 (external validation)

title: Image Quality Assessment of Fetal Brain MRI Using Multi-Instance Deep Learning Methods.

headline_result: Best model (MI-CB-DLM with gestational age): accuracy 0.86, AUC 0.93

title: Altered dynamic regional homogeneity in patients with conduct disorder.

title: Comparison of first trimester dating methods for gestational age estimation and their implication on preterm birth classification in a North Indian cohort.

title: Ultra-low-dose lung multidetector computed tomography in children - Approaching 0.2 millisievert.

headline_result: effective dose reduced to 0.23+/-0.11 mSv (MDCT2) vs 1.13+/-0.58 mSv (MDCT1), p<0.001; subjective image quality not significantly different

title: Preoperative Assessment for Event-Free Survival With Hepatoblastoma in Pediatric Patients by Developing a CT-Based Radiomics Model.

clinical_problem: Can CT radiomics, before surgery, predict event-free survival in children with hepatoblastoma, to help inform treatment planning?

headline_result: Combined radiomics-clinicopathologic nomogram C-index 0.88 (95% CI 0.829-0.933), improved over the clinicopathologic model alone (C-index 0.81 vs 0.85 reported for radiomics vs clinical)

title: Automated Segmentation of Abdominal Skeletal Muscle on Pediatric CT Scans Using Deep Learning.
model_family: paired U-Net models for level localization and muscle segmentation
patient_population: 370 patients sampled uniformly from 0 to 18 years and across both sexes
clinical_problem: measuring skeletal muscle mass on CT, a marker of nutritional status and sarcopenia, which requires finding the L3 level and outlining muscle by hand
model_description: Two problems in one pipeline: locating the L3 vertebral level on the sagittal reformat, then segmenting muscle on the corresponding axial slice. Sampling uniformly across ages from birth to 18 is the design choice that makes it pediatric rather than adult-with-children-included, since body habitus changes completely over that range. Level localization landed within the slice thickness.
headline_result: L3 localization error 3.23 ± 2.61 mm, within the reconstructed slice thickness; muscle segmentation Dice 0.93 ± 0.03

title: Deep reasoning neural network analysis to predict language deficits from psychometry-driven DWI connectome of young children with persistent language concerns.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, Non-P.H.S.

clinical_problem: Can deep learning analysis of diffusion tractography connectome data, combined with psychometric data, predict expressive and receptive language scores in young children with persistent language concerns?

headline_result: Pearson R 1.00 (expressive), 0.99 (receptive) between predicted and actual scores; MAE 0.28 for both

title: Distinct effects of prematurity on MRI metrics of brain functional connectivity, activity, and structure: Univariate and multivariate analyses.

title: Leveraging voxel-wise segmentation uncertainty to improve reliability in assessment of paediatric dysplasia of the hip.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery

clinical_problem: Can voxel-wise uncertainty quantification improve the reliability of automated deep learning segmentation used to assess developmental dysplasia of the hip on 3D ultrasound?

title: Single-participant structural similarity matrices lead to greater accuracy in classification of participants than function in autism in MRI.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 29,288 connectomes from six databases (1,555 with autism), mean age 30.72, range 0.42-78.00 years
clinical_problem: Can single-subject structural MRI similarity matrices classify individuals with autism more accurately than functional connectivity, across a wide age range?
model_description: Symmetric similarity matrices derived from regional grey-matter-volume histograms on T1-weighted MRI are fed into a CNN to classify participants as having autism or not, compared against functional-connectivity-based and univariate grey-matter-volume classifiers.
headline_result: Structural similarity AUROC 0.7298 (69.71% accuracy); functional connectivity AUROC 0.6964; combined AUROC 0.7354

title: MRI-based radiomics for prognosis of pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma: an international study.
model_family: LASSO Cox regression on wavelet-filtered radiomic features
patient_population: 177 treatment-naive children with diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma from an international cohort, split into training and independent testing sets
clinical_problem: prognostication in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, a uniformly fatal childhood tumor that is rarely biopsied
model_description: Predicts overall survival from texture features of the routine T1-post-contrast and T2 images at diagnosis, before any treatment. It beats a clinical-only model built from age and sex, and holds up in an independent test set, though the concordance drops from 0.70 to 0.59 when it does. For a tumor where biopsy is often avoided and MRI is the only longitudinal measure, an objective imaging prognostic is worth having even at that accuracy.
headline_result: concordance 0.68 for radiomics versus 0.57 for clinical variables alone in training; 0.59 in the independent testing dataset (P = .02)

title: An ensemble of neural networks provides expert-level prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, Non-P.H.S.
model_family: ensemble of neural networks with segmentation models
patient_population: fetuses at 18 to 24 weeks undergoing screening ultrasound or echocardiography
clinical_problem: prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease on screening ultrasound
model_description: Takes a whole fetal ultrasound survey, picks out the five recommended cardiac views, and classifies the heart as normal or complex congenital heart disease, while separate segmentation models compute standard cardiothoracic measurements. It addresses a specific failure of practice: the five screening views can detect 90% of complex disease, but real-world sensitivity is nearer 30%. Performance held up on outside-hospital and lower-quality images.
dataset_size: 107,823 training images from 1,326 echocardiograms and screening ultrasounds; internal test set of 4,108 fetal surveys and over 4.4 million images
headline_result: AUC 0.99, sensitivity 95%, specificity 96%, negative predictive value 100%; sensitivity comparable to clinicians

title: Training a deep neural network coping with diversities in abdominal and pelvic images of children and young adults for CBCT-based adaptive proton therapy.
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
venue_label: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 64 children and young adults (aged 1-23 years) treated with proton therapy
clinical_problem: correcting cone-beam CT images for accurate adaptive proton-therapy dose calculation in children and young adults
model_description: Pretreatment abdominal/pelvic cone-beam CT images, with body width normalized to reduce size-variation effects, are input to a cycle-consistent generative adversarial network that outputs corrected CT-equivalent images for proton dose recalculation, compared against same-day repeat planning CT.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 64 children and young adults (1-23 years); 14 held-out test patients
headline_result: mean absolute HU error 47±7 HU (combined model) vs. 51±8 HU (site-specific models); gamma passing rate 98.5±1.9%; proton range within ±3mm for 91.2±11.5% of beamlets

title: Using Machine Learning to Predict the Diagnosis, Management and Severity of Pediatric Appendicitis.
model_family: random forest, gradient boosting and logistic regression compared
patient_population: 430 children and adolescents aged 0-18 with suspected appendicitis
clinical_problem: three separate decisions in suspected pediatric appendicitis: is it appendicitis, does it need surgery, and is it complicated
model_description: Combines history, examination, laboratory values and abdominal ultrasound findings to predict diagnosis, management and severity at once, which no earlier model had done. The authors also identified small subsets of 6 to 18 predictors that performed as well as all 38, and deployed the result as a free online tool. Severity, the target that would justify antibiotics instead of surgery, remains the weakest of the three.
release_evidence: deployed as an open access easy-to-use online tool (the Appendicitis Prediction Tool)
headline_result: area under the precision-recall curve 0.94 for diagnosis, 0.92 for management and 0.70 for severity

title: Learn Fine-Grained Adaptive Loss for Multiple Anatomical Landmark Detection in Medical Images.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: deep learning with reinforcement-learning-optimized heatmap regression
patient_population: in-house prenatal ultrasound dataset and a public cephalometric x-ray landmark dataset
clinical_problem: Can anatomical landmarks be detected automatically and accurately across different medical imaging tasks, without needing to hand-tune the target precision for each landmark?
model_description: A reinforcement-learning framework dynamically searches for the optimal objective metric for regressing heatmaps during training of a landmark-detection neural network, avoiding hand-crafted, task-specific precision settings; applied to both prenatal ultrasound and cephalometric x-ray landmark detection.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development on two landmark-detection datasets
dataset_size: not stated (in-house prenatal US dataset; public cephalometric x-ray dataset)
headline_result: Improved localization accuracy and training stability versus existing heatmap-regression approaches (no single summary metric reported)

title: Delayed brain development of Rolandic epilepsy profiled by deep learning-based neuroanatomic imaging.
patient_population: 167 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 107 typically developing children
clinical_problem: Is Rolandic epilepsy associated with delayed brain development, measurable as an increased 'brain age gap' on MRI?
model_description: A 3D-CNN brain-age prediction model, trained on 1,155 typically developing children's structural MRIs, estimates a 'brain age' from a patient's structural MRI; the difference from chronological age (brain-predicted age difference) is used as a biomarker of developmental delay.
dataset_size: 1,155 MRIs for training (open-source datasets); 167 RE patients + 107 controls for application
headline_result: Children with Rolandic epilepsy showed a 0.45-year brain age delay compared to typically developing children

title: Bone Age Assessment of Iranian Children in an Automatic Manner.
journal: Journal of medical signals and sensors
venue_label: Journal of medical signals and sensors
model_family: support vector machine (with HOG/LBP/SIFT features) and k-nearest neighbor
patient_population: Iranian children's hand radiographs (test set); trained on the University of Southern California hand atlas
clinical_problem: automatic bone age assessment for growth-disorder screening
model_description: Computer-vision feature extraction (HOG, LBP, SIFT) from hand/wrist radiographs feeds an SVM classifier that automatically assesses bone age, validated on an independent Iranian pediatric radiograph cohort.
headline_result: accuracy 90% (female), 71.42% (male); MAE 0.16 years (female), 0.42 years (male)

title: Time-Dependent Deep Image Prior for Dynamic MRI.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: unsupervised deep image prior with a learned temporal manifold
patient_population: fetuses in retrospective and real fetal cardiac MRI datasets
clinical_problem: reconstructing a moving fetal heart from sparsely sampled dynamic MRI without cardiac gating
model_description: Reconstructs a dynamic MRI series by fitting a network to that one patient's measurements, with no prior training and no other data. For fetal cardiac imaging this matters because there is no reliable heartbeat signal to gate on, and this method needs none: a low-dimensional manifold encodes the temporal variation and a convolutional network generates the image series consistent with the acquired k-space.
headline_result: outperformed state-of-the-art methods quantitatively and qualitatively on retrospective and real fetal cardiac datasets

title: Is there any incremental benefit to conducting neuroimaging and neurocognitive assessments in the diagnosis of ADHD in young children? A machine learning investigation.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: machine learning classification comparing behavioral, cognitive and neuroimaging predictors
patient_population: 162 young children ages 4-7 (mean age 5.55, 82.6% Hispanic/Latino)
clinical_problem: evaluating whether adding neuroimaging and neurocognitive assessments improves machine-learning-based ADHD diagnosis in young children beyond behavior ratings
model_description: Inputs are parent/teacher behavior ratings, behavioral executive-function measures, and neuroimaging (cortical anatomy) measures; machine learning models compare the predictive value of each input type for classifying ADHD versus typically developing children.
study_design: cross-sectional single-center machine learning classification study
headline_result: teacher ratings of executive function were the most predictive of ADHD; neuroimaging measures of cortical anatomy added little incremental predictive value

title: Mapping fetal brain development based on automated segmentation and 4D brain atlasing.
model_family: U-net for brain extraction, followed by super-resolution reconstruction and iterative linear and nonlinear registration for atlas building
patient_population: fetal brain MRI between 23 and 36 weeks of gestation in a Chinese population
clinical_problem: quantitative analysis of fetal brain MRI, held back both by the lack of automated preprocessing and by the absence of normative templates - particularly for non-Western populations
model_description: Two deliverables: an automated pipeline that takes clinically acquired fetal MRI through extraction and super-resolution reconstruction, and the normative product that pipeline makes possible - a 4D spatiotemporal atlas of the fetal brain across mid-to-late gestation. The population specificity is the point, since existing fetal templates are built from other populations and normative comparison against the wrong reference is worse than none.
headline_result: average accuracy 97% for automated fetal brain extraction, supporting a 4D atlas quantifying morphological development between 23 and 36 weeks

title: A Prenatal Ultrasound Scanning Approach: One-Touch Technique in Second and Third Trimesters.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: AI-based automated plane recognition and measurement algorithm (architecture unspecified)
patient_population: 1,005 uncomplicated singleton pregnancies, second and third trimesters
clinical_problem: Can an AI-based ultrasound technique automatically recognize standard fetal planes and obtain biometric measurements to improve workflow efficiency during prenatal scanning?
model_description: Takes live prenatal ultrasound video as input; the Smart Fetus AI technique automatically recognizes standard fetal planes (thalami, abdomen, femur) and outputs biometric measurements (biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length).
headline_result: Successful automatic acquisition in 99.30% of cases (998/1005); high agreement with traditional technique; significantly shorter scan time

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of 3D Ultrasound and Artificial Intelligence for Detection of Pediatric Wrist Injuries.
model_family: neural network trained on 3D ultrasound sweeps, benchmarked against three human readers
patient_population: 30 children presenting to an emergency department with unilateral wrist injury, scanned on both the injured and uninjured limb, giving 55 wrists; radiographs of the symptomatic limb as comparison
clinical_problem: ruling out wrist fracture in children at the bedside, so that the many children without a fracture are not sent for radiographs
model_description: Two novelties stacked: three-dimensional ultrasound instead of a handheld 2D view, and automated interpretation of the sweep rather than a clinician reading it. Scanning both limbs gives every child their own control, which is how a pediatric emergency clinician would actually judge a subtle cortical break. Framed correctly as a rule-out tool - the sensitivity is what matters and both readers and network reached 1.0 - though on 30 children and 36 test images.
headline_result: human readers combined sensitivity 1.00 and specificity 0.90; AI detected all fractures in the 36-image test set (sensitivity 1.0) and was indistinguishable from human interpretation

title: Preliminary Radiogenomic Evidence for the Prediction of Metastasis and Chemotherapy Response in Pediatric Patients with Osteosarcoma Using 18F-FDF PET/CT, EZRIN and KI67.
model_family: random forest selected after comparing algorithms, using PET/CT image texture features with and without KI67 and EZRIN expression
patient_population: 52 pediatric osteosarcoma patients for algorithm selection, with 21 selected for model development based on simultaneous KI67 and EZRIN expression
clinical_problem: predicting chemotherapy response and metastasis in pediatric osteosarcoma, a tumor prone to metastasis with high mortality where both predictions guide treatment
model_description: Radiogenomics in the literal sense - image texture features combined with measured expression of two proteins - and the paper quantifies what the genomic half contributes: metastasis prediction accuracy rose about ten points when KI67 and EZRIN were added to texture alone. Twenty-one patients in the combined model is very small, so this is a direction rather than a result.
dataset_size: 52 patients for algorithm selection, 21 for the combined model
headline_result: chemotherapy response accuracy 0.83 with image texture alone rising to 0.85 (AUC 0.89) with KI67 and EZRIN; metastasis accuracy 0.76 rising to 0.85

title: Radiology "forensics": determination of age and sex from chest radiographs using deep learning.
patient_population: 112 120 frontal chest radiographs from NIH ChestX-ray14 covering ages 1 to 95, with separate pediatric-only models, and external testing on 662 radiographs from China
clinical_problem: reading demographic information - sex, adult versus child, and younger child versus adolescent - off a chest radiograph, for forensic identification and for finding the anatomic landmarks that encode age and sex
model_description: Interesting less for the forensic use case than for what the pediatric ablation reveals: separating boys from girls on a chest radiograph is essentially solved across all ages (AUC 1.0) but much harder within the pediatric subset alone (0.91), because the features the network uses are largely post-pubertal. Splitting children at 11 years works well (0.96), which suggests the radiograph carries a maturational signal. External validation on a Chinese population held up.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: AUC 1.0 for sex on the whole dataset and 0.91 on pediatric radiographs alone; 0.99 for under versus over 18 years and 0.96 for under 11 versus 11-18; externally 0.98 for sex and 0.91 for adult versus pediatric

title: Prenatal prediction and typing of placental invasion using MRI deep and radiomic features.
model_family: deep dynamic convolutional neural network (DDCNN) combined with radiomics and a multilayer perceptron classifier
patient_population: pregnant women undergoing abdominal MRI for suspected placental invasion
clinical_problem: predicting placental invasion (placenta accreta spectrum) and its invasion subtype prenatally
model_description: Takes abdominal MRI of the placenta, segmented with U-Net, as input and outputs a combined radiomic-and-deep-feature classification predicting placental invasion and its invasion subtype, using a deep dynamic CNN and multilayer perceptron classifier.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation study
headline_result: accuracy 0.877, sensitivity 0.857, specificity 0.954, AUC 0.904

title: An AI-based auxiliary empirical antibiotic therapy model for children with bacterial pneumonia using low-dose chest CT images.

model_description: Radiomics features extracted from low-dose chest CT images are used to build three machine-learning submodels (Gram-positive, Gram-negative, atypical) that are integrated into a support-vector-machine-based multi-class classifier predicting the causative bacterial class of pneumonia.
study_design: retrospective radiomics model development with internal train/test split
dataset_size: 389 children (122 Gram-positive, 159 Gram-negative, 108 atypical bacterial pneumonia)
headline_result: average AUC 0.75 (training), 0.73 (test); accuracy 0.58 (training), 0.54 (test)

title: Detecting lumbar lesions in 99m Tc-MDP SPECT by deep learning: Comparison with physicians.
patient_population: 65 lesion-absent pediatric SPECT studies with simulated inserted lesions; test set also reviewed by 5 physicians
clinical_problem: Detecting small lumbar stress lesions on 99mTc-MDP SPECT bone scans in pediatric patients with low back pain, compared with physician performance
model_description: A deep CNN trained on 2.5D views extracted from simulated lesion-present and lesion-absent 99mTc-MDP SPECT images is applied in a sliding-window fashion to generate a 3D heatmap of lesion probability at each lumbar location, compared against physician localization performance in an LROC study.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with cross-validation and a physician reader-comparison (LROC) study
dataset_size: 65 lesion-absent pediatric SPECT studies (artificial lesions inserted for evaluation)
headline_result: AUC-LROC 0.830 (deep learning) vs 0.785 (average of five physicians)

title: CT-Based Radiomics Signature With Machine Learning Predicts MYCN Amplification in Pediatric Abdominal Neuroblastoma.
model_family: radiomics with four classifiers compared, combined into a nomogram
patient_population: 172 children with abdominal neuroblastoma, 47 MYCN-amplified and 125 not
clinical_problem: identifying MYCN amplification in neuroblastoma, which defines the high-risk group and currently requires tissue
model_description: Extracts radiomic features from three-phase CT and predicts whether the tumor is MYCN-amplified, then folds the signature into a nomogram with clinicopathological and radiographic variables. If it held up prospectively it would let risk stratification start from the staging CT rather than waiting on genetics, which matters most where molecular testing is slow or unavailable.
headline_result: training AUC 0.940 for logistic and support vector machine models, 0.927 for random forest and 0.780 for Bayes

title: Machine learning-based quantitative analysis of barium enema and clinical features for early diagnosis of short-segment Hirschsprung disease in neonate.
model_family: support vector machine and L2-regularized logistic regression on colon-shape and clinical features
patient_population: neonates undergoing barium enema for abdominal symptoms: 54 with biopsy-confirmed short-segment Hirschsprung disease and 59 controls
clinical_problem: early diagnosis of short-segment Hirschsprung disease in neonates
model_description: Colon shape features are extracted from barium enema images and combined with clinical features to train SVM and logistic-regression classifiers that distinguish neonates with short-segment Hirschsprung disease from controls undergoing barium enema for abdominal symptoms. Model performance was compared with interpretation by two radiologists on the same cases.
study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison
dataset_size: 113 neonates (54 cases, 59 controls); 69 in training cohort, 44 in testing cohort
headline_result: best model achieved 86.36% accuracy, 81.82% sensitivity, 90.91% specificity, AUC 0.9132 (SVM) / 0.9318 (logistic regression); radiologists correctly classified 87 of 113 cases and could not decide on 20

title: Harmonized Segmentation of Neonatal Brain MRI.
model_family: deep learning (unsupervised domain adaptation segmentation network)
patient_population: preterm-born neonatal population (unseen target domain), count not stated
clinical_problem: Harmonizing automated brain tissue segmentation across preterm neonatal MRI acquired with different protocols/populations to enable consistent cortical measurement
model_description: Unsupervised domain adaptation techniques are applied to a deep learning tissue segmentation network to predict brain tissue maps on T2-weighted MRI of an unseen preterm neonatal cohort with different acquisition parameters than the training data, compared to a fully supervised baseline.

title: Estimating Gender and Age from Brain Structural MRI of Children and Adolescents: A 3D Convolutional Neural Network Multitask Learning Model.
patient_population: 894 healthy controls, 251 ASD, 357 ADHD (ABIDE-II and ADHD-200 public datasets)
clinical_problem: estimating age and gender from structural brain MRI in children and adolescents (including those with ASD/ADHD) to account for confounding variables in neurodevelopmental disorder assessment
model_description: A 3D CNN using voxel-based morphometry gray/white matter maps from structural brain MRI simultaneously estimates gender and age (a neurodevelopmental proxy) in children and adolescents with and without ASD/ADHD, with attention maps highlighting relevant brain regions.

headline_result: age mean absolute error 1.43 years (10-fold CV), 1.57 years (out-of-sample); gender AUC 0.85 (CV), 0.89 (out-of-sample)

title: Free-breathing Accelerated Cardiac MRI Using Deep Learning: Validation in Children and Young Adults.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, Non-P.H.S.
model_family: unrolled deep-learning reconstruction with separable 3D convolutions and data consistency steps
patient_population: 50 children and young adults aged 5-30 (mean 16 years) undergoing cardiac MRI at a children's hospital, prospectively scanned with both sequences
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: getting ventricular volumes and mass in children without repeated breath-holds
model_description: Reconstructs a 12-fold accelerated free-breathing cine cardiac MRI, so a child gets ventricular volumetry in about a minute of free breathing instead of three minutes of repeated breath-holds. The honest result is a trade: image quality scored slightly lower than the reference sequence, but the volumetric measurements two radiologists derived from it agreed closely, which is what the examination is actually for.
dataset_size: trained on 10 adult volunteers; prospectively validated in 50 children and young adults
headline_result: acquisition time 0.9 versus 3.0 minutes (P < .001); image quality 3.8 versus 4.3 on a five-point scale; intraclass correlation 0.76-0.97 for all measurements

title: Performance evaluation of a deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm in "double low" chest CTA in children: a feasibility study.
model_family: vendor deep learning CT reconstruction algorithm, high setting (DLIR-H)
patient_population: 46 children (mean age 5.9 +/- 4.2 years) scanned at 70 kVp with 0.8-1.2 ml/kg contrast, versus 46 age-matched controls at 100 kVp with 1.3-1.8 ml/kg
clinical_problem: cutting both radiation and iodinated contrast dose in pediatric chest CT angiography, where iterative reconstruction runs out of headroom at low dose and 100 kVp gives too little enhancement at low contrast dose
model_description: The clearest pediatric statement of what deep learning reconstruction actually buys: it is spent on lowering two doses at once. Dropping to 70 kVp raises vascular enhancement but also noise, and DLIR absorbs the noise, so the child receives 11 percent less radiation and 24 percent less contrast and the images come out quieter and better enhanced than the standard protocol. A vendor algorithm evaluated in clinical practice rather than a research model.
release_evidence: a vendor deep learning image reconstruction algorithm running on the clinical CT scanner, evaluated against the scanner's adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V
study_design: prospective feasibility study with two-reader qualitative scoring
dataset_size: 46 children in the study group and 46 age-matched controls
headline_result: dose-length-product down 11.2% (p = 0.01) and contrast dose down 24% (p < 0.001), with higher aortic enhancement (416.5 vs 342.0 HU) and lower noise (15.1 vs 18.6 HU), both p < 0.001

title: Automatic Segmentation of Diffuse White Matter Abnormality on T2-weighted Brain MR Images Using Deep Learning in Very Preterm Infants.

title: Analysis of maturation features in fetal brain ultrasound via artificial intelligence for the estimation of gestational age.
journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
venue_label: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: automated analysis of fetal brain morphology on the standard transthalamic axial plane

title: Deep learning-based parameter estimation in fetal diffusion-weighted MRI.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

title: A multi-modal MRI analysis of brain structure and function in relation to OXT methylation in maltreated children and adolescents.

clinical_problem: Predict outcome (Glasgow Outcome Scale, mortality, length of stay, need for surgery) in pediatric traumatic brain injury using automated CT densitometric analysis

title: Automatic measurement of fetal femur length in ultrasound images: a comparison of random forest regression model and SegNet.

clinical_problem: automated measurement of fetal femur length on ultrasound

title: Graph auto-encoding brain networks with applications to analyzing large-scale brain imaging datasets.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

patient_population: children/adolescents from the ABCD study and adults from the Human Connectome Project
clinical_problem: modeling brain structural connectome variation and its relationship to cognition

Applied to the ABCD study and the Human Connectome Project, it characterizes the population distribution of brain networks and relates the learned representations to cognitive traits, outperforming prior topological-feature and PCA-based approaches.

dataset_size: not stated precisely (ABCD and Human Connectome Project cohorts)

title: Validation of Deep Learning-based Augmentation for Reduced 18F-FDG Dose for PET/MRI in Children and Young Adults with Lymphoma.
patient_population: 20 patients with lymphoma (mean age 16.4 years)

clinical_problem: Enabling reduced-dose FDG PET/MRI in children and young adults with lymphoma using deep learning image augmentation while preserving accurate treatment response assessment.
