title: Improving Automatic Renal Segmentation in Clinically Normal and Abnormal Paediatric DCE-MRI via Contrast Maximisation and Convolutional Networks for Computing Markers of Kidney Function.
model_family: CNN (residual CNN localization + boundary-preserving fully convolutional dense nets)
patient_population: 60 4D DCE-MRI volumes from pediatric patients with varying conditions affecting kidney function
clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting the kidney and its cortex/medulla compartments from pediatric dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI to compute markers of kidney function such as glomerular filtration rate
model_description: A dual-stage deep-learning framework first localizes and segments each kidney using residual convolutional neural networks with spatial-temporal, boundary-preserving fully convolutional dense nets, then further segments the cortex and medulla to compute quantitative kidney-function markers from 4D DCE-MRI.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal evaluation on a pediatric DCE-MRI dataset
headline_result: 3.8% higher mean Dice similarity coefficient than a state-of-the-art comparison method (GrabCut + SVM)

title: Accurate Instance Segmentation in Pediatric Elbow Radiographs.

clinical_problem: automatically segment individual bones on pediatric elbow radiographs as an upstream task for automated fracture interpretation

study_design: retrospective methods development study on self-constructed dataset

title: Generative Adversarial Networks to Improve Fetal Brain Fine-Grained Plane Classification.
model_family: StyleGAN2-ADA generating synthetic fetal brain ultrasound images for data augmentation
patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound plane images
clinical_problem: fine-grained classification of fetal brain ultrasound planes, where the classes differ subtly and labelled data is limited

The evaluation is the right one: not whether the synthetic images look convincing, but whether adding them improves a downstream classifier, which they did, and best in combination with classical augmentation rather than instead of it.
headline_result: combining GAN-generated and classically augmented data increased both accuracy and area under the curve over baseline classifiers

title: Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Fetal Echocardiography: Application to Heart Standard View Segmentation for Congenital Heart Defects Detection.

clinical_problem: detecting congenital heart defects on fetal echocardiography via standard cardiac view segmentation

headline_result: standard view segmentation: 79.97% intersection-over-union, 89.70% Dice; CHD detection mean average precision 98.30% (intra-patient) and 82.42% (inter-patient)

title: Multimodal Ensemble Deep Learning to Predict Disruptive Behavior Disorders in Children.
patient_population: 1,100 children (419 female, 681 male), aged 108-131 months, Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study; 550 with DBD, 550 typically developing
clinical_problem: distinguishing children with disruptive behavior disorders from typically developing children using multimodal brain MRI
model_description: Input: diffusion, structural, and resting-state functional MRI; output: classification of disruptive behavior disorder vs. typically developing, using a multimodal ensemble 3D CNN with attention-based region identification.
study_design: retrospective case-control classification study using a multi-site cohort (ABCD Study)

headline_result: 90.24% classification accuracy, >5% improvement over classical contrastive learning baseline

title: Application of deep learning upon spinal radiographs to predict progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis at first clinic visit.
model_family: self-attentive capsule network with two-stage transfer learning, on a region of interest centered at the curve apex
patient_population: skeletally immature patients (Risser <= 2) with 11-30 degree curves presenting between October 2015 and April 2020: 328 for training and cross-validation, 110 for independent testing on biplanar EOS, plus 52 on standard PA radiographs for cross-platform validation
clinical_problem: telling at the first clinic visit which mild adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curves will progress, the prediction that decides who is braced and who is watched
model_description: Prior work showed three-dimensional morphology predicts progression but needed biplanar equipment and slow software reconstruction; this puts the same prediction on the plain standing PA radiograph every clinic already takes. The 3D reconstruction is used only to establish which parameters matter - apical rotation and torsion - and then discarded from the deployed pathway. The separate 52-patient cross-platform cohort on standard radiographs is the part that makes it portable beyond an EOS centre.
study_design: retrospective cohort model development with cross-platform validation
headline_result: accuracy 76.6%, sensitivity 75.2%, specificity 80.2% for progressive versus non-progressive curves, outperforming conventional CNNs and a clinical parameter logistic regression

title: Assessing the utility of low resolution brain imaging: treatment of infant hydrocephalus.
publication_types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: deep learning image enhancement (post hoc analysis within an RCT)
patient_population: Infants with post-infectious hydrocephalus, imaged as part of an ongoing randomized clinical trial, in low- to middle-income country settings
clinical_problem: Can deep learning enhance lower-quality (low-field or low-resolution) brain imaging enough to still guide hydrocephalus treatment planning in resource-limited settings, and is enhanced imaging safe to rely on?
model_description: CT images were artificially degraded in resolution, noise and contrast, then a deep learning algorithm enhanced the degraded images; three pediatric neurosurgeons rated the clinical usefulness of degraded, enhanced, and ground-truth images for hydrocephalus treatment planning.
study_design: post hoc analysis nested within a randomized controlled trial, with reader assessment
headline_result: Deep learning enhancement increased contrast-to-noise ratio but introduced structural errors that risked misleading clinical interpretation; lower-quality unenhanced images were sometimes judged preferable to enhanced ones

title: Individual prediction of trauma-focused psychotherapy response in youth with posttraumatic stress disorder using resting-state functional connectivity.

model_description: A cross-validated multivariate support vector machine classifier uses resting-state fMRI functional connectivity, based on independent-component-derived brain networks, to predict individual-level response to trauma-focused psychotherapy in youth with PTSD.
headline_result: Individual-level prediction accuracy 76% (pFWE=0.02), 87% sensitivity, 65% specificity, AUC 0.82, using a superior temporal gyrus-centered network

title: Extended Invariant Information Clustering Is Effective for Leave-One-Site-Out Cross-Validation in Resting State Functional Connectivity Modeling.

headline_result: Classification accuracy >0.8 at sites with the highest mean subject age using EIIC

title: Segmentation of Tricuspid Valve Leaflets From Transthoracic 3D Echocardiograms of Children With Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome Using Deep Learning.

release_evidence: "We are now working to deploy this network for public use" (not yet released at time of publication)
dataset_size: 133 training and 28 validation 3D echocardiogram image-segmentation pairs
headline_result: median Dice similarity coefficient 0.86 for merged tricuspid valve segmentation, mean boundary distance 0.35 mm

title: The Role of Diffusion Tensor MR Imaging (DTI) of the Brain in Diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder: Promising Results.

model_description: Input: diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) white-matter connectivity features; output: classification of ASD vs. typically developing individuals, via a machine learning framework with feature engineering
study_design: retrospective analysis of a public multi-site dataset
headline_result: balanced accuracy up to 99% (5-fold cross-validation)

title: Novel loss functions for ensemble-based medical image classification.

clinical_problem: Can improved loss functions for deep learning multi-class classifiers more reliably distinguish normal chest x-rays from bacterial and viral pneumonia in children, given that abnormalities are often imbalanced across classes?
model_description: Multiple state-of-the-art and newly proposed loss functions are benchmarked for training deep neural network classifiers on a pediatric chest x-ray dataset (normal vs. bacterial vs. viral pneumonia), with prediction-level and model-level ensembling and localization studies to interpret model behavior.
study_design: retrospective benchmarking and ensemble-model development study
headline_result: Weighted-averaging top-3/top-5 model-level ensembles achieved MCC 0.9068 (95% CI 0.8839-0.9297), significantly better than individual models and prior literature (p<0.05)

title: Radiomic signatures based on multiparametric MR images for predicting Ki-67 index expression in medulloblastoma.
model_family: radiomics + machine learning ensemble (random forest, SVM)

headline_result: best model: accuracy 0.771, AUC 0.697 (test set)

title: Artificial Intelligence to Automatically Assess Scan Quality in Hip Ultrasound.
patient_population: Infants screened for developmental dysplasia of the hip
clinical_problem: Can AI automatically assess whether a hip ultrasound image is of adequate quality to accurately diagnose developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), since poor scan quality can lead to misdiagnosis?
model_description: Separate CNN models detect the presence of each of four standard ultrasound landmarks (iliac wing, labrum, os ischium, femoral head) in a hip ultrasound image, to automatically classify scan quality as adequate or inadequate.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and validation against non-expert and expert readers
dataset_size: 100 3D ultrasound images for training, 107 for validation
headline_result: Accuracy >=85% for all four landmarks (ilium 0.89, labrum 0.94, os ischium 0.85, femoral head 0.98) as a binary adequate/inadequate classifier

title: Effectiveness of Learning Systems from Common Image File Types to Detect Osteosarcoma Based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) Models.
patient_population: Osteosarcoma patients from Lerdsin Hospital (exact ages not stated)
clinical_problem: Early detection of osteosarcoma, a bone cancer more common in children than adults, and its lung metastases from CT-derived images
model_description: CT images converted to common file formats (BMP/JPG/PNG) are classified as osteosarcoma-positive or -negative by three pretrained CNNs (VGG-16, ResNet-50, MobileNet-V2)
headline_result: VGG-16 was the most robust model across image formats; PNG was the preferred format (exact accuracy/F1 not given in abstract)

title: Standard Echocardiographic View Recognition in Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Defects in Children Using Deep Learning Based on Knowledge Distillation.
patient_population: 3,772 subjects, 367,571 echocardiographic image slices
clinical_problem: Can standard echocardiographic views be automatically recognized in children, a prerequisite step for automated diagnosis of congenital heart defects?
model_description: A deep learning neural network using knowledge distillation automatically identifies 23 standard echocardiographic views commonly used to diagnose congenital heart defects in children.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and internal testing
headline_result: F1 scores >=0.90 for a majority of the 23 standard views

title: Report of clinical bone age assessment using deep learning for an Asian population in Taiwan.
patient_population: 8,061 hand radiographs, ages 0-18 years
clinical_problem: Automatically assessing bone age from pediatric left-hand radiographs in a Taiwanese (Asian) population using deep learning
model_description: Input: posterior view left-hand X-ray plus age, gender, weight; output: estimated bone age in months, via an Inception ResNet V2-based deep neural network
headline_result: accuracy within 1 year: 95.3%; MAE 0.33y (male), 0.25y (female)

title: A Deep-Learning Aided Diagnostic System in Assessing Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip on Pediatric Pelvic Radiographs.
model_family: three-stage pipeline: Mask R-CNN pelvic bone segmentation, HRNet landmark localization, then measurement and classification
patient_population: 1265 pediatric pelvic radiographs for training and 133 from two other medical institutions for validation, with three orthopedic surgeons as comparators
clinical_problem: measuring and classifying developmental dysplasia of the hip on pediatric pelvic radiographs, where the acetabular index and centre-edge angle are drawn by hand and observers disagree
model_description: The decomposition matches how the measurement is actually made - find the ilium, pubis, ischium and femoral heads, then place the landmarks, then compute the angles - which makes each stage checkable. The result that matters clinically is not accuracy but variance: intraclass consistency across surgeons was 0.79-0.98 while the model's was 1.00, because a deterministic model measuring the same film twice cannot disagree with itself. It also matched an intermediate surgeon on Tonnis and IHDI grading, in less time.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation and observer comparison
headline_result: Tonnis and IHDI classification accuracy 0.86-0.95 for both hips; no statistically significant difference from surgeons on the numeric indices; intraclass consistency 1.00 for the model versus 0.79-0.98 among surgeons, and significantly faster

title: Harmonized neonatal brain MR image segmentation model for cross-site datasets.

clinical_problem: segmenting white matter, gray matter and CSF on neonatal brain MRI acquired at different sites/scanners
model_description: A CycleGAN harmonizes cross-site/cross-scanner neonatal brain MR images into the training-image domain (also reducing motion artifacts), after which a densely-connected U-Net segments white matter, gray matter and CSF.
headline_result: Better segmentation performance than existing methods on cross-site data and a grand-challenge dataset (no single metric reported in abstract)

title: Using Machine Learning Methods Incorporating Individual Reader Annotations to Classify Paediatric Chest Radiographs in Epidemiological Studies.

clinical_problem: Standardizing interpretation of pediatric chest radiographs across epidemiological pneumonia studies to reduce inter/intra-reader variability, per WHO classification

study_design: Retrospective multi-country model development and evaluation study
headline_result: Multi-class accuracy 61% (with individual reader annotations) vs 59% (aggregate only); country accuracy range 45-71%

title: Clinical application of artificial intelligence bone age measurement system based on deep learning
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
venue_label: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
model_family: deep learning (TW3-C-RUS based bone age assessment system)
patient_population: 80 children aged 5-12 years, hand-wrist radiographs
clinical_problem: bone age assessment to assist junior pediatric radiologists
model_description: A deep-learning bone-age assessment (BAA) system evaluates metacarpal and phalangeal maturity on hand-wrist radiographs using the TW3-C-RUS standard. It was compared against a junior pediatric radiologist reading alone and the same radiologist assisted by the system, referenced against a senior radiologist's assessment aided by BAA. With BAA assistance, the junior radiologist's error and reading time both improved.
headline_result: System RMSE 0.62 years, MAE 0.47 years; with BAA assistance junior radiologist RMSE improved from 0.71 to 0.27 years and MAE from 0.90 to 0.38 years; mean reading time shortened from 4 min 40 s to 2 min 15 s

title: 3D-MASNet: 3D Mixed-scale Asymmetric Convolutional Segmentation Network for 6-month-old Infant Brain MR Images
model_family: 3D mixed-scale asymmetric convolutional segmentation network, applied to five canonical CNN backbones
patient_population: 23 six-month-old infants (iSeg-2019 dataset), T1- and T2-weighted brain MRI
clinical_problem: infant brain tissue segmentation (gray matter, white matter, cerebrospinal fluid) for study of early brain development

Applied to T1- and T2-weighted MRI from 23 six-month-old infants, it segments the brain into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, improving five existing CNN segmentation models and ranking first among 30 teams on the iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set.
release_evidence: preprint (bioRxiv); no repository or product mentioned
headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.931 (GM), 0.912 (WM), 0.961 (CSF); ranked first among 30 teams on iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set

title: A comparison of machine learning classifiers for pediatric epilepsy using resting-state functional MRI latency data
model_family: XGBoost, SVM, and Random Forest classifiers
patient_population: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls; preoperative resting-state functional MRI
clinical_problem: detection of epilepsy from brain imaging
model_description: The model uses features derived from resting-state functional MRI hemodynamic 'latency' maps (via principal component analysis of latency z-scores across 36 brain seed regions) as inputs to machine-learning classifiers (XGBoost, SVM, Random Forest) to distinguish patients with epilepsy from healthy controls. It was trained and tested on preoperative rs-fMRI from 63 epilepsy patients and 259 controls, intended as an adjunctive diagnostic tool for pediatric epilepsy.
dataset_size: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls
headline_result: Best model (XGBoost) test AUC 0.79, accuracy 74%, specificity 73%, sensitivity 77%

title: Deep learning algorithm performance compared to experts in visual evaluation of interior vena cava collapse on ultrasound to determine intravenous fluid need in dehydration management
model_family: VGG-16-based deep learning architecture combined with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network
patient_population: pediatric patients presenting to a pediatric emergency department with dehydration (184 IVC ultrasound videos)
clinical_problem: assessing inferior vena cava collapse to guide intravenous fluid resuscitation in dehydrated children
model_description: A VGG-16-based deep learning model, run inside a Long Short-Term Memory architecture, analyzes real-time point-of-care ultrasound video of the inferior vena cava to classify complete versus incomplete IVC collapse in children being evaluated for intravenous fluid resuscitation. Trained and tested on 184 previously acquired, de-identified pediatric emergency department ultrasound videos (166 for training/validation, 18 held out for testing), and compared against two blinded point-of-care ultrasound experts.
dataset_size: 184 patient IVC ultrasound videos (166 training/validation, 18 held-out test)
headline_result: Substantial agreement with the PEM POCUS attending (Cohen's kappa 0.78, 95% CI 0.49-1.0) and with the PEM resident (kappa 0.66, 95% CI 0.31-1.0) on held-out test videos

title: Comparison of three methods of assessing the bone age in tibetan children and the features of their skeletal maturity

model_description: Ensemble machine learning methods (voting and stacking) combine 26 empirical fetal weight estimation formulas and statistical models based on prenatal ultrasound measurements to improve prediction of macrosomia and large-for-gestational-age infants.
study_design: retrospective cohort study using ensemble learning methods

title: Towards a new 3D classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: fuzzy c-means clustering over ten 3D parameters measured on biplanar radiograph reconstructions
patient_population: patients from a multicenter adolescent idiopathic scoliosis database, all with biplanar radiographs and 3D reconstruction of the entire spine; cluster sizes 11 to 290
clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis in three dimensions, since the classifications surgeons plan from are two-dimensional and do not describe the deformity they are actually operating on
model_description: Unsupervised, and deliberately so - the point is to let the data propose subgroups rather than test an existing scheme. Eleven clusters emerged from ten 3D parameters, and the validation step is the one that matters for a taxonomy: four experienced spine surgeons from the SRS 3D Scoliosis Committee reviewed representative cases and unanimously agreed each cluster was a group current classifications do not name. Whether these subgroups predict surgical outcome is the unanswered question.
headline_result: eleven statistically distinct 3D subgroups, all judged by four spine surgeons to be undefined in current classifications

title: Distinguishing between paediatric brain tumour types using multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning: A multi-site study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: machine learning classifiers on combined diffusion and perfusion features
patient_population: children with brain tumours imaged at multiple centres
clinical_problem: non-invasive diagnosis of the three common childhood brain tumour types, which is a genuine radiological challenge
model_description: Most quantitative work in this area is single-centre and single-modality; this combines diffusion and perfusion imaging across sites. It also takes features from the whole brain as well as the tumour, and finds both contribute, which is a useful observation for a field that segments the lesion and discards everything else.
dataset_size: a multi-centre paediatric brain tumour cohort
headline_result: combining diffusion and perfusion features from tumour and whole brain gave the optimal classifier at over 80% predictive precision

title: Using Deep Learning Algorithms to Grade Hydronephrosis Severity: Toward a Clinical Adjunct.
patient_population: 673 patients aged 0 to 116 months (mean 16.5 months) with 2,420 sagittal renal ultrasound images across all five Society for Fetal Urology grades
clinical_problem: grading hydronephrosis severity on renal ultrasound, currently a subjective five-point judgment
model_description: Assigns a Society for Fetal Urology grade to a renal ultrasound image. The reported numbers are refreshingly candid: it places 94% of images correctly or within one grade, but only 51% exactly right on the five-way task, and the clinically decisive distinctions (low versus high grade, and grade II versus III) reach 78% and 71%. The authors frame it as a decision and teaching aid rather than a grader.
headline_result: 94% of images correct or within one grade on the five-way task (51% exactly correct); 78% accuracy for low versus high grade and 71% for grade II versus III

title: Hierarchical Class Incremental Learning of Anatomical Structures in Fetal Echocardiography Videos.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
venue_label: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: fetal echocardiography video dataset annotated by sonographers
clinical_problem: automated identification of anatomical structures in fetal echocardiography videos, with the ability to add new anatomical classes over time without retraining from scratch
model_description: Input: fetal echocardiography ultrasound video frames; output: classification of anatomical structures/views, using an incremental learning hierarchical network that can add new anatomy classes without forgetting prior ones.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation
headline_result: reduced accuracy depreciation over old tasks from 6.75% to 1.10% (balanced) and 6.95% to 1.89% (imbalanced) with incremental learning

title: Ultrasound-Based Phenotyping of Lateral Ventricles to Predict Hydrocephalus Outcome in Premature Neonates.

headline_result: Segmentation Dice 0.86; outcome prediction accuracy 0.91

title: Probabilistic Learning Coherent Point Drift for 3D Ultrasound Fetal Head Registration.

model_family: random forest classification + Gaussian mixture model (probabilistic point-cloud registration)

title: Neural representations of transitive relations predict current and future math calculation skills in children.

model_description: Takes fMRI activity patterns during a transitive-relations task (intraparietal sulcus) as input to a machine learning model with cross-validation, predicting math calculation skill scores at baseline and 1.5 years later.
headline_result: IPS activity significantly predicted math calculation skills at both T1 and T2 (exact statistic not given)

title: Transdiagnostic Brain Mapping in Developmental Disorders.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: machine learning clustering (unsupervised) on cognitive and cortical morphology data; network-attack simulation on DWI connectome
patient_population: 479 children (299 boys) aged 62-223 months (about 5-18 years), 337 referred for learning-related cognitive problems
clinical_problem: relating brain network organization to childhood learning difficulties and developmental disorders
model_description: Cognitive test scores and cortical morphology/diffusion-weighted connectome data go in; machine learning identifies distinct cognitive and brain profiles and simulates network resilience to loss of connectome hubs.
study_design: cross-sectional cohort study with machine-learning clustering and connectome simulation
headline_result: distinct cognitive/brain profiles significantly associated with children's learning ability and cognitive impairment (hold-out cross-validation)

title: Estimating individual scores of inattention and impulsivity based on dynamic features of intrinsic connectivity network.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 95 children with ADHD and 105 healthy controls from the ADHD-200 database
clinical_problem: estimating inattention and impulsivity severity scores in ADHD from resting-state fMRI dynamic connectivity
model_description: Dynamic features of intrinsic connectivity networks from resting-state fMRI, together with head-motion and other measures, are input to support vector regression models. The models estimate individual clinical scores of inattention and impulsivity in children with and without ADHD, with the sensorimotor network most associated with inattention and the executive control network with impulsivity.
dataset_size: 95 children with ADHD, 105 healthy controls (ADHD-200 database)
headline_result: Estimated scores correlated significantly with inattention (r = 0.4 ± 0.02, p < 0.01) and impulsivity (r = 0.31 ± 0.02, p < 0.01)

title: Novel Deep Learning Network Analysis of Electrical Stimulation Mapping-Driven Diffusion MRI Tractography to Improve Preoperative Evaluation of Pediatric Epilepsy.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: deep convolutional neural network classifying diffusion MRI streamline trajectories, trained against electrical stimulation mapping findings
patient_population: 89 children with focal epilepsy, with electrical stimulation mapping as the reference
clinical_problem: identifying eloquent white matter before epilepsy surgery in children, so that resection margins spare motor, language and vision
model_description: The clinical validation goes well past accuracy. Three things are tested: whether the predicted pathways sit within the 1 cm spatial resolution of electrical stimulation mapping, whether respecting the predicted margins forecasts an absence of postoperative deficit (92% accurate), and whether the volume of language pathway actually removed tracks the postoperative change in language ability (R = 0.7). That last result is the one that turns a tract classifier into surgical evidence - it says the deficit follows the white matter you took, not only the cortex.
study_design: retrospective model development with surgical outcome correlation
headline_result: 98% tract classification accuracy; preserved margins predicted absence of postoperative deficit with 92% accuracy; change in language pathway volume correlated with change in language ability (R = 0.7, p < 0.001)

title: Automatic Spine Ultrasound Segmentation for Scoliosis Visualization and Measurement.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

patient_population: trained on eight healthy adult volunteers and tested on eight pediatric patients
clinical_problem: measuring scoliosis without radiographs, which children with scoliosis undergo repeatedly through growth
model_description: Segments the spine on tracked ultrasound and reconstructs a 3D volume from which the scoliosis angle is measured, offering a radiation-free substitute for the serial radiographs that scoliosis follow-up requires. The paper is honest about the adult-to-pediatric transfer: fuzzy segmentation metrics dropped when the network trained on adults was applied to children, and thresholds had to be re-optimized. Measurement error against radiography was nonetheless within 2.2 degrees.
dataset_size: eight adult volunteers for training, eight pediatric patients for testing
headline_result: maximum error 2.2 degrees against radiographic scoliosis measurement, with each measurement taking under one minute; segmentation metrics fell when translating from adults to children

title: Fully Automated Bone Age Assessment on Large-Scale Hand X-Ray Dataset.

patient_population: RSNA pediatric hand radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: automated bone age assessment for skeletal maturity in children
model_description: Takes a hand x-ray as input and outputs a predicted bone age, using a U-Net (trained via deep active learning) to segment the hand, pretrained CNNs to extract features via transfer learning, and ensemble regression models to predict age.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development on a public dataset
headline_result: mean discrepancy between predicted and actual bone age of 6.96 months (male) and 7.35 months (female); segmentation Dice score 0.95

title: PRIMAGE project: predictive in silico multiscale analytics to support childhood cancer personalised evaluation empowered by imaging biomarkers.
publication_types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: machine learning and multiscale tumour growth simulation on an open cloud platform
patient_population: children with neuroblastoma or diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma across 16 European partner institutions
clinical_problem: phenotyping, treatment allocation and prognosis in neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
model_description: Less a model than an attempt at the infrastructure pediatric AI lacks: a four-year European consortium with two imaging biobanks and three paediatric oncology units, building a cloud decision-support platform on pooled anonymised imaging, clinical, molecular and genetic data for two rare childhood cancers, with external validation at independent centres and results promised to the community. The choice of two rare tumors is deliberate, since these are exactly the diseases no single centre can study alone.
release_evidence: an open cloud-based platform, with final results promised to the scientific community
study_design: multicentre observational in silico study protocol
dataset_size: multi-institutional European cohorts for two tumour types

title: Diagnostic performance of convolutional neural network-based Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age assessment system.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
venue_label: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
model_family: convolutional neural network scoring the 13 RUS and 7 carpal bones of the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 system
patient_population: 9059 clinical left hand radiographs from PACS between January 2012 and December 2016, split 8005 training / 804 validation / 250 test; the test set was also read by four endocrinologists and two radiologists
clinical_problem: bone age assessment by the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method, which is more granular than Greulich and Pyle but requires staging twenty individual bones and is correspondingly slow and variable
model_description: Automates the scoring system endocrinologists prefer but rarely use because of its cost in time, and reports agreement bone by bone rather than only in aggregate - which localizes where humans disagree with each other (capitate, hamate, middle and distal phalanges) and where they do not. Six expert readers as the comparator. One and a half seconds per image against many minutes by hand.
study_design: retrospective model development with multi-reader comparison
headline_result: root mean square 0.50 years against the reviewers' consensus, with accuracy better than the individual reviewers' estimates and image processing in 1.5 +/- 0.2 s

title: Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Neonatal Brain Image Segmentation.
model_family: single-modality and dual-modality 3D convolutional networks retrained for neonatal data
patient_population: 24 pairs of neonatal T1 and T2 data from the Developing Human Connectome Project for retraining, with eight pairs for validation and eight for testing
clinical_problem: segmenting gray matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid in the term-equivalent neonatal brain, where the tissue contrast is inverted relative to the older infant brain that existing networks were tuned on
model_description: Takes two networks that won on 6-month infant data and asks whether they transfer to newborns, where the contrast is inverted - a concrete test of how narrow pediatric segmentation models are. Dual-modality HyperDense-Net won, and the ablation is practically useful: single-modality LiviaNET did better on T2 than T1 across every tissue type, which tells a site with only one sequence which to acquire. Training and inference times are reported, which papers rarely do and departments need. The models are being made available through the Canadian Neonatal Brain Platform.
release_evidence: the networks will be continuously retrained and made available through the Canadian Neonatal Brain Platform
dataset_size: 40 neonatal T1/T2 pairs from the dHCP public dataset
headline_result: dual-modality HyperDense-Net reached Dice 0.94/0.95/0.92 for the three tissue types versus 0.90/0.90/0.88 for single-modality LiviaNET on T2

title: Artificial intelligence system can achieve comparable results to experts for bone age assessment of Chinese children with abnormal growth and development.
model_family: fully automated artificial intelligence system based on the Greulich and Pyle method, developed on Chinese children
patient_population: developed on 8000 bone age radiographs from five medical centres across China, then tested on 745 consecutive children (360 boys, 385 girls) with abnormal growth and development from another tertiary centre in north China between January and October 2018
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in the children it actually gets ordered for - those with abnormal growth and development - rather than in the developmentally normal children most systems are validated on
model_description: The test set is what makes this worth recording: consecutive children with abnormal growth and development, which is the referral population, evaluated at a centre separate from the five that supplied training data. Accuracy within one year was 84.6% overall, and the paper names exactly where it broke down - short stature with bone deformity, severe osteomalacia, and hands where carpals and phalanges mature at different rates. Those are precisely the children a bone age is ordered for.
dataset_size: 8000 development radiographs from five centres; 745 test cases from a sixth
headline_result: 84.60% accuracy within 1 year against a two-expert consensus reference (89.45% in the 12-18 year group), RMSE 0.76 years, mean absolute difference 0.58 years

title: Predicting motor outcome in preterm infants from very early brain diffusion MRI using a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) model.
publication_types: Clinical Trial; Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

patient_population: 77 infants born under 31 weeks gestation, imaged at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age with motor outcome at 2 years corrected age
clinical_problem: identifying preterm infants headed for neuromotor delay early enough to refer them for intervention
model_description: Predicts abnormal motor outcome at two years from diffusion MRI acquired before term, which is earlier than most preterm prediction work and therefore closer to when intervention could start. Classification is done on image patches and aggregated with a tuned threshold, and heat maps show which brain locations drove the abnormal predictions. Accuracy is moderate and the confidence intervals are wide on 77 infants.
dataset_size: 77 very preterm infants (48 normal, 29 abnormal outcome)
headline_result: sensitivity 70%, specificity 74%, AUC 0.72 for abnormal motor outcome at 2 years from MRI acquired at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age

title: Neonatal Brain Microstructure and Machine-Learning-Based Prediction of Early Language Development in Children Born Very Preterm.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, Non-P.H.S.
model_family: multivariate logistic models with leave-one-out cross-validation and exhaustive feature selection over diffusion tensor metrics

clinical_problem: identifying which very-low-birth-weight preterm infants are heading for language delay, early enough to intervene while neuroplasticity is greatest
model_description: Near-term diffusion imaging used as a prognostic instrument rather than a descriptive one. Exhaustive feature selection narrows to three brain regions, which keeps the model small enough to interpret and to replicate. Separate models for composite, expressive and receptive language, with the strongest performance on expressive and receptive - and a side finding that cerebellar asymmetry tracked lower receptive scores. Nearly a third of the cohort scored below 85, so the outcome is common enough for the prediction to matter.
headline_result: sensitivity and specificity of 89%/86% for composite, 100%/90% for expressive and 100%/90% for receptive language risk

title: Deep Q-CapsNet Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intrauterine Cavity Segmentation in TTTS Fetal Surgery Planning.

clinical_problem: Segment the intrauterine cavity from fetal MRI to plan fetoscopic laser surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome
model_description: Takes axial, sagittal, and coronal fetal MRI stacks as input; a reinforcement-learning-based capsule network (with nnU-Net feature extraction) detects and segments the intrauterine cavity/womb for surgical planning.
study_design: retrospective segmentation model development, compared with 15 state-of-the-art networks
headline_result: Average Dice score above 0.91 across all ablations

title: Deep Learning Measurement of Leg Length Discrepancy in Children Based on Radiographs.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: segmentation network followed by geometric calculation
patient_population: 179 children aged 5-19 (mean 12 years) imaged for leg length discrepancy
clinical_problem: measuring leg length discrepancy, a task the paper describes as time consuming but cognitively simple
model_description: Segments the femurs and tibias on a full-length radiograph and computes each bone's length and the discrepancy between sides. The case it makes is not diagnostic accuracy but time: agreement with the radiology report was essentially perfect and the measurement took one second against 96 seconds by hand. This is the shape of the pediatric AI application most likely to pay for itself, an exact, repetitive measurement rather than a judgment call.
headline_result: correlation 0.99 with radiologist measurements (mean absolute error 0.45 cm for individual bones, 0.51 cm for discrepancy); 1 second versus 96 seconds per study

title: Ependymoma and pilocytic astrocytoma: Differentiation using radiomics approach based on machine learning.

clinical_problem: telling ependymoma from pilocytic astrocytoma before surgery, two posterior fossa tumors with different management that overlap on conventional MRI
model_description: A conventional radiomics pipeline whose most useful output is the feature ablation: Gabor, texture and wavelet features were compared head to head, and texture features alone matched the full 300-feature set. Small and slice-level rather than patient-level, so the headline accuracy should be read as a feasibility signal rather than a performance estimate.
headline_result: accuracy 0.878, sensitivity 0.929, specificity 0.800, AUC 0.865 on the selected feature set, with no significant loss versus the full feature set

title: A convolutional neural network to detect scoliosis treatment in radiographs.

headline_result: 98.3% of radiographs correctly classified (2.0% unclassified); 99.7% of brace radiographs correctly detected

study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
dataset_size: small quality-annotated training set (exact n not stated)
headline_result: Near-perfect accuracy with real-time (millisecond-per-volume) quality assessment

title: Automated abnormality classification of chest radiographs using deep convolutional neural networks.
model_family: deep CNN, pretrained on natural images and on adult radiographs
patient_population: adult cohorts for pretraining, then fine-tuned on pediatric patients for the pneumonia task
clinical_problem: flagging abnormal chest radiographs for worklist triage, and pneumonia in children specifically
model_description: Sorts frontal chest radiographs into normal and abnormal so that abnormal studies can be pushed up the worklist. The pediatric relevance is in the transfer step: a model pretrained on adult cohorts and fine-tuned on children reached higher performance for pneumonia than either alone, which is the practical recipe for a children's hospital with a smaller archive.
dataset_size: about 8,500 images for the pretraining benefit analysis; cohort sizes not stated
headline_result: AUC 0.982 for normal versus abnormal, 0.944 on an external dataset, and 0.985 for normal versus pneumonia after fine-tuning on children

title: Multi-instance Deep Learning of Ultrasound Imaging Data for Pattern Classification of Congenital Abnormalities of the Kidney and Urinary Tract in Children.
model_family: multi-instance deep learning with mean pooling across multiple images per patient in both sagittal and transverse views
patient_population: 86 children with posterior urethral valves and 71 with mild unilateral hydronephrosis, 3504 sagittal and 2558 transverse images from routine clinical care
clinical_problem: distinguishing posterior urethral valves - which need urgent intervention - from mild unilateral hydronephrosis in children, from the routine ultrasound
model_description: Multi-instance learning is the right match for how renal ultrasound is actually acquired - many images per child, no single one definitive - and the paper quantifies exactly what that buys: pooling lifted the AUC from about 0.80 on single images to 0.96. Combining both planes added a little more. Class activation mapping showed the network attending to anatomically meaningful parts of the kidney, and sensitivity (0.873) trails specificity (0.986), which is the wrong way round for a condition where a miss means renal damage.
headline_result: AUC 0.961 +/- 0.026 combining views with mean pooling, versus 0.796 and 0.815 for single sagittal and transverse images; specificity 0.986 and sensitivity 0.873

title: Computer-aided diagnosis for fetal brain ultrasound images using deep convolutional neural networks.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
venue_label: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
model_family: deep convolutional networks: segmentation of the craniocerebral region, then four-class classification, then class activation mapping for localization
patient_population: real-world clinical fetal brain ultrasound images at the transventricular and transcerebellar standard planes
clinical_problem: prenatal detection of five common fetal brain abnormalities on standard neurosonographic planes, where missed malformations change counseling and management
model_description: A three-stage design that gets weakly-supervised localization for free: the classifier is trained only on image-level labels, and lesions are then localized by class activation mapping rather than by any drawn box. That keeps the annotation burden low, and the numbers show the cost - classification is strong while localization overlap is modest. Positioned as support for junior operators, whose false negatives on fetal brain anomalies are the stated target.
headline_result: Dice 0.942 for craniocerebral segmentation, average F1 0.96 for classification, average mean IOU 0.497 for lesion localization

title: Healthy versus pathological learning transferability in shoulder muscle MRI segmentation using deep convolutional encoder-decoders.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
venue_label: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society

clinical_problem: segmenting the four rotator cuff muscles on MRI in children with obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, so that muscle volume - and from it force - can be estimated without hours of manual tracing
model_description: A study framed around the two constraints that define pediatric musculoskeletal AI: very little annotated data, and pathological anatomy that looks nothing like the healthy training examples. It answers the transferability question directly by comparing learning schemes, and the winner combines healthy and pathological annotated data with ImageNet pre-training rather than choosing between them. Supraspinatus, the smallest and most atrophied muscle, is where it degrades.
headline_result: Dice 82.4% deltoid, 82.0% infraspinatus, 71.0% supraspinatus and 82.8% subscapularis, with surface estimation errors below 83 mm2 except supraspinatus at 134.6 mm2

title: Artificial intelligence for interpretation of segments of whole body MRI in CNO: pilot study comparing radiologists versus machine learning algorithm.

headline_result: sensitivity 100% for detecting disease improvement/worsening, but only 33.3% of samples classified correctly overall vs. radiologist ground truth

title: Real-time diameter of the fetal aorta from ultrasound.

headline_result: MSE 0.09 mm^2 (vs. 0.31 state-of-the-art); relative error 5.3% (vs. 8.1%); 289 frames/sec

title: Planning stereoelectroencephalography using automated lesion detection: Retrospective feasibility study.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

patient_population: three cohorts: 34 patients with visible focal cortical dysplasia for training and cross-validation, 20 pediatric healthy controls for specificity, and 34 sEEG patients for the implantation feasibility analysis
clinical_problem: planning stereoelectroencephalography electrode placement in children with drug-resistant epilepsy whose MRI is diagnostically complex, where getting the electrodes to the seizure onset zone is the whole point of the procedure

Specificity in controls was 100%, which matters more than sensitivity for a tool that would add electrodes. The striking cases are the three patients where sEEG localized nothing and the classifier flagged abnormalities that had not been implanted.

title: Mimicking the radiologists' workflow: Estimating pediatric hand bone age with stacked deep neural networks.

The authors make the case explicitly against purely encoder-based architectures, which give a number and no account of it. Competitive on the RSNA challenge test set while remaining explainable, and the detector trains from a small annotated set.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public benchmark
dataset_size: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge data
headline_result: average error 4.56 months on the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge test set, with self-explanatory per-area results

title: A preliminary study to quantitatively evaluate the development of maturation degree for fetal lung based on transfer learning deep model from ultrasound images.

headline_result: Mean absolute GA error 0.72 months (normal weight) and 1.01 months (low birth weight) vs. last menstrual period

headline_result: kappa 0.72 vs ground truth, accuracy 78.0%

study_design: retrospective model development and validation with reader comparison
headline_result: sensitivity 0.90, specificity 0.82, AUC 0.86; outperformed technologists and matched radiologists

headline_result: Brain localization accuracy 100%; Dice score 0.958, sensitivity 0.950, precision 0.968; ~6 seconds per MRI stack

title: Automation analysis x-ray of the spine to objectify the assessment of the severity of scoliotic deformity in idiopathic scoliosis: A preliminary report

dataset_size: 300 digital spine X-rays of children with idiopathic scoliosis

patient_population: HC18 public fetal head ultrasound dataset

dataset_size: HC18 public dataset (fetal head ultrasound images)

title: Intelligent detection of fetal hydrocephalus

release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
headline_result: Machine-learning algorithms, notably Elastic Net, outperformed mass-univariate and OLS regression in out-of-sample prediction of cognition (specific metric not given).

title: Identifying Neuroanatomical and Behavioral Features for Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis in Children using Machine Learning

patient_population: 28 children aged 7-14 years, with and without autism spectrum disorder
clinical_problem: autism spectrum disorder diagnosis using neuroimaging and behavioral features

A novel evolutionary algorithm (CCEA) selects the most discriminating features from a small sample of 28 children aged 7-14, and a separate k-nearest-neighbors classifier validates the selected features for ASD prediction.
release_evidence: preprint (medRxiv); no repository or product mentioned

title: An atlas-free newborn brain image segmentation and classification scheme based on SOM-DCNN with sparse auto encoder
journal: Computer Methods in Biomechanics and Biomedical Engineering: Imaging and Visualization

title: Segmentation of uterus and placenta in MR images using a fully convolutional neural network
model_family: fully convolutional network for 3D segmentation with minimal operator interaction guiding placental localization
patient_population: 100 fetal MRI cases: 70 training, 10 validation and 20 for evaluation

Reporting volume estimation error alongside Dice is the right endpoint, since placental volume is what clinical studies use; the gap between the two structures (2% versus 9% volume error) shows how much harder the placenta is.
headline_result: Dice 92% for the uterine cavity and 82% for the placenta, with average volume estimation errors of 2% and 9%

title: Multi-task prediction of infant cognitive scores from longitudinal incomplete neuroimaging data.
model_family: multi-task machine learning framework with feature selection on neuroimaging measurements
patient_population: in-house longitudinal infant cohort with neuroimaging from as early as 24 months, cognitive scores measured at age 4

headline_result: root mean square error 0.18 for predicting cognitive scores at age 4 using imaging data from as early as 24 months

title: The initiation of cannabis use in adolescence is predicted by sex-specific psychosocial and neurobiological features.

clinical_problem: predicting adolescent risk of future cannabis use initiation from psychosocial, brain and genetic features

title: Longitudinal study of neonatal brain tissue volumes in preterm infants and their ability to predict neurodevelopmental outcome.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

patient_population: 84 infants born between 26 and 36 weeks gestation, imaged shortly after birth and again at term-equivalent age, with outcomes at 18-24 months and 5 years
clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome after preterm birth from brain growth in the neonatal period
model_description: Automatically segments serial neonatal T2-weighted MRI into cortical gray matter, unmyelinated white matter, subcortical gray matter, cerebellum and CSF, then asks which volumes and growth rates predict motor and cognitive outcome later. Volumes at birth and term-equivalent age predicted motor outcome at 18-24 months, while volumes and growth rates predicted cognition at 5 years. The sobering finding is that family socioeconomic status was more strongly associated with cognitive outcome than any brain volume.
headline_result: brain tissue volumes contributed to prediction of motor outcome at 18-24 months and cognitive scores at 5 years; socioeconomic status was strongly associated with cognitive outcome while brain volumes were not

title: DeepIGeoS: A Deep Interactive Geodesic Framework for Medical Image Segmentation.

User clicks are turned into geodesic distance maps and enforced as hard constraints, so a few interactions go a long way. Demonstrated on 2D placenta segmentation from fetal MRI and 3D brain tumor segmentation.
headline_result: large improvement over the automatic CNN, with comparable or better accuracy than traditional interactive methods at fewer interventions and less time

title: Deep Generative Adversarial Neural Networks for Compressive Sensing MRI.

clinical_problem: shortening contrast-enhanced MRI in children by reconstructing undersampled data
model_description: Takes an aliased image from undersampled k-space and returns a diagnostic-quality reconstruction in milliseconds. A generative adversarial network learns what real high-quality MR images look like, so the output keeps fine texture instead of the waxy appearance that pixel-wise losses produce. Trained and evaluated on a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MRI dataset with expert radiologist ratings.
dataset_size: a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MR dataset; size not stated
headline_result: expert radiologists rated it higher in fine texture detail than wavelet, dictionary-learning and pixel-wise deep learning reconstructions, at two orders of magnitude faster reconstruction

title: Towards Automated Semantic Segmentation in Prenatal Volumetric Ultrasound.

clinical_problem: getting reliable biometry out of 3D prenatal ultrasound, which is hard to interpret and therefore little used
model_description: Segments the fetus, gestational sac and placenta simultaneously in a 3D ultrasound volume. A convolutional network makes the initial dense labeling and a recurrent network sweeping in several directions fixes the boundaries, which is where ultrasound segmentation usually fails because contrast is poor and edges are ambiguous. The measurements agreed with experts and were reproducible across scanning variation.
dataset_size: large in-house datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: superior segmentation performance with decent agreement with expert measurements and high reproducibility against scanning variation

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation of bone age radiographs improves accuracy and decreases variability.
patient_population: 280 age- and sex-matched bone age radiographs from children aged 5 to 18
clinical_problem: whether AI assistance makes pediatric radiologists better at bone age, not whether AI alone beats them
model_description: The model itself is a bone age network the group had already published; the contribution here is the comparison design. Six subspecialty pediatric radiologists read the same 280 cases, then three read them again with the model's estimate in front of them. Every reader improved, and inter-reader variability fell. The conclusion — AI plus radiologist beats either alone — is the argument for deploying these tools as an adjunct rather than a replacement.
headline_result: AI alone 68.2% accurate versus 63.6% for the six-reader mean; pooled root mean squared error fell from 0.661 to 0.508 years with AI assistance, and every individual reader improved

title: Real-Time Deep Pose Estimation With Geodesic Loss for Image-to-Template Rigid Registration.

clinical_problem: aligning fetal brain images acquired in arbitrary orientations to a standard atlas, the step that motion-robust reconstruction depends on

Trained on T2-weighted fetal scans, it generalized to T1-weighted newborn scans once image contrast was transferred with a conditional GAN, which is a useful demonstration that a model can be moved across contrasts without retraining from scratch.
headline_result: 3D pose estimation with a wide capture range in under 100 ms, generalizing to newborn scans of a different contrast

title: Multivoxel pattern analysis of structural MRI in children and adolescents with conduct disorder.

clinical_problem: Can structural brain MRI patterns distinguish children/adolescents with conduct disorder from healthy controls, as a potential imaging biomarker?
model_description: A support vector machine with searchlight multivoxel pattern analysis classifies gray-matter spatial patterns on structural MRI to distinguish conduct disorder from healthy controls.
headline_result: Classification accuracy up to 83% using grey matter patterns in identified regions

title: Fetal brain growth portrayed by a spatiotemporal diffusion tensor MRI atlas computed from in utero images.

It makes group studies and computer-aided diagnosis from fetal diffusion imaging possible, which the authors note had not previously been feasible because individual in utero reconstructions are too noisy.
headline_result: the atlas reproduced the known sequence of limbic, projection and association fiber development between 21 and 39 weeks

title: Fully convolutional networks for automated segmentation of abdominal adipose tissue depots in multicenter water-fat MRI.

study_design: retrospective multicenter method-development and validation study
dataset_size: 90 scans (Tellus, cross-validation) plus 20 scans (BetaJudo, external test)
headline_result: U-Net Dice 0.988 (VAT)/0.992 (SAT) internal; 0.970 (VAT)/0.987 (SAT) on external multicenter test data

title: Accurate Age Determination for Adolescents Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Hand and Wrist with an Artificial Neural Network-Based Approach.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

model_description: Notable for a negative result that motivates the positive one: Tanner-Whitehouse 3 read from MRI systematically underestimated age, significantly so in girls and in older adolescents - the very cases where age assessment is contested. Feeding MRI-quantified bone marrow composition alongside the staging into a neural network removed that bias, and was about ten times more accurate than the staging alone. Seventy-nine adolescents from one ethnic group.
headline_result: neural network ages agreed with chronological age (p > 0.05) and were about ten-fold more accurate than the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method applied to MRI alone, which significantly underestimated age in girls and in 15-17 year olds

title: Regression Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Pediatric Bone Age Assessment From Hand Radiograph.

clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
model_description: Regresses bone age directly from the radiograph, with an attention module that first learns where the growth-relevant regions are and a loss that weights the hard cases more heavily during training. The attention idea addresses the specific failure mode of bone age networks, which is that most of the image is irrelevant and the informative epiphyses are small.
dataset_size: two large datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: average discrepancy of 5.2-5.3 months between clinical and automatic bone age on two large datasets

title: Curved planar reformatting and convolutional neural network-based segmentation of the small bowel for visualization and quantitative assessment of pediatric Crohn's disease from MRI.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
venue_label: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

patient_population: 23 pediatric patients with Crohn disease imaged at 1.5 T with a T1-weighted postcontrast VIBE sequence
clinical_problem: seeing and quantifying disease burden in pediatric Crohn disease on contrast-enhanced small bowel MRI, where following the bowel means scrolling back and forth through a 3D volume
model_description: The segmentation is a means, not the end. The markers are then tested for what a radiologist would want: whether they separate active from inactive segments and stricturing from non-stricturing, and whether they reproduce. Wall segmentation is more reliable than lumen.
headline_result: Dice 75 +/- 18% lumen, 81 +/- 8% wall, 97 +/- 2% background; wall thickness at minimum radius (P = 0.0013) and median relative contrast enhancement (P = 0.0033) separated active from non-active segments

title: Automated segmentation of the knee for age assessment in 3D MR images using convolutional neural networks.

clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting knee growth-plate structures on MRI to support chronological age estimation in adolescents and young adults lacking legal documentation
model_description: Input: 3D knee MR images; output: automatic segmentation of growth-plate structures used to derive estimated chronological age, via a U-Net-style encoder-decoder CNN
study_design: retrospective algorithm development, proof-of-concept internal validation
dataset_size: 76 MRI datasets (segmentation); 145 subjects for age estimation, 14-subject test set

title: Neuroanatomical features and its usefulness in classification of patients with PANDAS.
model_family: multivariate pattern analysis over voxel-based morphometry, diffusion tensor and surface features

clinical_problem: whether pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorder associated with streptococci has a neuroanatomical signature that could serve as a biomarker, in a condition whose very existence as an entity rests on distinguishing it from ordinary early-onset OCD
model_description: The first pattern-analysis study of this early-onset OCD subtype, and its negative results are as informative as the positive one: diffusion metrics and every cortical surface feature showed no group difference, while gray matter did, and only gray matter supported classification. The authors read that as consistent with an immune rather than a developmental origin. Fourteen pairs, so 75% accuracy is a signal that the question is worth pursuing rather than a usable test.

dataset_size: 1020 two-dimensional T2-weighted MRI images of preterm newborns
headline_result: Best model (RUSBoost): 85% positive predictive value, 75% sensitivity for QC Fail images

title: Computer-aided diagnosis of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract in children based on ultrasound imaging data by integrating texture image features and deep transfer learning image features.

patient_population: 50 children with congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract and 50 controls, imaged during routine care

model_description: Combines features learned by a pretrained network with hand-computed texture features and shows the combination beats either alone, which is the useful methodological finding on a 100-child dataset where a deep model alone would overfit. Uses images from routine clinical care rather than a curated research acquisition.
headline_result: AUC 0.92, 0.88 and 0.92 for left, right and bilateral abnormal kidney scans, significantly better than either feature set alone (p < 0.001)

title: Comparative effectiveness of convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures for radiology text report classification.
publication_types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural

clinical_problem: extracting whether a CT report says there is a pulmonary embolus, at scale and across institutions
model_description: Reads a free-text thoracic CT report and decides whether it describes a pulmonary embolus. The recurrent model builds up word, sentence and document representations and weights domain-specific phrases through an attention mechanism. The finding that matters for a children's hospital is the transfer: models trained on adult reports classified pediatric reports at the same F1 of 0.99, which is not what happens with image models.
dataset_size: over 7,370 thoracic CT reports from four centers
headline_result: F1 0.99 for pulmonary embolus in adults and 0.99 in the pediatric population, beating the rule-based PEFinder on multi-institutional test sets

title: Beyond Human Perception: Sexual Dimorphism in Hand and Wrist Radiographs Is Discernible by a Deep Learning Model.

clinical_problem: whether hand and wrist radiographs carry a sex signal, which bears on bone age assessment (a sex-specific reference) and on forensic identification
model_description: The clearest demonstration in this database of a model doing something people cannot: 95.9% against two radiologists at 58% and 46%, and the radiologists could not find the pattern even when shown the model's heat maps. The exploratory arm is the thoughtful part - in 44 patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity, agreement with phenotypic sex fell to 77.8%, which raises the question of what the model is measuring and complicates any forensic use.

headline_result: 95.9% accuracy (kappa 0.92) versus 58% and 46% for two radiologists; agreement with phenotypic sex fell to 77.8% in patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity

title: The RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge.

Almost every entry used convolutional neural networks. The paper reports what a coordinated community effort achieved and is the reference point later bone-age papers compare against.

title: Using an artificial neural network to predict traumatic brain injury.

The inputs are the radiologist's CT findings rather than the pixels, so this is decision support layered on the report rather than image analysis. Sensitivity above 99% is the operating point the problem demands, since the cost of a missed clinically relevant injury is not symmetric with the cost of an observation stay.
study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of a multi-center cohort
headline_result: prediction of clinically relevant traumatic brain injury with greater than 99% sensitivity and AUC 0.99

title: Predictive connectome subnetwork extraction with anatomical and connectivity priors.

title: Identifying lesions in paediatric epilepsy using morphometric and textural analysis of magnetic resonance images.

title: White Matter Connectome Edge Density in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: Potential Imaging Biomarkers Using Machine-Learning Models.

dataset_size: 14 boys with ASD, 33 typically developing boys

title: Evaluation of an improved tool for non-invasive prediction of neonatal respiratory morbidity based on fully automated fetal lung ultrasound analysis.

release_evidence: quantusFLM version 3.0, a commercial software tool

title: Evaluating reinforcement learning agents for anatomical landmark detection.

title: White matter connectomes at birth accurately predict cognitive abilities at age 2.

clinical_problem: predicting cognitive ability at age 2 from the brain's wiring at birth

title: Decision Fusion-Based Fetal Ultrasound Image Plane Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks.

Fusing decisions from both, without a prior on where to look, is the contribution, and localization falls out of the same machinery. The high mean accuracy alongside much lower precision and recall reflects 14 unbalanced classes. Its stated purpose is retrospective archive mining rather than live scanning.

title: Detection of Children/Youth With Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder Through Eye Movement, Psychometric, and Neuroimaging Data.

title: Objective Detection of Eloquent Axonal Pathways to Minimize Postoperative Deficits in Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery using Diffusion Tractography and Convolutional Neural Networks.

Ground truth comes from the invasive standard it would reduce.
release_evidence: the abstract states the implementation will be released at a GitHub repository
headline_result: 73-100% accuracy for objective detection of functionally important pathways, outperforming existing streamline classification models

title: Normalization enhances brain network features that predict individual intelligence in children with epilepsy.

A machine learning algorithm uses only these normalized metrics to predict each patient's IQ, with normalization substantially improving prediction accuracy over non-normalized metrics.
headline_result: Normalization substantially improved subject-level IQ prediction accuracy versus non-normalized network metrics

title: Intrinsic Functional Brain Connectivity Predicts Onset of Major Depression Disorder in Adolescence: A Pilot Study.

Its comparator is the right one - baseline clinical rating scales - and connectivity beat them. A pilot, with the sample size that word implies.
dataset_size: pilot cohort, size not stated in the abstract
headline_result: classification of converters versus non-converters from baseline connectivity reached high accuracy, sensitivity and specificity, superior to classification from baseline clinical rating scales

title: Fully automated radiological analysis of spinal disorders and deformities: a deep learning approach.

title: Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Based on Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks.

patient_population: children aged 5 to 10 years from the ABIDE I and ABIDE II datasets
clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children from resting-state functional MRI, before behavioral symptoms are established enough for interview and observation to settle it

The age restriction to 5-10 years is a deliberate cost - it shrinks an already small dataset - taken because a diagnostic aid is only useful before the clinical diagnosis is obvious. Combining classifiers and transferring features stand in for the data that does not exist. Accuracy in the low-to-mid 70s is representative of what ABIDE supports, and is a reminder of how far this is from clinical use.
study_design: retrospective model development on public datasets
dataset_size: ABIDE I and ABIDE II subjects aged 5-10
headline_result: ABIDE I accuracy 0.7273, sensitivity 0.712, specificity 0.7348; ABIDE II accuracy 0.700, sensitivity 0.582, specificity 0.804

title: Deep Learning Method for Automated Classification of Anteroposterior and Posteroanterior Chest Radiographs.

model_description: A quality-control task rather than a diagnostic one, and the pediatric interest is in the ablation: training on the 5% pediatric subset alone, a 95% reduction in data, cost almost nothing (AUC 0.997 versus 1.0, difference not significant). That is a concrete data point for the recurring pediatric worry that adult-scale datasets are needed for anything to work. Aimed at curating large datasets for machine learning and at departmental quality assurance.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public dataset
headline_result: AUC 1.0 and accuracy 99.6% for the full-dataset network versus AUC 0.997 and accuracy 98% for the pediatric-only network (difference not significant, p = 0.17)

title: White Matter Connectome Correlates of Auditory Over-Responsivity: Edge Density Imaging and Machine-Learning Classifiers.

dataset_size: 39 boys, ages 8-12 years (15 with auditory over-responsivity)
headline_result: Left superior longitudinal fasciculus FA gave AUC 0.756 for AOR prediction (p = 0.008); random forest with edge-density metrics had the highest classification accuracy among tested models

title: Longitudinal Prediction of Infant Diffusion MRI Data via Graph Convolutional Adversarial Networks.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: graph convolutional network over spatial and diffusion wave-vector domains, with a multi-scale residual architecture and adversarial learning
patient_population: longitudinal infant brain diffusion MRI

model_description: Attacks a problem specific to pediatric longitudinal imaging: infants move, scans fail, families drop out, and a missing timepoint costs a whole trajectory. Building the graph over both space and the diffusion wave-vector domain lets the network use the structure of the acquisition itself, not just the image. Imputing a missing scan is a strong claim that needs careful use downstream, but the alternative - discarding the subject - has its own bias.
headline_result: accurate and robust longitudinal prediction of missing infant brain diffusion MRI data

dataset_size: not stated (Digital Hand Atlas public dataset)

title: Automated semantic labeling of pediatric musculoskeletal radiographs using deep learning.

Problems this well-posed do not need large datasets. At 33 radiographs per second it is also fast enough to run over an archive, which is the curation use case the authors name.

title: Toward Automated 3D Spine Reconstruction from Biplanar Radiographs Using CNN for Statistical Spine Model Fitting.

headline_result: landmark errors 1.6-2.3 mm; absolute error 2.8-4.7 degrees for spinal and 1-2.1 degrees for pelvic parameters; 89% of measurements inside expert confidence intervals

title: Dilated Dense U-Net for Infant Hippocampus Subfield Segmentation.

The comparison is against 3D U-Net on the same data, and the gain of 2-2.5 Dice points is modest but consistent across both variants.
headline_result: average Dice improved by 2.1% (DUnet) and 2.5% (ResDUnet) over classic 3D U-net, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods

headline_result: comparable functional localization between resting-state fMRI classifier and electrocortical stimulation mapping (no single summary statistic given)

title: Automatic evaluation of fetal head biometry from ultrasound images using machine learning.
