clinical_problem: automating fetal abdominal circumference measurement and, separately, deciding whether the plane is acceptable to measure on at all
model_description: The fuller version of the same group's abdominal circumference work: the landmark classifier and Hough fit are joined by networks that locate the spine and the bone regions to refine the final circumference, and then by a U-Net and classifier that judge whether the image was a valid standard plane. Building the acceptance check into the pipeline is the part that makes it deployable - a measurement returned on the wrong plane is worse than no measurement.
headline_result: Dice similarity for abdominal circumference measurement, with 87.10% accuracy on the fetal abdominal standard plane acceptance check

title: Extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid in high-risk and normal-risk children with autism aged 2-4 years: a case-control study.
model_family: previously validated machine-learning classifier on CSF volume, brain volume, age and sex
patient_population: 159 children aged 2-4 with autism spectrum disorder (both simplex and multiplex families) and 77 with typical development
clinical_problem: whether extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid volume is an imaging marker of autism beyond infancy
model_description: Applies a classifier previously validated in infants to an independent cohort of 2-4 year olds, using extra-axial CSF volume together with brain volume, age and sex to separate children with autism from typically developing controls. The substantive finding is replication: the CSF excess is present in an independent sample, persists beyond infancy, and is the same in children with and without a family history.
headline_result: 15.1% more extra-axial CSF in the autism group after adjustment (p = 0.007, Cohen's d 0.39)

title: Detection of Traumatic Pediatric Elbow Joint Effusion Using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network.
model_family: deep convolutional neural networks of varying depth and architecture, some ImageNet-pretrained and some randomly initialized
patient_population: 882 children presenting to the emergency department with upper extremity trauma, 901 lateral elbow radiographs
clinical_problem: detecting traumatic joint effusion on lateral elbow radiographs, the indirect sign that often stands in for an occult pediatric fracture
model_description: A direct test of whether a small pediatric dataset is enough. Fewer than 700 training radiographs, transfer learning from ImageNet, and a hyperparameter search on 115 validation images produced a classifier that reads elbow effusion at roughly 91 percent sensitivity and specificity. The clinical framing matters more than the numbers: effusion is the finding that tells the emergency physician to treat a child as fractured when no fracture line is visible.
headline_result: test-set AUC 0.943, sensitivity 0.909, specificity 0.906

title: Characterization of coronary artery pathological formations from OCT imaging using deep learning.
model_family: deep features from three pre-trained convolutional networks combined by majority voting
patient_population: 33 retrospective pullbacks of intracoronary cross-sectional OCT images from pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease
clinical_problem: characterizing the intracoronary tissue changes caused by Kawasaki disease on optical coherence tomography, so that coronary involvement can be classified without expert manual interpretation of every cross-section
model_description: An unusual corner of pediatric imaging AI: intravascular OCT in the coronary arteries of children with Kawasaki disease, where the pathological formations differ from adult atherosclerosis and no reader has seen many of them. Rather than train from scratch on 33 cases, the authors take deep features from three ImageNet-pretrained networks and vote - the standard small-data recipe, applied to a disease that will never have a large dataset.
headline_result: accuracy, sensitivity and specificity up to 0.99 +/- 0.01 per tissue class with the majority voting scheme

title: Visual assessment versus computer-assisted gray scale analysis in the ultrasound evaluation of neonatal respiratory status.
model_family: computer-assisted gray scale analysis with textural features and machine learning, compared against a standardized visual score
patient_population: 75 neonates admitted to the NICU for respiratory distress, with a 600-frame ultrasound dataset; oxygenation ratio and alveolar-arterial gradient as reference standards
clinical_problem: grading neonatal respiratory status from lung ultrasound at the cot side, against oxygenation as the reference, so that point-of-care ultrasound can substitute for blood gas sampling in the NICU
model_description: The comparison is against a trained human reading the same frames, and the humans win - visual scoring correlated better with both oxygenation indices than the texture analysis did, with near-perfect interobserver agreement. That is a useful negative for a literature full of claims in the other direction, and the authors read it correctly, presenting computer-assisted analysis as a route to point-of-care diagnostics rather than as an improvement on the expert eye. Region-of-interest size mattered to the texture result.
headline_result: visual scoring correlated with oxygenation at r = -0.55 and 0.59 (kappa 0.91 between observers) versus r = -0.35 to -0.42 and 0.46 to 0.58 for gray scale texture analysis

title: A Deep Automated Skeletal Bone Age Assessment Model with Heterogeneous Features Learning.
model_family: CNN + support vector regression (SVR) with multiple kernel learning
patient_population: Two datasets of pediatric hand/wrist radiographs plus race and gender data (ages not fully specified)
clinical_problem: Automatically assessing skeletal bone age from left-hand and wrist X-rays in children, incorporating heterogeneous demographic features
model_description: Input: left-hand/wrist X-ray images plus race and gender; output: estimated bone age, via a CNN for image feature extraction combined with support vector regression using multiple kernel learning to fuse heterogeneous features
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and comparative evaluation
headline_result: improved accuracy over state-of-the-art on two datasets (no single summary number given)

title: Mutual Information Better Quantifies Brain Network Architecture in Children with Epilepsy.
journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
venue_label: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
model_family: machine learning regression algorithm using brain network graph metrics
patient_population: 24 children with focal epilepsy, ages 8-18 years
clinical_problem: predicting full-scale IQ from resting-state fMRI brain network metrics in children with epilepsy
model_description: Resting-state fMRI brain network metrics (clustering coefficient, modularity, path length, global efficiency), computed using either Pearson correlation or mutual information to define connectivity, are input to a machine learning algorithm trained to predict full-scale IQ in children with epilepsy. Mutual-information-based network metrics explained more IQ variance than correlation-based metrics.
headline_result: Mutual information network metrics explained 49% (95% CI 46-51%) of IQ variance versus 17% (95% CI 13-19%) for Pearson correlation

title: Ossification area localization in pediatric hand radiographs using deep neural networks for object detection.
patient_population: children from the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge cohort
clinical_problem: Localizing ossification centers in the hand to support bone age assessment
model_description: A Faster R-CNN object detector, pretrained on COCO and finetuned on 240 annotated pediatric hand radiographs, takes a hand X-ray as input and outputs bounding boxes localizing ossification centers, as a preprocessing step for bone age estimation.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal validation study
dataset_size: 240 training radiographs, 89 validation radiographs (RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge, >14,000 total)
headline_result: mAP@0.5IoU 92.92 ± 1.93; F1 91.85 ± 1.06 vs. expert radiologist

title: Machine-learning analysis outperforms conventional statistical models and CT classification systems in predicting 6-month outcomes in pediatric patients sustaining traumatic brain injury.
patient_population: 565 children under 18 who sustained traumatic brain injury and had a head CT within 24 hours
clinical_problem: predicting six-month outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury, where adult CT grading systems are the only tools available
model_description: Predicts whether a child will have a favorable Glasgow Outcome Scale score six months after traumatic brain injury, from the admission head CT and clinical record. The comparison is the point: the established adult CT grading systems (Helsinki, Rotterdam, Marshall) were first evaluated on this pediatric cohort and found only moderately predictive, and the pediatric-specific network substantially outperformed all three.
headline_result: AUC 0.946 ± 0.042 versus 0.781-0.838 for the Helsinki, Rotterdam and Marshall CT scores

title: Automatic classification of pediatric pneumonia based on lung ultrasound pattern recognition.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: neural network on brightness-distribution feature vectors
patient_population: 21 children under 5 in Lima, Peru (15 with clinically and radiographically confirmed pneumonia, 6 without lung disease)
clinical_problem: diagnosing childhood pneumonia where there is no radiologist and no radiography, using lung ultrasound
model_description: Strips out skin, fat and muscle from a lung ultrasound frame, divides the remaining image into rectangular segments, and classifies the brightness pattern of each as consolidated or normal lung. The motivation is explicitly resource-constrained: lung ultrasound detects pneumonia well but needs a trained interpreter, and this removes that requirement. The cohort is very small, which the accuracy figures should be read against.
dataset_size: 60 lung ultrasound frames from 21 children; 3,055 feature vectors
headline_result: 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity for pneumonia infiltrates

title: Imbalance of Functional Connectivity and Temporal Entropy in Resting-State Networks in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Machine Learning Approach.
patient_population: Individuals with ASD and controls from the ABIDE cohort (ages not stated in abstract)
clinical_problem: Distinguishing individuals with autism spectrum disorder from controls using patterns of brain network connectivity and signal irregularity on resting-state fMRI
model_description: Input: resting-state fMRI functional connectivity and wavelet-based temporal entropy across 264 brain regions; output: model distinguishing ASD from control individuals and associated with symptom severity
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a public neuroimaging cohort
headline_result: RSN entropy model significantly distinguished ASD from controls (p=0.01)

title: Multimodal Data and Machine Learning for Detecting Specific Biomarkers in Pediatric Epilepsy Patients With Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures.
patient_population: 14 children with generalized tonic-clonic seizure epilepsy and 30 age- and gender-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: identifying brain changes associated with generalized tonic-clonic seizure epilepsy in children
model_description: Takes gray matter volume and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) values from multimodal brain MRI as input and outputs an SVM classification distinguishing epileptic from healthy children.
study_design: retrospective case-control MRI study with machine-learning classification
headline_result: SVM accuracy 83.72% (fALFF, right thalamus) and 74.42% (gray matter volume, right thalamus), both P<0.002

title: Deep Learning Based Attenuation Correction of PET/MRI in Pediatric Brain Tumor Patients: Evaluation in a Clinical Setting.
model_family: deep learning for MR-derived attenuation correction
patient_population: 79 pediatric brain tumor examinations, 36 with active tumor volume above 1 mL analyzed
clinical_problem: quantitatively accurate FET-PET/MRI in children without a CT for attenuation correction, and without a second sedation
model_description: Generates the attenuation map that PET reconstruction needs directly from MRI, so a child having simultaneous FET-PET/MRI does not need a CT and does not need a second sedation for a sequential scan. Compared against a CT-derived reference and against a non-learned MR-based method on the clinical metrics that actually drive decisions, tumor-to-background activity ratios.
headline_result: the only method with all patients inside predefined clinical limits; tumor-to-background difference from CT-based reference -0.1% (95% CI -0.8 to 0.5) versus 5.9% for Dixon-based correction

title: Visualization and Interpretation of Convolutional Neural Network Predictions in Detecting Pneumonia in Pediatric Chest Radiographs.
model_family: customized VGG16 with visualization of class-relevant regions
patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection in children, and separating bacterial from viral pneumonia
model_description: Classifies a pediatric chest radiograph as normal or pneumonia and then as bacterial or viral, and, unusually for this literature, spends most of its effort on showing where the model looked. It introduces a way of localizing the region that drives predictions across all images of a class rather than one image at a time, on the argument that an unexplained black box is unusable for screening decisions.
headline_result: 96.2% accuracy detecting pneumonia and 93.6% distinguishing bacterial from viral

title: Random forest and Self Organizing Maps application for analysis of pediatric fracture healing time of the lower limb
model_family: random forest (feature ranking) and self-organizing maps (SOM)
patient_population: children aged 0-12 years with lower-limb long-bone fractures at a pediatric orthopedic unit
clinical_problem: prediction of fracture healing time in pediatric long-bone fractures
model_description: The model takes features derived from radiographs of pediatric lower-limb long-bone fractures (fracture type, angulation, percentage of bone contact area) together with age, gender, and bone type as input. Random forest ranks which variables most influence fracture healing time, and self-organizing maps then analyze the relationship between the top-ranked variables and healing time. It is intended to help predict expected fracture healing duration in children.
headline_result: age and fracture contact-area percentage were identified as the most important variables explaining fracture healing time

title: Occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy recognition using efficient machine learning for big data and structural connectivity abnormalities analysis
journal: Journal of Medical Imaging and Health Informatics
venue_label: Journal of Medical Imaging and Health Informatics
model_family: k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) classifier on structural connectivity network features
patient_population: children with occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy compared with age- and sex-matched healthy children
clinical_problem: identification of occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (brain injury not visible on conventional MRI)
model_description: The model uses structural brain connectivity networks derived from MRI as input. A k-nearest-neighbor classifier is trained to recognize children with 'occult' spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (no visible lesion on conventional MRI) from large datasets, and permutation testing compares network topology (global efficiency, clustering coefficient, path length) between the occult SDCP and healthy control groups. It is intended to identify subtle structural connectivity abnormalities invisible to conventional MRI reading.
study_design: retrospective case-control diagnostic accuracy / network analysis
headline_result: k-NN provided effective classification results; global efficiency was significantly lower in the occult SDCP group than in controls (p<0.001)

title: Computerized detection of spina bifida using SVM with Zernike moments of fetal skulls in ultrasound screening
model_family: support vector machine using Zernike moment shape features
patient_population: fetuses undergoing ultrasound screening for neural tube defects
clinical_problem: detection of spina bifida (neural tube defect) on prenatal ultrasound screening
model_description: The model takes ultrasound images of the fetal skull as input. It extracts Zernike moment shape features from the skull region and classifies them with a support vector machine to detect shape markers of spina bifida. Oversampling/undersampling techniques address the rarity of positive cases, and the system is intended as computer-aided decision support to help avoid false negatives.
headline_result: average F-measure 0.6276 and GMRP 0.6306 on non-sampled test data; accuracy 94% and specificity 98% under the best sampling configuration (400% borderline-SMOTE followed by 50% random undersampling)

title: Bone age assessment model based on multi-dimensional feature fusion using deep learning
journal: Academic Journal of Second Military Medical University
venue_label: Academic Journal of Second Military Medical University
model_family: deep convolutional neural network feature extraction combined with clinical/demographic data
patient_population: children undergoing left-hand radiography for bone age assessment
clinical_problem: bone age assessment
model_description: The model takes left-hand radiographs as input. A deep convolutional neural network automatically extracts 17 key regional bone-age features from the hand and wrist joint, which are combined with demographic data (sex, population statistics) to estimate bone age. It is intended to improve on traditional manual radiographic bone-age reading.
headline_result: mean absolute error of 0.455 years, better than traditional methods and end-to-end deep learning alone

title: Placental maturity grading via hybrid descriptors and fisher vector
model_family: hybrid CNN (19-layer, transfer learning) + hand-crafted texture features, Fisher vector encoding, SVM classifier
patient_population: pregnant women undergoing obstetric ultrasound (placental imaging)
clinical_problem: placental maturity grading to assess fetal growth and maternal health
model_description: The model takes B-mode and color Doppler energy ultrasound images of the placenta as input. It combines convolutional features from a deep CNN (with transfer learning) with hand-crafted texture features, encodes them with a Fisher vector, and classifies placental maturity grade using a support vector machine. It is intended to automate placental maturity grading, which is otherwise a subjective manual assessment.
headline_result: accuracy 94.15% with hybrid descriptors (19-layer network), 3.01% higher than the hand-crafted-feature model and 7.35% higher than the CNN-only feature model

title: Machine learning of structural magnetic resonance imaging predicts psychopathic traits in adolescent offenders.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: support vector machine on voxel-based morphometry data with out-of-sample cross-validation, using paralimbic regions of interest defined in an independent forensic sample
patient_population: 164 adolescents: 71 incarcerated youth with elevated psychopathic traits, 72 incarcerated youth with low traits, and 21 non-incarcerated healthy controls
clinical_problem: whether structural MRI can grade a personality dimension - psychopathic traits in incarcerated adolescents - rather than only separate a diagnosis from health
model_description: Framed by its authors as a proof of concept, and the accuracy pattern shows exactly why that framing is right: separating either incarcerated group from healthy controls worked well (around 81%), while separating high from low psychopathic traits within the incarcerated group - the only comparison that tests the trait rather than the circumstance - fell to 69%. Regions of interest were fixed from an independent forensic sample rather than fitted, which guards against circularity. The ethical stakes of prediction models for personality traits are considerable and the paper acknowledges them.
headline_result: 69.23% accuracy separating high from low psychopathic traits among incarcerated youth, 82.61% and 80.65% separating each from healthy controls

title: Neural Predictors of Initiating Alcohol Use During Adolescence.
patient_population: 137 healthy substance-naive adolescents aged 12-14, followed annually to age 18
clinical_problem: identifying adolescents at risk of initiating heavy alcohol use before they start
model_description: Takes structural and functional MRI together with demographic and neuropsychological measures from a substance-naive 12-14 year old and predicts whether that adolescent will have initiated moderate to heavy drinking by 18. The model is used as a variable-importance tool rather than a deployed classifier: its output is the ranked list of 34 contributing predictors, which mixes imaging with behavioral and social factors.
dataset_size: 137 adolescents (70 later initiated use, 67 did not)
headline_result: 34 predictors identified, including thinner cortex and reduced activation in diffusely distributed regions alongside demographic and behavioral factors; discrimination not quantified in the abstract

title: BrainNetCNN: Convolutional neural networks for brain networks; towards predicting neurodevelopment.
model_family: CNN with edge-to-edge, edge-to-node and node-to-graph convolutions on connectivity matrices
patient_population: infants born preterm, scanned between 27 and 46 weeks postmenstrual age
clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome after preterm birth
model_description: Takes a structural connectivity matrix built from diffusion tensor imaging and returns predicted Bayley-III cognitive and motor scores at 18 months, corrected for prematurity. The convolutions are designed for network topology rather than image space. It also estimates postmenstrual age at scan, and the learned edge weights can be inspected to see which connections drive the prediction.
study_design: technical development on a preterm cohort
headline_result: outperformed a fully connected network with the same parameter count and other comparison methods; estimated postmenstrual age to within about 2 weeks

title: Individual prediction of long-term outcome in adolescents at ultra-high risk for psychosis: Applying machine learning techniques to brain imaging data.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: support vector regression on structural MRI measures
patient_population: 64 ultra-high-risk and 62 typically developing adolescents aged 12-18, with outcome determined for 43 at six years
clinical_problem: predicting six-year functional and clinical outcome in adolescents at ultra-high risk for psychosis, most of whom will not convert
model_description: Predicts long-term functioning and symptom scores as continuous values rather than converting versus not converting, on the argument that most ultra-high-risk adolescents turn out resilient and a binary label throws that away. Baseline subcortical volumes carried the strongest signal. The effect size is medium and the authors are careful not to overclaim individual-level prediction from it.
dataset_size: 126 adolescents at baseline; 43 with six-year outcome
headline_result: highest predictive correlation r = 0.42 between baseline subcortical volumes and long-term level of functioning

title: Brain Network Architecture and Global Intelligence in Children with Focal Epilepsy.
patient_population: 30 children (4-18 years) with focal epilepsy undergoing 3T brain MRI with resting-state fMRI
clinical_problem: relating brain network architecture from resting-state fMRI to intelligence in children with focal epilepsy
model_description: Takes resting-state fMRI-derived graph-theoretical network metrics (clustering coefficient, transitivity, modularity, path length, global efficiency) as input and outputs a machine-learning-based estimate of each metric's independent contribution to full-scale intelligence quotient.
study_design: retrospective cohort study with machine-learning-based network analysis
headline_result: clustering coefficient and path length independently associated with full-scale IQ after adjusting for age and sex; longer epilepsy history associated with shorter path length (P=.008)

title: Deep learning for automated skeletal bone age assessment in X-ray images.
patient_population: children across all age ranges, races and both sexes in a public hand-radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
model_description: Takes a left-hand radiograph and returns a bone age, replacing Greulich-Pyle or Tanner-Whitehouse atlas matching. The paper's contribution is as much methodological as clinical: it is the first bone-age model tested on a public dataset across all ages, races and both sexes with source code released, and it uses that setting to compare learned against hand-crafted features and to ask how to train a network on few images.
release_evidence: first automated bone age work tested on a public dataset for which the source code is available
study_design: technical development on a public benchmark
dataset_size: a public hand-radiograph dataset; size not stated
headline_result: average discrepancy between manual and automatic bone age of about 0.8 years

title: DeepCut: Object Segmentation From Bounding Box Annotations Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
model_family: CNN in a densely connected conditional random field, trained from bounding boxes
patient_population: fetuses in a fetal MRI dataset
clinical_problem: segmenting fetal brain and lung on MRI without pixel-level annotation
model_description: Turns cheap annotation into pixel-level segmentations: an annotator draws only a bounding box, and the method alternates between training a network and re-estimating the segmentation inside the box until it converges. Extends the classical GrabCut idea with a learned classifier. Tested on fetal brain and lung segmentation from MRI.
headline_result: encouraging accuracy on fetal brain and lung segmentation from bounding boxes alone; figures not stated in the abstract

title: Neonatal neural networks predict children behavioral profiles later in life.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: support vector machine and canonical correlation analysis
patient_population: 120 neonates with diffusion tensor imaging-derived structural brain networks
clinical_problem: predicting childhood behavioral problems from neonatal brain structural connectivity
model_description: Input is DTI-tractography-derived structural brain network clustering coefficients from neonatal MRI; a support vector machine and canonical correlation analysis identify network features that predict internalizing/externalizing behavior problems at 24 and 48 months of age.
study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with SVM classification
headline_result: clustering coefficients of specific regions (e.g. right amygdala) significantly associated with behavior problems at 24 and 48 months; four neonatal network subgroups identified

title: Diagnostic model generated by MRI-derived brain features in toddlers with autism spectrum disorder.
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
venue_label: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
model_family: random forest classifier over regional cortical thickness, volume and surface area features
patient_population: 46 children with autism spectrum disorder and 39 children with developmental delay, aged 18 to 37 months
clinical_problem: finding an objective imaging biomarker to supplement autism diagnosis in toddlers, which currently rests on psychological evaluation, clinical observation and history and is therefore subjective and reporter-dependent
model_description: The comparison group is the useful design choice: developmental delay rather than typical development, which is the discrimination that is actually hard in a toddler clinic. Three anatomical feature families are compared head to head, and cortical thickness beats both volume and surface area. The authors are careful about the claim - a supplementary line of evidence for a diagnosis, not a replacement - which is the appropriate register for 85 toddlers.
headline_result: best performance from regional average cortical thickness of the 20 most important random forest features, outperforming volume-based and surface-area-based classification

title: Metrics of brain network architecture capture the impact of disease in children with epilepsy.
model_family: machine learning on global graph metrics of resting-state networks
patient_population: 45 children aged 4-19 with focal epilepsy, with full-scale IQ measured by a pediatric neuropsychologist
clinical_problem: quantifying the cumulative impact of epilepsy on a developing brain, as a route to a marker of cognitive deterioration
model_description: Parcellates the cortex into about 700 nodes, computes five global network metrics from resting-state MRI, and predicts epilepsy duration from them, using duration as a stand-in for how much the disease has affected the brain. Duration was itself inversely related to IQ. The prediction is near-perfect, which given 45 patients and five predictors warrants caution, but the framing — imaging metrics as a patient-level marker of cognitive deterioration — is the useful part.
headline_result: predicted and actual epilepsy duration correlated at r = 0.95 (p = 0.0001), driven mainly by network modularity

title: Semiautomatic classification of acetabular shape from three-dimensional ultrasound for diagnosis of infant hip dysplasia using geometric features.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
venue_label: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
patient_population: 79 3D ultrasound infant hip recordings from 42 patients (36 normal, 16 borderline, 27 dysplastic)
clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip from 3D ultrasound acetabular shape
model_description: Semiautomated graph-search segmentation produces 3D acetabular surface models; a random forest classifier uses geometric features from these models to classify hips as normal, borderline, or dysplastic.
study_design: retrospective method development and diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 79 3D ultrasound infant hip recordings from 42 patients
headline_result: 100% specificity, 97.2% sensitivity for normal vs dysplastic; true positive rates 94.4%/62.5%/89.9% for normal/borderline/dysplastic

title: A framework for analysis of linear ultrasound videos to detect fetal presentation and heartbeat.
model_family: frame-by-frame classifier regularized by a conditional random field over time, with a kernelized linear dynamical model for heartbeat detection
patient_population: 323 predefined free-hand ultrasound videos sweeping the maternal abdomen
clinical_problem: confirming pregnancy viability and fetal presentation - the two first questions of any obstetric ultrasound - from a simple predefined sweep that a novice can perform
model_description: Task-shifting by design. The scanning protocol is engineered so that a fixed straight sweep is guaranteed to cross the skull, abdomen and heart, and the algorithm then does the interpreting - which is what lets someone with no sonography training establish viability and presentation. Temporal structure is used twice: a conditional random field smooths the per-frame labels, and heartbeat is read out of the dynamics of consecutive cardiac frames rather than from any single image.
headline_result: mean classification accuracy 83.4% for detecting fetal skull, abdomen and heart, and 93.1% for heartbeat detection

title: Segmentation of Fetal Left Ventricle in Echocardiographic Sequences Based on Dynamic Convolutional Neural Networks.
model_family: dynamic convolutional neural network with fine-tuning
patient_population: 51 fetal echocardiographic sequences
clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal left ventricle for quantitative fetal cardiac function analysis
model_description: Input is a fetal echocardiographic image sequence; output is a frame-by-frame segmentation of the left ventricle, produced by a CNN pretrained on labeled data and fine-tuned per fetus, with a matching approach to track mitral valve base points.

title: Novel surface features for automated detection of focal cortical dysplasias in paediatric epilepsy.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: neural network classifier on surface-based morphometric features
patient_population: 22 children with focal epilepsy (mean age 12.1 years) and 28 healthy controls (mean age 14.6 years)
clinical_problem: finding focal cortical dysplasia on MRI in children with drug-resistant epilepsy, where detection determines whether surgery is offered
model_description: Scans the cortical surface vertex by vertex and flags candidate dysplastic regions. Alongside established measures (cortical thickness, gray-white blurring, FLAIR intensity, sulcal depth, curvature) it adds features designed for a developing brain: local cortical deformation, a doughnut measure of local variability against the surrounding cortex, and per-vertex interhemispheric asymmetry. Existing adult tools had not worked on children, which is precisely the gap it addresses.
headline_result: sensitivity rose from 59% with established features alone to 73% with the added novel features

title: 3-D Morphology Prediction of Progressive Spinal Deformities From Probabilistic Modeling of Discriminant Manifolds.
patient_population: 133 subjects with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, 745 longitudinal 3D spine reconstructions
clinical_problem: predicting progression of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from spine x-rays
model_description: Takes a 3D spine model reconstructed from biplanar x-ray images as input and outputs a prediction of whether the scoliosis curve will progress plus an estimated future curve angle, using a probabilistic manifold-embedding model.
study_design: retrospective longitudinal cohort study with model development
headline_result: 81% classification rate for progressive vs. non-progressive scoliosis; prediction error 2.1° in main curve angulation

title: Concatenated Spatially-localized Random Forests for Hippocampus Labeling in Adult and Infant MR Brain Images.
patient_population: Adult and infant brain MRI datasets (sizes not stated, described as 'large datasets')
clinical_problem: Automatically labeling (segmenting) the hippocampus on brain MRI in both adult and infant subjects to support imaging-based brain studies
model_description: Input: adult and infant brain MRI; output: automatic hippocampus segmentation labels, via a concatenated set of spatially-localized random forest classifiers with auto-context refinement

title: Automated detection of coarctation of aorta in neonates from two-dimensional echocardiograms.
patient_population: 26 neonates with coarctation of the aorta and 64 normal neonates (validation set)
clinical_problem: detecting coarctation of the aorta in neonates from echocardiography
model_description: Two-dimensional echocardiogram clips from the parasternal long-axis, apical four-chamber and suprasternal notch views are classified by deep-learning-based classifiers per view; the combined decisions across the three standard views output a coarctation-of-the-aorta detection.
headline_result: total error rate 12.9% (11.5% false-negative, 13.6% false-positive) combining three standard echocardiographic views

title: SEGMA: An Automatic SEGMentation Approach for Human Brain MRI Using Sliding Window and Random Forests.
patient_population: 179 individuals: newborns (38-42 weeks GA), children/adolescents (4-17 years), adults (35-71 years)
age_groups: neonate; child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: automatically segmenting brain MRI structures across the life course, including newborns and children, to study brain development
model_description: a sliding-window multi-class random forest classifier takes brain MRI as input and outputs automatic segmentation, trained to generalize across newborn, child, and adult ages
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study across the life course

title: Automatic quantification of ischemic injury on diffusion-weighted MRI of neonatal hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 20 subjects (training, manually annotated by two observers) plus 54 additional subjects (larger dataset, 1.5T and 3.0T)
clinical_problem: automatic detection and quantification of ischemic lesions on diffusion-weighted MRI in neonatal hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy
model_description: Input: diffusion-weighted MRI of neonates with hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy; output: automatic segmentation/quantification of ischemic lesion extent, condensed to a single injury score.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation against manual annotation
dataset_size: 20 subjects (training) plus 54 additional subjects (larger dataset), 1.5T and 3.0T
headline_result: Median sensitivity 0.72, specificity 0.99; F1-score median 0.52 (algorithm) vs. 0.56 (second human observer), no significant difference

title: Early brain development in infants at high risk for autism spectrum disorder.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
model_family: deep-learning classifier on cortical surface area features
patient_population: 106 infants at high familial risk of autism and 42 low-risk infants, imaged at 6, 12 and 24 months
clinical_problem: prediction of an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis before behavioral symptoms are established
model_description: Takes brain MRI acquired at 6 and 12 months of age, chiefly cortical surface area measurements, and returns a prediction of whether that individual child will meet criteria for autism at 24 months. Trained and cross-validated within a prospective high-familial-risk infant cohort. The clinical interest is identifying children before symptoms emerge, when early intervention is still possible.
headline_result: positive predictive value 81%, sensitivity 88% for a 24-month autism diagnosis

title: Intrinsic Connectivity Network-Based Classification and Detection of Psychotic Symptoms in Youth With 22q11.2 Deletions.

study_design: technical development on a public dataset

title: Predicting symptomatic cerebral vasospasm after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage with an artificial neural network in a pediatric population.

title: Computerized Bone Age Estimation Using Deep Learning Based Program: Evaluation of the Accuracy and Efficiency.

dataset_size: a large real-world clinical dataset; size not stated
headline_result: automatic verification approached human expert assessment

title: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging for surgical planning in pediatric patients: a preliminary experience.

A trained classifier identifies resting-state networks in the individual child, and the maps are loaded straight into the surgical navigation system. Six of the twenty children were sedated and it still worked, which is the point.

title: Fetal facial standard plane recognition via deep convolutional neural networks

title: Accurate anatomical landmark detection based on importance sampling for infant brain MR images

It is intended to support downstream tasks such as landmark-based segmentation, image registration, and disease prediction in infant brain imaging.

title: Texture analysis of the developing human brain using customization of a knowledge-based system

title: Pediatric Bone Age Assessment Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

title: Multivariate classification of autism spectrum disorder using frequency-specific resting-state functional connectivity--A multi-center study.

title: Quantitative Ultrasound for Measuring Obstructive Severity in Children with Hydronephrosis.

title: Pediatric laminopathies: Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging fingerprint and comparison with Sepn1 myopathy.
