title: Automatic bone age assessment for young children from newborn to 7-year-old using carpal bones.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
venue_label: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural
model_family: knowledge-based automatic segmentation with fuzzy classification (computer-aided diagnosis)
patient_population: children from newborn to 7 years old, hand radiographs from a digital hand atlas
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in young children
model_description: Building on an existing phalanx-based CAD bone-age system that worked well only from age 7 onward, this method automatically segments carpal bone boundaries on hand radiographs, extracts morphological features, and applies fuzzy classification to estimate bone age. It was evaluated on about 205 cases from a digital hand atlas against chronological age and two radiologists' readings.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation against radiologist readings
dataset_size: about 205 cases from a digital hand atlas

title: Multivariate examination of brain abnormality using both structural and functional MRI.
patient_population: 49 adolescents (24 normal, 25 prenatally cocaine-exposed teenagers)
clinical_problem: detecting brain abnormalities associated with prenatal cocaine exposure in adolescents from structural and functional MRI
model_description: Regional statistical features extracted from structural and functional MRI are combined via a hybrid feature-selection method with a nonlinear support vector machine to classify each adolescent as normal or prenatally cocaine-exposed.
study_design: case-control study with multivariate pattern classification, leave-one-out cross-validation

title: Computerized geometric features of carpal bone for bone age estimation.
model_family: neural network (back-propagation NN, radial basis function NN)
patient_population: 465 boys and 444 girls, hand X-ray films
clinical_problem: Estimating skeletal bone age in children from hand radiographs
model_description: Geometric shape, area, and sequence features are extracted from carpal bones on hand radiographs and classified by neural network classifiers (linear, nearest-neighbor, back-propagation NN, radial basis function NN) to estimate bone age.

title: Generating prior probabilities for classifiers of brain tumours using belief networks.
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
venue_label: BMC medical informatics and decision making
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: Database of over 1,300 pediatric brain tumor cases collected over five decades
clinical_problem: Generating prior probabilities of pediatric brain tumor type from anatomical location to improve MR-spectroscopy-based tumor classification
model_description: Belief networks built from a database of pediatric tumor cases generate a probability that a given tumor is each of several types (astrocytoma grades, ependymoma, PNET, germinoma, medulloblastoma, craniopharyngioma) based on anatomical location, combined with an MRS-based classifier
headline_result: Using network-derived prior probabilities improved classification accuracy compared with priors based on class prevalence alone

title: Cerebral metabolite differences in adolescents with low birth weight: assessment with in vivo proton MR spectroscopy.
patient_population: 54 adolescents (very low birth weight, small-for-gestational-age at term, and controls)
clinical_problem: distinguishing brain metabolite differences in adolescents with very low birth weight or small-for-gestational-age from controls
model_description: A probabilistic neural network takes chemical-shift regions (NAA, choline, creatine peaks) from proton MR spectroscopy as input and classifies adolescents into birth-history subgroups.
headline_result: Correct classification of 52/54 adolescents, sensitivity and specificity >93% for all groups

title: Computer-aided detection of therapy-induced leukoencephalopathy in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia patients treated with intravenous high-dose methotrexate.
publication_types: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: 228 children treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia, imaged at multiple time points
clinical_problem: differentiating chemotherapy-induced leukoencephalopathy from normal maturation in children treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia
model_description: a Kohonen self-organizing map takes multi-sequence MRI (T1, T2, PD, FLAIR) and tissue volume maps as input and outputs a computer-aided classification of white matter regions as leukoencephalopathy vs. normal-appearing
headline_result: agreement with consensus of two trained observers 84.1% (535/636)

title: Extracting information on pneumonia in infants using natural language processing of radiology reports.
publication_types: Clinical Trial; Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, P.H.S.
model_family: rule-based natural language processing (NLP) / expert system
patient_population: neonates (newborns) whose radiology reports were screened for healthcare-associated pneumonia
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection / surveillance from radiology reports
model_description: An NLP-based automated monitoring system reads free-text radiology reports and classifies them for presence of pneumonia, to support surveillance of healthcare-associated pneumonia in newborns. Its output was compared against clinicians' judgments in a feasibility study; the abstract does not describe the underlying training method or imaging modality in detail.
study_design: retrospective feasibility study, diagnostic accuracy validation of an NLP surveillance tool
headline_result: sensitivity 71%, specificity 99% versus clinicians' judgments

title: A tissue-specific adaptive texture filter for medical ultrasound images.
model_family: multivariate texture classifier (gray-level co-occurrence matrix based)
patient_population: 10 neonatal cranial ultrasound images
clinical_problem: Enhancing neonatal cranial ultrasound images to improve visual detection and boundary delineation of periventricular leukomalacia
model_description: A multivariate texture classifier based on the gray-level co-occurrence matrix, combined with an adaptive texture smoothing filter, enhances the visual contrast between healthy neonatal brain tissue and periventricular leukomalacia-affected tissue to aid computer-aided boundary delineation.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development compared with manual expert delineation and other speckle filters

title: Use of imaging biomarkers and ambulatory functional endpoints in Duchenne muscular dystrophy clinical trials: Systematic review and machine learning-driven trend analysis.
patient_population: 85 DMD trials and non-interventional studies (2010-2022), primarily pediatric males
clinical_problem: how MRI imaging biomarkers (fat fraction, T2 relaxation time) are used to track disease progression in Duchenne muscular dystrophy clinical trials, versus traditional ambulatory endpoints
model_description: A systematic review of 85 DMD trials characterizes the use of MRI imaging biomarkers versus functional endpoints for tracking disease progression; an XGBoost machine learning model analyzes trial-level predictors (duration, start year) of imaging biomarker adoption over time.
study_design: systematic review with machine learning trend analysis
headline_result: Only 13.3% of biologic intervention trials incorporated imaging biomarkers versus 93% using ambulatory functional endpoints; imaging biomarker studies averaged 4.5 years duration

title: Are Artificial Intelligence Models Reliable for Clinical Application in Pediatric Fracture Detection on Radiographs? A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
body_region: multiple (varies by study; rib fractures excluded)
patient_population: 10,203 pediatric patients (mean age 8.85 years), 21,789 radiographs across 16 studies
clinical_problem: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models for detecting fractures on pediatric radiographs.
model_description: Meta-analysis of 16 diagnostic accuracy studies of AI models (including CNNs) that take pediatric radiographs as input and output fracture detection.
study_design: systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA, PROSPERO registered)
headline_result: Pooled sensitivity 93%, specificity 91%, AUC 0.96 (external validation subset: sensitivity 93%, specificity 88%, AUC 0.95)

title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric respiratory medicine.
patient_population: pediatric respiratory medicine patients (review)
clinical_problem: review of how AI can improve diagnostics (including radiology), therapeutics, and clinical support in paediatric respiratory medicine
model_description: narrative review of AI applications in paediatric respiratory medicine, including radiology, primary ciliary dyskinesia diagnostics, sleep medicine, and pulmonary function tests, plus therapeutics/drug discovery and clinician support tools

title: Artificial intelligence in early onset scoliosis: a scoping review.
patient_population: Children with early onset scoliosis (younger than 10 years)
clinical_problem: Diagnosing, monitoring, and predicting outcomes in early onset scoliosis (children under 10) using AI
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; outcome prediction
model_description: Scoping review of 11 studies applying AI/ML (mostly CNNs such as Mask R-CNN, EfficientNet, U-Net) to automate radiographic measurements (Cobb angle, skeletal maturity), monitor growing-rod distraction, and predict complications/reoperation in early onset scoliosis.
headline_result: Mean accuracy 91.2% (range 86.1-94.0%) across 11 included studies

title: Pediatric pulmonary nodules: current state of knowledge, AI applications, and future directions.
patient_population: Pediatric patients with pulmonary nodules (review)
clinical_problem: Reviewing imaging characteristics and AI applications for differentiating benign from malignant pulmonary nodules in children.
model_description: Narrative review discussing current and emerging AI applications for evaluating pediatric pulmonary nodules on CT, including differentiation of benign versus malignant nodules.

title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted Ultrasound for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Across Segmentation, Angle Measurement, and Diagnostic Tasks.
patient_population: 34 studies pooled (infants undergoing hip ultrasound)
clinical_problem: Performance of AI for developmental dysplasia of the hip assessment on ultrasound (segmentation, angle measurement, diagnosis)
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling 34 studies of AI applied to hip ultrasound for DDH, across segmentation (Dice), angle measurement (ICC) and diagnostic classification tasks.
dataset_size: 34 studies; segmentation n=3,011, angle measurement n=2,012, diagnostic n=3,035-5,341
headline_result: Pooled segmentation Dice 0.876; pooled diagnostic AUC 0.937 (sensitivity 0.888, specificity 0.893)

title: Revisiting KANET in the context of fetal connectomics: defining optimal gestational windows for neurodevelopmental screening.
patient_population: fetuses assessed by 4D ultrasound behavioral observation (narrative review of 42 studies)
clinical_problem: define optimal gestational windows for KANET-based fetal neurodevelopmental screening using 4D ultrasound behavioral observation, with AI potential to enhance scoring objectivity
model_description: narrative review synthesizing evidence on fetal neurobehavior (KANET scoring) via 4D ultrasound and its correlation with neural circuit maturation; discusses emerging AI applications to improve scoring objectivity by detecting movement entropy, asymmetry, and latency

title: Artificial Intelligence Implementation in Pediatric Radiology for Patient Safety: A Multisociety Statement From the ACR, ESPR, SPR, SLARP, AOSPR, SPIN.
journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
venue_label: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing radiologic imaging generally
clinical_problem: safe and effective adoption of AI tools across pediatric radiology practice
model_description: Multisociety position statement (ACR, ESPR, SPR, SLARP, AOSPR, SPIN) addressing four pillars of AI adoption in pediatric radiology: regulation and purchasing, implementation and integration, interpretation and postmarket surveillance, and education. It recommends pediatric-specific safety ratings, diverse pediatric training datasets, transparency metrics, explainability, phased implementation with pilot testing, postmarket surveillance, and AI literacy training for pediatric radiology staff.

title: AI implementation in pediatric radiology for patient safety: a multi-society statement from the ACR, ESPR, SPR, SLARP, AOSPR, SPIN.
publication_types: Journal Article; Practice Guideline; Review; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
clinical_problem: how a children's hospital should buy, deploy, monitor and teach AI safely
model_description: A joint statement from the ACR, ESPR, SPR, SLARP, AOSPR and SPIN covering four pillars: regulation and purchasing, implementation, post-market surveillance, and education. Concretely it asks for pediatric-specific safety ratings, training data drawn from diverse pediatric populations, quantifiable transparency metrics, phased rollout with pilot testing and continuous benchmark monitoring, explicit protocols for discrepancies and adverse incidents, and AI literacy training for every clinician who touches these tools. This is the document to hand a procurement committee.

title: Application of Total-Body PET in Pediatric Patients.
patient_population: Pediatric patients undergoing PET imaging
clinical_problem: Clinical role of total-body PET imaging in pediatric patients
model_description: Review of total-body PET technology for pediatric imaging, including AI-enhanced image reconstruction as one of several innovations (alongside silicon photomultiplier detectors and ultralong axial field of view) that improve image quality and lower radiation dose.

title: Advanced neuroimaging in pediatric epilepsy surgery: state of the art and future perspectives.
model_family: review of ML/deep learning post-processing tools (MELD-Graph, MAP18, FLAT1, SUPR-FLAIR)
patient_population: children with drug-resistant epilepsy, including MRI-negative cases
clinical_problem: detecting subtle cortical abnormalities (e.g., focal cortical dysplasia) for presurgical planning in drug-resistant pediatric epilepsy
model_description: Narrative review of structural MRI post-processing tools for pediatric epilepsy surgery, including MELD-Graph (deep neural network surface-based lesion detection), MAP18 (voxel-based morphometry), FLAT1 (FLAIR/T1 ratio mapping) and SUPR-FLAIR (normalized FLAIR projection), describing how each increases sensitivity for focal cortical dysplasia and other subtle lesions when standard MRI appears normal.

title: The role of artificial intelligence in pediatric cardiovascular imaging: clinical applications and future directions in computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging.
patient_population: children with congenital and acquired heart disease
clinical_problem: diagnosis, monitoring and management of congenital and acquired pediatric heart disease using cardiac CT and MRI
model_description: Review of current and emerging AI applications in pediatric cardiac CT and MRI, covering image acquisition, segmentation, interpretation, diagnosis and outcome-prediction modeling, plus emerging directions such as multimodal risk stratification, digital twins, 3D modeling and computational fluid dynamics.

title: Triage and workflow optimization with artificial intelligence in pediatric imaging.
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing radiology department imaging
clinical_problem: using AI to triage patients and optimize workflow in pediatric imaging departments
model_description: Review of machine-learning-based algorithms for pediatric radiology triage and workflow optimization, including clinical referral appropriateness, exam scheduling, protocoling, radiation dose reduction, and follow-up reminders, and discussion of limited pediatric training data and multimodal (imaging plus genomic and clinical) datasets as a path forward.

title: Developmental Brain Age Estimation From MRI Data: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning Approaches and Open Datasets.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
venue_label: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
patient_population: Fetal stage to 2-year-old subjects across reviewed studies and open datasets
clinical_problem: Estimating developmental brain age from MRI (fetal stage to 2 years) as a biomarker of atypical neurodevelopment
model_description: Systematic review of deep learning approaches that take developmental brain MRI as input and output a predicted 'brain age' (fetal stage to 2 years), compared against chronological age as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental disorders, including review of open-access developmental MRI datasets.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics: Current Applications, Opportunities, and Clinical Implementation Challenges.
patient_population: pregnant patients / fetuses
clinical_problem: how AI can support prenatal diagnostic imaging, risk prediction, and intrapartum monitoring
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; outcome prediction
model_description: narrative review of AI applications across automated fetal biometry, structural anomaly detection, prediction of pregnancy complications, and intrapartum fetal surveillance

title: Enhancing Fetal Cardiac Imaging With Artificial Intelligence: A Review of the Current Evidence and Future Directions.
patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound screening for congenital heart disease
clinical_problem: improving prenatal detection of congenital heart disease on obstetric ultrasound
model_description: Review of AI applications in fetal cardiac ultrasound, including automated standard-view acquisition, congenital heart disease detection, and cardiac biometry, plus emerging generative AI, self-supervised learning, and NLP-based report automation.
headline_result: AI has shown expert-level performance in view classification, CHD detection, and cardiac biometry (as reported by cited literature)

title: Artificial Intelligence in Fetal MRI: Principles, Applications, Limitations, and Future Directions.
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal MRI
clinical_problem: overcoming motion, low signal-to-noise ratio, and slice misregistration limitations of fetal MRI
model_description: Review of AI applications in fetal MRI: image reconstruction, denoising, motion correction, automated segmentation, and quantitative analysis including gestational-age estimation and anomaly detection, noting that most studies use small single-center datasets with limited external validation.

title: Artificial intelligence and pediatric imaging data: ethical strategies for learning and collaboration.
clinical_problem: How to ethically develop, validate, and deploy AI models on pediatric imaging data
model_description: Review discussing ethical strategies for AI development and deployment in pediatric radiology, covering regulatory hurdles, bias mitigation, human oversight, and interdisciplinary collaboration among developers, clinicians, and families.

title: Game-Changing Advances in Infant Hip Dysplasia Evaluation With Ultrasound.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
venue_label: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
patient_population: Infants undergoing newborn hip ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: Reviewing advances in ultrasound screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip, including AI-assisted automated cine-sweep classification and quality control.
model_description: Narrative review of 3D ultrasound for volumetric hip visualization and AI-assisted 2D cine-sweep tools that add automated quality control and DDH classification for lightly trained operators, plus open-source software/datasets enabling external validation.
release_evidence: review notes that open-source software and datasets exist for this application

title: Reply to comment on impact of deep learning on CT-based organ-at-risk delineation for flank irradiation in paediatric renal tumours: A SIOP-RTSG radiotherapy committee.
model_family: Deep learning (auto-contouring, architecture not restated in this letter)
patient_population: Pediatric patients with renal tumors undergoing flank irradiation (SIOP-RTSG)
clinical_problem: Clarifying methodology of a deep-learning CT auto-contouring system for organ-at-risk delineation in pediatric flank irradiation for renal tumors.
model_description: A deep-learning auto-contouring system delineates organs-at-risk on CT for pediatric flank-irradiation planning; this reply clarifies the annotation protocol, addresses STAPLE consensus bias, and discusses limitations of the original clinical-adoption evaluation.
study_design: Letter/reply clarifying methodology of a prior deep-learning auto-contouring validation study.

title: Artificial intelligence performance in image-based biliary atresia identification: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
patient_population: 11,006 patients (2,357 biliary atresia, 8,649 non-BA) across 9 studies
clinical_problem: diagnosing biliary atresia from imaging
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling diagnostic accuracy of imaging-based AI models (predominantly ultrasound) for detecting biliary atresia.
headline_result: pooled sensitivity 93.8%, specificity 93.2%, AUC 0.94 (patient-level)

title: Emerging applications of artificial intelligence for obstetric ultrasound: A scoping review.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
venue_label: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
patient_population: review of 96 studies of obstetric ultrasound AI, Jan 2022-2024
clinical_problem: AI applications across obstetric ultrasound (fetal anomalies, biometry, placental abnormalities)
model_description: Scoping review synthesizing AI algorithms developed for obstetric ultrasound, categorized into seven areas including fetal biometry and anatomical evaluation.
headline_result: fetal biometry (25%) and fetal anatomical evaluation (20%) were the largest study categories

title: Craniometrics in Metopic Craniosynostosis: A Review of Craniometric Parameters and the Emergence of Machine Learning Models.
patient_population: 58 studies, 9,068 patients (2,425 with metopic craniosynostosis)
clinical_problem: assessing craniofacial morphology and severity of metopic craniosynostosis
model_description: Systematic review of craniometric imaging parameters and emerging machine-learning models (e.g., severity scores) that use CT and 3D photogrammetry to grade metopic craniosynostosis severity and guide surgical decisions.
headline_result: 18 of 58 studies (31%) used ML models introducing severity indices with high diagnostic accuracy

title: Artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and prognosis of pediatric bacterial pneumonia: current advances and challenges.
clinical_problem: Reviewing how AI can improve diagnostic accuracy and prognostic evaluation for pediatric bacterial pneumonia, which is difficult to distinguish clinically from other respiratory conditions
model_description: Narrative review of AI-driven diagnostic tools that process chest imaging and heterogeneous patient data to detect pediatric bacterial pneumonia and flag early signs of severe disease; no single model described.

title: Comment on "Deep learning in CT-based organ-at-risk delineation for pediatric flank irradiation": Methodological and clinical considerations.
patient_population: children undergoing flank irradiation
clinical_problem: reliability of automated organ-at-risk delineation for pediatric radiotherapy planning
model_description: critical commentary on a deep-learning organ-at-risk delineation study for pediatric flank irradiation, raising methodological concerns (annotation protocol transparency, circularity of STAPLE consensus, lack of dosimetric validation, no uncertainty quantification)

title: Advancements in radiation dose reduction for pediatric CT head Imaging: A scoping review of emerging Technologies, Protocols, and optimization strategies.
journal: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
venue_label: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
clinical_problem: Reviewing methods to reduce radiation dose in pediatric CT head imaging while maintaining diagnostic image quality, including AI-based deep-learning image reconstruction
model_description: Scoping review of 24 articles on radiation-dose reduction techniques for pediatric CT head imaging, concluding that deep-learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithms enhance image quality at ultra-low radiation doses compared with conventional reduction techniques.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled pediatric radiology in low-resource settings: addressing resource constraints in the African healthcare system.
clinical_problem: implementing AI in pediatric radiology under resource constraints (Sub-Saharan Africa)
model_description: Narrative review discussing barriers (hardware, annotated pediatric datasets, PACS integration, infrastructure) to deploying AI (image synthesis, reconstruction, segmentation) in pediatric radiology across African healthcare systems, and proposed solutions (federated learning, open datasets).

title: The application of artificial intelligence in blind ultrasound sweep diagnostics for prenatal medicine: A systematic literature review.
patient_population: 14 studies (12 original, 2 reviews) of AI applied to blind-sweep obstetric ultrasound
clinical_problem: using AI on minimally-trained blind ultrasound sweeps to expand access to prenatal diagnostics
model_description: Systematic review of AI models applied to standardized 'blind' transabdominal ultrasound sweeps performed by minimally trained operators, for gestational age estimation, breech detection, amniotic fluid assessment, and fetal anatomy segmentation.
headline_result: gestational age MAE 3-5 days; breech detection AUC ~0.98; amniotic fluid Dice ~0.88

title: Evaluating the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Medicine: Opportunities, Evidence, and Challenges, A Narrative Review.
patient_population: fetuses
clinical_problem: state of AI for prenatal anomaly detection, biometric analysis, and fetal diagnostics
model_description: narrative review of AI applications in fetal medicine, including congenital heart defect identification, brain structure segmentation, and fetal growth prediction

title: The current state of artificial intelligence research in pediatric radiology and recommendations for the future: a scoping review.
patient_population: 789 included articles on pediatric patients (<18 years), screened from 4,376
clinical_problem: mapping the landscape of AI research applied to pediatric radiology across clinical applications, modalities and subspecialties (2005-2024)
model_description: Scoping review of 789 articles (from 4,376 screened) applying AI to pediatric radiology, characterizing country of origin, imaging modality, subspecialty and AI task type.
headline_result: 789/4,376 articles included; top modalities radiography 37.8%, MRI 33.0%, ultrasound 14.4%; image interpretation/diagnosis 91.1% of tasks

title: Functional neurobehaviour of the human fetus: a comprehensive framework for prenatal assessment using 4D ultrasound and AI.
patient_population: 50 studies reviewed (2000-2025)
clinical_problem: Reviewing 4D ultrasound, structured scoring systems and AI platforms for prenatal assessment of fetal neurobehaviour to identify neurodevelopmental vulnerability
model_description: Narrative review of 4D-ultrasound-based fetal neurobehavioural assessment tools (KANET, prenatal General Movements Assessment) and AI-assisted classifiers providing objective quantification of fetal movement and facial activity from ultrasound video.

title: Artificial intelligence in diagnosis of pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders: a scoping review.
patient_population: 22 studies reviewed
clinical_problem: Reviewing AI technologies (deep learning, machine learning, decision support, biosignal analysis) for diagnosing pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders, including neuroimaging-based diagnosis
model_description: Scoping review of 22 studies: deep-learning models applied to neuroimaging achieved diagnostic accuracies exceeding 85% for pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders, while supervised machine learning improved autism/ADHD subtype classification.
headline_result: Deep-learning models exceeded 85% diagnostic accuracy in neuroimaging interpretation in most included studies

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Pediatric Endocrine Tumors: Opportunities, Pitfalls, and a Roadmap for Trustworthy Clinical Translation.
clinical_problem: Reviewing AI/ML applications, most robust in imaging, for diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment-response assessment in pediatric endocrine tumors
model_description: Pediatric-focused narrative review of AI/ML in endocrine tumors, covering imaging-based approaches such as CT/PET radiomics for metastatic risk and treatment response (largely extrapolated from adult evidence) alongside survival-prediction and recurrence models.

title: Deep learning in fetal, infant, and toddler neuroimaging research.
patient_population: fetuses, infants and toddlers in neuroimaging research broadly
clinical_problem: Reviewing how deep learning methods are being applied to fetal, infant, and toddler brain imaging research, given the field's especially scarce datasets and high anatomical variability
model_description: A narrative review, aimed at clinicians and developmental scientists without formal AI training, covering applications of deep learning in fetal, infant, and toddler neuroimaging research, including structural image analysis, enhancement of data acquisition, modeling of cognitive/perceptual processes, and automated video tagging.

title: Artificial intelligence and diagnosis and management of tuberculosis disease in children.
patient_population: 19 studies reviewed (Jan 2024-Jul 2025)
clinical_problem: Reviewing AI applications (chest X-ray CAD and prediction models) for diagnosing and managing pediatric tuberculosis in resource-constrained settings
model_description: Literature review of AI-driven chest X-ray analysis (CNNs, transfer learning, stacked ensemble ML) for detecting pediatric tuberculosis, alongside prediction models for treatment outcomes.
headline_result: Sensitivity 76.0-98.2%, specificity 70.0-98.0%, AUC up to 0.98 across reviewed AI-CXR TB detection studies

title: Performance of adult-trained artificial intelligence models in paediatric imaging-a scoping review.
body_region: multiple (radiography, CT, MRI, DEXA, ultrasound across various body regions)
patient_population: 16 pediatric imaging dataset cohorts across 20 included studies, ranging from 30 to 7,357 subjects
clinical_problem: Evaluating how much AI models trained on adult imaging data lose performance when applied to pediatric imaging without adaptation, across modalities, tasks and age groups
model_description: A scoping review of 20 studies evaluating adult-trained AI radiology tools (radiography, CT, MRI, DEXA, ultrasound; segmentation, classification, detection, and mixed tasks) applied to pediatric imaging without retraining, quantifying the resulting performance degradation by modality, task and age group.
headline_result: pulmonary nodule detection sensitivity dropped from 68-100% (adults) to 26-68% (children); segmentation Dice score reductions >0.10 across organs and modalities; greatest deficits in children 2 years old or younger

title: Foundation models in radiology: a primer for pediatric radiologists.
clinical_problem: applying foundation models across pediatric radiology tasks
model_description: Review introducing foundation model principles and architectures and their current/emerging applications in pediatric radiology (pathology detection/classification, segmentation, report generation, visual question answering), and challenges specific to pediatric imaging.

title: A modern radiologist's guide to artificial intelligence.
clinical_problem: Educate pediatric radiologists on AI concepts and applications across the radiology pipeline (referral, interpretation, recommendations) to help them evaluate clinical usefulness versus overpromise
model_description: A non-technical narrative overview of AI subfields and their potential applications and limitations for pediatric radiologists, emphasizing challenges specific to pediatrics such as smaller datasets and lack of pediatric-specific validation labeling.

title: Corrigendum to "Deep learning in fetal, infant, and toddler neuroimaging research"[Dev. Cognit. Neurosci. (2026), 101680].
model_description: Corrigendum (correction notice) to a review article on deep learning applications in fetal, infant, and toddler neuroimaging research; no substantive abstract content is available.

title: Artificial intelligence meets point-of-care ultrasound: implications for pediatric emergency and critical care.
clinical_problem: applying AI to point-of-care ultrasound in pediatric emergency and critical care
model_description: Narrative review of AI-assisted point-of-care ultrasound in pediatric emergency/critical care, covering image acquisition assistance, diagnostic accuracy, education, and limitations of adult-trained models applied to children.

title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric neuroradiology: current landscape, challenges, and future directions.
patient_population: pediatric and fetal neuroradiology patients (literature review)
clinical_problem: reviewing AI applications (segmentation, lesion detection, classification, prognostication, clinical decision support) in pediatric and fetal neuroradiology and barriers to clinical adoption
task: segmentation; detection / diagnosis; outcome prediction; other
model_description: Narrative review of deep-learning applications in paediatric brain imaging including automated brain tumour segmentation, epileptogenic lesion detection, and radiomics-based classifiers for tumour histology/molecular subtype prediction, alongside barriers to clinical adoption.

title: Leveraging AI solutions for sustainable practice in pediatric radiology: a practical guide and an educational tool.
clinical_problem: Illustrate how AI can address environmental, economic, and social sustainability challenges specific to pediatric imaging
model_description: A review proposing nine concrete AI solutions (three each for environmental, economic, and social sustainability pillars) to improve efficiency, equity and diagnostic accuracy in pediatric radiology practice.

title: [Delivering with Intelligence: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Intrapartum Ultrasound].
body_region: fetal head / maternal pelvis (intrapartum transperineal ultrasound)
patient_population: women in labor undergoing transperineal intrapartum ultrasound at Kaplan Medical Center
clinical_problem: automating measurement of fetal head position (Angle of Progression) to assess labor progression
model_description: A fully automated deep learning algorithm analyzes transperineal intrapartum ultrasound video, automatically identifies optimal frames, and measures the Angle of Progression without manual intervention, to standardize assessment of fetal head descent during labor.
release_evidence: preliminary results from a system developed at Kaplan Medical Center; no release stated
study_design: narrative review / single-center technical development, preliminary results

title: Data mining in pediatric radiology in the era of artificial intelligence.
patient_population: pediatric radiology patients generally
clinical_problem: how data mining and AI can be applied across pediatric radiology workflows, from diagnosis to operational analytics
model_description: A narrative review describing data mining and AI workflows in pediatric radiology, including deep learning, large language models, multimodal fusion and federated learning, applied to diagnosis, prognosis, radiation dose monitoring and operational analytics.

title: Automated Joint Space Width Assessment in Patients Treated for Juvenile Osteochondritis Dissecans of the Distal Femur: A Cross-Sectional Study and Systematic Review of the Literature.
patient_population: 21 skeletally immature patients treated for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the distal femur, 2002-2017
clinical_problem: monitoring joint space width / cartilage health after treatment for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the knee
model_description: IB Lab KOALA, a validated AI-based software, automatically measures joint space width on standardized anteroposterior knee radiographs, used here to compare the affected and contralateral knee and across treatment groups (conservative, drilling, fragment refixation) in juvenile osteochondritis dissecans.
release_evidence: validated AI-based software IB Lab KOALA(TM), Version 2.4
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional feasibility study with systematic review
headline_result: no significant JSW differences between affected/contralateral knee or treatment groups; average JSW >6 mm at median 64-month follow-up

title: Scaling Early Detection for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip With Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Imaging.
patient_population: infants and children evaluated for developmental dysplasia of the hip (literature review, no single cohort)
clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip using AI-assisted ultrasound and radiography
model_description: A literature review summarizing AI applications (deep learning, CNNs, segmentation networks, 3D convolutional models) for automated landmark detection and measurement of the alpha angle, beta angle, and acetabular index on hip ultrasound and radiographs, for diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip.

title: Artificial intelligence in preterm birth prediction: a narrative review of current approaches and clinical applicability.
patient_population: pregnant women assessed for preterm birth risk across reviewed studies
clinical_problem: predicting spontaneous preterm birth using AI
model_description: A narrative review of AI approaches to predicting spontaneous preterm birth, including electronic-health-record models, deep learning analysis of cervical ultrasound images, cervical texture/radiomics feature extraction, elastography-derived parameters, and multi-omics transformer models, evaluating their methodological quality against TRIPOD and risk-of-bias criteria.
